### The form's state, and starting over

Reading the form's state: `isValid` says whether the form passes without showing any error, `fields` gives its fields; each field has its `isValid()`, its `touched` and its `error`. The lines underneath change as you type.

"Bring the saved address" gives the fields a new starting value with `reset(value)`: as a record that comes from a server, untouched and with no error. "Start over" takes every field back to its first value with `form.reset()`.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.widthIn
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rules
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.field
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.rememberFormState
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.textfield.PantrixTextField
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val form = rememberFormState()
val street = form.field("street", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Type the street"))
val city = form.field("city", initial = "", Rules.notBlank("Type the city"))
val postcode = form.field("postcode", initial = "", Rules.matches(POSTCODE, "A postcode is five digits"))
Column(
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 400.dp),
    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md)
) {
    PantrixTextField(field = street, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), label = "Street")
    PantrixTextField(field = city, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), label = "City")
    PantrixTextField(
        field = postcode,
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        label = "Postcode",
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number)
    )
    val missing = form.fields.filterNot { it.isValid() }.map { ADDRESS_LABELS.getValue(it.id) }
    PantrixText(
        text = if (form.isValid) "The address is complete" else "Missing: ${missing.joinToString()}",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        tagKey = "address_state"
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = "Fields touched: ${form.fields.count { it.touched }} / ${form.fields.size}, " +
            "showing an error: ${form.fields.count { it.error != null }}",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
    )
    FlowRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
        PantrixButton(
            text = "Bring the saved address",
            onClick = {
                street.reset("Atatürk Bulvarı 12")
                city.reset("Ankara")
                postcode.reset("06690")
            },
            variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
            tagKey = "saved_address"
        )
        PantrixButton(
            text = "Start over",
            onClick = form::reset,
            variant = ButtonVariant.Text,
            tagKey = "start_over"
        )
    }
}

private val POSTCODE = Regex("[0-9]{5}")

private val ADDRESS_LABELS = mapOf("street" to "street", "city" to "city", "postcode" to "postcode")
```

### A component bound by hand

A component that takes no `field` joins a form too: it shows the field's `value`, calls `onValueChange` when it changes and `onFocusLost` when the focus leaves it, and writes the `error` itself. With the `focusRequester` bound to it, `focusFirstError()` can give the focus to it too. Here the delivery time is a `PantrixSegmentButton`, and no order is placed until one is chosen.

Press "Place the order" without choosing a time: the error shows under the segments and the focus goes to them.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.widthIn
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.focus.focusRequester
import androidx.compose.ui.focus.onFocusChanged
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rules
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.field
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.rememberFormState
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.textfield.PantrixTextField
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
val form = rememberFormState()
val slot = form.field<String?>("delivery", initial = null, Rules.required("Choose a delivery time"))
val note = form.field("note", initial = "", Rules.maxLength(80, "A note can be at most 80 characters"))
var hadFocus by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
Column(
    modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 400.dp),
    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md)
) {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        PantrixText(text = "Delivery time", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        PantrixSegmentButton(
            options = DELIVERY_SLOTS,
            selected = slot.value,
            onSelect = slot::onValueChange,
            modifier = Modifier
                .focusRequester(slot.focusRequester)
                .onFocusChanged { focus ->
                    if (hadFocus && !focus.hasFocus) slot.onFocusLost()
                    hadFocus = focus.hasFocus
                },
            tagKey = slot.id
        )
        slot.error?.let { error ->
            PantrixText(
                text = error,
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.danger.color
            )
        }
    }
    PantrixTextField(field = note, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), form = form, label = "Note to the courier")
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Place the order",
        onClick = {
            val chosen = DELIVERY_SLOTS.first { it.value == slot.value }
            report("Order placed: ${chosen.label}")
        },
        form = form,
        tagKey = "order"
    )
}

private val DELIVERY_SLOTS = listOf(
    SegmentOption<String?>("morning", "Morning", tagKey = "morning"),
    SegmentOption<String?>("afternoon", "Afternoon", tagKey = "afternoon"),
    SegmentOption<String?>("evening", "Evening", tagKey = "evening")
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

## API

### FormState

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.FormState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class FormState
```

A form's fields and its submission lifecycle.

Holds three things components would otherwise each reinvent, differently: which field to focus when validation fails, whether a submission is in flight, and what Enter does.

`@Stable` is a claim the compiler cannot prove but the class honours: everything a composable reads is snapshot state, and the one plain field — the submit handler — is never read during composition. Without it the compiler reports the class unstable, and the compiler-metrics gate rejects every component that takes a `form`.

Members:

- `fields: List<FormField<*>>`: The form's fields, in the order they were declared: the first one in error takes the focus on a submit.
- `isSubmitting: Boolean`: True while `submit` is running.

  `PantrixButton(form = ...)` reads this for its loading state, so a form cannot be submitted twice by an impatient second tap — the disabled state comes from the same source of truth as the spinner rather than from a separate flag someone has to remember to set.
- `isValid: Boolean`: Whether every field currently passes, without marking anything touched.
- `fun validateAll(): Boolean`: Validates everything and marks every field touched, so errors become visible.

  Touching on submit is what makes "press submit on an empty form" show all the errors at once rather than one per attempt.
- `fun focusFirstError(): Boolean`: Moves focus to the first field in error. Returns false when there is nothing to focus.

  Scrolling a long form to the problem is the difference between a fixable error and a user staring at a submit button that does nothing. Skips fields whose component is not currently composed — requesting focus on a detached FocusRequester throws.
- `suspend fun submit(block: suspend () -> Unit)`: Validates, then runs `block` if everything passed.

  Owns `isSubmitting` around the call so the flag cannot be left stuck on by an early return or an exception — the single most common bug in hand-written form submission.
- `fun reset()`: Starts the form over. Every field on screen goes back to its initial value, untouched and without an error, and is still validated. Fields that have left the screen are forgotten; one that comes back registers again.
- `fun requestSubmit()`: Invoked when a field reports that Enter was pressed.

### rememberFormState

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.rememberFormState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberFormState(): FormState
```

A `FormState` kept across recompositions; it is not saved state. Declare its fields with `field`.

### FormState.field

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.field`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> FormState.field(
    id: String,
    initial: T,
    vararg rules: Rule<T>
): FormField<T>
```

Declares a field.

Remembered by `id`, so the value survives recomposition but a genuinely different field — a different row of a dynamic list — gets its own state.

Parameters:

- `id: String`
- `initial: T`: the value the field starts with, and goes back to when it is reset.
- `vararg rules: Rule<T>`: the rules the value is checked against, in their order: the first one that fails gives the field's message.

### FormField

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.FormField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class FormField<T>
```

One field in a form: its value, its rules, and whether it is currently in error.

`id` doubles as the component's automation tag, so a form-bound component needs no `tagKey` — the field already carries a stable, locale-independent name.

`@Stable` for the same reason as `FormState`: `value`, `error` and `touched` are snapshot state, and `isAttached` is bookkeeping that composition never reads.

Parameters:

- `id: String`: The field's name in its form, and the automation tag of the component bound to it.

Members:

- `value: T`: What the field holds now: its first value until the user gives another, and that value again after a reset.
- `error: String?`: The message to show, or null.

  Stays null until the field has been `touched` or the form has been submitted. Showing "Required" the instant a form opens tells the user they have done something wrong before they have done anything at all.
- `touched: Boolean`: True once the user has interacted with this field.
- `focusRequester: FocusRequester`: What the field is focused by: the component bound to it attaches it, and a submit that finds the field in error moves the focus there.
- `fun onValueChange(newValue: T)`: Called by components on change. Re-validates only once the field has been touched.

  `newValue`: the value the user has given the field.
- `fun onFocusLost()`: Called by components on blur. Marks touched and validates, which is the usual moment to show an error.
- `fun validate(): Boolean`: Runs every rule and publishes the first failure. Returns true when the field is valid.
- `fun isValid(): Boolean`: Whether the field would pass, without publishing an error the user has not earned yet.
- `fun reset(newValue: T)`: Puts the field back as it was before the user touched it: `newValue` as its value, and no error.

### Rule

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rule`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
fun interface Rule<in T>
```

A validation rule. Returns the error message, or null when the value is acceptable.

Rules carry their own message rather than an error code because the message has to be translated by whoever wrote the form — the library cannot know that a field called `code` wants "Enter the 6-digit code" rather than "Invalid input".

Members:

- `fun check(value: T): String?`: The error message for `value`, or null when `value` is acceptable.

### Rules

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rules`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
object Rules
```

The rules that come up in nearly every form.

Members:

- `fun notBlank(message: String): Rule<String>`: For non-null text. Rejects whitespace-only input, which `isEmpty` would let through.

  `message`: what the field says while its text is blank.
- `fun <T : Any> required(message: String): Rule<T?>`: For nullable values — a select with nothing chosen, an unset date.

  `message`: what the field says while nothing is chosen.
- `fun mustBeTrue(message: String): Rule<Boolean>`: Consent checkboxes: "accept the terms" is not satisfied by merely having a value.

  `message`: what the field says while it is not ticked.
- `fun minLength(length: Int, message: String): Rule<String>`: At least `length` characters, not counting leading and trailing whitespace.

  `message`: what the field says while its text is shorter than `length`.
- `fun maxLength(length: Int, message: String): Rule<String>`: At most `length` characters, whitespace included.

  `message`: what the field says while its text is longer than `length`.
- `fun matches(pattern: Regex, message: String): Rule<String>`: The whole value matches `pattern`; matching part of it is not enough.

  `message`: what the field says while its text does not match `pattern`.
- `fun <T> satisfies(message: String, predicate: (T) -> Boolean): Rule<T>`: Escape hatch for rules that depend on something outside the field — a password confirmation, a date range, a server-side uniqueness check already performed.

  `message`: what the field says while `predicate` does not accept its value.

  `predicate`: whether a value is accepted.

### FormState.RegisterSubmit

`import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.RegisterSubmit`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun FormState.RegisterSubmit(onSubmit: () -> Unit)
```

Points Enter at a submit action.

The last registration wins, which matches what a user expects on a form with both "Save" and "Save and add another": Enter triggers the primary action, and the primary action is the one declared last in the footer.

Parameters:

- `onSubmit: () -> Unit`: what Enter in a field of the form does: the form's primary action.

# Date Picker

Choosing a day or a stretch of days from a calendar turned a month at a time. The calendar is the choice itself: it stands in the page, or is put in a popover, a dialog or a sheet. It does not keep the choice; the chosen day comes to `onSelect`.

- `PantrixDatePicker` (`com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker`, `com.pantrixui:components`): A calendar to choose a day or a stretch of days from, a month at a time, with the days that cannot be chosen drawn faint and a grid of years to turn it far. Keywords: calendar, date selector, date range, month view, day picker.

## Features

- **Navigation.** The arrows turn the month; pressing the title shows the years in place of the days, and choosing a year turns the calendar to the same month of it. Where the chosen day is not on show, the calendar goes to its month.
- **Days that cannot be chosen.** The days outside `minDate` and `maxDate`, and those `isDateEnabled` leaves out, are drawn faint and cannot be pressed; the arrows do not go past the ends.
- **Stretch.** The first press chooses the stretch's first day and the second its last; a press on a day before the first starts the stretch again there. While the last is chosen, the days to the one under the pointer are shown in a lighter colour.
- **Keyboard.** The calendar is one Tab stop. The arrows walk a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month, with Shift a year, Home and End to the week's first and last day; Enter and Space choose.
- **Screen reader.** Each day is read in full with the day of the week ("Saturday, October 17, 2026"); chosen, today, and the start, the middle and the end of a stretch are said. When the month changes, the new month is announced politely.
- **Week.** It starts on the language's day: Sunday in English, Monday in Turkish, Saturday in Arabic; `firstDayOfWeek` changes it.
- **Today.** The ringed day is the today of the screen's clock and turns by itself at midnight. The screen's clock is `LocalPantrixClock`, the device's by default (`PantrixClock.System`); another place's day is given by `today`, or for a whole screen by `LocalPantrixClock`.
- **Platform.** A day's room is the platform's least touch target on a phone (48dp on Android, 44pt on iOS), and 36dp on the desktop and the web. In a narrow place the days shrink until they fit.
- **Date type.** Days are `PantrixDate`s, and no date library is needed; docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md turns them into `kotlinx-datetime`'s or `java.time`'s.

## Usage

### A delivery day within the next month, on weekdays

```kotlin
var delivery by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
val today = rememberToday()
PantrixDatePicker(
    selected = delivery,
    onSelect = { delivery = it },
    minDate = today.plusDays(1),
    maxDate = today.plusMonths(1),
    isDateEnabled = { it.dayOfWeek <= 5 },
    tagKey = "delivery"
)
```

### The nights of a stay, from a week that starts on Monday

```kotlin
var stay by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDateRange?>(null) }
PantrixDatePicker(
    selectedRange = stay,
    onRangeSelect = { stay = it },
    minDate = rememberToday(),
    firstDayOfWeek = 1,
    tagKey = "stay"
)
```

## Examples

### One day in a popover

A button shows the chosen day and opens the calendar under it in a popover; choosing a day closes the popover. The days before today cannot be chosen.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.icon.PantrixIcon
import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PantrixPopover
import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.popover.PopoverAlignment
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var due by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixPopover(
    visible = open,
    onDismissRequest = { open = false },
    anchor = {
        PantrixButton(
            text = due?.let(strings::written) ?: "Choose a due date",
            onClick = { open = !open },
            variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
            leadingIcon = { PantrixIcon(PantrixIcons.Calendar, contentDescription = null) },
            tagKey = "due"
        )
    },
    alignment = PopoverAlignment.Start,
    tagKey = "due"
) {
    PantrixDatePicker(
        selected = due,
        onSelect = {
            due = it
            open = false
        },
        minDate = rememberToday(),
        tagKey = "due"
    )
}

private fun PantrixStrings.written(day: PantrixDate): String = date(day.day, day.month, day.year)
```

### A weekday stretch in the page

A stretch of leave from a calendar that stands in the page: only weekdays can be its ends, and the week starts on Monday in every language. The chosen stretch is written under the calendar.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDateRange
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var leave by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDateRange?>(null) }
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixDatePicker(
        selectedRange = leave,
        onRangeSelect = { leave = it },
        isDateEnabled = { it.dayOfWeek <= FRIDAY },
        firstDayOfWeek = MONDAY,
        tagKey = "leave"
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = leave?.let { "Leave: ${strings.written(it.start)} – ${strings.written(it.end)}" }
            ?: "Choose the first and the last day of the leave",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.body
    )
}

private fun PantrixStrings.written(day: PantrixDate): String = date(day.day, day.month, day.year)

private const val MONDAY = 1

private const val FRIDAY = 5
```

### Limited days in a dialog

One of the next thirty days, in a dialog. The choice in the calendar is a draft: OK takes it, and Cancel or a press outside the dialog leaves it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.dialog.PantrixDialog
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var appointment by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
var draft by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
val today = rememberToday()
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
PantrixButton(
    text = appointment?.let { "Appointment: ${strings.written(it)}" } ?: "Choose the appointment day",
    onClick = {
        draft = appointment
        open = true
    },
    variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
    tagKey = "appointment"
)
PantrixDialog(
    visible = open,
    onDismissRequest = { open = false },
    title = "Appointment day",
    actions = {
        PantrixButton(text = "Cancel", onClick = { open = false }, variant = ButtonVariant.Text, tagKey = "cancel")
        PantrixButton(
            text = "OK",
            onClick = {
                appointment = draft
                open = false
                report("Appointment chosen")
            },
            enabled = draft != null,
            tagKey = "accept"
        )
    },
    tagKey = "appointment"
) {
    PantrixDatePicker(
        selected = draft,
        onSelect = { draft = it },
        minDate = today,
        maxDate = today.plusDays(DAYS_AHEAD),
        tagKey = "appointment"
    )
}

private fun PantrixStrings.written(day: PantrixDate): String = date(day.day, day.month, day.year)

private const val DAYS_AHEAD = 30
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### A birthday in a sheet, with the years

A birthday in a sheet: no day after today can be chosen. A year far off is chosen from the years the title opens; the calendar turns to the same month of that year. The calendar fills the sheet's width (`fillMaxWidth`): its columns widen, and in a very wide sheet it stands in the middle.

```kotlin

import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
```

### Another place's today

The calendar's today by a hotel's clock, not the device's: `today` gives the ring of today, and `minDate` with it the first day that can be chosen. Kiritimati (UTC+14) and Pago Pago (UTC-11) are 25 hours apart, so the two are always on different days: as the place changes, the ring and the first day move by a day. Where `today` is not given it is the day of the screen's clock (`rememberToday()`) and turns by itself at midnight; this example reads the hotel's day as the place is chosen.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import kotlin.time.Clock
import kotlin.time.Duration
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.hours

var hotel by remember { mutableStateOf(Hotel.Kiritimati) }
var arrival by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
val today = remember(hotel) { PantrixDate.of(Clock.System.now(), offset = hotel.offset) }
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixSegmentButton(
        options = listOf(
            SegmentOption(Hotel.Kiritimati, "Kiritimati", tagKey = "kiritimati"),
            SegmentOption(Hotel.PagoPago, "Pago Pago", tagKey = "pago_pago")
        ),
        selected = hotel,
        onSelect = {
            hotel = it
            arrival = null
        },
        fullWidth = false,
        tagKey = "hotel"
    )
    PantrixDatePicker(
        selected = arrival,
        onSelect = { arrival = it },
        minDate = today,
        today = today,
        tagKey = "arrival"
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = "Today at the hotel: ${strings.written(today)} (${hotel.zone})",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.body
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = arrival?.let { "Arrival: ${strings.written(it)}" } ?: "Choose the day of arrival",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.body
    )
}

private enum class Hotel(
    val zone: String,
    val offset: Duration
) {
    Kiritimati("UTC+14", 14.hours),
    PagoPago("UTC-11", (-11).hours)
}

private fun PantrixStrings.written(day: PantrixDate): String = date(day.day, day.month, day.year)
```

### The screen's clock

A whole screen's clock: `LocalPantrixClock` gives the hotel's clock, and everything inside it reads it. The calendar is given no `today`; its ring, `rememberToday()` and the time itself are by the hotel's clock. A preview or a test shows a screen on a day and at an hour this way: `PantrixClock(clock, utcOffset)` takes a `Clock` of its own as well.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.CompositionLocalProvider
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.LocalPantrixClock
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixClock
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import kotlin.time.Clock
import kotlin.time.Duration
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.hours

var hotel by remember { mutableStateOf(Hotel.Kiritimati) }
val clock = remember(hotel) { PantrixClock(Clock.System) { hotel.offset } }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixSegmentButton(
        options = listOf(
            SegmentOption(Hotel.Kiritimati, "Kiritimati", tagKey = "kiritimati"),
            SegmentOption(Hotel.PagoPago, "Pago Pago", tagKey = "pago_pago")
        ),
        selected = hotel,
        onSelect = { hotel = it },
        fullWidth = false,
        tagKey = "screen_hotel"
    )
    CompositionLocalProvider(LocalPantrixClock provides clock) {
        var arrival by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
        PantrixDatePicker(selected = arrival, onSelect = { arrival = it }, tagKey = "screen_arrival")
        val today = rememberToday()
        val now = LocalPantrixClock.current.time()
        val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
        PantrixText(
            text = "Today on the screen: ${strings.written(today)}, at ${strings.clock(now.hour, now.minute)}",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.body
        )
    }
}

private enum class Hotel(
    val zone: String,
    val offset: Duration
) {
    Kiritimati("UTC+14", 14.hours),
    PagoPago("UTC-11", (-11).hours)
}

private fun PantrixStrings.written(day: PantrixDate): String = date(day.day, day.month, day.year)
```

### Its own colours and disabled

The calendar's own colours and measure, and a switch that disables it. The ends of a stretch are in the success colour, the days between in its light fill, and the ring of today in the warning colour; every colour not given is the theme's. The calendar has no padding of its own (`padding = 0.dp`): it stands in the card's. With the switch off the calendar is faint: no day is chosen and the month does not turn, and the chosen stretch stays.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.DatePickerColors
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.DatePickerStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDateRange
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var trip by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDateRange?>(null) }
var enabled by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixSwitchButton(
        checked = enabled,
        onCheckedChange = { enabled = it },
        label = "Can be chosen",
        tagKey = "trip_enabled"
    )
    PantrixDatePicker(
        selectedRange = trip,
        onRangeSelect = { trip = it },
        enabled = enabled,
        style = DatePickerStyle(padding = 0.dp),
        colors = DatePickerColors(
            selectedContainer = colors.success.color,
            rangeContainer = colors.success.container,
            today = colors.warning.color
        ),
        tagKey = "trip"
    )
}
```

## API

### PantrixDatePicker

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDatePicker(
    selected: PantrixDate?,
    onSelect: (PantrixDate) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    style: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A calendar to choose a day from, a month at a time: the month's title between the arrows that turn it, the days of the week over its columns, and its days.

The calendar is the choice itself, and stands where it is put: in the page, or in a `PantrixPopover`, a `PantrixDialog` or a `PantrixSheet` that a button or a field opens. It paints no ground of its own and holds nothing of the choice: `selected` is the caller's, and a press on a day hands it to `onSelect`. What it keeps is the month on show, which starts at the chosen day's, or today's, and goes to the chosen day's month when the caller chooses one that is not on show.

The days a calendar cannot take are drawn faint and cannot be chosen: those before `minDate` and after `maxDate`, which the arrows do not turn to either, and those between that `isDateEnabled` leaves out, a weekend, a day that is full. Pressing the title shows the years in place of the days, and choosing one turns the calendar to the same month of that year.

The calendar is one stop for Tab, on the chosen day, today or the month's first, and its keys walk the days as a calendar's do: the arrows a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month, with Shift a year, Home and End the week's first and last day; Enter and Space choose. A screen reader hears each day in full, with the day of the week, and is told politely when the month changes.

Days are `PantrixDate`s, with no library of dates: docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md turns them into an app's own.

```kotlin
var due by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
PantrixDatePicker(
    selected = due,
    onSelect = { due = it },
    minDate = PantrixDate.today(),
    tagKey = "due"
)
```

Parameters:

- `selected: PantrixDate?`: the chosen day, or null while none is.
- `onSelect: (PantrixDate) -> Unit`: handed the day a press chose: one that can be chosen.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the calendar's modifier. The calendar is seven days wide, and narrower where it is given less room. Given a width, as `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` gives it the width of a sheet, it fills it: its columns grow as far as `DatePickerStyle.maxCellWidth`, and past that it stands in the middle.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day that can be chosen, or null for none so early.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day that can be chosen, or null for none so late.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether a day between them can be chosen, or null where every one can.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the weeks start on, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Null is the language's, `PantrixLocale.firstDayOfWeek`: Sunday in English, Monday in Turkish, Saturday in Arabic.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a day can be chosen at all. A calendar that takes no choice is drawn faint.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day marked as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight. A test gives a day of its own.
- `style: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: DatePickerColors?`: this calendar's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the calendar's automation key: it is `DatePicker_<tagKey>`, and its days are `DatePicker_<tagKey>.Day_2026_10_17`.

### PantrixDatePicker

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.PantrixDatePicker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDatePicker(
    selectedRange: PantrixDateRange?,
    onRangeSelect: (PantrixDateRange) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    style: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    colors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A calendar to choose a stretch of days from: a stay, a leave, the days a report is of. It is the calendar that chooses a day, pressed twice: its first press chooses the first day of the stretch and its second the last.

The second press ends the stretch on its day, or on the first day again for a stretch of one day, and `onRangeSelect` is handed the stretch; one before the first day starts the stretch again from there. Between the two presses the first day is the calendar's own, and under a pointer the stretch it would make is drawn lighter. A stretch may run over days that cannot be chosen; its first and its last day are ones that can.

`selectedRange` is the caller's: the calendar draws it with its first and last day marked and a band under the days between, and goes to its first day's month when the caller chooses one of which no day is on show.

Parameters:

- `selectedRange: PantrixDateRange?`: the chosen stretch, or null while none is.
- `onRangeSelect: (PantrixDateRange) -> Unit`: handed the stretch two presses chose.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the calendar's modifier. The calendar is seven days wide, and narrower where it is given less room; given a width, it fills it as far as `DatePickerStyle.maxCellWidth` lets its columns grow.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day that can be chosen, or null for none so early.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day that can be chosen, or null for none so late.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether a day between them can be the first or the last day of a stretch, or null where every one can.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the weeks start on, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Null is the language's, `PantrixLocale.firstDayOfWeek`.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether a stretch can be chosen at all. A calendar that takes no choice is drawn faint.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day marked as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight. A test gives a day of its own.
- `style: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: DatePickerColors?`: this calendar's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the calendar's automation key: it is `DatePicker_<tagKey>`, and its days are `DatePicker_<tagKey>.Day_2026_10_17`.

### DatePickerStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.DatePickerStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class DatePickerStyle(
    public val cellSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val daySize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val padding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val maxCellWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<DatePickerStyle>
```

`PantrixDatePicker`'s geometry: the room of a day, the round mark a chosen day is drawn in, and the room around the month.

A day's room is as wide as a column of the week and as tall as a row of it, and the days touch: a press anywhere in the room is the day's. On a phone it is the platform's least touch target, 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS, so that a month is seven targets wide, 360dp across on Android as a Material calendar is. Under a pointer it is 36dp. A place too narrow for the month makes every day's room narrower, and its mark with it, by the same share. A calendar given more width than that, as a sheet gives it with `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`, widens its columns to fill it, up to `maxCellWidth`, and stands in the middle of what is left; its rows and its marks keep their size.

The room around the month and the gap under its title follow the density; a day's room, its widest and its mark do not, as a touch target does not.

Parameters:

- `cellSize: Dp`: The width and the height of a day's room: the column and the row. The title and the year's rooms are as tall.
- `daySize: Dp`: The width and the height of the round mark a chosen day, today and the day under a pointer are drawn in, in the middle of its room. A stretch of days is a band as tall.
- `padding: Dp`: The room between the calendar's edge and what it holds.
- `gap: Dp`: Between the title and the days of the week over the month.
- `maxCellWidth: Dp`: The widest a column grows to where the calendar is given more width than seven days' rooms: half as wide again as `cellSize`.

### DatePickerColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datepicker.DatePickerColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class DatePickerColors(
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val weekday: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContainer: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val selectedContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val rangeContainer: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val rangeContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val today: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val hover: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val disabled: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixDatePicker` is painted with, in place of the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

A `selectedContainer` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for the chosen day's number, unless `selectedContent` is given too, and a `rangeContainer` brings its pair for the days of a stretch, unless `rangeContent` is given. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

The calendar paints no ground of its own: it stands on what is under it, a popover's, a dialog's, a sheet's or a page's, and its words are the theme's for its grounds.

Parameters:

- `content: Color`: The days' numbers, the title and the arrows. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `weekday: Color`: The days of the week over the columns. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `selectedContainer: Color`: The round mark of a chosen day, and of a stretch's first and last. The primary role's `color`.
- `selectedContent: Color`: The number on it. The primary role's `onColor`, or the colour a role's fill given as `selectedContainer` gives what stands on it.
- `rangeContainer: Color`: The band under the days between a stretch's first and last. The primary role's `container`. While the last is being chosen under a pointer, the band to the day under it is drawn in half of it.
- `rangeContent: Color`: The numbers on the band. The primary role's `onContainer`.
- `today: Color`: The ring around today, and its number. The primary role's `color`.
- `hover: Color`: The round mark under a pointer: which day a press would choose. A share of `content`.
- `disabled: Color`: The numbers of the days that cannot be chosen, and everything of a calendar that takes no choice. The theme's `textDisabled`.

### PantrixDate

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
class PantrixDate(
    public val year: Int,
    public val month: Int,
    public val day: Int
) : Comparable<PantrixDate>
```

A day on the calendar: a year, a month and a day of the month, with no time of day and no time zone.

Pantrix takes no library of dates. A component that spoke one would put it into the API of every app that shows a date, and which one an app uses is not a design system's to choose: this is three numbers, which an app turns into its own type and back in a line, `PantrixDate(date.year, date.month.number, date.day)` from `kotlinx-datetime`'s `LocalDate` and the same from `java.time`'s. docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md has the lines for each.

The calendar is the one in use now, the Gregorian, and is taken back before its start as it is forwards: a year before the first is written as nought, then as less than nought.

Parameters:

- `year: Int`: The year, as it is written.
- `month: Int`: The month, 1 for January to 12 for December.
- `day: Int`: The day of the month, from 1 to the month's last.

Members:

- `dayOfWeek: Int`: The day of the week this day falls on, as ISO 8601 numbers it: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday.
- `epochDays: Long`: The days from the first of January 1970 to this one: nought on that day, and less than nought before it.
- `fun plusDays(days: Int): PantrixDate`: The day `days` after this one, or before it where `days` is less than nought.
- `fun plusMonths(months: Int): PantrixDate`: The same day `months` months after this one, or before it where `months` is less than nought. Where that month is shorter, its last day: a month after the 31st of January is the last day of February.
- `fun plusYears(years: Int): PantrixDate`: The same day `years` years after this one, or before it: the 29th of February is the 28th in a common year.
- `fun at(time: PantrixTime, offsetAt: (Instant) -> Duration = ::systemUtcOffset): Instant`: The moment a clock shows `time` on this day: by default the device's own clock, whose offset from UTC `offsetAt` tells for each moment, as `systemUtcOffset` does, summer time and all.

  Where the clock is put back and shows the time twice, it is the first of the two, as `java.time` takes it. Where it is put forward and never shows the time, it is as far past the hour it skips as the time is into it: half past two on a night that goes from two to three is half past three.

On the type:

- `PantrixDate.ofEpochDays(days: Long): PantrixDate`: The day `days` days after the first of January 1970, or before it where `days` is less than nought.
- `PantrixDate.of(moment: Instant, offset: Duration = systemUtcOffset(moment)): PantrixDate`: The day a clock `offset` ahead of UTC shows at `moment`: by default the device's own clock, as `systemUtcOffset` tells it.
- `PantrixDate.today(): PantrixDate`: The day the device's clock shows now. A screen reads `rememberToday` instead: the day the screen's clock shows, asked again at each midnight.
- `PantrixDate.parse(text: String): PantrixDate`: The day ISO 8601 writes as `text`: `2026-10-17`, with four digits of year or more and a sign before a year less than nought, as `toString` writes it.
- `PantrixDate.daysInMonth(year: Int, month: Int): Int`: How many days the month `month` of `year` has: 28 to 31, the 29th of February in a leap year.
- `PantrixDate.isLeapYear(year: Int): Boolean`: Whether `year` has a 29th of February: every fourth year, but not every hundredth, but every four hundredth.

### PantrixDateRange

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDateRange`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
class PantrixDateRange(
    public val start: PantrixDate,
    public val end: PantrixDate
)
```

A stretch of days from `start` to `end`, both of them in it: a stay, a leave, the days a report is of. A stretch of one day starts and ends on it.

Parameters:

- `start: PantrixDate`
- `end: PantrixDate`

Members:

- `operator fun contains(date: PantrixDate): Boolean`: Whether `date` is one of the stretch's days, its first and its last among them.

### rememberToday

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberToday(): PantrixDate
```

The day the screen's clock shows, as a screen that stays open past midnight has it: it turns to the next day as the clock does, and what reads it is drawn again. A calendar marks today by it. The clock is `LocalPantrixClock`'s: the device's, unless a test or a preview gives another.

It asks the clock again at each midnight of the clock's own time, and not in between: a clock set by hand or a journey into another time zone shows the next time the screen is built, or at the next midnight.

### PantrixClock

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixClock`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
class PantrixClock(
    public val clock: Clock,
    public val utcOffset: (Instant) -> Duration
)
```

Where a screen reads the time: the moment it is now, and how far the clock it is shown by is ahead of UTC at a moment. `rememberToday` reads the day from it, the time field the hour its picker opens at, the elastic date picker its ranges and a chart its moments. `System` is the device's; a test or a preview gives one of its own through `LocalPantrixClock`, to see a screen on a day and at an hour it chooses.

Parameters:

- `clock: Clock`: what the moment is now.
- `utcOffset: (Instant) -> Duration`: how far the clock is ahead of UTC at a moment: three hours in Istanbul, less than nought west of Greenwich, and summer time where it is kept.

Members:

- `fun today(): PantrixDate`: The day this clock shows now.
- `fun time(): PantrixTime`: The time this clock shows now, to the second.

On the type:

- `PantrixClock.System: PantrixClock`: The device's clock, in the device's time zone.

### LocalPantrixClock

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.LocalPantrixClock`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalPantrixClock: ProvidableCompositionLocal<PantrixClock>
```

The clock the screen is read by: `PantrixClock.System` unless a test or a preview gives another.

# Date Text Field

A text field for a day: the day is typed in digits, or chosen from a calendar that the button at the box's end opens. The label stands above the box; the field is drawn as a `PantrixTextField`.

- `PantrixDateTextField` (`com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield`, `com.pantrixui:components`): A text field for a day, typed in digits in the locale's order or chosen from a calendar its button opens, with its own errors for a day it does not take. Keywords: date input, birthday, date entry, masked date, calendar input.

## Features

- **Digits alone.** The field takes digits alone; as each part is whole its mark comes by itself: in Turkish `18102026` becomes `18.10.2026`, in American English `10182026` becomes `10/18/2026`. A phone opens its keyboard of digits. Backspace after a mark deletes the digit before it.
- **A pasted day.** A day written out is read as it is written: in the field's order first, and else with the year first, as in ISO 8601. In Turkish `2026-10-18` becomes `18.10.2026` too; a year of two digits is one of the hundred years around today (`18.10.26`, 2026). A text not read so comes in as its digits.
- **Format.** `format` gives the order of the parts and the mark between them; by default it comes from the theme's language and region: Turkish and German `GG.AA.YYYY`, Britain and Arabic `DD/MM/YYYY`, the US `MM/DD/YYYY`, a language not known ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`). While empty the field shows the pattern; a screen reader hears it as the order of the parts ("Day, Month, Year").
- **Value.** `onValueChange` is called each time the field's day changes: a whole day the calendar takes, or null where the field holds nothing, half a day, digits that make no day or a day it does not take. A half-typed day stays on the screen while `value` is null; another day from outside is written into the field.
- **Its own error.** The field writes what is typed wrong under the box itself: a date not finished, once the field is left, a day the calendar has not (31 February), a day outside `minDate` and `maxDate`, a day `isDateEnabled` does not take. The app's `error` comes first; its message is `supportingText`.
- **Calendar.** It opens with the button, with Alt+↓ on the desktop and the web, by pressing the box of a read-only field, and with Enter or Space. `presentation` says what it opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one; or in every window a popover, a sheet or a dialog; the same on every platform. Pressing a day in the calendar takes the day and closes the calendar; Escape and pressing outside close it with nothing changed. Opened with the keyboard the focus goes to the chosen day, or else to today; once it closes it is back on the field.
- **Three overloads.** The one with `value` and `onValueChange`; the one with `state` (`rememberDateTextFieldState()`): `date` is the field's day, setting it puts the day in the field, `text` tells a half-typed field from an empty one; the one with `field` binds to a form's field.
- **Date type.** Days are `PantrixDate`s; to convert them to `kotlinx-datetime` or `java.time`, docs/guide/date-time/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md.

## Usage

### A birthday, typed

```kotlin
var birthday by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
PantrixDateTextField(
    value = birthday,
    onValueChange = { birthday = it },
    label = stringResource(Res.string.birthday),
    maxDate = rememberToday(),
    tagKey = "birthday"
)
```

### A delivery day on a weekday, from a sheet

```kotlin
var delivery by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
val today = rememberToday()
PantrixDateTextField(
    value = delivery,
    onValueChange = { delivery = it },
    label = stringResource(Res.string.delivery_day),
    minDate = today.plusDays(1),
    maxDate = today.plusMonths(1),
    isDateEnabled = { it.dayOfWeek <= 5 },
    presentation = DatePickerPresentation.Sheet,
    tagKey = "delivery"
)
```

### On a state, half typed or whole

```kotlin
val start = rememberDateTextFieldState()
PantrixDateTextField(
    state = start,
    label = stringResource(Res.string.start_date),
    format = DateFieldFormat.Iso,
    tagKey = "start"
)
val shown = start.date?.toString() ?: if (start.text.isEmpty()) "–" else "…"
```

## Examples

### A birthday, typed

A birthday, typed: a day after today is not taken. The calendar opens too, but typing a far year is quicker. Once the day is whole it is written below; left half typed, the field shows its error that says the pattern.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var birthday by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixDateTextField(
        value = birthday,
        onValueChange = { birthday = it },
        label = "Birthday",
        maxDate = rememberToday(),
        showClearButton = true,
        tagKey = "birthday"
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = birthday?.let { "Birthday: ${strings.date(it.day, it.month, it.year)}" } ?: "No day yet",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.body
    )
}
```

### A delivery day on a weekday

A delivery day on a weekday within the next month. In the calendar the weekends are faint. A Saturday typed is not taken and the field says "This day cannot be chosen"; a day past the month says the bounds.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday

var delivery by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
val today = rememberToday()
PantrixDateTextField(
    value = delivery,
    onValueChange = { delivery = it },
    label = "Delivery day",
    supportingText = "Delivered on weekdays only",
    minDate = today.plusDays(1),
    maxDate = today.plusMonths(1),
    isDateEnabled = { it.dayOfWeek <= FRIDAY },
    tagKey = "delivery"
)

private const val FRIDAY = 5
```

### The calendar in a sheet or a dialog

The calendar opens in a sheet: near the thumb on a phone, as wide as the screen. `presentation = Dialog` opens it in a dialog in the middle of the window. A day chosen closes the sheet and is written into the field.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.common.DatePickerPresentation
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var appointment by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
var presentation by remember { mutableStateOf(DatePickerPresentation.Sheet) }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixSegmentButton(
        options = listOf(
            SegmentOption(DatePickerPresentation.Popover, "Popover", tagKey = "popover"),
            SegmentOption(DatePickerPresentation.Sheet, "Sheet", tagKey = "sheet"),
            SegmentOption(DatePickerPresentation.Dialog, "Dialog", tagKey = "dialog")
        ),
        selected = presentation,
        onSelect = { presentation = it },
        fullWidth = false,
        tagKey = "presentation"
    )
    PantrixDateTextField(
        value = appointment,
        onValueChange = { appointment = it },
        label = "Appointment day",
        minDate = rememberToday(),
        presentation = presentation,
        tagKey = "appointment"
    )
}
```

### The app's error and disabled

The app's own error comes before the field's: a day already taken is said with `error` and `supportingText`. The field under it is disabled: it takes no focus and opens no calendar.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate

var meeting by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(PantrixDate(2026, 11, 2)) }
val taken = meeting == PantrixDate(2026, 11, 2)
PantrixDateTextField(
    value = meeting,
    onValueChange = { meeting = it },
    label = "Meeting day",
    supportingText = if (taken) "This day is taken, choose another" else "A day the office is open",
    error = taken,
    tagKey = "meeting"
)
PantrixDateTextField(
    value = PantrixDate(2026, 10, 1),
    onValueChange = {},
    enabled = false,
    label = "Contract start",
    tagKey = "contract"
)
```

### Read-only: from the calendar alone

A read-only field is not typed into: the day is chosen from the calendar alone. A press on the box, Enter or Space opens the calendar. For a place where a day must be chosen, and what is typed must not be misread.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday

var checkIn by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
PantrixDateTextField(
    value = checkIn,
    onValueChange = { checkIn = it },
    readOnly = true,
    label = "Check-in day",
    placeholder = "Choose from the calendar",
    minDate = rememberToday(),
    tagKey = "check_in"
)
```

### Bound to a form

Bound to a form's field: with no day, "Save" shows the error and sends the focus to the field. The error shows on leaving the field too; going into the calendar is no leaving it. Digits that make no day leave the value null, and the rule catches it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.Rules
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.field
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.form.rememberFormState
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

val form = rememberFormState()
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
val start = form.field<PantrixDate?>("start", initial = null, Rules.required("Enter the start day"))
PantrixDateTextField(
    field = start,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    form = form,
    label = "Start day",
    minDate = rememberToday()
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Save",
    onClick = { scope.launch { form.submit { report("Saved") } } },
    form = form,
    tagKey = "save_start"
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### On a state, as ISO 8601 writes a day

On a state: `state.date` is the field's day, `state.text` the digits typed. Together they tell an empty field from a half-typed one. ISO 8601 reads the same in every language. The button changes the state's day, and the field writes it in itself.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.common.DateFieldFormat
import com.pantrixui.components.date.common.rememberDateTextFieldState
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val state = rememberDateTextFieldState()
val today = rememberToday()
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixDateTextField(
        state = state,
        label = "Report day",
        format = DateFieldFormat.Iso,
        tagKey = "report_day"
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = when {
            state.date != null -> "Day: ${state.date}"
            state.text.isEmpty() -> "The field is empty"
            else -> "Half typed: ${state.text}"
        },
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.body
    )
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Write today",
        onClick = { state.date = today },
        variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
        tagKey = "write_today"
    )
}
```

### An own format

The field's format comes from the theme's language; `format` says another. The formats of most languages are ready in `DateFieldFormat` (`DayMonthYearDots`, `MonthDayYearSlashes`, `Iso`, …); an own format is the order of the parts (`DateFieldOrder`) and a mark: the first here puts the year first, with slashes, as Japanese does. Change the format: the field's day stays the same, only the way it is written changes.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.date.common.DateFieldFormat
import com.pantrixui.components.date.common.DateFieldOrder
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var shipping by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(PantrixDate(2026, 10, 18)) }
var format by remember { mutableStateOf(DateFieldFormat(DateFieldOrder.YearMonthDay, '/')) }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixSegmentButton(
        options = listOf(
            SegmentOption(DateFieldFormat(DateFieldOrder.YearMonthDay, '/'), "YYYY/MM/DD", tagKey = "year_first"),
            SegmentOption(DateFieldFormat.MonthDayYearSlashes, "MM/DD/YYYY", tagKey = "month_first"),
            SegmentOption(DateFieldFormat(DateFieldOrder.DayMonthYear, '-'), "DD-MM-YYYY", tagKey = "day_first")
        ),
        selected = format,
        onSelect = { format = it },
        fullWidth = false,
        tagKey = "format"
    )
    PantrixDateTextField(
        value = shipping,
        onValueChange = { shipping = it },
        label = "Shipping day",
        format = format,
        tagKey = "shipping"
    )
}
```

### A sheet in a narrow window

The default `presentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive`: in a narrow window the calendar opens in a sheet from the bottom, near the finger and as wide as the window; in a wider window in a popover under the box. Pick "Narrow" in the card's window selector and open the calendar. It is chosen as the calendar opens: it does not change while it is open, even if the window does.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.date.common.DatePickerPresentation
import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixDate
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.rememberToday

var day by remember { mutableStateOf<PantrixDate?>(null) }
// The card's window is as tall as the example: the example is kept tall so that a sheet opened in a narrow window has room.
Column(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(460.dp)) {
    PantrixDateTextField(
        value = day,
        onValueChange = { day = it },
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        label = "Meeting day",
        minDate = rememberToday(),
        presentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
        tagKey = "adaptive_day"
    )
}
```

## API

### PantrixDateTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDateTextField(
    value: PantrixDate?,
    onValueChange: (PantrixDate?) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    error: Boolean = false,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,
    firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null,
    today: PantrixDate = rememberToday(),
    format: DateFieldFormat = DateFieldFormat.of(PantrixTheme.locale),
    presentation: DatePickerPresentation = DatePickerPresentation.Adaptive,
    style: TextFieldStyle? = null,
    colors: TextFieldColors? = null,
    pickerStyle: DatePickerStyle? = null,
    pickerColors: DatePickerColors? = null,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null
)
```

A text field for a day: the day is typed in digits, or chosen from a calendar that a button at the box's end opens.

It is drawn as `PantrixTextField` is, the label above the box, and takes digits alone: the `format`'s mark comes in by itself as each part of the day is whole, so `18102026` shows as `18.10.2026` in Turkish and `10182026` as `10/18/2026` in American English. A phone shows its keyboard of digits. While the box is empty it shows the pattern, `GG.AA.YYYY` in Turkish and `MM/DD/YYYY` in American English, which a screen reader is told as the order of the parts. A day pasted written out is read as it is written, in the `format`'s order and else with the year first as ISO 8601 has it: `2026-10-18` pasted in Turkish shows as `18.10.2026`, and a year of two digits is the one of the hundred years around `today` that ends in them.

`onValueChange` is told the day the field holds each time it changes: a whole day the calendar takes, as it is typed or chosen, and null while the field is empty, half typed, or holds digits that make no day or a day it does not take. The field keeps what is typed itself, so a half-typed day stays on the screen while `value` is null. A `value` that is a day other than the field's is written in, and a null `value` empties a field that holds a day.

The field writes its own error under the box where what is typed is wrong: digits that make no whole day, once the user has left the field; a day the calendar has not, the 31st of February; a day before `minDate` or after `maxDate`; and a day `isDateEnabled` turns down. An `error` of the caller's comes first, its `supportingText` the message.

The calendar opens by its button, by Alt and ↓, and in a `readOnly` field by a press on the box, by Enter or by Space too: a read-only field takes a day from the calendar alone. It opens in what `presentation` says, the same on every platform. A day pressed in it is the field's at once and closes it; Escape and a press outside close it and change nothing. Opened by the keyboard, the focus goes to its chosen day, or to today, and comes back to the field as it closes.

Parameters:

- `value: PantrixDate?`: the day the field shows, or null.
- `onValueChange: (PantrixDate?) -> Unit`: told the field's day each time the user changes it: a day, or null for none.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field: its label, its box and what is under it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the field can be used. One that cannot takes no focus and opens no calendar.
- `readOnly: Boolean`: whether the day can only be chosen from the calendar, and not typed.
- `label: String?`: what the field is for, written above the box: the field's name for a screen reader, and its calendar's.
- `placeholder: String?`: shown in the box while it is empty, in the place of the pattern the field shows by itself.
- `supportingText: String?`: help under the box. With `error` it is the message that says what to put right; without it, the field's own error takes its place while there is one.
- `error: Boolean`: whether the caller finds the day wrong, as a day already taken: the field is drawn in error, and `supportingText` is the message.
- `leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the text. A slot does not size what is put in it.
- `showClearButton: Boolean`: shows a button that empties the field, while it can be typed into and is not empty.
- `minDate: PantrixDate?`: the first day the field takes, or null for no first. Not after `maxDate`.
- `maxDate: PantrixDate?`: the last day the field takes, or null for no last.
- `isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)?`: whether the field takes a day between the two, or null for every day: a weekday, a day not yet booked.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int?`: the day the calendar's weeks start on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday as ISO 8601 numbers them, or null for the language's.
- `today: PantrixDate`: the day the calendar marks as today: by default the one the screen's clock shows (`rememberToday`), which turns at midnight.
- `format: DateFieldFormat`: the order the parts are typed in and the mark between them: the theme's language's and region's by default. `of`: The role of the theme this tone is drawn in.
- `presentation: DatePickerPresentation`: what the calendar opens in: by default a sheet in a narrow window and a popover under the box in a wider one, chosen as it opens; or always a popover, a sheet or a dialog.
- `style: TextFieldStyle?`: this call's own style of the field: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: TextFieldColors?`: this call's own colours of the field, in place of the theme's roles.
- `pickerStyle: DatePickerStyle?`: this call's own style of the calendar.
- `pickerColors: DatePickerColors?`: this call's own colours of the calendar.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what a screen reader says for the field where it has no `label`.
- `tagKey: String?`: the field's automation key: the field is `DateTextField_<tagKey>`, its button `DateTextFieldCalendar_<tagKey>`, its clear button `DateTextFieldClear_<tagKey>` and its calendar `DatePicker_<tagKey>`. The field reports that the calendar opened and that a day was chosen in it, and never the day.
- `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource?`: the field's interactions, hoisted: its focus, its hover and its presses.

### PantrixDateTextField

`import com.pantrixui.components.date.datetextfield.PantrixDateTextField`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixDateTextField(
```
```kotlin
    field: FormField<PantrixDate?>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    form: FormState? = null,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    readOnly: Boolean = false,
    label: String? = null,
    placeholder: String? = null,
    supportingText: String? = null,
    leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    showClearButton: Boolean = false,
    minDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    maxDate: PantrixDate? = null,
    isDateEnabled: ((PantrixDate) -> Boolean)? = null,

```

A date field bound to a form's field: its day, its error and its name come from `field`.

The field's value is the day the date field holds, null while it holds none, and a change made to the value in code, a reset among them, is written in. When the user leaves the field, the calendar not counting as leaving it, the field is marked touched and checked. While it is in error its message takes the place of `supportingText`, and of the date field's own error. Digits that make no day leave the value null: give the field a rule for null where a day is required, and its message is shown once the user has left. The field's id is the automation key, `DateTextField_<id>`, and the form can send the focus here.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the modifier of the whole field.
