```kotlin
@Composable
private fun AdminShowcase() {
    Column(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
        Logo()
        Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
        PantrixText(
            text = "“Pantrix changed how we understand our mobile users. The insights we gained helped us increase " +
                "retention by 40 percent in three months.”",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.title.copy(fontStyle = FontStyle.Italic)
        )
        PantrixText(text = "— Head of product, a game studio", modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 12.dp))
        Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
        Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(32.dp)) {
            Figure(value = "10M+", label = "Events tracked")
            Figure(value = "500+", label = "Active projects")
            // How a percentage is written depends on the language; with no letters in it, the translation file does not know it.
            Figure(value = said(tr = "%99,9", en = "99.9%"), label = "Uptime")
        }
        Copyright(modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 24.dp))
    }
}

@Composable
private fun Logo() {
    Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
        Box(
            modifier = Modifier
                .size(40.dp)
                .background(PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color, PantrixTheme.shapes.md),
            contentAlignment = Alignment.Center
        ) {
            PantrixIcon(DemoIcons.Chart, contentDescription = null, tint = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.onColor)
        }
        PantrixText(text = "Pantrix", style = PantrixTheme.typography.title)
    }
}

@Composable
private fun Copyright(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    inABar: Boolean = false
) {
    PantrixText(
        text = "© 2026 Pantrix. All rights reserved. by @developersancho.",
        modifier = modifier,
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        color = if (inABar) PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary else Color.Unspecified,
        textAlign = if (inABar) TextAlign.Center else null
    )
}

@Composable
private fun LanguageMenu() {
    var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var language by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("tr") }
    PantrixMenu(
        visible = open,
        onDismissRequest = { open = false },
        anchor = {
            PantrixIconButton(
                imageVector = DemoIcons.Globe,
                contentDescription = "Language",
                onClick = { open = true },
                tagKey = "language"
            )
        },
        alignment = PopoverAlignment.End,
        tagKey = "language"
    ) {
        PantrixMenuItem(text = "Türkçe", onClick = { language = "tr" }, tagKey = "tr", selected = language == "tr")
        PantrixMenuItem(text = "English", onClick = { language = "en" }, tagKey = "en", selected = language == "en")
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ColumnScope.SignInForm() {
    val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
    val email = rememberTextFieldState()
    val password = remember { TextFieldState() }
    var keep by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
    Heading(title = "Welcome back", line = "Sign in to your account to continue")
    Spacer(Modifier.height(24.dp))
    PantrixTextField(
        state = email,
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        label = "Email",
        placeholder = "name@example.com",
        leadingIcon = { PantrixIcon(DemoIcons.Mail, contentDescription = null) },
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email),
        tagKey = "email"
    )
    Spacer(Modifier.height(16.dp))
    PantrixSecureTextField(
        state = password,
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        label = "Password",
        leadingIcon = { PantrixIcon(DemoIcons.Lock, contentDescription = null) },
        tagKey = "password"
    )
    PantrixLink(
        text = "Forgot your password?",
        onClick = { report("A password reset was asked for") },
        modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.End).padding(vertical = 12.dp),
        tagKey = "forgot"
    )
    PantrixCheckbox(checked = keep, onCheckedChange = { keep = it }, label = "Remember me", tagKey = "remember")
    Spacer(Modifier.height(16.dp))
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Sign in",
        onClick = { report("Signed in: ${email.text}") },
        enabled = email.text.isNotEmpty() && password.text.isNotEmpty(),
        fullWidth = true,
        shape = PantrixTheme.shapes.full,
        tagKey = "sign_in"
    )
}

@Composable
private fun SignUpInstead() {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
        PantrixHorizontalDivider(label = "DON'T HAVE AN ACCOUNT?")
        PantrixButton(
            text = "Sign up",
            onClick = {},
            variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
            fullWidth = true,
            shape = PantrixTheme.shapes.full,
            tagKey = "sign_up"
        )
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ShowcaseExampleFrame(content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    PantrixSurface(
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(SHOWCASE_EXAMPLE_HEIGHT),
        border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider
    ) {
        Box { content() }
    }
}

private val NAVY = Color(0xFF131F4B)

@Composable
private fun Figure(
    value: String,
    label: String
) {
    Column {
        PantrixText(text = value, style = PantrixTheme.typography.headline)
        PantrixText(text = label, style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ColumnScope.Heading(
    title: String,
    line: String
) {
    PantrixText(
        text = title,
        modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterHorizontally),
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.headline,
        role = TextRole.Heading(level = 1)
    )
    PantrixText(
        text = line,
        modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterHorizontally).padding(top = 8.dp),
        color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
    )
}

private val SHOWCASE_EXAMPLE_HEIGHT = 640.dp
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `said`: A text written in two languages, as it reads in the app's current language: for the shell's own texts, and in an example for a text the translation files do not know because it has no letters in it, as a percentage. The text's two languages stand side by side where it is used; whoever changes a button's name sees both together.
- `DemoIcons`: The sample app's own icons: for the sections in the navigation and the buttons on the top bar. The library's icons (`PantrixIcons`) are as many as a component library cannot do without; an app's home, grid or settings icon is its own.
- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### Signing in beside slides

Slides that turn in the showcase (`PantrixCarousel`): each a heading and a sentence. With `showcaseFrom = WindowWidthClass.Medium` the showcase is shown from 600 dp on, in "Medium" too. In "Book" the showcase is in one half and the form in the other, and they meet at the fold; in "Tabletop" only the form is left. In "Narrow" the showcase is not composed at all: its slides do not turn.

```kotlin
            pageCount = HIGHLIGHTS.size,
            currentPage = page,
            onPageChange = { page = it },

                PantrixText(text = title, style = PantrixTheme.typography.headline)
                PantrixText(text = line, modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 8.dp))
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Signing up on a picture

Signing up on a picture. A gradient stands where the picture would: the showcase's background (`showcaseBackground`) and what the card stands on (`backdrop`). The showcase is at the end (`showcaseSide = ShowcaseSide.End`); `scrim = ShowcaseScrim.Bottom` deepens the background towards its foot so that the line at the bottom reads. The showcase stands in the card with corners of its own (`showcaseInset`). In "Wide" the layout is a card, which `ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive` draws from Large on; in "Short" it reaches the edges.


### A page not found

A page not found, with `formLayout = ShowcaseFormLayout.Spread`: the logo at the top, the words in the middle of the side, the help link under them and the copyright line in the bottom bar (`bottomBar`). The showcase is a large "404" in the theme's neutral colour: a colour that is the theme's brings the colour of what is written on it with it.

## API

### PantrixShowcaseScaffold

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.PantrixShowcaseScaffold`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixShowcaseScaffold(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    showcase: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    showcaseBackground: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    title: String? = null,
    topBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    header: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    footer: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    bottomBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    backdrop: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    showcaseSide: ShowcaseSide = ShowcaseSide.Start,
    showcaseFrom: WindowWidthClass = WindowWidthClass.Expanded,
    frame: ShowcaseFrame = ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive,
    formLayout: ShowcaseFormLayout = ShowcaseFormLayout.Centered,
    scrim: ShowcaseScrim = ShowcaseScrim.None,
    windowInsets: WindowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.union(WindowInsets.displayCutout),
    colors: ShowcaseScaffoldColors? = null,
    style: ShowcaseScaffoldStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    content: @Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit
)
```

A screen that stands outside the app's shell: sign in, sign up, a password reset, an invitation, a welcome, a page not found. A showcase stands on one side, a picture, a quote or slides, and the form on the other; in a narrow room only the form is left.

- **Showcase.** `showcase` stands beside the form once the scaffold is as wide as `showcaseFrom`, Expanded by default, on the side `showcaseSide` says. Narrower, it is not composed at all: its slides do not turn and its pictures are not loaded. The scaffold goes by its own width, not the window's. `showcaseBackground` fills the showcase to its edges, a picture or a gradient, under the system's bars, while what `showcase` holds keeps clear of them; `scrim` shades the background under what is written on it. The showcase is drawn in its own colours.

- **Form.** `content` is the form, no wider than the style's form width, in the middle of its side. `header` stands above it, a heading, and `footer` under it, a way to sign up instead. `formLayout` puts the header, the form and the footer together in the middle of the side's height, or apart: the header at the top and the footer at the foot.

- **Bars.** `topBar` is a row across the top of the form's side, a logo at its start and a language at its end; `bottomBar` is a row across its foot, a line of copyright. They stay where they are as the form scrolls between them. Where the showcase is not shown, a line parts each bar from the form; a bar with nothing in it takes no room. The bars and the form's parts are each told whether the showcase is shown, so that the logo the showcase carries in a wide window can stand in the top bar of a narrow one.

- **Frame.** With `ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive`, from the Large class on, the scaffold is a card in the middle of the window, no wider and no taller than its style says, on its `backdrop`; a card with no showcase is the form's width and as tall as what it holds. Narrower, and with `ShowcaseFrame.Edge` at every width, it reaches the window's edges.

- **Folds.** Where a fold upright divides the room, a device held like a book, the showcase is in one half and the form in the other, and they meet at the fold. A fold across the room, a device on a table, leaves only the form.

- **Room.** The scaffold keeps clear of the system's bars and the display's cut-out itself, as `windowInsets` says: it stands outside the app's shell, where nothing else does. Only the form's side scrolls; it ends above the keyboard, and a field that takes the focus is brought into view.

- **What it remembers.** The form and the showcase are each composed in one place whatever the layout: what they remember, a typed address or a slide's place, stays as the room changes, a phone turned on its side or a window widened into a card. A showcase a narrow room hides forgets, as it is not composed there.

- **The window's title.** With a `title`, the scaffold names the window after the screen while it is shown: the browser's tab on the web, the title bar on the desktop. The title is not drawn: the form has its own heading. A scaffold inside a page's content, as an example of one is, leaves the window's title to the page.

- **Screen reader and focus.** The form is read first, and takes the focus first, wherever the showcase stands; the showcase is read after it, as one group. The title is the screen's name as it comes into view, which TalkBack says on Android.

- **Reported shown.** A scaffold with a `tagKey` reports a `show` event to the theme's analytics each time it comes into the composition.

- **Automation.** The scaffold is tagged `ShowcaseScaffold_<tagKey>`, its sides `ShowcaseScaffold_<tagKey>.Pane_form` and `ShowcaseScaffold_<tagKey>.Pane_showcase`. What the app puts in it stands in `TestScope(tagKey)`: a button tagged `sign_in` there is `sign_in.Button_sign_in` on a scaffold keyed `sign_in`.

- **Reading direction.** The start and the end are the language's: `ShowcaseSide.Start` is on the right where the language is read from right to left.

The scaffold takes the room it is given, which is to be bounded both ways: the window, or `Modifier.fillMaxSize()`.

Parameters:

- `modifier: Modifier`: the scaffold's modifier.
- `showcase: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands beside the form in a wide room: a quote, a picture's caption, slides. Null for a screen with only its form.
- `showcaseBackground: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)?`: what fills the showcase to its edges, under what it holds: a picture or a gradient.
- `title: String?`: the screen's name: the window's title, and the screen's for a screen reader. Not drawn.
- `topBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)?`: the row across the top of the form's side: a logo, a language, a way back.
- `header: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands above the form: a heading.
- `footer: (@Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands under the form: another way in, as signing up instead.
- `bottomBar: (@Composable ShowcaseBarScope.() -> Unit)?`: the row across the foot of the form's side: a line of copyright, the terms.
- `backdrop: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)?`: what the card stands on in a wide window, with `ShowcaseFrame.Adaptive`: a picture or a gradient.
- `showcaseSide: ShowcaseSide`: which side the showcase stands on: the start or the end.
- `showcaseFrom: WindowWidthClass`: the narrowest class of width the showcase is shown in.
- `frame: ShowcaseFrame`: whether the scaffold is a card on its backdrop in a wide window, or reaches the window's edges.
- `formLayout: ShowcaseFormLayout`: whether the header, the form and the footer stand together or apart.
- `scrim: ShowcaseScrim`: what shades the showcase's background, so that what is written on it reads.
- `windowInsets: WindowInsets`: what the scaffold keeps clear of: the system's bars and the display's cut-out by default.
- `colors: ShowcaseScaffoldColors?`: what the scaffold is painted with, over the theme's.
- `style: ShowcaseScaffoldStyle?`: the scaffold's geometry, over the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the screen's automation key, the same in every language: what the scaffold and its sides are tagged by, the TestScope of what it holds, and the screen its `show` event is of.
- `content: @Composable ShowcaseScaffoldScope.() -> Unit`: the form, in a column.

### ShowcaseSide

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseSide`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ShowcaseSide
```

Which side of a `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` its showcase stands on, beside the form.

Entries:

- `Start`: At the start: on the left, and on the right where the language is read from right to left.
- `End`: At the end: on the right, and on the left where the language is read from right to left.

### ShowcaseFrame

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseFrame`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ShowcaseFrame
```

Whether a `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` stands as a card on a backdrop in a wide window, or reaches its edges.

Entries:

- `Adaptive`: A card in the middle of the backdrop from the Large class on, no wider and no taller than its style says; narrower, it reaches the window's edges.
- `Edge`: It reaches the window's edges at every width.

### ShowcaseFormLayout

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseFormLayout`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ShowcaseFormLayout
```

How the form side of a `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` lays its header, its form and its footer out, top to bottom.

Entries:

- `Centered`: The header, the form and the footer together, as one block in the middle of the side's height.
- `Spread`: The header at the top, the form in the middle and the footer at the foot.

### ShowcaseScrim

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseScrim`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class ShowcaseScrim
```

What a `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` lays over its showcase's background so that what is written on it reads.

Entries:

- `None`: Nothing: the showcase's background is shown as it is.
- `Bottom`: A shade that deepens towards the foot, under a line written at the bottom of a picture.
- `Full`: A shade over the whole background, under what is written anywhere on a picture.

### ShowcaseScaffoldScope

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseScaffoldScope`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
interface ShowcaseScaffoldScope : ColumnScope
```

Where the form side of a `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` lays out its header, its form and its footer, each in a column.

Members:

- `showcaseShown: Boolean`: Whether the showcase is shown beside the form now.

### ShowcaseBarScope

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseBarScope`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
interface ShowcaseBarScope : RowScope
```

Where a bar of the form side of a `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` lays out what it holds: a row across the side, its parts a little apart and together in its middle; a part with a weight pushes the others to the ends.

Members:

- `showcaseShown: Boolean`: Whether the showcase is shown beside the form now. A logo or a line the showcase carries in a wide window goes in a bar when it is not: the logo at the top bar's start, the copyright in the bottom bar.

### ShowcaseScaffoldStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseScaffoldStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ShowcaseScaffoldStyle(
    public val showcaseShare: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val formMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val formPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sectionGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val showcasePadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val showcaseInset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val showcaseShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val cardMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val cardMaxHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val cardMargin: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val cardShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val cardElevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ShowcaseScaffoldStyle>
```

`PantrixShowcaseScaffold`'s geometry: how the room is shared between the showcase and the form, how wide the form is, the rooms inside each side, and the card it stands as in a wide window.

The rooms follow the density; the widths, the corners and the shadow do not. Its colours are not part of its style: they are `ShowcaseScaffoldColors`.

Parameters:

- `showcaseShare: Float`: How much of the room the showcase takes beside the form, more than nought and less than one: half on every platform. A fold that divides the room shares it instead.
- `formMaxWidth: Dp`: How wide the form, its header and its footer are at the most, in the middle of their side: 440dp.
- `formPadding: Dp`: The room between the edges of the form's side and what it holds: 24dp on Android and iOS, 40dp on desktop and the web.
- `sectionGap: Dp`: The room between the header, the form and the footer: 24dp on Android and iOS, 32dp on desktop and the web.
- `showcasePadding: Dp`: The room between the edges of the showcase and what it holds: 24dp on Android and iOS, 40dp on desktop and the web. The showcase's background runs to its edges.
- `showcaseInset: Dp`: The room around the showcase, inside its side, where it stands as a panel of its own: none on every platform, so that it reaches its side's edges.
- `showcaseShape: ShapeSpec`: The showcase's corners where it is inset: large on every platform. Not inset, it has the corners of what it stands in.
- `cardMaxWidth: Dp`: How wide the card the scaffold stands as in a wide window is at the most: 1120dp.
- `cardMaxHeight: Dp`: How tall that card is at the most: 760dp. A card with no showcase is as tall as its form.
- `cardMargin: Dp`: The room between that card and the window's edges, past the system's bars: 32dp.
- `cardShape: ShapeSpec`: That card's corners: large on every platform.
- `cardElevation: Dp`: The shadow under that card: 2dp on Android, none on iOS, 1dp on desktop and the web.
- `barPadding: Dp`: The room above and below what a bar of the form's side holds: 12dp on Android and iOS, 16dp on desktop and the web.

### ShowcaseScaffoldColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.showcase.ShowcaseScaffoldColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class ShowcaseScaffoldColors(
    public val showcase: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val showcaseContent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val form: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val backdrop: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val scrim: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What `PantrixShowcaseScaffold` is painted with: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out is the theme's.

```kotlin
PantrixShowcaseScaffold(
    showcase = { Testimonial() },
    colors = ShowcaseScaffoldColors(showcase = brand.navy, showcaseContent = Color.White)
) {
    SignInForm(form)
}
```

Parameters:

- `showcase: Color`: The showcase's fill, under its background: the theme's primary colour.
- `showcaseContent: Color`: What the showcase holds is drawn in, unless a child sets a colour of its own: the colour the theme pairs with `showcase` where that is one of its own, and the one on its primary colour otherwise. A fill the theme does not have is to be given its content too.
- `form: Color`: The form's side: the theme's surface, as a card's.
- `backdrop: Color`: What the card stands on in a wide window, under the backdrop the scaffold is given: the theme's background.
- `scrim: Color`: The shade laid over the showcase's background with a `ShowcaseScrim`: the theme's scrim.

# Accordion

Sections whose content folds away under their headers, so that a long page can be read a part at a time.

Which sections are open is the screen's state: the accordion is given the keys of the open sections (`expanded`), and when a header is pressed it reports back the new set that is to be open (`onExpandedChange`). The accordion changes nothing by itself. That is what lets a screen open the section a link points at, keep what was open across a rotation, or close everything from a button of its own.

- `PantrixAccordion` (`com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion`, `com.pantrixui:components`): Sections whose content folds away under their headers: three ways of telling them apart, one or many open at a time. Keywords: collapse, expandable, disclosure, expansion panel, faq, collapsible section.

## Features

- **Three variants.** `variant` says how the sections are told apart: `Plain` puts a line between them, `Bordered` puts one edge around them all, `Separated` makes each section a card of its own.
- **One section or many.** Any number of sections stay open at once; with `singleExpanded`, opening one closes the one that was open.
- **The parts of a header.** The header of an `AccordionSection` has its `title`, with `subtitle` under it, `icon` before it and `trailing` at its end. `trailing` is a part of the header's button and is read with it: a count, a badge; a control of its own does not belong there.
- **Keys.** Each section's `key` is the same in every language, and no two sections of an accordion have one key.
- **A closed section is not composed.** A section's content is composed only while the section is open; what it kept with `rememberSaveable` is there again when the section is opened again.
- **Disabled.** The accordion's `enabled` keeps every header from being pressed, and a section's own `enabled` only that section's; open or closed, the section stays as it is.
- **Screen reader.** A header is a button and a heading that carries its section's name. A screen reader is offered what a press does, to expand the section or to collapse it, and is told whether the section is open. The chevron is a picture of that, and is not read.
- **Platform.** A header is a row of a list: 56dp on Android, 44dp on iOS and the web, 40dp on desktop; it is never lower than the platform's touch target, and grows with a long title and a large type. The corners are the card's.
- **Colour.** `AccordionColors` gives the fill, the text's colour and the lines. The variants that have no fill stand on what is behind them: on a fill, they are written in the colour that fill gives what stands on it.
- **Automation.** With `tagKey` the accordion is `Accordion_<tagKey>`, a header in it `Accordion_<tagKey>.Header_<key>` and what it opens `Accordion_<tagKey>.Content_<key>`. A press is reported as `expand` or `collapse`, with the section's key.

## Usage

### Questions and answers

```kotlin
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(emptySet<String>()) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "delivery", title = stringResource(Res.string.when_will_it_arrive)) {
            PantrixText(stringResource(Res.string.delivery_answer))
        },
        AccordionSection(key = "returns", title = stringResource(Res.string.how_do_i_return)) {
            PantrixText(stringResource(Res.string.returns_answer))
        }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    tagKey = "faq"
)
```

### One open at a time, each a card of its own

```kotlin
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(
            key = "account",
            title = stringResource(Res.string.account),
            subtitle = stringResource(Res.string.account_summary),
            icon = PantrixIcons.Person
        ) { AccountSettings() },
        AccordionSection(key = "billing", title = stringResource(Res.string.billing), icon = PantrixIcons.Folder) {
            BillingSettings()
        }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Separated,
    singleExpanded = true,
    tagKey = "settings"
)
```

### Inside one edge, with a count at a header's end

```kotlin
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(
            key = "open",
            title = stringResource(Res.string.open_orders),
            trailing = { PantrixText(text = orders.size.toString(), style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote) }
        ) { Orders(orders) }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Bordered,
    tagKey = "orders"
)
```

## Examples

### Frequently asked questions: a line between them

The plainest form, questions and answers. The keys of the open sections are the screen's state and are kept with `rememberSaveable`; the accordion takes them as `expanded` and, when a header is pressed, reports the new set with `onExpandedChange`. Any number of sections stay open at once.

No variant is given: `Plain`, a line between the sections and nothing around them. A long title that does not fit on one line runs onto a second, and the header grows with it. The last section's `enabled` is false: it cannot be pressed, is written in the disabled text's colour and stays closed.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("delivery")) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "delivery", title = "When will my order arrive?") {
            PantrixText(text = "Within two working days. Orders placed before noon are delivered the next day.")
        },
        AccordionSection(key = "returns", title = "How do I return an item?") {
            PantrixText(text = "Within thirty days, in its box. Shipping is on us.")
        },
        AccordionSection(
            key = "gift",
            title = "Can I have my order gift-wrapped, and can I have a note put inside the parcel?"
        ) { PantrixText(text = "Yes. Tick the gift-wrap option at checkout.") },
        AccordionSection(key = "invoice", title = "Company invoice", subtitle = "Coming soon", enabled = false) {
            PantrixText(text = "Not available yet.")
        }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    tagKey = "faq"
)
```

### Inside one edge, with a count at a header's end

`AccordionVariant.Bordered` puts the sections inside one edge; there is still a line between them.

The `icon` before the title is drawn in the title's colour, and a screen reader passes over it. The count at the header's end is given with `trailing`: it stands between the title and the chevron, is a part of the header's button, and a screen reader reads it with the title. Here it is written in small type and is given no colour.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("open")) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(
            key = "open",
            title = "Open orders",
            icon = PantrixIcons.Folder,
            trailing = { PantrixText(text = "2", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote) }
        ) {
            PantrixText(text = "SIP-2026-0914 · On its way")
            PantrixText(text = "SIP-2026-0921 · Preparing")
        },
        AccordionSection(
            key = "past",
            title = "Past orders",
            icon = PantrixIcons.Calendar,
            trailing = { PantrixText(text = "14", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote) }
        ) { PantrixText(text = "Last order: 12 September") }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Bordered,
    tagKey = "orders"
)
```

### Each section a card, only one open at a time

`AccordionVariant.Separated` makes each section a card of its own, with a gap between them. With `singleExpanded` only one section stays open at a time: opening one closes the one that was open. It is for pages where two open sections would push the rest off the screen.

`subtitle` is the second line, under the title, and gives the section's summary: flip the switches, and the subtitle of "Notifications" changes between "On" and "Off".

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("notifications")) }
var email by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
var push by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(
            key = "notifications",
            title = "Notifications",
            subtitle = if (email || push) "On" else "Off",
            icon = PantrixIcons.Star
        ) {
            PantrixSwitchButton(
                checked = email,
                onCheckedChange = { email = it },
                label = "Email",
                tagKey = "email"
            )
            PantrixSwitchButton(checked = push, onCheckedChange = { push = it }, label = "Push", tagKey = "push")
        },
        AccordionSection(
            key = "account",
            title = "Account",
            subtitle = "ada@pantrix.io",
            icon = PantrixIcons.Person
        ) { PantrixText(text = "Member since 2024") }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Separated,
    singleExpanded = true,
    tagKey = "settings"
)
```

### A section that closes keeps what was typed

A closed section's content is not composed at all; yet the section keeps, even while it is closed, everything that was saved to be restored. The field keeps its text with `rememberTextFieldState()`, and that state is saved.

Type something into the "Delivery note" section, close the section and open it again: when the section closes the field leaves the screen, and when it opens again what you typed is there.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.input.rememberTextFieldState
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.components.inputs.textfield.PantrixTextField

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("note")) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "note", title = "Delivery note") {
            PantrixTextField(
                state = rememberTextFieldState(),
                modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
                label = "Note for the courier",
                placeholder = "The doorbell does not work, please knock",
                tagKey = "accordion_note"
            )
        },
        AccordionSection(key = "address", title = "Delivery address") {
            PantrixText(text = "Pantrix A.Ş., Maslak, İstanbul")
        }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Bordered,
    tagKey = "remembers"
)
```

### Opening and closing from outside

Since the open sections are the screen's state, they change from outside the accordion too. The two buttons above press no header; they only change the set: one puts every key into it, the other empties it. The accordion draws the new set.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonSize
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(emptySet<String>()) }
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Open all",
        onClick = { open = setOf("monday", "tuesday", "wednesday") },
        variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
        size = ButtonSize.Small,
        tagKey = "accordion_open_all"
    )
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Close all",
        onClick = { open = emptySet() },
        variant = ButtonVariant.Text,
        size = ButtonSize.Small,
        tagKey = "accordion_close_all"
    )
}
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "monday", title = "Monday") { PantrixText(text = "09.00 Weekly planning") },
        AccordionSection(key = "tuesday", title = "Tuesday") { PantrixText(text = "14.00 Design review") },
        AccordionSection(key = "wednesday", title = "Wednesday") { PantrixText(text = "No meetings") }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Bordered,
    tagKey = "week"
)
```

### All disabled

With `enabled = false` no header can be pressed and every section is held as it is: an open one stays open and a closed one closed. The headers are written in the disabled text's colour. A section's own `enabled` does the same for that section alone.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText

PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "summary", title = "Order summary", subtitle = "Confirmed") {
            PantrixText(text = "The order is confirmed; it can no longer be changed.")
        },
        AccordionSection(key = "payment", title = "Payment") { PantrixText(text = "Paid by card") }
    ),
    expanded = setOf("summary"),
    onExpandedChange = {},
    variant = AccordionVariant.Bordered,
    enabled = false,
    tagKey = "locked"
)
```

### In its own colours

`colors` gives the accordion the colours set there in place of the theme's: here, cards in a colour the theme does not have. The fill is given with `container`; the headers and the content take the `content` colour, and the line is given separately, with `divider`. A colour that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionColors
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText

val own = ownColors()
var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("plan")) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "plan", title = "Plan", subtitle = "Team") {
            PantrixText(text = "Up to ten users, billed monthly.")
        },
        AccordionSection(key = "usage", title = "Usage") { PantrixText(text = "48,2 million requests this month") }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Separated,
    colors = AccordionColors(container = own.container, content = own.onContainer, divider = own.color),
    tagKey = "own"
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ownColors`: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

### On a fill

The `Plain` and `Bordered` variants have no fill of their own: they stand on what is behind them. Here the accordion is inside a surface painted with a role's fill, and is given no colours: the titles, the subtitle and the chevron are written in the colour that fill gives what stands on it, and the lines are drawn in a share of that colour. The theme's line would not read on this fill.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("shipping")) }
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), color = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.container) {
    PantrixAccordion(
        sections = listOf(
            AccordionSection(key = "shipping", title = "Shipping", subtitle = "Free", icon = PantrixIcons.Inbox) {
                PantrixText(text = "Ships tomorrow before noon.")
            },
            AccordionSection(key = "warranty", title = "Warranty") { PantrixText(text = "Two years") }
        ),
        expanded = open,
        onExpandedChange = { open = it },
        modifier = Modifier.padding(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm),
        tagKey = "on_a_fill"
    )
}
```

### In its own style

`style` changes the accordion's geometry; only the fields that are given change, and the rest comes from the platform's style. Here the header's least height is set to 64dp and the gap between the cards to 16dp; the corners are not a step of the brand's shape scale but a fixed 20dp: `ShapeSpec.Fixed`.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.shape.RoundedCornerShape
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.token.shape.ShapeSpec

var open by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("first")) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "first", title = "Step one") { PantrixText(text = "Create your account.") },
        AccordionSection(key = "second", title = "Step two") { PantrixText(text = "Verify your email.") }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    variant = AccordionVariant.Separated,
    style = AccordionStyle(
        shape = ShapeSpec.Fixed(RoundedCornerShape(20.dp)),
        headerMinHeight = 64.dp,
        sectionGap = 16.dp
    ),
    tagKey = "own_style"
)
```

## API

### PantrixAccordion

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.PantrixAccordion`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAccordion(
    sections: List<AccordionSection>,
    expanded: Set<String>,
    onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    variant: AccordionVariant = AccordionVariant.Plain,
    singleExpanded: Boolean = false,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    style: AccordionStyle? = null,
    colors: AccordionColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

Sections whose content folds away under their headers, so that a long page can be read a part at a time.

Which sections are open is the caller's state, as a sidebar's is: give `expanded` and act on `onExpandedChange`. That is what lets a screen open the section a link points at, keep what was open across a rotation, or close everything from a button of its own.

A header is a button and a heading that carries its section's name. A screen reader is offered what a press does, to expand the section or to collapse it, and is told whether the section is open: by that action on Android, and in the theme's words elsewhere. The chevron is a picture of that, and is passed over. A header is never lower than the platform's touch target, and grows with a longer title and a larger type.

What a section shows is composed only while the section is open. What it kept with `rememberSaveable` is there again when the section is opened again. The accordion fills the width it is given and does not scroll: it stands in a page that does.

```kotlin
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(setOf("delivery")) }
PantrixAccordion(
    sections = listOf(
        AccordionSection(key = "delivery", title = stringResource(Res.string.when_will_it_arrive)) {
            PantrixText(stringResource(Res.string.delivery_answer))
        },
        AccordionSection(key = "returns", title = stringResource(Res.string.how_do_i_return)) {
            PantrixText(stringResource(Res.string.returns_answer))
        }
    ),
    expanded = open,
    onExpandedChange = { open = it },
    tagKey = "faq"
)
```

Parameters:

- `sections: List<AccordionSection>`: the sections, in the order they are shown. No two of them have one key.
- `expanded: Set<String>`: the keys of the sections that are open.
- `onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit`: called with the keys that are to be open after a header was pressed. The accordion changes nothing by itself.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the accordion's modifier. The accordion is as wide as the room it is given and as tall as its headers and what the open ones show.
- `variant: AccordionVariant`: how the sections are told apart: by a line between them, by an edge around the set, or each as a card of its own.
- `singleExpanded: Boolean`: whether opening a section closes whichever was open: for a page where two open sections would push the rest off the screen.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the headers can be pressed. False holds every section as it is, and a section says the same of itself alone.
- `style: AccordionStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: AccordionColors?`: this accordion's own colours, where they are not the theme's: the ones set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the accordion's automation key: the accordion is `Accordion_<tagKey>`, a header in it `Accordion_<tagKey>.Header_<key>` and what it opens `Accordion_<tagKey>.Content_<key>`. A press is reported as an `Accordion` event: `expand` and `collapse`, with the section's key.

### AccordionSection

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionSection`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class AccordionSection(
    public val key: String,
    public val title: String,
    public val subtitle: String? = null,
    public val icon: ImageVector? = null,
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
    public val tagKey: String? = null,
    public val trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    public val content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit
)
```

One section of a `PantrixAccordion`: its header, and what the header opens.

```kotlin
AccordionSection(key = "delivery", title = stringResource(Res.string.when_will_it_arrive)) {
    PantrixText(stringResource(Res.string.delivery_answer))
}
```

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What the accordion's `expanded` holds for this section. It is the same in every language, so a translated screen opens the same section, and no two sections of an accordion have one key.
- `title: String`: The header's text, and the section's name for a screen reader.
- `subtitle: String?`: A second line under the title, or null for none.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: Drawn before the title, in the title's colour, or null for none. A screen reader passes over it.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the header can be pressed. One that cannot is written in the disabled text's colour, and its section stays open or closed as the accordion's `expanded` has it.
- `tagKey: String?`: The section's automation key, the same in every language, where it is to be another than `key`: the header is `Header_<tagKey>` and what it opens `Content_<tagKey>`, inside the tag of an accordion that has a key, as `Accordion_faq.Header_delivery`.
- `trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: What stands between the title and the chevron, or null for nothing: a count, a badge. It is a part of the header's button and is read with it: a control of its own does not belong there.
- `content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit`: What the section shows while it is open, one thing under another with the theme's small spacing between them, as in a card. A closed section composes none of it.

### AccordionVariant

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionVariant`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class AccordionVariant
```

How the sections of a `PantrixAccordion` are told apart.

Entries:

- `Plain`: A line between one section and the next, and nothing around the set: for a page's own column.
- `Bordered`: One edge around the whole set, with a line between the sections inside it.
- `Separated`: Each section a card of its own, with a gap between one and the next.

### AccordionStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class AccordionStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val headerMinHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val contentPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val iconSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val borderWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sectionGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<AccordionStyle>
```

`PantrixAccordion`'s geometry: the room in a section's header and around what the header opens, and the edge.

A header is a row of a list. On Android it is Material 3's one-line list item, 56dp tall with 16dp at its sides. On iOS it is a row of 44pt, the least a finger is given there. Desktop and the web are tighter, for a pointer, and the web's header is no lower than 44dp: a browser may be a touch screen's.

The corners are the card's on each platform, since a section of `AccordionVariant.Separated` is a card: medium on Android, large on iOS, small on desktop and the web.

The header's height, the paddings and the gaps follow the density, since they are the room around the words. The icon's size, the edge's width and the shape do not.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The corners of the edge around the set in `AccordionVariant.Bordered`, and around each section in `AccordionVariant.Separated`: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `headerMinHeight: Dp`: The least height of a header. A title on two lines, a subtitle or a larger type makes it taller, and the platform's touch target is its floor.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between a header's sides and what it holds.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: The room over and under a header's lines, where they need more than the least height.
- `contentPadding: Dp`: The room at the sides of what an open section shows, and under it.
- `iconGap: Dp`: Between a header's icon, its title, what it has at its end and its chevron.
- `iconSize: Dp`: The width and height of a header's icon and of its chevron.
- `borderWidth: Dp`: The width of the lines between sections, and of the edges. Zero draws none.
- `sectionGap: Dp`: Between one section and the next in `AccordionVariant.Separated`.

### AccordionColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.accordion.AccordionColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class AccordionColors(
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val divider: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixAccordion` is painted with, for an accordion that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
// Each section a card in the primary role's soft fill, written in what the theme pairs with it.
PantrixAccordion(…, colors = AccordionColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.container))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The fill behind the sections. None in `AccordionVariant.Plain` and `AccordionVariant.Bordered`, which stand on what is behind them, and the theme's `surface` under each section of `AccordionVariant.Separated`.
- `content: Color`: A header's title and its icon, and what a section shows where that gives no colour of its own. The theme's `textPrimary`, or on a fill that is not the accordion's, the colour that fill gives what stands on it. A subtitle and a chevron are the theme's `textSecondary` on the theme's own grounds, and this colour elsewhere and where it is given.
- `divider: Color`: The lines between sections, and the edges. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

# Tabs

A row of tabs that switches between views of the same content: one is selected, and an indicator slides to the one selected next.

The tabs are only the row; the app draws the selected view itself, below the row. Which tab is selected is the screen's state too: the row is given its index (`selectedIndex`), and reports back the one the user chose (`onSelect`). The row selects nothing by itself.

- `PantrixTabs` (`com.pantrixui.components.container.tab`, `com.pantrixui:components`): A row of tabs that switches between views of the same content, one selected; the arrow keys move the selection. Keywords: tab row, tab strip, tabbed view, tab layout, page tabs, top tabs.

## Features

- **Indicator.** The style's `indicator` marks the selected tab: a line under it, a line over it, a pill behind it, or its colour alone. The indicator slides when the selection changes; in a theme with reduced motion it takes its place at once.
- **A shared row, or one that scrolls.** The tabs share the row's width. With `scrollable` each is as wide as its label and the row scrolls sideways: it opens on the selected tab, and brings each tab selected after that to its middle.
- **Icon and badge.** `TabItem.icon` stands before the label and `TabItem.badge` after it: a count or a dot. Where the tab is narrow it is the label that is cut, and the badge stays whole.
- **Disabled tab.** A press does nothing on a tab whose `enabled` is false, the arrow keys skip it, and it is drawn in the theme's disabled text colour whatever colour is given.
- **Keyboard.** The row is one stop for the Tab key, on the selected tab. The arrow keys select the next and the previous tab, the other way round in a right-to-left layout; Home and End the first and the last. While a tab has the focus, the focus goes with the selection.
- **Screen reader.** Each tab is a tab that says whether it is selected, and together they are one group. The badge's description is read after the label, as a part of the tab.
- **Platform.** A tab's least height is 48dp on Android, 44dp on iOS, and 40dp on the desktop and the web; a tab is never shorter than the platform's touch target.
- **Colour.** The row has no fill of its own: it sits on the page or on a surface. `TabsColors` gives the colours of the selected tab and of the others, of the indicator, and of the hairline below.
- **Automation.** With a `tagKey` the row is `Tabs_<tagKey>` and its tabs are `Tabs_<tagKey>.Tab_<key>`. A selection is reported with the tab's index and whether a press or a key made it; never with its label.

## Usage

### Views of one account

```kotlin
var tab by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
Column {
    PantrixTabs(
        tabs = listOf(
            TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.overview), tagKey = "overview"),
            TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.activity), tagKey = "activity"),
            TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.settings), tagKey = "settings")
        ),
        selectedIndex = tab,
        onSelect = { tab = it },
        tagKey = "account"
    )
    when (tab) {
        0 -> AccountOverview()
        1 -> AccountActivity()
        else -> AccountSettings()
    }
}
```

### Many categories in a row that scrolls

```kotlin
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = categories.map { TabItem(it.name, icon = it.icon, tagKey = it.id) },
    selectedIndex = categories.indexOf(current),
    onSelect = { current = categories[it] },
    scrollable = true,
    tagKey = "categories"
)
```

### A count on a tab, which a screen reader hears after its label

```kotlin
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.all), tagKey = "all"),
        TabItem(
            label = stringResource(Res.string.unread),
            tagKey = "unread",
            badge = TabBadge(
                contentDescription = pluralStringResource(Res.plurals.unread_messages, unread, unread),
                count = unread
            )
        )
    ),
    selectedIndex = tab,
    onSelect = { tab = it },
    tagKey = "inbox"
)
```

### A pill for the selected tab, as a segmented control has

```kotlin
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.day), tagKey = "day"),
        TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.week), tagKey = "week"),
        TabItem(stringResource(Res.string.month), tagKey = "month")
    ),
    selectedIndex = period.ordinal,
    onSelect = { period = Period.entries[it] },
    style = TabsStyle(indicator = TabIndicator.Pill),
    tagKey = "period"
)
```

### In colours of its own

```kotlin
val success = PantrixTheme.colors.success
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = views,
    selectedIndex = view,
    onSelect = { view = it },
    colors = TabsColors(selectedContent = success.color, indicator = success.color),
    tagKey = "account"
)
```

## Examples

### Views of a profile

At its plainest: three tabs that share the row's width equally, and the selected view below them. The selected tab's index is the screen's state; it is kept with `rememberSaveable`, and is not lost when the screen rotates.

The tabs do not draw the view: the text below them is chosen here, with `when`. The default indicator is the line under the selected tab.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var tab by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(label = "General", tagKey = "general"),
        TabItem(label = "Security", tagKey = "security"),
        TabItem(label = "Notifications", tagKey = "notifications")
    ),
    selectedIndex = tab,
    onSelect = { tab = it },
    tagKey = "profile"
)
PantrixText(
    text = when (tab) {
        0 -> "Name, email and language"
        1 -> "Password and two-step verification"
        else -> "Which notifications you get"
    },
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)
```

### Tabs with badges

`TabItem.badge` puts a `TabBadge` after the label: a number where `count` is given, a dot where it is not. The "Activity" tab shows the number of unseen transactions; when the tab is opened the number goes to zero and the badge goes away. The dot on "Settings" says an update is waiting.

A screen reader reads the badge's `contentDescription` after the tab's name: "Activity, 3 new transactions". A number alone says nothing of what it counts; that is why the description has no default, and giving null is a decision.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabBadge
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.BadgeTone
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var view by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
var unseen by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(3) }
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(label = "Overview", tagKey = "overview"),
        TabItem(
            label = "Activity",
            tagKey = "activity",
            badge = if (unseen > 0) TabBadge(contentDescription = "$unseen new transactions", count = unseen) else null
        ),
        TabItem(
            label = "Settings",
            tagKey = "settings",
            badge = TabBadge(contentDescription = "Update available", tone = BadgeTone.Primary)
        )
    ),
    selectedIndex = view,
    onSelect = { chosen ->
        view = chosen
        if (chosen == 1) unseen = 0
    },
    tagKey = "account"
)
PantrixText(
    text = when (view) {
        0 -> "Account overview: balance and recent transactions"
        1 -> "Transactions of the last thirty days"
        else -> "Notifications, language and privacy"
    },
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)
```

### The selected tab's indicator

The style says what marks the selected tab: `TabsStyle(indicator = ...)`. The four rows show the same selection, each with the name of its indicator written above it; press another tab in one of them, and all four change together.

`Underline` is the default on every platform: a line along the selected tab's bottom edge. `Top` puts the same line along the top edge, for a row that sits below what it switches. `Pill` puts a pill in the primary role's pale fill behind the selected tab, and does not draw the hairline under the row: it is how iOS draws its segmented control, and here it picks a chart's period. `None` draws no indicator; the selected tab is marked by its colour alone.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabIndicator
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabsStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var period by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(1) }
val caption = PantrixTheme.typography.caption
val quiet = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
PantrixText(text = "Underline", style = caption, color = quiet)
PantrixTabs(tabs = PERIODS, selectedIndex = period, onSelect = { period = it }, tagKey = "underline")
PantrixText(text = "Top", style = caption, color = quiet)
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = PERIODS,
    selectedIndex = period,
    onSelect = { period = it },
    style = TabsStyle(indicator = TabIndicator.Top),
    tagKey = "top"
)
PantrixText(text = "Pill", style = caption, color = quiet)
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = PERIODS,
    selectedIndex = period,
    onSelect = { period = it },
    style = TabsStyle(indicator = TabIndicator.Pill),
    tagKey = "period"
)
PantrixText(text = "None", style = caption, color = quiet)
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = PERIODS,
    selectedIndex = period,
    onSelect = { period = it },
    style = TabsStyle(indicator = TabIndicator.None),
    tagKey = "none"
)

private val PERIODS = listOf(
    TabItem(label = "Day", tagKey = "day"),
    TabItem(label = "Week", tagKey = "week"),
    TabItem(label = "Month", tagKey = "month")
)
```

### Categories with icons in a row that scrolls

More categories than the row has room for, each with its icon. With `scrollable = true` each tab is as wide as its label and the row scrolls sideways. The selected tab comes to the middle of the row, so that the tabs on both sides of it can be seen and pressed.

The count on "Inbox" is over the largest number that is written: "99+". The last category is disabled: it cannot be pressed, and the arrow keys skip it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabBadge
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons

var category by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = CATEGORIES,
    selectedIndex = category,
    onSelect = { category = it },
    scrollable = true,
    tagKey = "categories"
)

private val CATEGORIES = listOf(
    TabItem(
        label = "Inbox",
        icon = PantrixIcons.Inbox,
        tagKey = "inbox",
        badge = TabBadge(contentDescription = "More than 99 unread messages", count = 128)
    ),
    TabItem(label = "Starred", icon = PantrixIcons.Star, tagKey = "starred"),
    TabItem(label = "Folders", icon = PantrixIcons.Folder, tagKey = "folders"),
    TabItem(label = "People", icon = PantrixIcons.Person, tagKey = "people"),
    TabItem(label = "Calendar", icon = PantrixIcons.Calendar, tagKey = "calendar"),
    TabItem(label = "Search", icon = PantrixIcons.Search, tagKey = "search"),
    TabItem(label = "Archive", icon = PantrixIcons.Folder, enabled = false, tagKey = "archive")
)
```

### With pages that are swiped

The app changes the selection as much as the user does. Here the selected tab is a pager's page: swipe the page sideways, and the indicator slides to the new tab. When a tab is pressed the tabs only report which one; it is the code in `onSelect` that turns the page.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height
import androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager
import androidx.compose.foundation.pager.rememberPagerState
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

val pager = rememberPagerState { 3 }
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(label = "Photos", tagKey = "photos"),
        TabItem(label = "Videos", tagKey = "videos"),
        TabItem(label = "Documents", tagKey = "documents")
    ),
    selectedIndex = pager.currentPage,
    onSelect = { scope.launch { pager.animateScrollToPage(it) } },
    tagKey = "library"
)
HorizontalPager(state = pager, modifier = Modifier.height(96.dp)) { page ->
    Box(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) {
        PantrixText(
            text = when (page) {
                0 -> "248 photos"
                1 -> "12 videos"
                else -> "37 documents"
            }
        )
    }
}
```

### With no tab selected

When `selectedIndex` is an index outside the tabs, no tab is selected and no indicator is drawn: the app is in a place that is no tab's view. Press the button: the selection goes. Press a tab: it comes back.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonSize
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var view by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(label = "Feed", tagKey = "feed"),
        TabItem(label = "Explore", tagKey = "explore"),
        TabItem(label = "Saved", tagKey = "saved")
    ),
    selectedIndex = view,
    onSelect = { view = it },
    tagKey = "home"
)
PantrixButton(
    text = "Open search results",
    onClick = { view = -1 },
    variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
    size = ButtonSize.Small,
    tagKey = "tabs_open_search"
)
PantrixText(
    text = if (view < 0) "Search results are open: no tab is selected" else "A tab's view is open",
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)
```

### In its own colours

With `colors` the row takes the colours it is given, not the theme's. The first row is given the colour of the selected tab and of the line; the tabs that are not selected and the hairline below stay in the theme's colours. The badge of the "Pending" tab, too, is filled with the colour it is given and not with its tone's.

The second row is a row of pills, and only the pill's fill is given. That fill is the colour of one of the theme's roles, so the theme pairs the selected label's colour with it. On a fill no role has, `selectedContent` is given as well.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabBadge
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabIndicator
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabsColors
import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabsStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.badge.BadgeColors
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val own = ownColors()
var order by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
var period by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = listOf(
        TabItem(
            label = "Pending",
            tagKey = "pending",
            badge = TabBadge(
                contentDescription = "2 pending orders",
                count = 2,
                colors = BadgeColors(container = own.color, content = own.onColor)
            )
        ),
        TabItem(label = "Shipped", tagKey = "shipped"),
        TabItem(label = "Delivered", tagKey = "delivered")
    ),
    selectedIndex = order,
    onSelect = { order = it },
    colors = TabsColors(selectedContent = own.color, indicator = own.color),
    tagKey = "orders"
)
PantrixTabs(
    tabs = PERIODS,
    selectedIndex = period,
    onSelect = { period = it },
    style = TabsStyle(indicator = TabIndicator.Pill),
    colors = TabsColors(indicator = PantrixTheme.colors.success.container),
    tagKey = "success_pill"
)

private val PERIODS = listOf(
    TabItem(label = "Day", tagKey = "day"),
    TabItem(label = "Week", tagKey = "week"),
    TabItem(label = "Month", tagKey = "month")
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ownColors`: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

## API

### PantrixTabs

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.PantrixTabs`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTabs(
    tabs: List<TabItem>,
    selectedIndex: Int,
    onSelect: (index: Int) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    scrollable: Boolean = false,
    style: TabsStyle? = null,
    colors: TabsColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A row of tabs that switches between views of the same content: one is selected, and a mark slides to the one selected next.

What marks the selected tab is the style's `TabsStyle.indicator`: a line under it, a line over it, a pill behind it, or its colour alone. The mark is where its tab is. It follows the tab when the row changes size, and slides only when the selection changes: at once under reduced motion.

The row is one stop for Tab, on the selected tab, as the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern has it. The arrow keys select the next or the previous tab, the other way round in a right-to-left layout, and Home and End the first and the last; a tab that is disabled is skipped. While a tab has the focus, the focus goes with the selection, whoever makes it: a key, a press, or the app, as when a pager is swiped to the next view. A press on a tab asks for it, and the focus goes to the row's one stop, the selected tab, where a press can take the focus. For a screen reader each tab is a tab that says whether it is selected, in one group.

A tab may carry a badge after its label, a count or a dot: `TabItem.badge`. A screen reader hears the badge's description after the label, as a part of the tab.

With `scrollable`, each tab is as wide as its label and the row scrolls sideways. It opens on the selected tab, and brings the one selected next to its middle, so that the tabs on both sides of it can be seen and pressed.

A tab is at least as tall as the platform's touch target, whatever the style's height and the density say. The row has no fill of its own: it sits on the page or on a surface, and its labels read on both. The tabs are only the row: the view that `selectedIndex` stands for is the app's, below it.

Parameters:

- `tabs: List<TabItem>`: the tabs, in order.
- `selectedIndex: Int`: the selected tab's index. Outside `tabs`, no tab is selected and no mark is drawn.
- `onSelect: (index: Int) -> Unit`: called with the index of the tab the user chose, by a press or by the keys, whether or not it is selected already. The row selects nothing by itself: a tab is selected when `selectedIndex` says so.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the row's modifier. The row fills the width it is given.
- `scrollable: Boolean`: false shares the row's width between the tabs. True makes each as wide as its label, at least the style's `minTabWidth`, in a row that scrolls sideways and keeps the selected tab in its middle.
- `style: TabsStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TabsColors?`: this row's own colours: the ones it sets, with the theme's for the rest. A disabled tab keeps the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the row's automation key: the row is `Tabs_<tagKey>`, and its tabs are named inside it, `Tabs_<tagKey>.Tab_<key>`, so that two rows with the same tabs are told apart. A selection is reported as a `Tabs` event that carries the tab's index and whether a press or a key chose it, and never its label.

### TabItem

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabItem`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TabItem(
    public val label: String,
    public val icon: ImageVector? = null,
    public val enabled: Boolean = true,
    public val tagKey: String? = null,
    public val badge: TabBadge? = null
)
```

One tab of `PantrixTabs`: its label, an icon before it, a badge after it, and a key for automation.

Parameters:

- `label: String`: The visible text, and the tab's name for a screen reader.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: Drawn before the label, in the label's colour, or null for none.
- `enabled: Boolean`: Whether the tab can be selected. A press does nothing on one that cannot, and the arrow keys skip it.
- `tagKey: String?`: The tab's automation key, the same in every language: the tab is `Tab_<tagKey>`, or `Tab_<index>` without one, inside the tag of a row that has a key: `Tabs_mail.Tab_inbox`.
- `badge: TabBadge?`: A count or a dot after the label, or null for none.

### TabBadge

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabBadge`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TabBadge(
    public val contentDescription: String?,
    public val count: Int? = null,
    public val tone: BadgeTone = BadgeTone.Danger,
    public val colors: BadgeColors? = null
)
```

A badge on a tab of `PantrixTabs`: a count, or a dot where there is nothing to count.

The badge comes after the tab's label, and takes its room from the label where the tab is narrow: a long label is cut, and the badge is whole. It is a `PantrixBadge`, as large as that is and in its colours, on a tab of any state.

A screen reader hears `contentDescription` after the tab's label, as a part of the tab: "Inbox, 3 unread". A number alone would say nothing of what it counts, so the badge is silent without one, which is right only where the label says it already. It has no default for that reason: null is a decision.

Parameters:

- `contentDescription: String?`: What a screen reader says of the badge, after the tab's label, or null to say nothing.
- `count: Int?`: The number to show, or null for a dot. It is capped as a badge's is: `99+`.
- `tone: BadgeTone`: The colour role the badge is filled from.
- `colors: BadgeColors?`: The badge's own colours, in place of its tone's: the ones it sets, with the tone's for the rest.

### TabIndicator

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.tab.TabIndicator`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class TabIndicator
```

How `PantrixTabs` marks the selected tab.
