### Where the title stands: at the start and in the middle

Where the title stands follows the platform: at the start on Android, desktop and the web, in the middle of the bar on iOS. Here the same bar is drawn twice, and the place is given with `style`: `TopBarStyle(titleAlignment = ...)`. Both show, whichever platform you are on.

A title in the middle is in the middle of the bar whatever stands beside it: the back button does not push it aside.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarTitleAlignment
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Settings",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "start_back") },
        style = TopBarStyle(titleAlignment = TopBarTitleAlignment.Start),
        tagKey = "start"
    )
}
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Settings",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "center_back") },
        style = TopBarStyle(titleAlignment = TopBarTitleAlignment.Center),
        tagKey = "center"
    )
}
```

### The back button's icon

`PantrixBackButton` takes the icon it draws from the bar's style: `TopBarStyle.backIcon`. The platform's own icon is an arrow on Android, desktop and the web, a chevron on iOS. Here each of the two bars is given an icon with `style`; a back button in a bar's `navigationIcon` uses the style that bar was given.

Both turn round in a right-to-left layout: flip the reading direction from the "Typeface and direction" menu in the app's top bar and look.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.BackButtonIcon
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarStyle
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Arrow",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "arrow_back") },
        style = TopBarStyle(backIcon = BackButtonIcon.Arrow),
        tagKey = "arrow"
    )
}
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Chevron",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "chevron_back") },
        style = TopBarStyle(backIcon = BackButtonIcon.Chevron),
        tagKey = "chevron"
    )
}
```

### With nowhere to go back to

On the first screen of a flow there is nowhere to go back to: the `enabled` of `PantrixBackButton` is false and the button cannot be pressed. Move on with the button at the end: the back button is enabled from the second step on.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.iconbutton.PantrixIconButton
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var step by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Step ${step + 1} / 3",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = { step -= 1 }, enabled = step > 0, tagKey = "step_back") },
        actions = {
            PantrixIconButton(
                imageVector = PantrixIcons.ArrowForward,
                contentDescription = "Next step",
                onClick = { step += 1 },
                enabled = step < 2,
                tagKey = "step_next"
            )
        },
        tagKey = "steps"
    )
}
```

### A large title that collapses as the list scrolls

A collapsing title: the state is the app's and is kept with `rememberPantrixTopBarState()`; the list hands the bar its scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll(state)`. While the bar is open the title is written large, in the theme's `headline` style, in a band under the row. The large title stands at the bar's start on every platform; the title in the row stands where the platform has it, in the middle on iOS.

Scroll the list up: first the band closes and the title comes into the row, and only then does the list scroll. The bar opens again only once the list is back at its top. Left between its two heights by a finger, it goes on to the nearer; after a mouse wheel it goes on the way the wheel was last turned. A screen reader reads the title in the row: that one is there all the time, and the title is not read twice.

The bar and the list are inside a scaffold, as they would be in an app: the list fills the whole scaffold and is given the bar's height as its top inset. As the bar closes and opens the list itself stays where it is; only its inset changes. The button below takes the list back to its top and opens the bar by setting `collapsedFraction` to zero.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.PaddingValues
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.WindowInsets
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height
import androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn
import androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.rememberLazyListState
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.container.scaffold.PantrixScaffold
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.rememberPantrixTopBarState
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.topBarScroll
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonSize
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.iconbutton.PantrixIconButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

val topBar = rememberPantrixTopBarState()
val list = rememberLazyListState()
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val spacing = PantrixTheme.spacing
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixScaffold(
        modifier = Modifier.height(320.dp),
        topBar = { insets ->
            PantrixTopBar(
                title = "Inbox",
                subtitle = "3 unread",
                navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "collapsing_back") },
                actions = {
                    PantrixIconButton(
                        imageVector = PantrixIcons.Search,
                        contentDescription = "Search",
                        onClick = {},
                        tagKey = "collapsing_search"
                    )
                },
                scrolled = list.canScrollBackward,
                state = topBar,
                insets = insets,
                tagKey = "collapsing"
            )
        },
        containerColor = PantrixTheme.colors.surface,
        // A box inside the page: the system bars are in the page's scaffold, and this one has no insets.
        windowInsets = WindowInsets(0, 0, 0, 0)
    ) { padding ->
        LazyColumn(
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().topBarScroll(topBar),
            state = list,
            contentPadding = PaddingValues(
                start = spacing.lg,
                top = padding.calculateTopPadding() + spacing.lg,
                end = spacing.lg,
                bottom = spacing.lg
            ),
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.md)
        ) {
            items(24) { index -> PantrixText(text = "Conversation ${index + 1}") }
        }
    }
}
PantrixButton(
    text = "Back to top and open the bar",
    onClick = {
        scope.launch {
            list.scrollToItem(0)
            topBar.collapsedFraction = 0f
        }
    },
    variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
    size = ButtonSize.Small,
    tagKey = "collapsing_to_top"
)
```

### The insets the bar keeps clear

`insets` is the room the bar keeps clear at its edges: room for the status bar and a cutout. A `PantrixScaffold` hands it to its top bar itself; here a top inset of 28dp is given by hand. The bar's fill runs behind the inset, and the title and the back button stay below it: the bar is as tall as its style's height plus the inset.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.PaddingValues
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarColors
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Settings",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "insets_back") },
        colors = TopBarColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.container),
        insets = PaddingValues(top = 28.dp),
        tagKey = "insets"
    )
}
```

### In its own colours

`colors` gives the bar colours of its own in place of the theme's. The first bar's fill is the colour of one of the theme's roles, and that alone is given: the theme pairs the colour of the title, the subtitle and the back button with it.

The second bar is in a colour the theme does not have, the app's own purple: the colour that reads on it is given with `content`. The title, the subtitle and the back button take the `content` colour. The icon button has colours of its own: the colour that reads on the fill is given to it separately.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar
import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarColors
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonColors
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.iconbutton.PantrixIconButton
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val own = ownColors()
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Inbox",
        subtitle = "Only the fill is given",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "role_back") },
        colors = TopBarColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color),
        tagKey = "role"
    )
}
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixTopBar(
        title = "Inbox",
        subtitle = "3 unread",
        navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = {}, tagKey = "own_back") },
        actions = {
            PantrixIconButton(
                imageVector = PantrixIcons.Search,
                contentDescription = "Search",
                onClick = {},
                colors = ButtonColors(container = Color.Transparent, content = own.onColor),
                tagKey = "own_search"
            )
        },
        colors = TopBarColors(container = own.color, content = own.onColor),
        tagKey = "own"
    )
}
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ownColors`: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

## API

### PantrixTopBar

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBar`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTopBar(
    title: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    subtitle: String? = null,
    titleStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.title,
    subtitleStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    navigationIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    scrolled: Boolean = false,
    state: PantrixTopBarState? = null,
    style: TopBarStyle? = null,
    colors: TopBarColors? = null,
    insets: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(),
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

The bar at the top of a screen: the screen's title, with a navigation icon before it and actions after it.

Where the title stands follows the platform (`TopBarStyle.titleAlignment`): at the start on Android, the desktop and the web, in the middle of the bar on iOS. A title in the middle is in the middle of the bar, whatever is beside it, while it fits there; one too wide for that moves over, away from the wider side. Neither kind runs under the navigation icon or the actions: a title that is too long for the room between them is cut short, and so is the `subtitle` under it. The title is the screen's heading for a screen reader.

The bar is as wide as what holds it, and as tall as its style says under the `insets` it keeps clear. It is taller only where what it holds needs it, as a title in a larger type does: the title's lines keep a little clear of its top and its bottom.

```kotlin
val list = rememberLazyListState()
PantrixScaffold(
    topBar = { insets ->
        PantrixTopBar(
            title = stringResource(Res.string.conversation),
            navigationIcon = { PantrixBackButton(onClick = onBack, tagKey = "back") },
            scrolled = list.canScrollBackward,
            insets = insets,
            tagKey = "conversation"
        )
    }
) { padding -> Messages(list, padding) }
```

With a `state` the bar has a collapsing title. It starts `TopBarStyle.expandedHeight` tall, with the title in a large type, and the subtitle under it, in a band of their own under the navigation icon and the actions, at the bar's start on every platform. As the content under the bar scrolls up the band closes and the bar comes down to `TopBarStyle.height`, the title in the row coming in as the one in the band goes. The content hands the bar its scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll(state)`. A screen reader reads the title in the row, which is there all the time, and never meets the title twice.

A screen reader and the Tab key go through the bar in the order it reads: the navigation icon, the title and the subtitle under it, the actions.

**In the system's vertical bar.** Inside a `PantrixScaffold` that holds the column the iPhone Duo's outer screen keeps along its side, the bar hands its navigation icon and its actions over to it: they stand at the column's top, under the status bar, the navigation icon in a capsule of the bar's fill and the actions one above another in another, as UIKit puts a navigation bar's buttons there. The bar keeps its title, which then has the bar's width. Of two bars handing buttons over at once, as while one page slides over another, the column shows the one that came last.

Parameters:

- `title: String`: the screen's name, on one line.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the bar's modifier.
- `subtitle: String?`: a line under the title in a smaller type, a count or a state, or null for none.
- `titleStyle: TextStyle`: the type the title is set in, in the row: the theme's `title` unless given. A larger one makes the bar as tall as its line needs. Its colour is the bar's unless the style has one of its own. The large title of a collapsing bar is the theme's `headline`, whatever this is.
- `subtitleStyle: TextStyle`: the type the subtitle is set in, in the row and in a collapsing bar's band: the theme's `footnote` unless given. Its colour is the bar's unless the style has one of its own.
- `navigationIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands before the title: a `PantrixBackButton`, or a button that opens a drawer. Null for none, and the title then starts at the bar's own inset.
- `actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what stands after the title, in a row: icon buttons for what the screen can do, the most used first. A button draws in its own colours, the brand's unless it is given others: on a bar with a fill of its own, give each the colour that reads there.
- `scrolled: Boolean`: whether a line is drawn along the bar's bottom edge, to part it from what is scrolled under it: pass whether the content can scroll back, as `listState.canScrollBackward`. The line is inside the bar's height, and nothing moves as it comes and goes.
- `state: PantrixTopBarState?`: gives the bar a collapsing title: kept with `rememberPantrixTopBarState`, and handed the content's scroll with `Modifier.topBarScroll`. Null is a bar of one height.
- `style: TopBarStyle?`: this bar's own geometry, which a `PantrixBackButton` in `navigationIcon` draws with too. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: TopBarColors?`: this bar's own colours, or null for the theme's: its `surface`, with the title in `textPrimary` and the subtitle in `textSecondary`.
- `insets: PaddingValues`: the room the bar keeps clear at its edges, the status bar's and a cutout's, as a `PantrixScaffold` hands its top bar. The bar's fill runs behind them.
- `tagKey: String?`: the bar's automation key, the same in every language: the bar is tagged `TopBar_<tagKey>`, and the large title of a collapsing one `TopBar_<tagKey>.Title_large`.

### PantrixBackButton

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixBackButton`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixBackButton(
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    tagKey: String? = null
)
```

A button that goes back to the screen before, for a `PantrixTopBar`'s navigation icon: an icon button a screen reader calls "Back" in the theme's language.

It draws the platform's own icon (`TopBarStyle.backIcon`): an arrow on Android, the desktop and the web, a chevron on iOS. Both turn round in a right-to-left layout. In a top bar's `navigationIcon` it takes the style that bar was given.

It is a `PantrixIconButton`, and on the theme's grounds it is drawn as one: in the brand's colour. On a fill, and in a bar that was given a colour for what it holds, it is drawn in that colour. It is tagged `IconButton_<tagKey>` and reports an `IconButton` `click`.

Parameters:

- `onClick: () -> Unit`: called at a press: go back to the screen before.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the button's modifier.
- `enabled: Boolean`: whether the button can be pressed.
- `tagKey: String?`: the button's automation key, the same in every language.

### rememberPantrixTopBarState

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.rememberPantrixTopBarState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberPantrixTopBarState(): PantrixTopBarState
```

A `PantrixTopBarState` that survives a configuration change, for a `PantrixTopBar` with a collapsing title.

### PantrixTopBarState

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.PantrixTopBarState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PantrixTopBarState(collapsedFraction: Float = 0f)
```

How far a `PantrixTopBar` with a collapsing title has collapsed, and the scroll that collapses it.

A bar given a state is `TopBarStyle.expandedHeight` tall, with its title in a large type in a band under the navigation icon and the actions. As the content under it scrolls up the band closes, the title comes into the row, and the bar is `TopBarStyle.height` tall. The content hands the bar its scroll with `topBarScroll`: the bar collapses before the content moves, and opens again only once the content is back at its top, so the large title does not come back in the middle of a list. A finger that leaves the bar between its two heights is followed by the bar going on to the nearer, and a mouse wheel by the bar going on the way the wheel was last turned.

The state is the app's, as a scroll state is: keep it with `rememberPantrixTopBarState`, which survives a configuration change, and read `collapsedFraction` for anything else that follows the bar.

Parameters:

- `collapsedFraction: Float`: how far the bar is collapsed to begin with: 0, all open, unless it is told.

Members:

- `collapsedFraction: Float`: 0 while the bar is all open, 1 once it has collapsed. Set, it is kept between the two: set to 0, as a screen that has just gone back to its top does, it opens the bar.

On the type:

- `PantrixTopBarState.Saver: Saver<PantrixTopBarState, Float>`: Keeps how far the bar had collapsed across a configuration change.

### Modifier.topBarScroll

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.topBarScroll`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
fun Modifier.topBarScroll(state: PantrixTopBarState): Modifier
```

Hands the scroll of the content this is on to `state`, so that the top bar over it collapses as the content scrolls up, and opens again once the content is back at its top. It watches a mouse wheel over the content too: a wheel says nothing of when its scroll is over, and content at its top has no use for a wheel turned up.

```kotlin
val topBar = rememberPantrixTopBarState()
LazyColumn(modifier = Modifier.topBarScroll(topBar), contentPadding = padding) { ... }
```

Parameters:

- `state: PantrixTopBarState`

### TopBarTitleAlignment

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarTitleAlignment`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class TopBarTitleAlignment
```

Where a `PantrixTopBar` puts its title.

Entries:

- `Start`: At the start, after the navigation icon: the top bars of Android, the desktop and the web.
- `Center`: In the middle of the bar, whatever stands beside it, while it fits there: the navigation bar of iOS.

### BackButtonIcon

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.BackButtonIcon`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class BackButtonIcon
```

The icon a `PantrixBackButton` draws.

Entries:

- `Arrow`: An arrow: the back button of Android, the desktop and the web.
- `Chevron`: A chevron: the back button of iOS.

### TopBarStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TopBarStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val expandedHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val titleInset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val titleGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val titleAlignment: TopBarTitleAlignment? = null,
    public val backIcon: BackButtonIcon? = null
) : PantrixStyle<TopBarStyle>
```

`PantrixTopBar`'s geometry, and the icon `PantrixBackButton` draws.

`titleInset` keeps the title clear of an edge that has nothing beside it; next to a navigation icon or the actions the title is `titleGap` away from them. The bar is taller than `height` only where what it holds needs it. The heights and the room in the bar follow the density; where the title stands and which icon goes back do not. A top bar's colours are not part of its style: they are the theme's, and `TopBarColors` where a bar has its own.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: How tall the bar is, under the insets it keeps clear: 54dp on Android and iOS, 56dp on desktop and the web.
- `expandedHeight: Dp`: How tall a bar with a collapsing title is before it collapses: `height`, and under it the band that holds the title in a large type. 106dp on Android and iOS, 104dp on desktop and the web: a band of 52dp, and of 48dp on desktop and the web. A band is taller only where its lines need it, and a style that sets this no higher than `height` has no band: its bar is of one height, with a state or without.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the bar's edges and the navigation icon and the actions: 8dp.
- `titleInset: Dp`: How far the title stands from the bar's start edge where there is no navigation icon, and from its end edge where there are no actions: 16dp. The title is never nearer an edge than `horizontalPadding`.
- `titleGap: Dp`: The room between the navigation icon and the title, and between the title and the actions: 8dp.
- `titleAlignment: TopBarTitleAlignment?`: Where the title stands: in the middle on iOS, at the start elsewhere.
- `backIcon: BackButtonIcon?`: What a `PantrixBackButton` draws: a chevron on iOS, an arrow elsewhere.

### TopBarColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.topbar.TopBarColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class TopBarColors(
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val divider: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a `PantrixTopBar` is painted with, for a bar that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
// A bar in the brand's own colour, written in what the theme pairs with it.
PantrixTopBar(title = title, colors = TopBarColors(container = PantrixTheme.colors.primary.color))
```

A `container` given here that is one of the theme's role colours brings the colour the theme pairs with it for what the bar holds, unless `content` is given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The bar's fill, which runs behind the insets the bar keeps clear. The theme's `surface`.
- `content: Color`: The title, the subtitle, and the icons of the navigation icon and the actions that give no colour of their own. On the theme's own fill the title is the theme's `textPrimary`, the subtitle its `textSecondary`, and an icon its own default.
- `divider: Color`: The line along the bar's bottom edge while content is scrolled under it. The theme's `divider` on the theme's own grounds. On a fill, where that line would not read, a share of `content`: the edge a subtle button has.

# Alert

A message about what the user is doing, beside the thing it is about: the form that was just sent, the row about to be deleted, the field that needs a second look.

The alert stands in the content, is as wide as what holds it, and stays until the screen takes it away. What the app has just done, said for a few seconds over the whole screen, is a snackbar.

- `PantrixAlert` (`com.pantrixui.components.container.alert`, `com.pantrixui:components`): A message about what the user is doing, beside the thing it is about: six tones, three ways of drawing it, an action and a close button. Keywords: callout, inline message, notice, message bar, inline notification, warning.

## Features

- **Six tones.** `tone` chooses the alert's colour, its icon and how it is announced. The four semantic tones, `Info`, `Success`, `Warning` and `Danger`, say how something went in three ways: a colour alone fails whoever cannot see it. `Primary` and `Neutral` say nothing of that, and have no icon of their own.
- **Three variants.** `variant`: `Soft` is the tone's pale fill, `Outline` an edge with no fill, and `Accent` the fill with a bar down its leading edge: on the left in a left-to-right layout, on the right in a right-to-left one.
- **A message with a link.** `message` can be an `AnnotatedString` too: a `LinkAnnotation` in it becomes a link, underlined, in the alert's text colour.
- **Title and icon.** `title` is a line above the message, in a heavier type. `icon` puts another icon in place of the tone's own, or takes the icon away with null.
- **Action.** `action` puts one or two small buttons under the message, at the trailing edge.
- **Dismissal.** With `onDismiss` the alert has a close button. An alert does not go away by itself: it stays until the caller stops showing it.
- **Screen reader.** The title and the message are read as one, and the action and the close button after them. The alert is announced when it appears or changes: assertively for `Danger`, politely for the rest. `announce = false` turns this off.
- **First line.** The icon and the close button stand on the text's first line, however large the type is set. An alert with an icon and one without are as tall as each other.
- **Platform.** The corners are medium on Android and iOS, and small on desktop and the web; the padding is 12dp and 10dp, and the bar 4dp and 3dp (`AlertStyle`).
- **Text.** `textStyle` changes the type of the message, and of the title in its bold; the icon and the close button stand on that type's first line.
- **Colours of its own.** `AlertColors` gives the fill, the colour of the text and of what marks the tone, and `border` the colour of an edge apart from the icon's; the tone still decides the icon and the way the alert is announced.
- **Automation.** With `tagKey` the alert is `Alert_<tagKey>` and its close button `AlertClose_<tagKey>`. A dismissal is reported with its tone and its variant, and never with its message.

## Usage

### What went wrong with the form

```kotlin
if (error != null) {
    PantrixAlert(message = error, tone = AlertTone.Danger, tagKey = "form_error")
}
```

### A standing note inside a card

```kotlin
PantrixAlert(
    message = stringResource(Res.string.archived_records_cannot_be_edited),
    variant = AlertVariant.Outline,
    title = stringResource(Res.string.read_only),
    announce = false,
    tagKey = "read_only"
)
```

### A warning with an action, which the user can close

```kotlin
if (showStorageWarning) {
    PantrixAlert(
        message = stringResource(Res.string.storage_almost_full),
        tone = AlertTone.Warning,
        variant = AlertVariant.Accent,
        action = {
            PantrixButton(
                text = stringResource(Res.string.manage_storage),
                onClick = onManageStorage,
                variant = ButtonVariant.Text,
                size = ButtonSize.Small,
                colors = PantrixTheme.colors.warning.buttonColors(ButtonVariant.Text)
            )
        },
        onDismiss = { showStorageWarning = false },
        tagKey = "storage"
    )
}
```

## Examples

### Message and title

The least it takes is `message` alone: the tone is then `Info` and the variant `Soft`, and the icon comes from the tone. The alert fills the width it is given.

`title` puts a line in a heavier type above the message: it says in a few words what the alert is about. A screen reader hears the title and the message as one.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert

PantrixAlert(message = "Your profile photo has been updated", tagKey = "plain")
PantrixAlert(
    message = "We have sent a verification link to your new address",
    title = "Verify your email",
    tagKey = "titled"
)
```

### Six tones

`tone` is one of the theme's colour roles; it chooses the alert's colour, its icon and how it is announced to a screen reader, all at once. The four semantic tones reach the user three ways: as a colour, as an icon and in the way they are announced. `Danger` is the one tone announced assertively.

`Primary` and `Neutral` do not say how something went, and have no icon. An alert in one of them is a note set apart from the text around it: a feature to try, something to know that does not ask for the eye.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert

PantrixAlert(message = "A new version is ready to install", tagKey = "info")
PantrixAlert(message = "Your changes have been saved", tone = AlertTone.Success, tagKey = "success")
PantrixAlert(message = "Your storage is almost full", tone = AlertTone.Warning, tagKey = "warning")
PantrixAlert(message = "The message could not be sent", tone = AlertTone.Danger, tagKey = "danger")
PantrixAlert(message = "Try the new editor", tone = AlertTone.Primary, tagKey = "primary")
PantrixAlert(message = "Last opened: yesterday", tone = AlertTone.Neutral, tagKey = "neutral")
```

### Three variants

`variant` chooses how the alert is drawn: a pale fill, an edge alone, or the fill with a bar down its leading edge. `Soft` is the default, and what a page wants. `Accent` tells alerts one under another apart at a glance.

`Outline` is for a card or a dialog: a pale fill would be lost on their own fill. The one here is inside a filled card: it has no fill of its own, so the card's fill shows, and its text is written in the colour that reads on the card. This alert's `announce` is false as well: a note that was there before the user came is not announced when it appears.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert
import com.pantrixui.components.container.card.CardVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.card.PantrixCard

PantrixAlert(
    message = "A pale fill: this is how it looks on a page",
    title = "Soft",
    tagKey = "soft"
)
PantrixCard(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = CardVariant.Filled) {
    PantrixAlert(
        message = "Archived records cannot be changed",
        variant = AlertVariant.Outline,
        title = "Outline: read-only",
        // It was already here when the user came: a screen reader gets to it in its own time.
        announce = false,
        tagKey = "outline"
    )
}
PantrixAlert(
    message = "Alerts one under another are told apart at a glance",
    tone = AlertTone.Success,
    variant = AlertVariant.Accent,
    title = "Accent",
    tagKey = "accent"
)
```

### Changing and removing the icon

`icon` is the mark before the text: the tone's own unless one is given, and none when null. The `Primary` and `Neutral` tones have no icon of their own; here each of them was given one. The icon is never read out: the message says what it stands for.

An alert with an icon and one without are as tall as each other: the text's first line takes the room of an icon, with one beside it or without.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons

PantrixAlert(message = "An info note with its icon removed", icon = null, tagKey = "no_icon")
PantrixAlert(
    message = "Added to your favourites",
    tone = AlertTone.Primary,
    icon = PantrixIcons.Star,
    tagKey = "star_icon"
)
PantrixAlert(
    message = "The meeting is at 10.00 tomorrow",
    tone = AlertTone.Neutral,
    icon = PantrixIcons.Calendar,
    tagKey = "calendar_icon"
)
```

### Action and dismissal

A warning with two actions and a close button. `action` puts the buttons under the message, at the trailing edge. A text button's own colour is the brand's; `buttonColors(ButtonVariant.Text)`, taken from the tone's role, draws it in the tone's colour, which reads on the tone's fill.

There is a close button because `onDismiss` is given. Press the cross or "Later": it is the screen's state that takes the alert away, not the alert; the button that brings it back takes its place. Someone using a screen reader can also close the alert with the dismiss action, without finding the button.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonSize
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.buttonColors
import com.pantrixui.components.overlay.snackbar.LocalPantrixSnackbars
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
var shown by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
// A text button's own colour is the brand's; on the alert's fill it is the tone's own colour that reads.
val inTheTone = PantrixTheme.colors.warning.buttonColors(ButtonVariant.Text)
if (shown) {
    PantrixAlert(
        message = "New photos may not be backed up",
        tone = AlertTone.Warning,
        variant = AlertVariant.Accent,
        title = "Your storage is almost full",
        action = {
            PantrixButton(
                text = "Later",
                onClick = { shown = false },
                variant = ButtonVariant.Text,
                size = ButtonSize.Small,
                colors = inTheTone,
                tagKey = "storage_later"
            )
            PantrixButton(
                text = "Manage",
                onClick = { scope.launch { snackbars?.show(message = "Storage opened", tagKey = "storage") } },
                variant = ButtonVariant.Text,
                size = ButtonSize.Small,
                colors = inTheTone,
                tagKey = "storage_manage"
            )
        },
        onDismiss = { shown = false },
        tagKey = "storage"
    )
} else {
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Show the warning again",
        onClick = { shown = true },
        variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
        tagKey = "storage_again"
    )
}
```

### Form error

A form that fails when it is sent. Press "Send": the error alert appears above the button at once. Because its tone is `Danger`, it is announced to a screen reader straight away, interrupting what it is saying. The cross takes it away.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton

var failed by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
if (failed) {
    PantrixAlert(
        message = "Check the address and try again in a few minutes",
        tone = AlertTone.Danger,
        title = "Sending failed",
        onDismiss = { failed = false },
        tagKey = "form_error"
    )
}
PantrixButton(text = "Send", onClick = { failed = true }, tagKey = "form_send")
```

### A message with a link

The message can be an `AnnotatedString` too: to set a word in bold, or to put a link in it. A link is a `LinkAnnotation`; the alert draws it in its text's colour, underlined. A `LinkAnnotation.Clickable` does the app's own work when it is pressed, a `LinkAnnotation.Url` opens its address in the browser.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.text.LinkAnnotation
import androidx.compose.ui.text.buildAnnotatedString
import androidx.compose.ui.text.withLink
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert

val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
PantrixAlert(
    message = buildAnnotatedString {
        append("This page goes away in the next release. Read ")
        withLink(LinkAnnotation.Clickable(tag = "guide") { report("New guide opened") }) {
            append("the new guide")
        }
        append(" instead.")
    },
    tone = AlertTone.Warning,
    title = "Old page",
    tagKey = "with_link"
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### In its own colours

An alert whose fill, text and marks are in colours the caller gives. `AlertColors` takes three colours: the fill (`container`), the text (`content`) and what marks the tone (`accent`): the icon, the edge of `Outline` and the bar of `Accent`. A colour that is left out stays the tone's. The tone still gives the alert its icon and the way it is announced: only what it is painted in changes.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertColors
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val own = ownColors()
PantrixAlert(
    message = "The colours of its fill, its text and its marks were given by the caller",
    variant = AlertVariant.Accent,
    colors = AlertColors(container = own.container, content = own.onContainer, accent = own.color),
    tagKey = "own"
)
PantrixText(
    text = "Colours are given with AlertColors; a colour that is left out stays the tone's.",
    style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
    color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ownColors`: The "app's own colour" of the examples: a purple that is in none of the theme's roles. It is there to show what changes when a component is given `colors`; given one of the theme's roles, nobody could tell whether the colour came from the component's tone or from the parameter.

### In its own style

`style` changes the alert's geometry: its corners, its padding, the room between its parts, and how thick the edge of `Outline` and the bar of `Accent` are. Only the fields that are set change; the rest comes from the platform's style.

The third is a note: its fill and its icon are the tone's, its edge a colour apart from them (`AlertColors(border = …)`), its padding one across and another up and down (`horizontalPadding`, `verticalPadding`), and its text the theme's `label` (`textStyle`): the icon and the close button stand on that text's first line, and its colour is still the alert's.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.RectangleShape
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertColors
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import com.pantrixui.foundation.token.shape.ShapeSpec

PantrixAlert(
    message = "Square corners, bar 8dp",
    tone = AlertTone.Success,
    variant = AlertVariant.Accent,
    style = AlertStyle(shape = ShapeSpec.Fixed(RectangleShape), accentWidth = 8.dp),
    tagKey = "own_style_accent"
)
PantrixAlert(
    message = "Padding 20dp, edge 2dp",
    tone = AlertTone.Warning,
    variant = AlertVariant.Outline,
    style = AlertStyle(padding = 20.dp, borderWidth = 2.dp),
    tagKey = "own_style_outline"
)
PantrixAlert(
    message = "An edge in a colour apart from the fill and the icon; padding of 14 across and 10dp up and down; text the size of a label",
    tone = AlertTone.Warning,
    style = AlertStyle(horizontalPadding = 14.dp, verticalPadding = 10.dp),
    colors = AlertColors(border = PantrixTheme.colors.warning.color.copy(alpha = 0.45f)),
    tagKey = "own_style_note",
    textStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.label
)
```

## API

### PantrixAlert

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAlert(
    message: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    tone: AlertTone = AlertTone.Info,
    variant: AlertVariant = AlertVariant.Soft,
    title: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = tone.icon(),
    action: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    announce: Boolean = true,
    style: AlertStyle? = null,
    colors: AlertColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.body
)
```

A message about what the user is doing, shown beside the thing it is about: the form that was just sent, the row about to be deleted, the one field that needs a second look.

It stands in the content, next to that thing, and is as wide as what holds it. It stays until the screen takes it away: what the app has just done, said for a few seconds over the whole screen, is a snackbar.

A semantic tone reaches the user three ways, as a colour, as an icon and as the way a screen reader is told, because a colour alone fails whoever cannot see it. A screen reader hears the title and the message as one, and the action and the close button after them.

The icon and the close button stand on the text's first line, as a bullet does, however large the type is set. That line is as tall as an icon with one beside it or without, so alerts one under another are as tall as each other. The close button is as large as its cross where it is laid out, so the alert is no taller for it, and its touch target reaches past it into the room around.

Parameters:

- `message: String`: what happened, or what to know: a sentence or two.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the alert's modifier. The alert fills the width it is given.
- `tone: AlertTone`: what the alert is telling: its colours, its icon and the way it is announced.
- `variant: AlertVariant`: how it is drawn: a pale fill, an edge alone, or the fill with a bar.
- `title: String?`: a line above the message, in a heavier type: what it is about, in a few words.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: the mark before the text: the tone's own unless another is given, and none when null. A primary and a neutral alert have none of their own. It is never read out: the message says what it stands for. `icon`: The tone's own icon; a primary and a neutral alert have none.
- `action: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what the user can do about it, under the message at the end: one or two small buttons. A text button's own colour is the brand's: `PantrixTheme.colors.warning.buttonColors(ButtonVariant.Text)` draws it in the tone's, which reads on the tone's fill. A button there takes the room it is drawn in: the room a finger needs around it reaches into the alert's padding, and the alert is no taller for it.
- `onDismiss: (() -> Unit)?`: called when the close button is pressed, or a screen reader's dismiss action is used. Null leaves the button out. The alert stays until the caller stops showing it.
- `announce: Boolean`: whether a screen reader is told when the alert appears or changes: assertively for `AlertTone.Danger`, politely for the rest. Turn it off for an alert that was there before the user came, as a note that a record cannot be changed: a screen reader gets to it in its own time.
- `style: AlertStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density. Only the fields it sets change, on every platform.
- `colors: AlertColors?`: this alert's own colours, where they are not its tone's: the ones set here, with the tone's for the rest.
- `tagKey: String?`: the alert's automation key: the alert is `Alert_<tagKey>` and its close button `AlertClose_<tagKey>`. A dismissal is reported as an `Alert` event, `dismiss`, with the tone and the variant and never the message.
- `textStyle: TextStyle`: the type the message is set in, and the title in its bold: the theme's `body` unless given. A colour in it is not the text's, which is the alert's.

### PantrixAlert

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.PantrixAlert`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixAlert(
    message: AnnotatedString,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    tone: AlertTone = AlertTone.Info,
    variant: AlertVariant = AlertVariant.Soft,
    title: String? = null,
    icon: ImageVector? = tone.icon(),
    action: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    onDismiss: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    announce: Boolean = true,
    style: AlertStyle? = null,
    colors: AlertColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    textStyle: TextStyle = PantrixTheme.typography.body
)
```

`PantrixAlert` for a message with more in it than words: a value set as code, a word set in bold, a link to the page that says more. It is drawn, announced and reported as the other form is; a screen reader hears the message's words with the title, and reaches each link on its own, as it reaches the action.

A link that carries no styles of its own is drawn as a link in the alert: underlined, in what the alert writes in, so that it reads on the tone's fill. One that carries its own keeps them.

```kotlin
PantrixAlert(
    message = buildAnnotatedString {
        append("Put the token in ")
        withStyle(SpanStyle(fontFamily = FontFamily.Monospace)) { append("gradle.properties") }
        append(", never in the project. ")
        withLink(LinkAnnotation.Url(tokensHelpUrl)) { append("How to make one") }
    },
    tone = AlertTone.Warning,
    tagKey = "token"
)
```

Parameters:

- `message: AnnotatedString`: what happened, or what to know, with its spans and links.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the alert's modifier. The alert fills the width it is given.
- `tone: AlertTone`: what the alert is telling: its colours, its icon and the way it is announced.
- `variant: AlertVariant`: how it is drawn: a pale fill, an edge alone, or the fill with a bar.
- `title: String?`: a line above the message, in a heavier type: what it is about, in a few words.
- `icon: ImageVector?`: the mark before the text: the tone's own unless another is given, and none when null. `icon`: The tone's own icon; a primary and a neutral alert have none.
- `action: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)?`: what the user can do about it, under the message at the end: one or two small buttons.
- `onDismiss: (() -> Unit)?`: called when the close button is pressed, or a screen reader's dismiss action is used. Null leaves the button out.
- `announce: Boolean`: whether a screen reader is told when the alert appears or changes.
- `style: AlertStyle?`: this call's own style: over every enclosing one and under the density.
- `colors: AlertColors?`: this alert's own colours, where they are not its tone's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the alert's automation key: the alert is `Alert_<tagKey>` and its close button `AlertClose_<tagKey>`.
- `textStyle: TextStyle`: the type the message is set in, and the title in its bold: the theme's `body` unless given. A colour in it is not the text's, which is the alert's.

### AlertTone

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertTone`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class AlertTone
```

What an alert is telling the user: one of the theme's colour roles, which also decides its icon and how it is announced.

The semantic tones, `Info`, `Success`, `Warning` and `Danger`, say how something went, and reach the user as a colour and as an icon, because a colour alone fails whoever cannot see it. `Primary` and `Neutral` say nothing of that, and have no icon of their own: an alert in one of them is a note set apart from the text around it.

Entries:

- `Info`: Something worth knowing that is neither good nor bad.
- `Success`: Something that worked.
- `Warning`: Something to look at before it becomes a problem.
- `Danger`: Something that failed. The one tone announced assertively: it interrupts what a screen reader is saying.
- `Primary`: Something the app wants noticed, in the brand's colour, without an icon: a feature to try, an offer.
- `Neutral`: A note with no hue of its own, in the theme's grey, without an icon: what does not ask for the eye.

### AlertVariant

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertVariant`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class AlertVariant
```

How an alert is drawn, so that it can be seen on whatever it stands on.

Entries:

- `Soft`: The tone's pale fill. The default, and what a page wants.
- `Outline`: An edge in the tone's colour and no fill: for a card or a dialog, whose own fill a pale one would be lost on.
- `Accent`: The pale fill with a bar down its leading edge: for alerts one under another, told apart at a glance.

### AlertStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class AlertStyle(
    public val shape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val padding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val contentGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val borderWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val accentWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val horizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val verticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<AlertStyle>
```

`PantrixAlert`'s geometry: its corners, the room around what it holds and between its parts, and the two lines its variants draw, an edge all the way round or a bar down the leading edge.

The room follows the density; the corners and the lines do not: they are not air. An alert's colours are not part of its style: they come from its `AlertTone` and its `AlertVariant`, and from `AlertColors` where an alert has its own.

Parameters:

- `shape: ShapeSpec`: The alert's corners: medium on Android and iOS, small on desktop and the web.
- `padding: Dp`: The room between the alert's edge and what it holds: 12dp on Android and iOS, 10dp on desktop and the web.
- `contentGap: Dp`: The room between the icon and the text, and between the text and the close button: 8dp.
- `borderWidth: Dp`: How thick the edge of `AlertVariant.Outline` is: 1dp.
- `accentWidth: Dp`: How wide the bar of `AlertVariant.Accent` is: 4dp on Android and iOS, 3dp on desktop and the web.
- `horizontalPadding: Dp`: The room between the alert's start and end edges and what it holds, where it is not `padding`: unspecified on every platform, which takes `padding`.
- `verticalPadding: Dp`: The room between the alert's top and bottom edges and what it holds, where it is not `padding`: unspecified on every platform, which takes `padding`.

### AlertColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.container.alert.AlertColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class AlertColors(
    public val container: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val content: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val accent: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val border: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What `PantrixAlert` is painted with, for an alert that does not take its tone's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the tone's.

```kotlin
PantrixAlert(
    message = stringResource(Res.string.new_version_ready),
    colors = AlertColors(container = brand.container, content = brand.onContainer, accent = brand.color)
)
```

A tone still gives an alert its icon and the way it is announced: only what it is painted in changes.

A fill given here that is a role's own brings the colour the theme pairs with it, for what is written on it and for the icon and the lines, unless those are given too. A fill no role has does not: what reads on it is the caller's to give.

Parameters:

- `container: Color`: The alert's fill. The `container` of its tone's role; none in `AlertVariant.Outline`, which shows what the alert stands on.
- `content: Color`: The title and the message, what the action is drawn in unless it has a colour of its own, and the close button's cross: the colour that reads on `container`. The `onContainer` of its tone's role. None in `AlertVariant.Outline`, where the alert has no fill: its text is drawn as a text is where the alert stands, `textPrimary` on the page and the content colour of a fill around it.
- `accent: Color`: What marks the tone: the icon, the edge of `AlertVariant.Outline` unless `border` is given, and the bar of `AlertVariant.Accent`. The `color` of its tone's role.
- `border: Color`: The edge all the way round the alert, at the style's `borderWidth`, where it is not the icon's colour: an alert of any variant given one draws it, over its fill and beside the bar of `AlertVariant.Accent`. Left out, `AlertVariant.Outline`'s edge is `accent` and the other two variants draw none.

# Breadcrumb

The trail of pages above the one on screen: each a link back to it, the last the page on screen itself. In a path of folders, in the sections of a document or in a catalogue, it tells the reader where they are and how to go up one. The row at the top of this page is a `PantrixBreadcrumb` too.

A trail is one line, and never wraps. When it does not fit its row it folds by itself: the pages after the first go behind a button, as few of them as it takes, and the button opens them as a menu.

- `PantrixBreadcrumb` (`com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb`, `com.pantrixui:components`): The trail of pages above the one on screen, each a link back to it, ending in the page on screen; a trail too long for its row folds its middle into a menu. Keywords: breadcrumbs, trail, path, location, hierarchy navigation, crumbs.

## Features

- **Links and the page on screen.** The pages above are links, each underlined; when one is pressed, `onSelect` reports its key. The last page is the page on screen: it is a text, it is not pressed, and its key is never reported.
- **It folds by itself.** Where the row is too narrow, the trail keeps its first page and its last ones, and those between them go into the menu that the three-dot button opens. Where the first page and the last do not fit beside the button either, the long names are cut to one width, and a short one stays as it is.
- **The most pages.** With `maxItems` the row shows no more pages than that, even where it has room. It has to be at least two: a trail always shows its first page and its last.
- **Icons.** `BreadcrumbItem.icon` stands before the page's name; with `iconOnly` it takes the name's place, and the page is a button that says its name to a screen reader.
- **Type and sizes.** `textStyle` is the names' type, the theme's `label` where it is not given. `BreadcrumbStyle` gives the room between the names and the marks, and the size of the mark and of the icon; these are the same on every platform. `minHeight` makes the row lower than the touch target, and `linkUnderline` says when the links are underlined.
- **Colours.** `BreadcrumbColors` paints the links, the page on screen and the marks one by one. On a fill, all of a trail that is given no colour is in the colour that is written on the fill.
- **Screen reader.** The row is a group named "Breadcrumb", the last page is read with the state "Current page", and the marks in between are not read. On iOS the group has no name: a screen reader there reads a group's name after what the group holds.
- **Right to left.** In languages read from right to left the trail starts on the right, and the marks turn round.
- **Automation.** In a trail that is given a `tagKey`, the pages and the button for the folded pages are named inside it: `Breadcrumb_docs.Item_components`, `Breadcrumb_docs.More_pages`.

## Usage

### Over a page of the documentation

```kotlin
PantrixBreadcrumb(
    items = listOf(
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "home", label = stringResource(Res.string.home)),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "components", label = stringResource(Res.string.components)),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "breadcrumb", label = stringResource(Res.string.breadcrumb))
    ),
    onSelect = { key -> onOpen(key) },
    tagKey = "docs"
)
```

### Folders, the first shown by its icon alone and never more than four in the row

```kotlin
PantrixBreadcrumb(
    items = listOf(BreadcrumbItem(key = "root", label = rootName, icon = PantrixIcons.Folder, iconOnly = true)) +
        folders.map { BreadcrumbItem(key = it.id, label = it.name) },
    onSelect = onOpenFolder,
    maxItems = 4,
    tagKey = "folders"
)
```

## Examples

### Navigating folders

At its plainest: the trail's pages (`items`) and what happens when one of them is pressed (`onSelect`). Which page the app is on is the screen's state; the trail does not hold it, and only reports the key of the page that was pressed.

Press a folder above: the app goes up to it, and the trail ends in that folder. "Go deeper" makes the path longer again. The last page is not pressed: that is where the app already is.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonSize
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.BreadcrumbItem
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.PantrixBreadcrumb
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var depth by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(FOLDERS.size) }
PantrixBreadcrumb(
    items = FOLDERS.take(depth),
    onSelect = { key -> depth = FOLDERS.indexOfFirst { it.key == key } + 1 },
    tagKey = "folders"
)
FolderControls(depth = depth, onDeeper = { depth++ }, tagKey = "folders_deeper")

private val FOLDERS = listOf(
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "home", label = "Home"),
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "documents", label = "Documents"),
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "projects", label = "Projects"),
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "pantrix", label = "Pantrix"),
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "design", label = "Design")
)

@Composable
private fun FolderControls(
    depth: Int,
    onDeeper: () -> Unit,
    tagKey: String
) {
    Row(
        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
    ) {
        PantrixButton(
            text = "Go deeper",
            onClick = onDeeper,
            variant = ButtonVariant.Soft,
            size = ButtonSize.Small,
            enabled = depth < FOLDERS.size,
            tagKey = tagKey
        )
        PantrixText(text = "You are here: ${FOLDERS[depth - 1].label}", color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary)
    }
}
```

### A row that shows three pages at the most

`maxItems = 3`: the row shows no more than three pages, even where it has room. The first page and the last two stay; those between them are behind the three-dot button.

Press the button: the folded folders open as a menu, in the order of the trail. A folder chosen in the menu is reported through `onSelect` as one pressed in the row is, and the app goes up to it. When the path is down to three pages the button goes.

```kotlin

import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.BreadcrumbItem
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.PantrixBreadcrumb
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixBreadcrumb(

) {

        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
```

### Icons: before the name or in its place

`icon` stands before the page's name, in the name's colour. The icon and the name are one link: a press on the icon is a press on the name, and the icon is no second stop for the keyboard and no second thing for a screen reader.

In the first trail the first page is shown by its icon alone, with `iconOnly`: it is a button that says its name to a screen reader. A page without an icon is written by its name whatever `iconOnly` says.

In the second trail two pages that are shown by their icons alone are folded away. Press the three-dot button: the menu writes each page's name beside its icon.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.BreadcrumbItem
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.PantrixBreadcrumb
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons

PantrixBreadcrumb(
    items = listOf(
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "files", label = "Files", icon = PantrixIcons.Folder, iconOnly = true),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "starred", label = "Starred", icon = PantrixIcons.Star),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "schedule", label = "Calendar", icon = PantrixIcons.Calendar)
    ),
    onSelect = {},
    tagKey = "icons"
)
PantrixBreadcrumb(
    items = listOf(
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "files", label = "Files", icon = PantrixIcons.Folder, iconOnly = true),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "starred", label = "Starred", icon = PantrixIcons.Star, iconOnly = true),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "schedule", label = "Calendar", icon = PantrixIcons.Calendar, iconOnly = true),
        BreadcrumbItem(key = "today", label = "Today")
    ),
    onSelect = {},
    maxItems = 2,
    tagKey = "icons_folded"
)
```

### A path too long for its row folds by itself

No `maxItems` is given: the trail folds to the width that is left to it. First the pages after the first go behind the button, as few of them as it takes; the trail keeps its first page, where it began, and its last ones, where it is. Where the first page and the last do not fit beside the button either, the long names are cut to one width, and a short one stays as it is.

The same path at three widths: the first as wide as the example, the others in frames 480dp and 240dp wide at the most. In the middle frame the page in between is behind the button; in the narrow frame the last page's name is cut as well. Narrow the window: the first trail folds in the same order.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.width
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.BreadcrumbItem
import com.pantrixui.components.navigation.breadcrumb.PantrixBreadcrumb
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixBreadcrumb(items = LONG_PATH, onSelect = {}, tagKey = "long")
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.width(480.dp), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixBreadcrumb(
        items = LONG_PATH,
        onSelect = {},
        modifier = Modifier.padding(horizontal = PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
        tagKey = "long_medium"
    )
}
PantrixSurface(modifier = Modifier.width(240.dp), border = PantrixTheme.colors.divider) {
    PantrixBreadcrumb(
        items = LONG_PATH,
        onSelect = {},
        modifier = Modifier.padding(horizontal = PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
        tagKey = "long_narrow"
    )
}

private val LONG_PATH = listOf(
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "home", label = "Home"),
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "systems", label = "Design systems and component libraries"),
    BreadcrumbItem(key = "navigation", label = "Navigation for wide and narrow windows")
)
```

### On a fill

A trail on a fill that is not one of the theme's grounds. No colour is given: the fill says what is written on it, and all of the trail, its links, the page on screen and the marks, is written in that colour. The theme's link and text colours are for the theme's own grounds; here a link is told from the page on screen by its underline.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
```
