### Pressing a slice

`onSelect` gives the slice that is pressed: its key, its name, its value and how the chart writes it. Press a slice, or go to one with the keyboard and press Enter: the line under the card writes what was pressed.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PantrixPieChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieSlice

val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
PantrixPieChart(
    slices = VISIT_SOURCES.map { PieSlice(it.key, it.name, it.visits) },
    description = "Visits by source",
    onSelect = { point -> report("${point.name}: ${point.text}") },
    tagKey = "pressed"
)

private data class VisitSource(
    val key: String,
    val name: String,
    val visits: Int,
    val before: Int
)

private val VISIT_SOURCES = listOf(
    VisitSource("direct", "Direct", visits = 420, before = 380),
    VisitSource("search", "Search", visits = 310, before = 240),
    VisitSource("social", "Social", visits = 150, before = 260),
    VisitSource("mail", "E-mail", visits = 80, before = 90),
    VisitSource("other", "Other", visits = 40, before = 30)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### Values that change

When the values change the slices go from where they were to where they are now. Turn the switch: the chart shows last year's visits. The slices are matched by their keys: a slice whose name or value changes is the same slice, and keeps its colour and its place in the legend.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartDataLabels
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PantrixPieChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieSlice
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton

var before by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = before,
    onCheckedChange = { before = it },
    label = "Last year",
    tagKey = "pie_before"
)
PantrixPieChart(
    slices = VISIT_SOURCES.map { PieSlice(it.key, it.name, if (before) it.before else it.visits) },
    hole = 0.6f,
    labels = ChartDataLabels(),
    description = if (before) "Visits by source last year" else "Visits by source this year",
    tagKey = "changing"
)

private data class VisitSource(
    val key: String,
    val name: String,
    val visits: Int,
    val before: Int
)

private val VISIT_SOURCES = listOf(
    VisitSource("direct", "Direct", visits = 420, before = 380),
    VisitSource("search", "Search", visits = 310, before = 240),
    VisitSource("social", "Social", visits = 150, before = 260),
    VisitSource("mail", "E-mail", visits = 80, before = 90),
    VisitSource("other", "Other", visits = 40, before = 30)
)
```

### Your own colours and sizes

A chart's own look. Each slice names its own colour (`PieSlice(color = …)`): shades of one violet from the palette in place of the theme's chart colours. `ChartStyle` gives the sizes: no gap between the slices (`sliceGap`) and a lower chart (`height`). A field that is not given stays the theme's.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartDataLabels
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PantrixPieChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieSlice
import com.pantrixui.foundation.token.color.PantrixPalette

val dark = LocalDemoDarkTheme.current
val violet = PantrixPalette.Violet
val tones = if (dark) {
    listOf(violet.shade300, violet.shade400, violet.shade500, violet.shade600, violet.shade700)
} else {
    listOf(violet.shade800, violet.shade600, violet.shade500, violet.shade400, violet.shade300)
}
PantrixPieChart(
    slices = VISIT_SOURCES.mapIndexed { index, source ->
        PieSlice(source.key, source.name, source.visits, color = tones[index])
    },
    labels = ChartDataLabels(),
    description = "Visits by source",
    style = ChartStyle(sliceGap = 0.dp, height = 180.dp),
    tagKey = "own_look"
)

private data class VisitSource(
    val key: String,
    val name: String,
    val visits: Int,
    val before: Int
)

private val VISIT_SOURCES = listOf(
    VisitSource("direct", "Direct", visits = 420, before = 380),
    VisitSource("search", "Search", visits = 310, before = 240),
    VisitSource("social", "Social", visits = 150, before = 260),
    VisitSource("mail", "E-mail", visits = 80, before = 90),
    VisitSource("other", "Other", visits = 40, before = 30)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalDemoDarkTheme`: Whether the app's theme is dark right now: the system's mode while the setting is "System", and the setting itself otherwise.

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the pie as it is on the screen, the legend under it; the slice that is pointed at and its tooltip are not in it. What stands in the hole by `center` is not in the file either.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PantrixPieChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieSlice
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixPieChart(
    slices = VISIT_SOURCES.map { PieSlice(it.key, it.name, it.visits) },
    hole = 0.6f,
    center = { PantrixText(text = "Visits", color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary) },
    description = "Visits by source",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "visit-sources") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

private data class VisitSource(
    val key: String,
    val name: String,
    val visits: Int,
    val before: Int
)

private val VISIT_SOURCES = listOf(
    VisitSource("direct", "Direct", visits = 420, before = 380),
    VisitSource("search", "Search", visits = 310, before = 240),
    VisitSource("social", "Social", visits = 150, before = 260),
    VisitSource("mail", "E-mail", visits = 80, before = 90),
    VisitSource("other", "Other", visits = 40, before = 30)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixPieChart

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PantrixPieChart`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixPieChart(
    slices: List<PieSlice>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    hole: Float = 0f,
    center: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    startAngle: Float = 0f,
    sweepAngle: Float = 360f,
    sort: PieSort = PieSort.Given,
    others: PieOthers? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A pie chart: the parts of a whole as the slices of a disc, each as much of the turn as its value is of their sum. With a `hole` in its middle it is a ring, a donut, which has room in the hole for a total or a title.

The pie is given its `slices`, each with a key, a name and a value. They lie in the order they are given, or the order `sort` says, clockwise from `startAngle`, and take a whole turn or the `sweepAngle` it is given: half of one for a half pie. Each is in the theme's chart colour for its place unless it names its own. A slice whose value is no number, or is not over nought, has no part of the pie, and keeps its place in the legend. Where the pie is given `others`, its smallest slices are gathered into one, last.

Around the pie stand the parts a chart with axes has, each given by what describes it and taken away by `null`: the `legend`, which lists the slices and takes one out of the pie when its entry is pressed, and the `tooltip`, which shows the value of the slice that is pointed at and its share of the whole.

**Pointing at a slice.** A pointer over a slice points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the slice it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the pie is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from slice to slice round the pie, and past the last to the first again, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The slice stands out past the pie's rim, the tooltip is shown for it, and it is told to `state`. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`. In a window and in a browser a press on the pie takes the focus, as a press on a button does, so that the arrows after it go through this pie.

**To a screen reader** the pie is its `description`, then each slice with its value and its share, in the slices' order; the legend's entries are switches.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room. A height on its modifier is the whole chart's, the legend's with it; given none, it is as tall as the chart's style says and a legend above or under it adds its own. The pie is the largest that has room in what the legend leaves, in the middle of it: of a half pie, the half that is drawn. Where its labels are written outside it, it keeps room for them at its sides, and where that room would leave it less than half as large, it writes on its slices only.

The pie turns the same way in a language read from the right; its legend and its tooltip follow the reading direction.

```kotlin
PantrixPieChart(
    slices = listOf(
        PieSlice("direct", "Direct", 420),
        PieSlice("search", "Search", 310),
        PieSlice("social", "Social", 150)
    ),
    hole = 0.6f,
    description = "Visits by where they came from",
    tagKey = "sources"
)
```

Parameters:

- `slices: List<PieSlice>`: the slices, in the order they lie in the pie where `sort` keeps it, clockwise from `startAngle`. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's, the legend's with it.
- `hole: Float`: how much of the pie's radius is cut out of its middle: nought for a whole pie, and six tenths for a ring with room to write in. No more than nine tenths.
- `center: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands in the hole of a ring: a total, a title. It has the largest box the hole holds, of a half ring in the half that is drawn. A whole pie has no place for it.
- `labels: ChartDataLabels?`: what is written about the slices: each slice's share of the whole, or its value as the labels' `format` writes it. On a slice it is written in black or white, whichever reads on the slice; outside it, the slice's name comes before it, with a line in the slice's colour leading to it. Their `position` says where: `Outside` outside every slice, `Auto` on each slice that holds its words and outside the others, and any other on the slices only, where a slice too small to hold its words has none. Words outside stand in a column at each side; where a side has no room for all of them, one under another, the smallest slices there have none. `null` writes nothing about them.
- `legend: ChartLegend?`: where the names of the slices stand. `null` shows none.
- `tooltip: ChartTooltip?`: what is shown for the slice that is pointed at: its value, as the tooltip's `format` writes it or in the theme's language, and its share of the whole. `null` shows none. Whether a tooltip is `shared` and whether it has a `crosshair` say nothing to a pie.
- `empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.
- `state: ChartState`: what the reader has hidden and what they point at: the chart's own where none is given. A slice is hidden by its key, and pointed at by a selection whose `x` is its key.
- `description: String?`: what the pie shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its slices.
- `onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)?`: called with the slice that is pressed: its key as the point's `series` and its `x`, its name, its value, and what the pie writes for it.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the chart's automation key: the chart is `PieChart_<tagKey>`, the pie `PieChart_<tagKey>.Plot`, a slice `PieChart_<tagKey>.Slice_<number>` counted from one, the legend's entry of a slice `PieChart_<tagKey>.Legend_<slice's key>` and the tooltip `PieChart_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a slice is reported as a `PieChart` `select` event with the slice's key, and a press on a legend's entry as a `toggle` event with the key and whether the slice is shown. Nothing of the values is reported.
- `startAngle: Float`: where the first slice begins, in degrees clockwise from twelve o'clock: 270 begins at nine o'clock.
- `sweepAngle: Float`: how many degrees the slices take together: a whole turn, 360, or 180 for a half pie, from over nought up to a whole turn.
- `sort: PieSort`: the order the slices lie in: as given, the largest first or the smallest first.
- `others: PieOthers?`: how the smallest slices are gathered into one. `null` gathers none.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. What stands in the hole, `center`, is not in the file.

### PieSlice

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieSlice`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PieSlice(
    public val key: String,
    public val name: String,
    public val value: Number?,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

A slice of a `PantrixPieChart`: one of the parts of the whole the pie shows.

```kotlin
PieSlice("search", "Search", 310)
```

Two are the same slice where everything they were built from is the same; a whole number and the same number with a fraction of nought are one value.

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What tells the slice from the others of its pie, and stays the same while its value changes: what the legend keeps a hidden slice by, what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.
- `name: String`: What the slice is called: in the legend, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.
- `value: Number?`: How much the slice is of the whole. A slice whose value is no number, or is not over nought, has no part of the pie: a share of a whole is no less than nothing.
- `color: Color`: The colour the slice is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the slices of the pie: the first of them for the first.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture the slice is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the slices: none for the first.

### PieSort

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieSort`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class PieSort
```

The order a pie's slices lie in, from where they begin.

Entries:

- `Given`: As they are given.
- `Descending`: The largest first.
- `Ascending`: The smallest first.

### PieOthers

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.pie.PieOthers`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class PieOthers(
    public val share: Float = 0.03f,
    public val name: String? = null,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

How a pie gathers its smallest slices into one, so that a crowd of slivers is read as one slice: every slice that is less of the whole than `share` goes into a slice after all the others, which the tooltip and a screen reader open into the slices it holds. A single slice that small keeps its own place.

```kotlin
PieOthers(share = 0.05f)
```

The gathered slice's key is `others`: a pie that gathers keeps that key for it, and refuses a slice of its own with it. Its legend's entry takes the gathered slices out together.

Parameters:

- `share: Float`: How much of the whole a slice is at the least to stand on its own: three hundredths, and from nought, where none is gathered, to one.
- `name: String?`: What the gathered slice is called. Left out, it is the theme's word for it (`PantrixStrings.others`, "Other").
- `color: Color`: The gathered slice's colour. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place: the last.

### ChartLegend

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartLegend`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class ChartLegend(
    public val position: ChartLegendPosition = ChartLegendPosition.Bottom,
    public val alignment: ChartLegendAlignment = ChartLegendAlignment.Center,
    public val toggles: Boolean = true,
    public val always: Boolean = false
)
```

A chart's legend: where the names of its series stand, each beside a sample of how the series is drawn.

A chart of one series has no legend: what the one line is belongs in the words around the chart. `always` gives it one all the same.

An entry is a switch for its series. Pressed, it takes the series out of the chart, and the chart is drawn for the series that are left; pressed again, it brings the series back. The entry stays, drawn faint, so that what was taken out can be brought back. A screen reader hears each entry as a switch, with the series' name and whether it is on.

Parameters:

- `position: ChartLegendPosition`: Which side of the chart the legend stands on. Above and under it the entries stand in a row, on as many lines as they need; beside it they stand under each other.
- `alignment: ChartLegendAlignment`: Where in the room it has the legend stands: along the chart's width above and under it, and from the chart's top beside it.
- `toggles: Boolean`: Whether pressing an entry takes its series out of the chart and brings it back.
- `always: Boolean`: Whether a chart of one series has a legend too.

### ChartTooltip

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartTooltip`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartTooltip(
    public val shared: Boolean = true,
    public val crosshair: Boolean = true,
    public val format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    public val content: (@Composable (points: List<ChartPoint>) -> Unit)? = null
)
```

A chart's tooltip: the values at the place that is pointed at, on a small card beside it.

It comes up under a pointer, where a finger touches the chart or is drawn along it, and at the place the arrow keys have gone to. It goes when the pointer leaves, at a second touch on the place, and at Escape. It stands inside the chart, beside the place and on the side that has room for it. In a chart too narrow to have room on either side it stands over the place, at the end of the plot that the place's values are not at. It takes no press: what is under it is pressed as if it were not there.

`null` in its place shows none. The place pointed at is still marked, and still told to the chart's state.

Parameters:

- `shared: Boolean`: Whether the tooltip is of the place, with the value every series has there, or of the one series nearest the pointer. Together is how a chart is read at a place, and under a finger it asks for no aim; apart suits a chart whose series are read each on its own.
- `crosshair: Boolean`: Whether the place is marked across the chart: by a line through it, and in a chart with bars by a shade over its band.
- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: How a value is written in the tooltip and to a screen reader, where that is not how the axis writes it: a chart with no axis of values says here what its numbers are. Left out, the axis' `format` writes them, and the theme's language where the axis has none.
- `content: (@Composable (points: List<ChartPoint>) -> Unit)?`: The card's own content, in the place of the heading and the rows: given the values at the place, the one pointed at where the series are told apart. The card around it stays the chart's.

### ChartDataLabels

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartDataLabels`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartDataLabels(
    public val format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    public val position: ChartDataLabelPosition = ChartDataLabelPosition.Auto,
    public val total: Boolean = false
)
```

The values of a series written in the chart, each at its mark: over a point of a line, at the end of a bar, and inside a bar of a stack, in the one of black and white that reads better on the bar's colour.

```kotlin
BarSeries("revenue", "Revenue", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.revenue }, labels = ChartDataLabels())
BarSeries("online", "Online", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.online }, stack = "sales",
    labels = ChartDataLabels(position = ChartDataLabelPosition.InsideEnd, total = true))
```

A value has its label where the label has room. Placed by itself, one that would stand on another, or reach out of the chart, is written under its point instead, or inside the end of its bar; where it has no room there either it is left out, as is one that a bar is too small to hold. Placed where its `position` says, it has no other place. The tooltip and the screen reader still have the value. A chart of more than two hundred places writes none.

A line the chart draws to read the values by, through a label, is covered where the label is: the label is written on a plate, of the tooltip's colour past a bar and of the bar's colour inside it.

Its `position` and its `total` are of a chart with axes: a pie and a heatmap write their labels where they do.

Two are the same where they write a value the same way, at the same place.

Parameters:

- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: How a value is written. Left out, it is written as the axis the series is read by writes its values, and where that says nothing in the theme's language, short from ten thousand on. In a stack that stands as shares, it is given a value's share, and left out the share is written as a share of a hundred.
- `position: ChartDataLabelPosition`: Where on its bar a value is written. A point of a line has its label over it, or under it where it has no room over it, whatever this says.
- `total: Boolean`: Whether what a stack of the series comes to at each place is written past its end: over the stack where it comes to nought or more, and under it where it comes to less. It is written as `format` says, but in a stack that stands as shares in the theme's language, for it is no share. One series of the stack asking for it is enough.

### ChartState

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartState(hidden: Set<String> = emptySet())
```

What a reader has done to a chart: the series they have put out of sight from its legend, and the place a pointer, a finger or the keys are on.

A chart keeps one for itself. A screen that wants to know either, or to say them, makes its own with `rememberChartState` and gives it to the chart. Two charts given the same state are one to their reader: a series hidden in the one is hidden in the other, and the place pointed at in the one is marked in both, where both have it.

A chart with axes that is given a `zoom` keeps the part of its places that is in view here too, as `window`: two such charts given the same state are looked at closer together. A Gantt chart keeps the part of its time there, and a scatter chart the part of its values across in `window` and up its side in `valueWindow`.

To a pie its slices are what its series are to a chart with axes: a slice is put out of sight by its key, and the slice that is pointed at is the selection whose `x` is that key.

In a scatter chart the point that is pointed at is the selection whose `series` is the key of its series and whose `x` is its place among that series' rows, counted from nought.

Parameters:

- `hidden: Set<String>`: the keys of the series that are out of sight to begin with.

Members:

- `hidden: Set<String>`: The keys of the series that are not drawn: what the legend's entries turn on and off.
- `selection: ChartSelection?`: The place that is pointed at, and the tooltip is shown for: null while none is. A pointer over the chart, a finger on it and the arrow keys set it; a pointer that leaves, and Escape, clear it.
- `window: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>`: The part of the chart's places that is in view, from a share of the way along them to another: `0f..1f`, the whole of them, unless the chart is looked at closer. A chart with axes that is given a `zoom` lets its reader change it; a screen changes it with `zoomTo` and `resetZoom`.
- `zoomed: Boolean`: Whether a part of the chart's places, or of its values, is in view, and not all of them.
- `fun toggle(series: String)`: Puts the series with the key `series` out of sight where it is drawn, and back where it is not.
- `fun zoomTo(start: Float, end: Float)`: Brings the part of the places from `start` to `end` into view, each a share of the way along them from nought to one: `zoomTo(0.5f, 1f)` shows the later half. The two are taken in order and kept within the whole, and a part narrower than a thousandth of it is widened to that.
- `fun resetZoom()`: Shows all the places, and all the values, again.
- `valueWindow: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>`: The part of the chart's values that is in view up its side, from a share of the way up them to another: `0f..1f`, all of them, unless the chart is looked at closer. Only a scatter chart given a `zoom` looks closer at its values up its side; a screen changes the part with `zoomValuesTo` and `resetZoom`.
- `fun zoomValuesTo(start: Float, end: Float)`: Brings the part of the values up the chart's side from `start` to `end` into view, each a share of the way up them from nought to one: `zoomValuesTo(0f, 0.5f)` shows the lower half. The two are taken as `zoomTo` takes its two.

### ChartPoint

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartPoint`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class ChartPoint(
    public val series: String,
    public val name: String,
    public val x: Any,
    public val label: String,
    public val value: Double,
    public val text: String,
    public val color: Color,
    public val from: Double? = null,
    public val high: Double? = null,
    public val low: Double? = null
)
```

A value of a chart, as it is handed to what a screen does with one: a press on it, a tooltip of the screen's own.

A slice of a pie is handed over as one too: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its share of the whole after it.

So is a point of a scatter chart: its `x` is its place among its series' rows, counted from nought, its `label` what the point is called, or its series' name where it is called nothing, and its `value` its value up the chart.

So is a cell of a heatmap: its `x` is its datum's place among the chart's data, counted from nought, its `label` its column as the chart writes it and its `name` its row; it is of no series, and its `series` is empty.

And a tile of a treemap: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its share of the whole after it.

A range is handed over as its higher value, with its lower as `from`, and its `text` is the two with a dash between them. A step of a waterfall is what the step adds, with the level it starts from as `from`; its `text` has the step's sign. A total of a waterfall is what it comes to. A candle is handed over as its close, with its opening as `from` and the two ends of its wick as `high` and `low`; its `text` is the four, each called by what it is.

What a stack comes to at a place, which a tooltip of the place writes after the stack's values, is handed to the tooltip's own content as one too: it is of no series, and its `series` is empty; its name is the theme's word for a total, its `value` the sum of the stack's values and its colour unspecified. In a stack that stands as shares, a value's `text` has its share after it.

Parameters:

- `series: String`: The key of the series the value is of.
- `name: String`: The name of that series.
- `x: Any`: Where the value stands, as the series' rows name it.
- `label: String`: That place as the chart writes it.
- `value: Double`: The value.
- `text: String`: The value as the chart writes it.
- `color: Color`: The colour the series is drawn in, and for a step of a waterfall the colour of the way it goes.
- `from: Double?`: Where the value's mark starts, for a value that is drawn neither from nought nor on a stack: the lower value of a range, the level a step of a waterfall starts from, and the opening of a candle. Null for any other value.
- `high: Double?`: The highest a candle reached. Null for any other value.
- `low: Double?`: The lowest a candle reached. Null for any other value.

# Gauge

One value on a scale: it is read by how much of an arc it fills. A speed, a load, the used share of a quota: a measure read against its least and its most.

The scale turns clockwise along three quarters of a turn: `min` at the lower left, `max` at the lower right; both are written under the ends. The value fills the arc from where the scale begins up to itself, and is written in the middle of the gauge.

- `PantrixGauge` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge`, `com.pantrixui:components`): One reading on a scale, as an arc filled up to it or a needle that points at it, with ranges of the scale in colours of their own and the reading said to a screen reader with the range it is in. Keywords: dial, meter, speedometer, kpi, needle, arc.

## Features

- **Scale.** `min` and `max` are the ends of the scale. A value past an end stands at that end and is written as it is. A gauge with no value (`null`) shows only its scale.
- **Ranges.** `segments` gives parts of the scale a colour and a name: the range that is fine, the range that is too much. Each `GaugeSegment` says where it ends (`upTo`); the first begins where the scale does, the others where the one before ends. The arc fills in the colour of the range the value has reached; the ranges themselves stay under it in their faint colours.
- **Needle.** With `needle` a hand reaches from the middle to the value, and the value is written under it. In a gauge with both a needle and ranges the ranges are drawn in their full colours and the arc is not filled: the hand is read against them.
- **Writing.** `format` says how the value and the two ends of the scale are written; left out, they are written as numbers in the theme's language. `center` puts your own content in place of the value's writing.
- **Screen reader.** The gauge is one thing: its `description`, then the value as it is written and, where it has one, the name of the range it is in.
- **Size and motion.** The gauge is as wide as the room it is given and as tall as the chart's style says; the arc is the largest that fits there. When the value changes the arc and the hand go to the new value; where the system asks for reduced motion they do not go, they are there.
- **Direction.** The scale turns the same way in a language read from right to left too.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** `Gauge_<tagKey>`.

## Usage

### A reading on a scale

```kotlin
PantrixGauge(
    value = usedGigabytes,
    max = 50,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" },
    description = stringResource(Res.string.storage_used),
    tagKey = "storage"
)
```

### A needle read against ranges

```kotlin
PantrixGauge(
    value = load,
    segments = listOf(
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, name = normal),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 85, name = high),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 100, name = critical)
    ),
    needle = true,
    description = stringResource(Res.string.processor_load),
    tagKey = "load"
)
```

## Examples

### A value on a scale

At its plainest: a value and the end of the scale. Thirty-two gigabytes of a storage of fifty are used; `format` writes the value and the two ends of the scale with their unit.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge

PantrixGauge(
    value = 32,
    max = 50,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" },
    description = "Storage used",
    tagKey = "plain"
)
```

### Ranges

The scale has three ranges: normal up to sixty, high up to eighty-five, critical after that. The arc fills in the colour of the range the value has reached; the ranges show under it in their faint colours.

Choose a value: the arc goes there and its colour changes with the range it has reached. A screen reader says the range's name after the value too: "72%, High". `format` writes the value in the theme's language (`PantrixTheme.strings.percent`).

The ranges name their own colours here: the theme's success, warning and danger colours. A range that is given no colour takes the theme's next chart colour; those colours carry no meaning.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.GaugeSegment
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var load by remember { mutableStateOf(72) }
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = loadReadings(),
    selected = load,
    onSelect = { load = it },
    fullWidth = false,
    tagKey = "gauge_load"
)
PantrixGauge(
    value = load,
    segments = loadRanges(),
    format = { strings.percent(it / 100) },
    description = "Processor load",
    tagKey = "segments"
)

@Composable
private fun loadRanges(): List<GaugeSegment> {
    val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
    return listOf(
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, color = colors.success.color, name = "Normal"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 85, color = colors.warning.color, name = "High"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 100, color = colors.danger.color, name = "Critical")
    )
}

@Composable
private fun loadReadings(): List<SegmentOption<Int>> {
    val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
    return listOf(40 to "low", 72 to "high", 93 to "critical").map { (load, key) ->
        SegmentOption(value = load, label = strings.percent(load / 100.0), tagKey = key)
    }
}
```

### A needle

A gauge with a needle: a hand reaches from the middle to the value, and the value is written under it. The ranges are drawn in their full colours and the arc is not filled: the hand is read against them.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
```

### A scale that does not start at nought

A gauge with a needle and no ranges: the arc fills up to the value and the hand points at it too. A scale need not start at nought: this thermometer goes from twenty below to forty.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixGauge(
    value = 7.5,
    min = -20,
    max = 40,
    needle = true,
    format = { "${strings.decimal(it, fractionDigits = 1)}°" },
    description = "Outside temperature",
    tagKey = "below_zero"
)
```

### Your own content in the middle

`center` puts your own content in place of the value's writing: here the unit under the value. The content fits the room the arc leaves in its middle.

A screen reader hears the value from the gauge itself (`description` and `format`); what is written in the middle is for the eye.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixGauge(
    value = 86,
    max = 120,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} km/h" },
    center = {
        Column(horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally) {
            PantrixText(text = "86", style = PantrixTheme.typography.headline)
            PantrixText(text = "km/h", color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary)
        }
    },
    description = "Speed",
    tagKey = "own_center"
)
```

### Your own sizes

A gauge's own sizes: a thinner arc (`gaugeWidth`) and a lower gauge (`height`). No gap between the ranges (`sliceGap`). A field that is not given stays the theme's.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.GaugeSegment
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixGauge(
    value = 54,
    segments = loadRanges(),
    format = { strings.percent(it / 100) },
    description = "Processor load",
    style = ChartStyle(gaugeWidth = 8.dp, height = 160.dp, sliceGap = 0.dp),
    tagKey = "own_look"
)

@Composable
private fun loadRanges(): List<GaugeSegment> {
    val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
    return listOf(
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, color = colors.success.color, name = "Normal"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 85, color = colors.warning.color, name = "High"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 100, color = colors.danger.color, name = "Critical")
    )
}
```

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The value in the middle is written in the file too; content put there by `center` is not in the file.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixGauge(
    value = 32,
    max = 50,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" },
    description = "Storage used",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "storage") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixGauge

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.PantrixGauge`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixGauge(
    value: Number?,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    min: Number = 0,
    max: Number = 100,
    segments: List<GaugeSegment> = emptyList(),
    needle: Boolean = false,
    format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    center: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    description: String? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A gauge: one reading on a scale, as how far round an arc it reaches. A speed, a load, a share of a quota: a value that is read against the least and the most it can be.

The scale runs clockwise round three quarters of a turn, from `min` at the lower left to `max` at the lower right, with both written under its ends. The `value` fills the arc from where the scale begins up to itself, and is written in the middle of the gauge; a value past an end of the scale stands at that end, and is written as it is.

**Segments.** `segments` give stretches of the scale a colour and a name: the range that is fine, the range that is too much. The arc is then drawn in the colour of the segment the value has reached, over the segments themselves in a faint shade of their own colours.

**A needle.** With `needle` a hand points at the value from the middle of the gauge, as on a dial, and the value is written under it, between the arc's two ends. A gauge with a needle and segments shows the segments in their full colours and no filled arc: the hand is read against them.

**To a screen reader** the gauge is one thing: its `description`, then the value as it is written, and the name of the segment it is in where the segment has one.

**Its size.** The gauge is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as the chart's style says unless its modifier gives it a height; the arc is the largest that has room in that, in the middle of it. A change of the value moves the arc and the hand to it, unless the system asks for reduced motion.

The scale runs the same way in a language read from the right: a dial is no line of text.

```kotlin
PantrixGauge(
    value = 72,
    segments = listOf(
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, name = "Normal"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 85, name = "High"),
        GaugeSegment(upTo = 100, name = "Critical")
    ),
    format = { "${it.toInt()}%" },
    description = "Processor load",
    tagKey = "load"
)
```

Parameters:

- `value: Number?`: the reading. `null`, and what is no number, is no reading: the gauge shows its scale and nothing on it.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the gauge's modifier. A height here is the gauge's.
- `min: Number`: where the scale begins.
- `max: Number`: where the scale ends: more than `min`.
- `segments: List<GaugeSegment>`: the stretches of the scale that have a colour and a name, in the order they lie along it; each ends past where the one before it does. None, and the arc is drawn in the first of the chart's colours.
- `needle: Boolean`: whether a hand points at the value.
- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: how a value is written: the reading, and the two ends of the scale. Left out, they are written as numbers in the theme's language.
- `center: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands in the gauge in place of the reading as it is written: the reading with a unit under it, an icon. It has the room the arc leaves in its middle, or the room between the arc's two ends where the gauge has a needle.
- `description: String?`: what the gauge measures, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the gauge.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this gauge's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this gauge's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the gauge's automation key: the gauge is `Gauge_<tagKey>`.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. What stands in the middle, `center`, is not in the file; the reading the gauge writes there of itself is.

### GaugeSegment

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gauge.GaugeSegment`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class GaugeSegment(
    public val upTo: Number,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val name: String? = null,
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

A stretch of a `PantrixGauge`'s scale that has a colour and a name of its own: the range in which a reading is fine, the one in which it is high.

```kotlin
GaugeSegment(upTo = 60, name = "Normal")
```

The segments of a gauge are given in the order they lie along its scale: the first begins where the scale does, and each of the others where the one before it ends.

Two are the same segment where everything they were built from is the same; a whole number and the same number with a fraction of nought are one value.

Parameters:

- `upTo: Number`: Where the segment ends: a reading up to this value, the value itself with it, is the segment's.
- `color: Color`: The colour the segment is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the gauge's segments.
- `name: String?`: What a reading in the segment is called, which a screen reader says after the reading: "Normal", "High". Left out, the reading is said by itself.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture the segment is drawn with besides its colour, and the filled arc while it reaches into the segment. Left out, none, and where the gauge's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the segments: none for the first.

### ChartStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val lineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val selectedMarkerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gridWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val labelGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tickSpacing: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val legendGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val legendItemGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val swatchSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val swatchGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipHorizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipVerticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipElevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barRadius: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sliceGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val selectedSliceOffset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gaugeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val meterHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val trackerHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val bubbleMinSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val bubbleMaxSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val navigatorHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barBandShare: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val markLineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markBandAlpha: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val patterns: Boolean? = null,
    public val nodeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val nodeGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ChartStyle>
```

A chart's geometry: how tall it is where nothing says, how thick its lines and how large its marks are, and the room between its parts; and whether its fills have textures besides their colours.

A chart is as tall on a phone as leaves room for what is around it, and taller in a window with room to spare. Under a finger its values' lines stand a little further apart than under a pointer.

The rooms between the parts follow the density, the gaps between bars and between slices among them. The height, the widths of the lines, the sizes of the marks and of the bubbles, a bar's width and corners, how far a pointed slice stands out, how thick a gauge's arc is, how tall a meter's bar, a tracker's blocks and a navigator's strip are, and the tooltip's corners and shadow do not: a chart's lines are as thick in a dense layout as in a roomy one.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: How tall a chart's plot is, with its axes, where the chart's modifier gives it no height. A legend above or under the plot adds its own.
- `lineWidth: Dp`: The width of a series' line.
- `markerSize: Dp`: The width and height of the mark on a point.
- `selectedMarkerSize: Dp`: The same of the mark on the point that is pointed at.
- `gridWidth: Dp`: The width of the grid's lines, of the lines along the axes and of the line that marks the place pointed at. Zero draws none.
- `labelGap: Dp`: Between the plot and what is written beside it and under it, and between that and an axis' title.
- `tickSpacing: Dp`: The least room between two values marked along the axis of values: what decides how many are marked where the axis does not say.
- `legendGap: Dp`: Between the legend and the chart it stands beside.
- `legendItemGap: Dp`: Between one entry of the legend and the next.
- `swatchSize: Dp`: How wide the sample of a series is in the legend and in the tooltip: a short run of its line, or a patch of its fill.
- `swatchGap: Dp`: Between that sample and the name after it.
- `tooltipShape: ShapeSpec`: The tooltip's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `tooltipHorizontalPadding: Dp`: Between the tooltip's sides and what it holds.
- `tooltipVerticalPadding: Dp`: Between its top and bottom and what it holds, and between its heading and rows.
- `tooltipGap: Dp`: Between the place pointed at and the tooltip beside it.
- `tooltipElevation: Dp`: The tooltip's shadow.
- `barGap: Dp`: Between two bars that stand side by side at a place. Bars too thin for it stand closer.
- `barMaxWidth: Dp`: The widest a bar is, however much room its place has: a chart of three places is not three slabs.
- `barRadius: Dp`: How round the corners of a bar's end are, the end away from nought.
- `sliceGap: Dp`: Between two slices of a pie that lie side by side, the same from the pie's middle to its rim.
- `selectedSliceOffset: Dp`: How far the slice of a pie that is pointed at stands out past the pie's rim. The pie keeps this much room about itself, so that the slice has where to stand.
- `gaugeWidth: Dp`: How thick the arc of a gauge is. An arc is no thicker than half its radius.
- `meterHeight: Dp`: How tall the bar of a meter group is.
- `trackerHeight: Dp`: How tall the blocks of a status tracker are.
- `bubbleMinSize: Dp`: How far across the smallest bubble of a scatter chart is: a point whose size is nothing, or too little to be seen as an area, is still a point.
- `bubbleMaxSize: Dp`: How far across its largest bubble is: the one whose size is the most of the chart's.
- `navigatorHeight: Dp`: How tall the strip under a chart's plot is, on which the part of the chart that is in view is marked and moved, in a chart whose zoom has one: how wide, beside a plot whose places go down its side.
- `barBandShare: Float`: How much of a place's band its bars take, more than nought and one at the most: the rest is the room between one place's bars and the next's. Bars are no wider than `barMaxWidth` all the same.
- `markLineWidth: Dp`: The width of a mark's line: a target, a limit, a day. Zero draws none, and the mark's words are written all the same.
- `markBandAlpha: Float`: How much of its colour a mark's band is drawn in, from nought to one: a band lies behind the series, and is a tint.
- `patterns: Boolean?`: Whether the fills of a chart's series, slices and tiles are drawn with textures besides their colours, and its lines broken in turn (`ChartPattern`): what tells them apart for a reader who cannot tell the colours apart. Left out, as the system is set: on where it is set to tell things apart without colour, iOS's "Differentiate Without Color" and Android's colour correction, and off otherwise.
- `nodeWidth: Dp`: How wide a node of a sankey is.
- `nodeGap: Dp`: Between two nodes of a column of a sankey.

### ChartColors

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartColors`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class ChartColors(
    public val series: List<Color> = emptyList(),
    public val grid: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val axis: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val label: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val crosshair: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipContainer: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipBorder: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipText: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipLabel: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val rising: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val falling: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

What a chart is painted with, for a chart that does not take the theme's colours: a colour that is set is used, and one that is left out stays the theme's.

```kotlin
// A chart in the brand's two colours, whatever the theme's chart colours are:
PantrixChart(series = series, colors = ChartColors(series = listOf(brand, accent)))
```

A chart has no fill of its own: it is drawn on what it stands on. On the theme's own grounds its lines and its words are the theme's. On a fill, which gives what stands on it a colour, the theme's are not known to read: the words are written in that colour and the lines drawn in a share of it. The colours of the series are drawn as they are given wherever the chart stands, and on a fill it is the caller who knows which read there.

Parameters:

- `series: List<Color>`: The colours the series are drawn in, in the order they are handed out, for the series that name none of their own. Empty, they are the theme's chart colours.
- `grid: Color`: The lines drawn across the chart at the marks of an axis. The theme's `divider`.
- `axis: Color`: The line along an axis. The theme's `border`.
- `label: Color`: What is written beside the axes: the values, the places and the axes' titles, and the names in the legend. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `crosshair: Color`: The line that marks the place pointed at. The theme's `borderHover`: stronger than the grid it crosses, and quieter than the series it stands behind.
- `tooltipContainer: Color`: The tooltip's fill. The theme's `surface`.
- `tooltipBorder: Color`: The tooltip's edge. The theme's `border`.
- `tooltipText: Color`: The tooltip's heading and its values. The theme's `textPrimary`.
- `tooltipLabel: Color`: The names of the series in the tooltip. The theme's `textSecondary`.
- `rising: Color`: What a value that goes up is drawn in: a step of a waterfall that adds. The theme's `success`.
- `falling: Color`: What a value that goes down is drawn in: a step of a waterfall that takes away. The theme's `danger`.

# Progress Circle

A ring that fills as a piece of work goes on: how much of an upload has gone, how many steps of a set-up are behind, how much of a quota is used. It shows a share of a whole whose end is known; for work whose end is not known there is the spinner.

- `PantrixProgressCircle` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle`, `com.pantrixui:components`): A ring that fills clockwise as a known amount of work gets done, with room in its middle for the share or an icon, read by a screen reader as a progress bar. Keywords: circular progress, progress ring, determinate progress, completion, percent.

## Features

- **Value.** The ring starts at twelve o'clock and fills clockwise by `value` over `max`; a faint ring shows the whole. A value under nought is nought, and one past `max` is the whole.
- **Middle.** `content` stands in the middle of the ring: the share as a number, an icon.
- **Colour.** The ring is drawn in `color`, or else in the content colour of where it stands (as on a filled card), or else in the primary colour; its track is a faint share of the same colour (unless `trackColor` says otherwise).
- **Sizes.** `ProgressCircleStyle` gives the ring's size and thickness; a size on the modifier is the ring's too.
- **Motion.** When the value changes the ring goes to the new value; where the system asks for reduced motion it does not go, it is there.
- **Screen reader.** It is a progress bar whose name is `contentDescription` and which says the share it has reached. A number written in its middle is read too; it is better hidden from the screen reader, which already hears the share.
- **Direction.** The ring fills clockwise in a language read from right to left too.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** `ProgressCircle_<tagKey>`.

## Usage

### A share of a whole

```kotlin
PantrixProgressCircle(value = upload.sent, max = upload.size, contentDescription = stringResource(Res.string.uploading))
```

### With the share written in its middle

```kotlin
PantrixProgressCircle(
    value = done,
    max = steps,
    contentDescription = stringResource(Res.string.setup),
    style = ProgressCircleStyle(size = 72.dp, strokeWidth = 8.dp),
    tagKey = "setup"
) {
    PantrixText(text = "$done/$steps", modifier = Modifier.clearAndSetSemantics { })
}
```

## Examples

### A share of a whole

At its plainest: a piece of work seventy-two per cent done. `max` is a hundred where it is not given.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle.PantrixProgressCircle

PantrixProgressCircle(value = 72, contentDescription = "Uploaded", tagKey = "plain")
```

### With its share in the middle

The share is written in the middle of the ring and changes with the buttons: the ring goes to the new value. The writing in the middle is hidden from the screen reader (`clearAndSetSemantics`): the ring itself says the share.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf

import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.clearAndSetSemantics
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle.PantrixProgressCircle
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle.ProgressCircleStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton

import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

Row(
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
) {
    PantrixProgressCircle(
        value = done,
        max = 8,
        contentDescription = "Set-up",
        style = ProgressCircleStyle(size = 72.dp, strokeWidth = 8.dp),
        tagKey = "share"
    ) {
        PantrixText(text = "$done/8", modifier = Modifier.clearAndSetSemantics { })
    }
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Back",
        onClick = { done = (done - 1).coerceAtLeast(0) },
        variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
        tagKey = "progress_back"
    )
    PantrixButton(text = "Next", onClick = { done = (done + 1).coerceAtMost(8) }, tagKey = "progress_next")
}
```

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file draws the ring as far as it is filled; what stands in it by `content` is not in the file. `export` comes before `content`: the trailing lambda is still what stands in the middle.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle.PantrixProgressCircle
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixProgressCircle(
    value = 72,
    contentDescription = "Uploaded",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "uploaded") { file = it }
) {
    PantrixText(text = PantrixTheme.strings.percent(0.72), style = PantrixTheme.typography.caption)
}
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixProgressCircle

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle.PantrixProgressCircle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixProgressCircle(
    value: Number,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    max: Number = 100,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    trackColor: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    style: ProgressCircleStyle? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    content: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null
)
```

A ring that fills as something gets done: how much of an upload has gone, how many steps of a set-up are behind, how much of a quota is used. It shows a share of a whole that is known; for work whose end is not known there is the spinner.

The ring fills clockwise from twelve o'clock, `value` of `max` of the way round, over a faint ring that shows the whole. A value under nought is nought, and one over `max` is the whole. What is given as `content` stands in the middle of the ring: the share as a number, an icon.

It is drawn in `color`, or else the content colour of where it stands, as on a filled card, or the primary colour; its track is a faint share of the same colour unless `trackColor` says otherwise. A change of the value moves the ring to it, unless the system asks for reduced motion.

**To a screen reader** it is a progress bar with `contentDescription` for its name and the share it has reached. What stands in its middle is read too, as whatever it is: a number written there is better hidden from the screen reader, which has the share already.

The ring fills the same way in a language read from the right, as a clock's hand goes.

```kotlin
PantrixProgressCircle(value = 72, contentDescription = "Uploaded") {
    PantrixText(text = "72%", style = PantrixTheme.typography.caption)
}
```

Parameters:

- `value: Number`: how much is done, between nought and `max`. What is no number counts as nought.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the circle's modifier. A size here is the circle's.
- `max: Number`: how much the whole is: more than nought.
- `color: Color`: the colour of the ring.
- `trackColor: Color`: the colour of the ring's track, the whole it fills.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what is progressing, in a word or two, for a screen reader.
- `style: ProgressCircleStyle?`: this circle's own geometry: its size and how thick its ring is.
- `tagKey: String?`: the circle's automation key: the circle is `ProgressCircle_<tagKey>`.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the circle out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over it makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, it has no such button. What stands in the circle, `content`, is not in the file. It comes before `content`, which stays last.
- `content: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what stands in the middle of the ring. It has the room inside the ring.

### ProgressCircleStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.progresscircle.ProgressCircleStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ProgressCircleStyle(
    public val size: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val strokeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ProgressCircleStyle>
```

`PantrixProgressCircle`'s geometry.

The circle is a mark and not room between things: neither of its sizes follows the density.

Parameters:

- `size: Dp`: The circle's width and height: 56dp on every platform, unless a brand or a theme sets another.
- `strokeWidth: Dp`: How thick the ring is: 6dp. A ring is no thicker than a quarter of its circle.

# Meter Group

Several amounts of one whole, side by side on one bar: what a storage is filled with, where a budget goes. The parts are read against each other and against what is left.

The bar is as long as `max`. Each `MeterItem` takes as much of the bar as its value; the parts are set out in order from the start of the line, each drawn in the theme's next chart colour unless it names its own. What no part takes shows the bar's track.

- `PantrixMeterGroup` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.metergroup`, `com.pantrixui:components`): Several amounts of one whole, side by side on one bar, with a legend that writes each amount beside its colour. Keywords: stacked progress, usage bar, storage bar, segmented bar, quota.

## Features

- **Values.** A part's value is counted in what `max` is counted in. A part with no value, or one that is not over nought, takes none of the bar, and its name stays in the legend. What the parts come to past `max` is cut off at the bar's end.
- **Legend.** It writes each part's name, then its value, beside its colour. It stands above the bar or under it: a legend at the start counts as above, one at the end as under. Its entries are no switches here: the bar shows what it is given.
- **Writing.** `format` says how a value is written in the legend; left out, it is written as a number in the theme's language.
- **Screen reader.** The bar is a picture with its `description`; the legend's entries say the parts. A bar with no legend says its parts itself.
- **Direction.** In a language read from right to left the first part stands at the right.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** `MeterGroup_<tagKey>`; the bar `.Bar`, the legend's entries `.Legend_<the part's key>`.

## Usage

### What a whole is filled with

```kotlin
PantrixMeterGroup(
    items = usage.map { MeterItem(it.id, it.name, it.gigabytes) },
    max = capacity,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" },
    description = stringResource(Res.string.storage),
    tagKey = "storage"
)
```

### With its legend above it

```kotlin
PantrixMeterGroup(
    items = spending.map { MeterItem(it.id, it.name, it.share) },
    legend = ChartLegend(position = ChartLegendPosition.Top, alignment = ChartLegendAlignment.Start),
    tagKey = "budget"
)
```

## Examples

### What fills a whole

At its plainest: four things that fill a storage of sixty-four gigabytes. The end of the bar that is not filled shows the room that is left; the legend writes each part with its value.

```kotlin
)
```
