## API

### PantrixMeterGroup

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.metergroup.PantrixMeterGroup`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixMeterGroup(
    items: List<MeterItem>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    max: Number = 100,
    format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    description: String? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A meter group: several amounts of one whole, side by side on one bar. What a storage is filled with, how a budget is spent: the parts are read against each other and against what is left.

The bar is as long as `max`. Each of the `items` takes as much of it as its value, one after the other from where lines start, in the theme's chart colour for its place unless it names its own; what no item takes shows the bar's track. What the items come to past `max` is cut off at the bar's end.

The `legend` writes each item's name with its value after it, beside a patch of its colour. It stands above the bar or under it: a legend at the start is above, and one at the end under. Its entries are no switches here: a meter group shows what it is given.

**To a screen reader** the bar is a picture with its `description`, and the legend's entries say the items. A group with no legend says the items with the bar.

In a language read from the right the first item stands at the right.

```kotlin
PantrixMeterGroup(
    items = listOf(
        MeterItem("apps", "Apps", 16),
        MeterItem("photos", "Photos", 24),
        MeterItem("system", "System", 10)
    ),
    max = 64,
    format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" },
    description = "Storage",
    tagKey = "storage"
)
```

Parameters:

- `items: List<MeterItem>`: the amounts, in the order they lie on the bar. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the group's modifier.
- `max: Number`: how much the whole bar is: more than nought.
- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: how a value is written in the legend. Left out, it is written as a number in the theme's language.
- `legend: ChartLegend?`: where the names of the items stand, above the bar or under it. `null` shows none.
- `description: String?`: what the bar measures, in a few words, for a screen reader.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this group's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this group's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the group's automation key: the group is `MeterGroup_<tagKey>`, its bar `MeterGroup_<tagKey>.Bar` and the legend's entry of an item `MeterGroup_<tagKey>.Legend_<item's key>`.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The legend stands under the bar in the file.

### MeterItem

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.metergroup.MeterItem`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class MeterItem(
    public val key: String,
    public val name: String,
    public val value: Number?,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

One of the amounts a `PantrixMeterGroup` sets side by side on its bar.

```kotlin
MeterItem("photos", "Photos", 24)
```

Two are the same item where everything they were built from is the same; a whole number and the same number with a fraction of nought are one value.

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What tells the item from the others of its group, and stays the same while its value changes. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.
- `name: String`: What the item is called, in the legend and to a screen reader.
- `value: Number?`: How much of the bar the item takes, counted in what the bar's `max` is counted in. An item whose value is no number, or is not over nought, takes none of it, and keeps its name in the legend.
- `color: Color`: The colour the item is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the group's items.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture the item is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the group's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the items: none for the first.

### ChartLegend

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartLegend`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class ChartLegend(
    public val position: ChartLegendPosition = ChartLegendPosition.Bottom,
    public val alignment: ChartLegendAlignment = ChartLegendAlignment.Center,
    public val toggles: Boolean = true,
    public val always: Boolean = false
)
```

A chart's legend: where the names of its series stand, each beside a sample of how the series is drawn.

A chart of one series has no legend: what the one line is belongs in the words around the chart. `always` gives it one all the same.

An entry is a switch for its series. Pressed, it takes the series out of the chart, and the chart is drawn for the series that are left; pressed again, it brings the series back. The entry stays, drawn faint, so that what was taken out can be brought back. A screen reader hears each entry as a switch, with the series' name and whether it is on.

Parameters:

- `position: ChartLegendPosition`: Which side of the chart the legend stands on. Above and under it the entries stand in a row, on as many lines as they need; beside it they stand under each other.
- `alignment: ChartLegendAlignment`: Where in the room it has the legend stands: along the chart's width above and under it, and from the chart's top beside it.
- `toggles: Boolean`: Whether pressing an entry takes its series out of the chart and brings it back.
- `always: Boolean`: Whether a chart of one series has a legend too.

### ChartStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val lineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val selectedMarkerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gridWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val labelGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tickSpacing: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val legendGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val legendItemGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val swatchSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val swatchGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipHorizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipVerticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipElevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barRadius: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sliceGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val selectedSliceOffset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gaugeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val meterHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val trackerHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val bubbleMinSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val bubbleMaxSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val navigatorHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barBandShare: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val markLineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markBandAlpha: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val patterns: Boolean? = null,
    public val nodeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val nodeGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ChartStyle>
```

A chart's geometry: how tall it is where nothing says, how thick its lines and how large its marks are, and the room between its parts; and whether its fills have textures besides their colours.

A chart is as tall on a phone as leaves room for what is around it, and taller in a window with room to spare. Under a finger its values' lines stand a little further apart than under a pointer.

The rooms between the parts follow the density, the gaps between bars and between slices among them. The height, the widths of the lines, the sizes of the marks and of the bubbles, a bar's width and corners, how far a pointed slice stands out, how thick a gauge's arc is, how tall a meter's bar, a tracker's blocks and a navigator's strip are, and the tooltip's corners and shadow do not: a chart's lines are as thick in a dense layout as in a roomy one.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: How tall a chart's plot is, with its axes, where the chart's modifier gives it no height. A legend above or under the plot adds its own.
- `lineWidth: Dp`: The width of a series' line.
- `markerSize: Dp`: The width and height of the mark on a point.
- `selectedMarkerSize: Dp`: The same of the mark on the point that is pointed at.
- `gridWidth: Dp`: The width of the grid's lines, of the lines along the axes and of the line that marks the place pointed at. Zero draws none.
- `labelGap: Dp`: Between the plot and what is written beside it and under it, and between that and an axis' title.
- `tickSpacing: Dp`: The least room between two values marked along the axis of values: what decides how many are marked where the axis does not say.
- `legendGap: Dp`: Between the legend and the chart it stands beside.
- `legendItemGap: Dp`: Between one entry of the legend and the next.
- `swatchSize: Dp`: How wide the sample of a series is in the legend and in the tooltip: a short run of its line, or a patch of its fill.
- `swatchGap: Dp`: Between that sample and the name after it.
- `tooltipShape: ShapeSpec`: The tooltip's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `tooltipHorizontalPadding: Dp`: Between the tooltip's sides and what it holds.
- `tooltipVerticalPadding: Dp`: Between its top and bottom and what it holds, and between its heading and rows.
- `tooltipGap: Dp`: Between the place pointed at and the tooltip beside it.
- `tooltipElevation: Dp`: The tooltip's shadow.
- `barGap: Dp`: Between two bars that stand side by side at a place. Bars too thin for it stand closer.
- `barMaxWidth: Dp`: The widest a bar is, however much room its place has: a chart of three places is not three slabs.
- `barRadius: Dp`: How round the corners of a bar's end are, the end away from nought.
- `sliceGap: Dp`: Between two slices of a pie that lie side by side, the same from the pie's middle to its rim.
- `selectedSliceOffset: Dp`: How far the slice of a pie that is pointed at stands out past the pie's rim. The pie keeps this much room about itself, so that the slice has where to stand.
- `gaugeWidth: Dp`: How thick the arc of a gauge is. An arc is no thicker than half its radius.
- `meterHeight: Dp`: How tall the bar of a meter group is.
- `trackerHeight: Dp`: How tall the blocks of a status tracker are.
- `bubbleMinSize: Dp`: How far across the smallest bubble of a scatter chart is: a point whose size is nothing, or too little to be seen as an area, is still a point.
- `bubbleMaxSize: Dp`: How far across its largest bubble is: the one whose size is the most of the chart's.
- `navigatorHeight: Dp`: How tall the strip under a chart's plot is, on which the part of the chart that is in view is marked and moved, in a chart whose zoom has one: how wide, beside a plot whose places go down its side.
- `barBandShare: Float`: How much of a place's band its bars take, more than nought and one at the most: the rest is the room between one place's bars and the next's. Bars are no wider than `barMaxWidth` all the same.
- `markLineWidth: Dp`: The width of a mark's line: a target, a limit, a day. Zero draws none, and the mark's words are written all the same.
- `markBandAlpha: Float`: How much of its colour a mark's band is drawn in, from nought to one: a band lies behind the series, and is a tint.
- `patterns: Boolean?`: Whether the fills of a chart's series, slices and tiles are drawn with textures besides their colours, and its lines broken in turn (`ChartPattern`): what tells them apart for a reader who cannot tell the colours apart. Left out, as the system is set: on where it is set to tell things apart without colour, iOS's "Differentiate Without Color" and Android's colour correction, and off otherwise.
- `nodeWidth: Dp`: How wide a node of a sankey is.
- `nodeGap: Dp`: Between two nodes of a column of a sankey.

# Status Tracker

A run of steps as a row of blocks: each block in the colour of what was the case at that step. The days a service was up, the builds that passed: where the bad ones are is seen at a glance, and which they are is read by going over them.

Each `StatusBlock` is a name and a colour. The blocks are set side by side from the start of the line, each with an even share of the width. A block that is given no colour is drawn in the colour of the chart's grid: a step of which nothing is known.

- `PantrixStatusTracker` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker`, `com.pantrixui:components`): A run of steps as a row of coloured blocks, with the name of the block that is pointed at written under it, reachable by keys and by a screen reader. Keywords: uptime, status bar, health history, timeline blocks, incident history.

## Features

- **The block pointed at.** The name of the block under the pointer, or of the one that is touched, is written under the row beside its colour; the others are drawn faint. With a finger, another touch on the block that is pointed at lets go of it.
- **The line under the row.** With `caption` off the name is not written. The line's room is kept whether a block is pointed at or not: the row does not move.
- **Keyboard.** The row is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from block to block and stop at the ends, Home and End go to the first and the last block, Escape lets go, Enter and Space press the block that is pointed at.
- **Pressing.** `onSelect` gives the place of the block that is pressed, counted from nought.
- **State.** The block that is pointed at is kept in `ChartState`, as a selection whose `x` is the block's place.
- **Screen reader.** The row says its `description`, then each block by its name. A row of more than two hundred blocks is told by its description alone.
- **Direction.** In a language read from right to left the first block stands at the right, and the arrows go the way they point.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** `StatusTracker_<tagKey>`; the row `.Blocks`, the blocks `.Block_<number>`, the line under the row `.Caption`.

## Usage

### The days a service was up

```kotlin
PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = days.map { StatusBlock(it.summary, colorOf(it.status)) },
    description = stringResource(Res.string.uptime_last_thirty_days),
    tagKey = "uptime"
)
```

### Opening a step when its block is pressed

```kotlin
PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = builds.map { StatusBlock(it.title, colorOf(it.result)) },
    caption = false,
    onSelect = { openBuild(builds[it]) },
    tagKey = "builds"
)
```

## Examples

### The days of a service

The last thirty days of a service: up on the green days, slow on the yellow ones, down on the red one; the grey day has no record.

Move the pointer over a block, or touch it: the day's name is written under the row and the other days fade. On the keyboard the arrows go from day to day.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.PantrixStatusTracker
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.StatusBlock
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = uptimeDays(),
    description = "Status of the last thirty days",
    tagKey = "plain"
)

@Composable
private fun uptimeDays(): List<StatusBlock> {
    val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
    return List(30) { index ->
        val day = "Day ${index + 1}"
        when (index) {
            7, 21 -> StatusBlock("$day: Slow", colors.warning.color)
            13 -> StatusBlock("$day: Outage", colors.danger.color)
            26 -> StatusBlock("$day: No record")
            else -> StatusBlock("$day: No problems", colors.success.color)
        }
    }
}
```

### Pressing a block

`onSelect` gives the place of the block that is pressed: press a day, or go to one with the keyboard and press Enter, and the line under the card writes what was pressed. The line of the name under the row is off here (`caption = false`).

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.PantrixStatusTracker
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.StatusBlock
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
val days = uptimeDays()
PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = days,
    caption = false,
    description = "Status of the last thirty days",
    onSelect = { report(days[it].name) },
    tagKey = "pressed"
)

@Composable
private fun uptimeDays(): List<StatusBlock> {
    val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
    return List(30) { index ->
        val day = "Day ${index + 1}"
        when (index) {
            7, 21 -> StatusBlock("$day: Slow", colors.warning.color)
            13 -> StatusBlock("$day: Outage", colors.danger.color)
            26 -> StatusBlock("$day: No record")
            else -> StatusBlock("$day: No problems", colors.success.color)
        }
    }
}
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### Your own sizes

A row's own sizes: taller blocks (`trackerHeight`), wider gaps between them (`barGap`) and sharp corners (`barRadius`). A field that is not given stays the theme's.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.PantrixStatusTracker
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.StatusBlock
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = uptimeDays().take(14),
    description = "Status of the last two weeks",
    style = ChartStyle(trackerHeight = 48.dp, barGap = 6.dp, barRadius = 0.dp),
    tagKey = "own_look"
)

@Composable
private fun uptimeDays(): List<StatusBlock> {
    val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
    return List(30) { index ->
        val day = "Day ${index + 1}"
        when (index) {
            7, 21 -> StatusBlock("$day: Slow", colors.warning.color)
            13 -> StatusBlock("$day: Outage", colors.danger.color)
            26 -> StatusBlock("$day: No record")
            else -> StatusBlock("$day: No problems", colors.success.color)
        }
    }
}
```

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the row of blocks; the line under it, which names the block that is pointed at, is not in it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.PantrixStatusTracker
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.StatusBlock
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = uptimeDays(),
    description = "Status of the last thirty days",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "last-thirty-days") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

@Composable
private fun uptimeDays(): List<StatusBlock> {
    val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
    return List(30) { index ->
        val day = "Day ${index + 1}"
        when (index) {
            7, 21 -> StatusBlock("$day: Slow", colors.warning.color)
            13 -> StatusBlock("$day: Outage", colors.danger.color)
            26 -> StatusBlock("$day: No record")
            else -> StatusBlock("$day: No problems", colors.success.color)
        }
    }
}
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixStatusTracker

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.PantrixStatusTracker`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks: List<StatusBlock>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    caption: Boolean = true,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A status tracker: a run of steps as a row of blocks, each in the colour of what was the case at it. The days a service was up, the builds that passed: where the bad ones are is seen at a glance, and which they were is read by pointing at them.

The `blocks` stand side by side from where lines start, each as wide as an even share of the row. The name of the block that is pointed at is written under the row, beside a patch of its colour, unless `caption` says otherwise; with a block pointed at, the others are drawn faint.

**Pointing at a block.** A pointer over a block points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the block it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the row is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from block to block, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The block is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is its place counted from nought. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the row is its `description`, then each block by its name, in the blocks' order. A row of more than two hundred blocks is told by its description alone.

In a language read from the right the first block stands at the right, and the arrows go the way they point.

```kotlin
PantrixStatusTracker(
    blocks = days.map { StatusBlock("${it.date}: ${it.status}", colorOf(it.status)) },
    description = "Uptime, last thirty days",
    tagKey = "uptime"
)
```

Parameters:

- `blocks: List<StatusBlock>`: the blocks, in the order they are read.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the tracker's modifier.
- `caption: Boolean`: whether the name of the block that is pointed at is written under the row. The line's room is kept whether a block is pointed at or not, so that the row does not move.
- `state: ChartState`: what the reader points at: the tracker's own where none is given.
- `description: String?`: what the row shows, in a few words, for a screen reader.
- `onSelect: ((Int) -> Unit)?`: called with the place of the block that is pressed, counted from nought.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this tracker's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this tracker's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the tracker's automation key: the tracker is `StatusTracker_<tagKey>`, its row `StatusTracker_<tagKey>.Blocks`, a block `StatusTracker_<tagKey>.Block_<number>` counted from one and the line under the row `StatusTracker_<tagKey>.Caption`. A press on a block is reported as a `StatusTracker` `select` event with the block's number. Nothing of the names is reported.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The line under the row is not in it.

### StatusBlock

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.statustracker.StatusBlock`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class StatusBlock(
    public val name: String,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

One block of a `PantrixStatusTracker`: what was the case at one step of a run, as a colour and a few words.

```kotlin
StatusBlock("12 October: operational", color = PantrixTheme.colors.success.color)
```

Two are the same block where their names and their colours are.

Parameters:

- `name: String`: What the block stands for, in words: its step and what was the case at it. Written under the row when the block is pointed at, and said to a screen reader.
- `color: Color`: The colour of the block. Left out, the block is in the colour of a chart's grid: a step of which nothing is known.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture the block is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the tracker's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), the turn of its colour among the row's colours, in the order they first come: a status is one texture, as it is one colour, and the first status none.

### ChartState

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartState`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartState(hidden: Set<String> = emptySet())
```

What a reader has done to a chart: the series they have put out of sight from its legend, and the place a pointer, a finger or the keys are on.

A chart keeps one for itself. A screen that wants to know either, or to say them, makes its own with `rememberChartState` and gives it to the chart. Two charts given the same state are one to their reader: a series hidden in the one is hidden in the other, and the place pointed at in the one is marked in both, where both have it.

A chart with axes that is given a `zoom` keeps the part of its places that is in view here too, as `window`: two such charts given the same state are looked at closer together. A Gantt chart keeps the part of its time there, and a scatter chart the part of its values across in `window` and up its side in `valueWindow`.

To a pie its slices are what its series are to a chart with axes: a slice is put out of sight by its key, and the slice that is pointed at is the selection whose `x` is that key.

In a scatter chart the point that is pointed at is the selection whose `series` is the key of its series and whose `x` is its place among that series' rows, counted from nought.

Parameters:

- `hidden: Set<String>`: the keys of the series that are out of sight to begin with.

Members:

- `hidden: Set<String>`: The keys of the series that are not drawn: what the legend's entries turn on and off.
- `selection: ChartSelection?`: The place that is pointed at, and the tooltip is shown for: null while none is. A pointer over the chart, a finger on it and the arrow keys set it; a pointer that leaves, and Escape, clear it.
- `window: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>`: The part of the chart's places that is in view, from a share of the way along them to another: `0f..1f`, the whole of them, unless the chart is looked at closer. A chart with axes that is given a `zoom` lets its reader change it; a screen changes it with `zoomTo` and `resetZoom`.
- `zoomed: Boolean`: Whether a part of the chart's places, or of its values, is in view, and not all of them.
- `fun toggle(series: String)`: Puts the series with the key `series` out of sight where it is drawn, and back where it is not.
- `fun zoomTo(start: Float, end: Float)`: Brings the part of the places from `start` to `end` into view, each a share of the way along them from nought to one: `zoomTo(0.5f, 1f)` shows the later half. The two are taken in order and kept within the whole, and a part narrower than a thousandth of it is widened to that.
- `fun resetZoom()`: Shows all the places, and all the values, again.
- `valueWindow: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>`: The part of the chart's values that is in view up its side, from a share of the way up them to another: `0f..1f`, all of them, unless the chart is looked at closer. Only a scatter chart given a `zoom` looks closer at its values up its side; a screen changes the part with `zoomValuesTo` and `resetZoom`.
- `fun zoomValuesTo(start: Float, end: Float)`: Brings the part of the values up the chart's side from `start` to `end` into view, each a share of the way up them from nought to one: `zoomValuesTo(0f, 0.5f)` shows the lower half. The two are taken as `zoomTo` takes its two.

# Sparkline

The run of a number in the room of a word: it stands beside the number it belongs to. It has no axes, no legend and nothing to point at: it shows which way the number has gone, and a chart shows the rest.

- `PantrixSparkline` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline`, `com.pantrixui:components`): The run of a number in the room of a word, as a line, an area or bars, with no axes and nothing to point at. Keywords: mini chart, inline chart, trend line, microchart, word-sized chart.

## Features

- **Values.** The values are set out at even steps from the start of the line to its end. A line and an area are drawn between the least and the most of the values: the run fills the height it has. Bars are drawn from nought.
- **Ends.** `min` is the value at the foot of the height and `max` the one at its top: several runs read on one scale. A value past the ends is cut off at the box's edge. An end not given comes from the values and the reference line.
- **Curve.** `curve` says how a line and an area go from one value to the next (`ChartCurve`): straight, rounded without going past the values, or in steps. Bars have no curve.
- **Last value.** `markLast = true` marks the last value: a dot on a line and an area, and on bars the last bar in full colour and the others fainter. The last value is the last one that is a number.
- **Reference line.** `reference` draws a dashed line behind the values, in the colour charts write in: a target, or where the run began.
- **Style.** `style` goes over the theme's sizes: the line's width (`lineWidth`), the gap between bars (`barGap`), the last value's dot (`markerSize`) and the reference line's width (`markLineWidth`).
- **Kind.** `SparklineKind.Line` is a line, `Area` a line faintly filled under it, `Bar` a bar for each value.
- **A missing value.** A value that is `null`, or no number, is a gap in a line and an empty place among bars.
- **Size and colour.** It is 96dp wide and 32dp tall unless the modifier says otherwise; it is drawn in `color`, or else in the theme's first chart colour.
- **Screen reader.** With a `contentDescription` it is a picture of that name; with none it is not read at all: that suits a run beside a number that says the same.
- **Direction.** In a language read from right to left the first value stands at the right.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** `Sparkline_<tagKey>`.

## Usage

### Beside the number it belongs to

```kotlin
Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    PantrixText(text = total, style = PantrixTheme.typography.title)
    PantrixSparkline(values = lastThirtyDays, contentDescription = null)
}
```

### A rounded line with its last value and a target

```kotlin
PantrixSparkline(
    values = temperatures,
    curve = ChartCurve.Smooth,
    markLast = true,
    reference = 20,
    contentDescription = stringResource(Res.string.temperature_today)
)
```

### Bars, for amounts that are counted from nought

```kotlin
PantrixSparkline(
    values = ordersByDay,
    kind = SparklineKind.Bar,
    contentDescription = stringResource(Res.string.orders_this_week),
    tagKey = "orders"
)
```

## Examples

### Beside a number

At its plainest: beside a number, the run of that number over the last twelve weeks. Since the number and its name are written beside it, the run has nothing more to say to a screen reader (`contentDescription = null`).

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.PantrixSparkline
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
Row(
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.lg),
    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
) {
    Column {
        PantrixText(text = "Visits", color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary)
        PantrixText(text = strings.decimal(SPARK_VISITS.last()), style = PantrixTheme.typography.title)
    }
    PantrixSparkline(values = SPARK_VISITS, tagKey = "plain")
}

private val SPARK_VISITS = listOf(8200, 8650, 8400, 9100, 9800, 9300, 10400, 10100, 11200, 11800, 11500, 12480)
```

### Missing values and under nought

The weeks with no measure (`null`) are a gap in the line; a single value with none before it and none after it is a dot. The bars of values under nought go down from nought.

### Your own size and colour

The modifier gives the size, `color` the colour: a rising run in the success colour, a falling one in the danger colour, in a wider room.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue

import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.PantrixSparkline
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.SparklineKind
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val colors = PantrixTheme.colors
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.lg)) {
    PantrixSparkline(
        values = SPARK_VISITS,
        modifier = Modifier.size(160.dp, 48.dp),
        kind = SparklineKind.Area,
        color = colors.success.color,
        contentDescription = "Rising visits",
        tagKey = "up"
    )
    PantrixSparkline(
        values = SPARK_VISITS.reversed(),
        modifier = Modifier.size(160.dp, 48.dp),
        kind = SparklineKind.Area,
        color = colors.danger.color,
        contentDescription = "Falling visits",
        tagKey = "down"
    )

private val SPARK_VISITS = listOf(8200, 8650, 8400, 9100, 9800, 9300, 10400, 10100, 11200, 11800, 11500, 12480)
```

### Curve, last value and target

`curve` says how the line goes from one value to the next: `Smooth` rounds it without going past the values, `StepAfter` holds each value until the next. `markLast = true` marks the last value with a dot; on bars the last bar is drawn in full colour and the others fainter. `reference` draws a dashed line behind: here 20 degrees for the temperature, and the daily target for the orders.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartCurve
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.PantrixSparkline
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.SparklineKind
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.lg)) {
    PantrixSparkline(
        values = SPARK_TEMPERATURE,
        contentDescription = "Today's temperature",
        tagKey = "smooth",
        curve = ChartCurve.Smooth,
        markLast = true,
        reference = 20
    )
    PantrixSparkline(
        values = SPARK_TEMPERATURE,
        contentDescription = "Today's temperature, in steps",
        tagKey = "steps",
        curve = ChartCurve.StepAfter,
        markLast = true
    )
    PantrixSparkline(
        values = SPARK_ORDERS,
        kind = SparklineKind.Bar,
        contentDescription = "This week's orders",
        tagKey = "orders",
        markLast = true,
        reference = 40
    )
}

private val SPARK_TEMPERATURE = listOf(12.5, 11.8, 13.2, 16.4, 19.8, 22.6, 24.1, 23.4, 21.0, 18.2, 16.9, 15.7)

private val SPARK_ORDERS = listOf(32, 45, 38, 51, 29, 47, 43)
```

### A shared scale and your own style

`min` and `max` give the ends of the height: two servers' processor use on one scale, from nought to a hundred. One is barely working, the other is full; with no ends given each would stand between its own least and most value, and both would look as high. The dashed line in both is the warning threshold at eighty percent (`reference`). `style` makes the line thicker and the last value's dot larger.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.width
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.PantrixSparkline
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val style = ChartStyle(lineWidth = 3.dp, markerSize = 10.dp)
val servers = listOf(Triple("Server A", SPARK_QUIET, "quiet"), Triple("Server B", SPARK_BUSY, "busy"))
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
    servers.forEach { (name, load, key) ->
        Row(
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
            verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
        ) {
            PantrixText(text = name, modifier = Modifier.width(80.dp))
            PantrixSparkline(
                values = load,
                modifier = Modifier.size(160.dp, 40.dp),
                contentDescription = "$name, processor use",
                tagKey = key,
                style = style,
                markLast = true,
                reference = 80,
                min = 0,
                max = 100
            )
            PantrixText(text = PantrixTheme.strings.percent(load.last() / 100.0))
        }
    }
}

private val SPARK_QUIET = listOf(12, 18, 15, 22, 19, 14, 25, 21, 17, 23)

private val SPARK_BUSY = listOf(71, 78, 84, 80, 92, 88, 95, 99, 90, 86)
```

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

A small line is exported too: the button stands over the line, and the file is the line alone.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.PantrixSparkline

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixSparkline(
    values = SPARK_VISITS,
    contentDescription = "Visits of the last twelve days",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "visits") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

private val SPARK_VISITS = listOf(8200, 8650, 8400, 9100, 9800, 9300, 10400, 10100, 11200, 11800, 11500, 12480)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixSparkline

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.PantrixSparkline`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSparkline(
    values: List<Number?>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    kind: SparklineKind = SparklineKind.Line,
    color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    contentDescription: String? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    curve: ChartCurve = ChartCurve.Linear,
    markLast: Boolean = false,
    reference: Number? = null,
    min: Number? = null,
    max: Number? = null
)
```

A sparkline: the run of a number in the room of a word, beside the number it belongs to. It has no axes, no legend and nothing to point at: it shows which way the number has gone, and a chart shows the rest.

The `values` are set out at even steps from where lines start to where they end. Its height goes from `min` up to `max`; where they are not given, a line and an area go from the least of the values to the most, so that the run fills the height it has, and bars from nought, or from the least of them where it is under nought. A `reference` line is taken in too. A value past an end that is given is cut off at the box's edge. A value that is `null`, or no number, is a gap in a line and a place with no bar.

It is 96dp wide and 32dp tall unless its modifier says otherwise, and is drawn in `color` or in the first of the theme's chart colours, as thick as the `style`'s `lineWidth`. In a language read from the right its first value stands at the right.

**To a screen reader** it is a picture with `contentDescription` for its name; with none it is not there at all, which suits a sparkline beside a number that says the same.

```kotlin
PantrixSparkline(values = visits, contentDescription = "Visits, last thirty days")
PantrixSparkline(values = temperature, curve = ChartCurve.Smooth, markLast = true, reference = 20)
```

Parameters:

- `values: List<Number?>`: the values, in the order they are read.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the sparkline's modifier. A size here is the sparkline's.
- `kind: SparklineKind`: whether the values are a line, an area or bars.
- `color: Color`: the colour it is drawn in.
- `contentDescription: String?`: what the run is of, in a few words, for a screen reader. `null` leaves it out of what a screen reader reads.
- `tagKey: String?`: the sparkline's automation key: the sparkline is `Sparkline_<tagKey>`.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: the sizes it is drawn in over the theme's: the line's width (`lineWidth`), the gap between two bars (`barGap`), the mark of the last value (`markerSize`) and the reference line's width (`markLineWidth`).
- `curve: ChartCurve`: how a line or an area goes from one value to the next. Bars have none.
- `markLast: Boolean`: whether the last value is marked: a dot on a line or an area, as large as the style's `markerSize`, and on bars the last one in `color` and the rest in a quieter share of it. The last value is the last that is a number.
- `reference: Number?`: a value a dashed line is drawn across the sparkline at, behind its values, in the colour charts write in: a target, or where the run began. `null` draws none.
- `min: Number?`: the value at the sparkline's foot, or `null` for the least of its values. A number, and less than `max`.
- `max: Number?`: the value at its top, or `null` for the most of them.

### SparklineKind

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sparkline.SparklineKind`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SparklineKind
```

How a `PantrixSparkline` draws its values.

Entries:

- `Line`: A line through the values.
- `Area`: A line through the values, with what is under it filled in a faint share of its colour.
- `Bar`: A bar for each value, up from nought or down from it.

# Scatter Chart

Points set out by two values: one along the chart, the other up it. It shows how two things go together: do sales rise with the temperature, does what costs more rate higher too. Give each point a size by a third value and it is a bubble chart.

The chart is given its series; each `ScatterSeries` carries its own rows: where a row stands along the chart (`x`), where up it (`y`) and, for bubbles, how large it is (`size`). Both axes are of values: each goes from a round number under its values to one over them, and marks the round values between.

- `PantrixScatterChart` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter`, `com.pantrixui:components`): Points set out by two values, and bubbles sized by a third, with two axes of values, lines and bands to read them by, a legend that takes series out and brings them back, a tooltip for the point pointed at, and every point reachable by keys and by a screen reader. Keywords: scatter plot, bubble chart, xy chart, correlation, point cloud.

## Features

- **Bubbles.** The points of a series that is given `size` are bubbles. A bubble's area is as much as its size is of the largest size in the chart: twice the value, twice the area. How large the smallest and the largest bubble are is in the chart's style (`bubbleMinSize`, `bubbleMaxSize`). A chart with bubbles keeps room for the largest at the ends of its axes.
- **A point's name.** `label` says what a point is called: a country, a product. It is the tooltip's heading and what a screen reader says.
- **Axes.** `xAxis` and `yAxis` are the `ChartAxis` of a chart with places: title, format, ends, grid lines. The titles are what the values are called in the tooltip. `sizeAxis` says what the size is called (`title`), how it is written (`format`) and the value the largest bubble stands for (`max`); nothing of it is drawn.
- **Marks.** `marks` draws a line at a value or a band between two; here a mark's `x` is a value of the axis along the chart.
- **The point pointed at.** The point under the pointer, or near it, or touched by a finger, is pointed at: a ring about it, two lines through it and the tooltip that writes its values. Of points that lie on one another, the smallest is pointed at.
- **Keyboard.** The chart is one stop for Tab: the right and left arrows go along the chart between the points of a series, the up and down arrows to the series before and after, Home and End to the series' first and last point, Escape lets go, Enter and Space press the point that is pointed at.
- **State and pressing.** The point that is pointed at is kept in `ChartState`, as a selection whose `x` is the row's place in its series and whose `series` is the series' key. `onSelect` gives the pressed point with the same place.
- **Screen reader.** The chart says its `description`, then each point, series by series, with its name and its values. A chart of more than two hundred points is told by its description alone.
- **Direction.** In a language read from right to left the values along the chart start from the right, and those up it are written at the right.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Zoom.** With `zoom` the reader looks closer at both values at once: a wheel (with Ctrl or Command), two fingers, the plus and minus keys and the buttons look closer; a drag moves what is in view every way.
- **Automation.** `ScatterChart_<tagKey>`; the plot is `.Plot`, the points `.Point_<series>_<number>`, the legend's entries `.Legend_<series>`, the tooltip `.Tooltip`.

## Usage

### Two groups of points

```kotlin
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("trial", stringResource(Res.string.trial), trial, x = { it.dose }, y = { it.response }),
        ScatterSeries("control", stringResource(Res.string.control), control, x = { it.dose }, y = { it.response })
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = stringResource(Res.string.dose)),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = stringResource(Res.string.response)),
    tagKey = "study"
)
```

### Bubbles, each called by its name, with a line at the average

```kotlin
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries(
            key = "countries",
            name = stringResource(Res.string.countries),
            data = countries,
            x = { it.income },
            y = { it.lifeExpectancy },
            size = { it.population },
            label = { it.name }
        )
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = stringResource(Res.string.income), format = { strings.compact(it) }),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = stringResource(Res.string.life_expectancy)),
    sizeAxis = ChartAxis(title = stringResource(Res.string.population), format = { strings.compact(it) }),
    marks = listOf(ChartReferenceLine(y = 72, label = stringResource(Res.string.world_average))),
    legend = null,
    tagKey = "countries"
)
```

## Examples

### Two values, two groups

Fifty days of a café: the day's temperature and the cold drinks sold that day. Weekdays and weekends are separate series; the points go up with the temperature, and the weekends higher still.

Move the pointer near a point, or touch one: the tooltip writes the day's two values under the titles of the axes. Pressing an entry of the legend takes that series out of the chart.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries

PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("weekdays", "Weekdays", cafeDays(weekend = false), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold }),
        ScatterSeries("weekend", "Weekend", cafeDays(weekend = true), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold })
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Temperature (°C)"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Cold drinks"),
    description = "Cold drinks sold by temperature",
    tagKey = "plain"
)

internal fun cafeDays(weekend: Boolean): List<CafeDay> = List(50) { it }
    .filter { (it % 7 >= 5) == weekend }
    .map { day ->
        val heat = 12.0 + (day * 7 % 19) + (day % 4) * 0.5
        val wobble = (day * 37 % 29) - 14
        val busy = if (weekend) 45 else 0
        CafeDay(
            heat = heat,
            sold = (heat * 6.5 - 40 + wobble + busy).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            hot = (190 - heat * 4.5 + wobble).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            food = 85 + wobble + busy / 3
        )
    }

internal class CafeDay(
    val heat: Double,
    val sold: Int,
    val hot: Int,
    val food: Int
)
```

### Bubbles

The products of a shop: price, rating and, as the bubble's size, how many were sold in the month. Each point goes by the product's name (`label`); `sizeAxis` says what the size is.

The area grows with the value: the bubble of a product that sold twice as many takes twice the area, not twice the width. Bubbles are drawn half transparent, so that one under another shows through.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries(
            key = "products",
            name = "Products",
            data = shopProducts(),
            x = { it.price },
            y = { it.rating },
            size = { it.sold },
            label = { it.name }
        )
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Price", format = { "${strings.decimal(it)} ₺" }),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Rating", min = 3.0, max = 5.0),
    sizeAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Sales", format = { "${strings.decimal(it)} sold" }),
    description = "Price, rating and sales of the products",
    tagKey = "bubbles"
)

internal fun shopProducts(): List<ShopProduct> = listOf(
    ShopProduct("Headset", 1450.0, 4.6, 820),
    ShopProduct("Keyboard", 980.0, 4.3, 540),
    ShopProduct("Mouse", 420.0, 4.4, 1260),
    ShopProduct("Monitor", 5200.0, 4.7, 310),
    ShopProduct("Webcam", 760.0, 3.9, 280),
    ShopProduct("Speaker", 1890.0, 4.1, 190),
    ShopProduct("Microphone", 2350.0, 4.5, 150),
    ShopProduct("Charger", 310.0, 4.0, 1640),
    ShopProduct("Cable", 120.0, 3.6, 2100),
    ShopProduct("Tablet pen", 1150.0, 4.2, 95),
    ShopProduct("Laptop stand", 640.0, 4.8, 470),
    ShopProduct("External disk", 2780.0, 4.4, 360)
)

internal class ShopProduct(
    val name: String,
    val price: Double,
    val rating: Double,
    val sold: Int
)
```

### Lines and bands

Marks that help read the points: a line at the average temperature, a line at the day's target, and a band over the hottest days. A mark's `x` is here not the name of a place but a value of the axis along the chart.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartReferenceBand
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartReferenceLine
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries

PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("days", "Days", cafeDays(weekend = false), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold })
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Temperature (°C)"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Cold drinks"),
    marks = listOf(
        ChartReferenceBand(x1 = 28, label = "Hot days"),
        ChartReferenceLine(y = 150, label = "Target"),
        ChartReferenceLine(x = 21, label = "Average")
    ),
    description = "Cold drinks sold by temperature, with the target",
    tagKey = "marks"
)

internal fun cafeDays(weekend: Boolean): List<CafeDay> = List(50) { it }
    .filter { (it % 7 >= 5) == weekend }
    .map { day ->
        val heat = 12.0 + (day * 7 % 19) + (day % 4) * 0.5
        val wobble = (day * 37 % 29) - 14
        val busy = if (weekend) 45 else 0
        CafeDay(
            heat = heat,
            sold = (heat * 6.5 - 40 + wobble + busy).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            hot = (190 - heat * 4.5 + wobble).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            food = 85 + wobble + busy / 3
        )
    }

internal class CafeDay(
    val heat: Double,
    val sold: Int,
    val hot: Int,
    val food: Int
)
```

### Telling series apart by shape

Series are told apart by shape as well as by colour: each is drawn with its own mark (`marker`). It reads for someone who cannot tell the colours apart, and on a black and white print.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartMarker
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries

val days = cafeDays(weekend = false)
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("cold", "Cold drinks", days, x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold }),
        ScatterSeries("hot", "Hot drinks", days, x = { it.heat }, y = { it.hot }, marker = ChartMarker.Square),
        ScatterSeries("food", "Food", days, x = { it.heat }, y = { it.food }, marker = ChartMarker.Triangle)
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Temperature (°C)"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Sales"),
    description = "Sales of three groups of products by temperature",
    tagKey = "markers"
)

internal fun cafeDays(weekend: Boolean): List<CafeDay> = List(50) { it }
    .filter { (it % 7 >= 5) == weekend }
    .map { day ->
        val heat = 12.0 + (day * 7 % 19) + (day % 4) * 0.5
        val wobble = (day * 37 % 29) - 14
        val busy = if (weekend) 45 else 0
        CafeDay(
            heat = heat,
            sold = (heat * 6.5 - 40 + wobble + busy).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            hot = (190 - heat * 4.5 + wobble).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            food = 85 + wobble + busy / 3
        )
    }

internal class CafeDay(
    val heat: Double,
    val sold: Int,
    val hot: Int,
    val food: Int
)
```

### Pressing a point

`onSelect` gives the point that is pressed: its `x` is the row's place in its series, its `label` the point's name. Press a bubble, or go to one with the keyboard and press Enter, and the line under the card writes the product that was pressed.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries

val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
val products = shopProducts()
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries(
            key = "products",
            name = "Products",
            data = products,
            x = { it.price },
            y = { it.rating },
            size = { it.sold },
            label = { it.name }
        )
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Price"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Rating", min = 3.0, max = 5.0),
    sizeAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Sales"),
    onSelect = { point -> report("${point.label}: ${products[point.x as Int].sold} sold") },
    description = "Price, rating and sales of the products",
    tagKey = "pressed"
)

internal fun shopProducts(): List<ShopProduct> = listOf(
    ShopProduct("Headset", 1450.0, 4.6, 820),
    ShopProduct("Keyboard", 980.0, 4.3, 540),
    ShopProduct("Mouse", 420.0, 4.4, 1260),
    ShopProduct("Monitor", 5200.0, 4.7, 310),
    ShopProduct("Webcam", 760.0, 3.9, 280),
    ShopProduct("Speaker", 1890.0, 4.1, 190),
    ShopProduct("Microphone", 2350.0, 4.5, 150),
    ShopProduct("Charger", 310.0, 4.0, 1640),
    ShopProduct("Cable", 120.0, 3.6, 2100),
    ShopProduct("Tablet pen", 1150.0, 4.2, 95),
    ShopProduct("Laptop stand", 640.0, 4.8, 470),
    ShopProduct("External disk", 2780.0, 4.4, 360)
)

internal class ShopProduct(
    val name: String,
    val price: Double,
    val rating: Double,
    val sold: Int
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the axes, the points and the legend under them; the point that is pointed at and its tooltip are not in it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("weekdays", "Weekdays", cafeDays(weekend = false), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold }),
        ScatterSeries("weekend", "Weekend", cafeDays(weekend = true), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold })
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Temperature (°C)"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Cold drinks"),
    description = "Cold drinks sold by temperature",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "cold-drinks") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

internal fun cafeDays(weekend: Boolean): List<CafeDay> = List(50) { it }
    .filter { (it % 7 >= 5) == weekend }
    .map { day ->
        val heat = 12.0 + (day * 7 % 19) + (day % 4) * 0.5
        val wobble = (day * 37 % 29) - 14
        val busy = if (weekend) 45 else 0
        CafeDay(
            heat = heat,
            sold = (heat * 6.5 - 40 + wobble + busy).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            hot = (190 - heat * 4.5 + wobble).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            food = 85 + wobble + busy / 3
        )
    }

internal class CafeDay(
    val heat: Double,
    val sold: Int,
    val hot: Int,
    val food: Int
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

### Looking closer

`zoom = ChartZoom()` lets the reader look closer at both values at once: a wheel with Ctrl or Command and two fingers look closer about the point between them, plus and minus on the chart about the point that is pointed at, and the buttons about the middle. A drag of the mouse moves what is in view every way; the point the arrows go to comes into view.

Both axes are marked anew for the values in view, and what lies past the plot's edges is cut off. The part across is `state.window`, the part up `state.valueWindow`.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartAxis
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartZoom
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.PantrixScatterChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.scatter.ScatterSeries

PantrixScatterChart(
    series = listOf(
        ScatterSeries("weekdays", "Weekdays", cafeDays(weekend = false), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold }),
        ScatterSeries("weekend", "Weekend", cafeDays(weekend = true), x = { it.heat }, y = { it.sold })
    ),
    xAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Temperature (°C)"),
    yAxis = ChartAxis(title = "Cold drinks"),
    description = "Cold drinks sold by temperature",
    tagKey = "zoomed",
    zoom = ChartZoom()
)

internal fun cafeDays(weekend: Boolean): List<CafeDay> = List(50) { it }
    .filter { (it % 7 >= 5) == weekend }
    .map { day ->
        val heat = 12.0 + (day * 7 % 19) + (day % 4) * 0.5
        val wobble = (day * 37 % 29) - 14
        val busy = if (weekend) 45 else 0
        CafeDay(
            heat = heat,
            sold = (heat * 6.5 - 40 + wobble + busy).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            hot = (190 - heat * 4.5 + wobble).toInt().coerceAtLeast(4),
            food = 85 + wobble + busy / 3
        )
    }

internal class CafeDay(
    val heat: Double,
    val sold: Int,
    val hot: Int,
    val food: Int
)
```
