### Pressing a tile

`onSelect` gives the tile that is pressed: press a tile, or go to one with the keyboard and press Enter, and the line under the card writes what was pressed. The values are written in a way of their own: in the tiles by `ChartDataLabels(format)`, in the tooltip by `ChartTooltip(format)`.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartDataLabels
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartTooltip
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.treemap.PantrixTreemap
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.treemap.TreemapItem

val report = LocalExampleEvents.current
PantrixTreemap(
    items = diskFolders(),
    labels = ChartDataLabels(format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" }),
    tooltip = ChartTooltip(format = { "${it.toInt()} GB" }),
    onSelect = { tile -> report("${tile.name}: ${tile.text}") },
    description = "The folders that fill the disk",
    tagKey = "pressed"
)

internal fun diskFolders(): List<TreemapItem> = listOf(
    TreemapItem("photos", "Photos", 148),
    TreemapItem("video", "Videos", 96),
    TreemapItem("apps", "Apps", 64),
    TreemapItem("music", "Music", 41),
    TreemapItem("docs", "Documents", 27),
    TreemapItem("mail", "Mail", 14),
    TreemapItem("other", "Other", 9)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `LocalExampleEvents`: Where an example tells its card what happens in it: a button pressed, a row chosen, a dialog closed. The card writes the last thing told under the example, on its "Last event" line.

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the tiles and their names; the tooltip of the tile that is pointed at is not in it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.treemap.PantrixTreemap
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.treemap.TreemapItem

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixTreemap(
    items = diskFolders(),
    description = "The folders that fill the disk",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "disk") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

internal fun diskFolders(): List<TreemapItem> = listOf(
    TreemapItem("photos", "Photos", 148),
    TreemapItem("video", "Videos", 96),
    TreemapItem("apps", "Apps", 64),
    TreemapItem("music", "Music", 41),
    TreemapItem("docs", "Documents", 27),
    TreemapItem("mail", "Mail", 14),
    TreemapItem("other", "Other", 9)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixTreemap

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.treemap.PantrixTreemap`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixTreemap(
    items: List<TreemapItem>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = ChartDataLabels(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    scale: HeatmapScale? = null,
    legend: ChartLegend? = ChartLegend(),
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A treemap: a box cut into tiles, each as large as its value is of the whole. It suits a whole of many parts, where a pie would have too many slices to read: the folders of a disk, a budget by its lines, a market by its companies. What is large is seen at once, and the small parts still have their place.

The chart is given its `items`. Each of them is a tile, or a group whose own items are its tiles: a group's tiles lie together in a block, in the group's colour, with the group's name over them where the block has room for it. The blocks are set out the largest first from where lines start, and in each block its tiles the largest first, every tile as near a square as the cutting lets it be. An item that counts for nothing has no tile.

A tile has its name and its value written in it where it has room for them, in the one of black and white that reads better on its colour; a tile too small for its name has neither, and the `tooltip` and a screen reader still have both.

**Shaded by value.** Given a `scale`, every tile is drawn in the shade of its value along it, as a heatmap's cells are, whatever colour its item or its group names: the larger a tile, the further along the scale, so that two tiles of nearly one size, or of two blocks far apart, are still told apart at a glance. The blocks still lie together under their groups' names, a tile keeps its group's texture, and the `legend` shows the scale with its least and its most.

**Pointing at a tile.** A pointer over a tile points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the tile it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: an arrow goes to the nearest tile the way it points, Home and End to the largest tile and the last, and Escape lets go. The tile is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the item's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each tile with its group, its name, its value and its share of the whole, the largest block first. A chart of more than two hundred tiles is told by its description alone.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says or, given no height, as the chart's style says.

In a language read from the right the largest tile lies at the right.

```kotlin
PantrixTreemap(
    items = listOf(TreemapItem("photos", "Photos", 48), TreemapItem("video", "Video", 31)),
    description = "What fills the disk",
    tagKey = "disk"
)
```

Parameters:

- `items: List<TreemapItem>`: the tiles and the groups of tiles. Their keys tell the tiles apart, and two tiles with one key are refused.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.
- `labels: ChartDataLabels?`: what is written in the tiles: each tile's name, and under it its value, written as `format` says or short where it says nothing. `null` writes nothing in them.
- `tooltip: ChartTooltip?`: what is shown for the tile that is pointed at: its group as the heading, where it lies in one, and under it its name and its value with its share of the whole. A tile has no place to share and no line through it: `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.
- `empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.
- `state: ChartState`: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.
- `description: String?`: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of the items it was given.
- `onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)?`: called with the tile that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its share of the whole after it.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. Two tiles are a `sliceGap` apart, and their corners as round as `barRadius` says.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Treemap_<tagKey>`, its tiles together `Treemap_<tagKey>.Plot`, a tile `Treemap_<tagKey>.Tile_<number>`, counted from one as the tiles are laid out, the scale `Treemap_<tagKey>.Legend` and the tooltip `Treemap_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a tile is reported as a `Treemap` `select` event with the item's key. Nothing of the values is reported.
- `scale: HeatmapScale?`: what shades the tiles by their values, as a heatmap's scale does its cells: where it names no ends, they are the least and the most of the tiles' values. `null`, each tile has its own colour or its group's.
- `legend: ChartLegend?`: where the scale of shades stands, where the treemap has a `scale`: without one there is nothing for it to show. `null` shows none.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button. The scale of shades stands under the tiles in the file.

### TreemapItem

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.treemap.TreemapItem`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class TreemapItem(
    public val key: String,
    public val name: String,
    public val value: Number? = null,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val children: List<TreemapItem> = emptyList(),
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

One item of a `PantrixTreemap`: a tile with a value, or a group of tiles.

```kotlin
TreemapItem("docs", "Documents", 12)
TreemapItem(
    key = "design",
    name = "Design",
    children = listOf(TreemapItem("ui", "Interface", 42), TreemapItem("brand", "Brand", 18))
)
```

An item with no `children` is a tile, as large as its `value` is of all the values. An item with children is a group: its tiles are its children, they lie together under its name, and what it counts for is what they count for together; a value given to a group is not read. A child that has children of its own is one tile, which counts for all of them.

Two items are the same item where everything they were built from is the same.

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What tells the item from the others, and stays the same while its value changes: what a selection names and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.
- `name: String`: What it is called: in its tile, over its group, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.
- `value: Number?`: How much it counts for. An item whose value is no number, or is not over nought, has no tile.
- `color: Color`: The colour it is drawn in. Left out, a tile has its group's colour, and an item the treemap was given the theme's chart colour for its place among them: the first of them for the first.
- `children: List<TreemapItem>`: The tiles of a group.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture it is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, a tile has its group's, and an item the treemap was given none, or where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among them: none for the first.

### HeatmapScale

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.heatmap.HeatmapScale`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class HeatmapScale(
    public val min: Double? = null,
    public val max: Double? = null,
    public val steps: Int = 0,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val low: Color = Color.Unspecified
)
```

How a `PantrixHeatmap` turns a value into a shade: the two ends of its scale, how many shades it has, and its colours. A PantrixTreemap given one shades its tiles by it.

```kotlin
HeatmapScale(min = 0.0, max = 100.0, steps = 5)
HeatmapScale(low = Color(0xFFFFF3B0), color = Color(0xFFB3261E))
```

A cell is drawn in `color`, the more of it the further its value is along the scale: a little of it for the least, and all of it for the most. The colour lies on what the chart stands on, so that a scale reads in a light theme and in a dark one. Given a `low` colour, the scale goes from it to `color` instead: the two are mixed in Oklab, where each step along looks as large as the next, and the least is drawn in `low` itself. Such a scale is the same in a light theme and a dark one: the two colours are the caller's to choose for both. A value under `min` is drawn as the least, and one over `max` as the most.

Two scales are the same where all five are.

Parameters:

- `min: Double?`: The value the lightest shade stands for. Left out, it is the least of the chart's values.
- `max: Double?`: The value the full colour stands for. Left out, it is the most of them.
- `steps: Int`: How many shades the scale has: with five, the scale is cut into five even ranges and every value of a range has that range's shade. Nought, every value has a shade of its own.
- `color: Color`: The colour of the most. Left out, it is the first of the theme's chart colours.
- `low: Color`: The colour of the least. Left out, the least is a little of `color` on what the chart stands on.

### ChartDataLabels

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartDataLabels`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartDataLabels(
    public val format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    public val position: ChartDataLabelPosition = ChartDataLabelPosition.Auto,
    public val total: Boolean = false
)
```

The values of a series written in the chart, each at its mark: over a point of a line, at the end of a bar, and inside a bar of a stack, in the one of black and white that reads better on the bar's colour.

```kotlin
BarSeries("revenue", "Revenue", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.revenue }, labels = ChartDataLabels())
BarSeries("online", "Online", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.online }, stack = "sales",
    labels = ChartDataLabels(position = ChartDataLabelPosition.InsideEnd, total = true))
```

A value has its label where the label has room. Placed by itself, one that would stand on another, or reach out of the chart, is written under its point instead, or inside the end of its bar; where it has no room there either it is left out, as is one that a bar is too small to hold. Placed where its `position` says, it has no other place. The tooltip and the screen reader still have the value. A chart of more than two hundred places writes none.

A line the chart draws to read the values by, through a label, is covered where the label is: the label is written on a plate, of the tooltip's colour past a bar and of the bar's colour inside it.

Its `position` and its `total` are of a chart with axes: a pie and a heatmap write their labels where they do.

Two are the same where they write a value the same way, at the same place.

Parameters:

- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: How a value is written. Left out, it is written as the axis the series is read by writes its values, and where that says nothing in the theme's language, short from ten thousand on. In a stack that stands as shares, it is given a value's share, and left out the share is written as a share of a hundred.
- `position: ChartDataLabelPosition`: Where on its bar a value is written. A point of a line has its label over it, or under it where it has no room over it, whatever this says.
- `total: Boolean`: Whether what a stack of the series comes to at each place is written past its end: over the stack where it comes to nought or more, and under it where it comes to less. It is written as `format` says, but in a stack that stands as shares in the theme's language, for it is no share. One series of the stack asking for it is enough.

### ChartLegend

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartLegend`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
data class ChartLegend(
    public val position: ChartLegendPosition = ChartLegendPosition.Bottom,
    public val alignment: ChartLegendAlignment = ChartLegendAlignment.Center,
    public val toggles: Boolean = true,
    public val always: Boolean = false
)
```

A chart's legend: where the names of its series stand, each beside a sample of how the series is drawn.

A chart of one series has no legend: what the one line is belongs in the words around the chart. `always` gives it one all the same.

An entry is a switch for its series. Pressed, it takes the series out of the chart, and the chart is drawn for the series that are left; pressed again, it brings the series back. The entry stays, drawn faint, so that what was taken out can be brought back. A screen reader hears each entry as a switch, with the series' name and whether it is on.

Parameters:

- `position: ChartLegendPosition`: Which side of the chart the legend stands on. Above and under it the entries stand in a row, on as many lines as they need; beside it they stand under each other.
- `alignment: ChartLegendAlignment`: Where in the room it has the legend stands: along the chart's width above and under it, and from the chart's top beside it.
- `toggles: Boolean`: Whether pressing an entry takes its series out of the chart and brings it back.
- `always: Boolean`: Whether a chart of one series has a legend too.

### ChartTooltip

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartTooltip`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartTooltip(
    public val shared: Boolean = true,
    public val crosshair: Boolean = true,
    public val format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    public val content: (@Composable (points: List<ChartPoint>) -> Unit)? = null
)
```

A chart's tooltip: the values at the place that is pointed at, on a small card beside it.

It comes up under a pointer, where a finger touches the chart or is drawn along it, and at the place the arrow keys have gone to. It goes when the pointer leaves, at a second touch on the place, and at Escape. It stands inside the chart, beside the place and on the side that has room for it. In a chart too narrow to have room on either side it stands over the place, at the end of the plot that the place's values are not at. It takes no press: what is under it is pressed as if it were not there.

`null` in its place shows none. The place pointed at is still marked, and still told to the chart's state.

Parameters:

- `shared: Boolean`: Whether the tooltip is of the place, with the value every series has there, or of the one series nearest the pointer. Together is how a chart is read at a place, and under a finger it asks for no aim; apart suits a chart whose series are read each on its own.
- `crosshair: Boolean`: Whether the place is marked across the chart: by a line through it, and in a chart with bars by a shade over its band.
- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: How a value is written in the tooltip and to a screen reader, where that is not how the axis writes it: a chart with no axis of values says here what its numbers are. Left out, the axis' `format` writes them, and the theme's language where the axis has none.
- `content: (@Composable (points: List<ChartPoint>) -> Unit)?`: The card's own content, in the place of the heading and the rows: given the values at the place, the one pointed at where the series are told apart. The card around it stays the chart's.

### ChartStyle

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartStyle`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartStyle(
    public val height: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val lineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val selectedMarkerSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gridWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val labelGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tickSpacing: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val legendGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val legendItemGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val swatchSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val swatchGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipShape: ShapeSpec = ShapeSpec.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipHorizontalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipVerticalPadding: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val tooltipElevation: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barMaxWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barRadius: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val sliceGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val selectedSliceOffset: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val gaugeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val meterHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val trackerHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val bubbleMinSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val bubbleMaxSize: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val navigatorHeight: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val barBandShare: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val markLineWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val markBandAlpha: Float = Float.NaN,
    public val patterns: Boolean? = null,
    public val nodeWidth: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
    public val nodeGap: Dp = Dp.Unspecified
) : PantrixStyle<ChartStyle>
```

A chart's geometry: how tall it is where nothing says, how thick its lines and how large its marks are, and the room between its parts; and whether its fills have textures besides their colours.

A chart is as tall on a phone as leaves room for what is around it, and taller in a window with room to spare. Under a finger its values' lines stand a little further apart than under a pointer.

The rooms between the parts follow the density, the gaps between bars and between slices among them. The height, the widths of the lines, the sizes of the marks and of the bubbles, a bar's width and corners, how far a pointed slice stands out, how thick a gauge's arc is, how tall a meter's bar, a tracker's blocks and a navigator's strip are, and the tooltip's corners and shadow do not: a chart's lines are as thick in a dense layout as in a roomy one.

Parameters:

- `height: Dp`: How tall a chart's plot is, with its axes, where the chart's modifier gives it no height. A legend above or under the plot adds its own.
- `lineWidth: Dp`: The width of a series' line.
- `markerSize: Dp`: The width and height of the mark on a point.
- `selectedMarkerSize: Dp`: The same of the mark on the point that is pointed at.
- `gridWidth: Dp`: The width of the grid's lines, of the lines along the axes and of the line that marks the place pointed at. Zero draws none.
- `labelGap: Dp`: Between the plot and what is written beside it and under it, and between that and an axis' title.
- `tickSpacing: Dp`: The least room between two values marked along the axis of values: what decides how many are marked where the axis does not say.
- `legendGap: Dp`: Between the legend and the chart it stands beside.
- `legendItemGap: Dp`: Between one entry of the legend and the next.
- `swatchSize: Dp`: How wide the sample of a series is in the legend and in the tooltip: a short run of its line, or a patch of its fill.
- `swatchGap: Dp`: Between that sample and the name after it.
- `tooltipShape: ShapeSpec`: The tooltip's corners: a step of the brand's shape scale, or a fixed shape.
- `tooltipHorizontalPadding: Dp`: Between the tooltip's sides and what it holds.
- `tooltipVerticalPadding: Dp`: Between its top and bottom and what it holds, and between its heading and rows.
- `tooltipGap: Dp`: Between the place pointed at and the tooltip beside it.
- `tooltipElevation: Dp`: The tooltip's shadow.
- `barGap: Dp`: Between two bars that stand side by side at a place. Bars too thin for it stand closer.
- `barMaxWidth: Dp`: The widest a bar is, however much room its place has: a chart of three places is not three slabs.
- `barRadius: Dp`: How round the corners of a bar's end are, the end away from nought.
- `sliceGap: Dp`: Between two slices of a pie that lie side by side, the same from the pie's middle to its rim.
- `selectedSliceOffset: Dp`: How far the slice of a pie that is pointed at stands out past the pie's rim. The pie keeps this much room about itself, so that the slice has where to stand.
- `gaugeWidth: Dp`: How thick the arc of a gauge is. An arc is no thicker than half its radius.
- `meterHeight: Dp`: How tall the bar of a meter group is.
- `trackerHeight: Dp`: How tall the blocks of a status tracker are.
- `bubbleMinSize: Dp`: How far across the smallest bubble of a scatter chart is: a point whose size is nothing, or too little to be seen as an area, is still a point.
- `bubbleMaxSize: Dp`: How far across its largest bubble is: the one whose size is the most of the chart's.
- `navigatorHeight: Dp`: How tall the strip under a chart's plot is, on which the part of the chart that is in view is marked and moved, in a chart whose zoom has one: how wide, beside a plot whose places go down its side.
- `barBandShare: Float`: How much of a place's band its bars take, more than nought and one at the most: the rest is the room between one place's bars and the next's. Bars are no wider than `barMaxWidth` all the same.
- `markLineWidth: Dp`: The width of a mark's line: a target, a limit, a day. Zero draws none, and the mark's words are written all the same.
- `markBandAlpha: Float`: How much of its colour a mark's band is drawn in, from nought to one: a band lies behind the series, and is a tint.
- `patterns: Boolean?`: Whether the fills of a chart's series, slices and tiles are drawn with textures besides their colours, and its lines broken in turn (`ChartPattern`): what tells them apart for a reader who cannot tell the colours apart. Left out, as the system is set: on where it is set to tell things apart without colour, iOS's "Differentiate Without Color" and Android's colour correction, and off otherwise.
- `nodeWidth: Dp`: How wide a node of a sankey is.
- `nodeGap: Dp`: Between two nodes of a column of a sankey.

# Funnel Chart

A chart that shows the stages of a way that fewer and fewer get through: the stages stand one under another, each as wide as the number that reached it. It shows where the others were lost: of those who visited, those who signed up; of those, the ones who tried; of those, the ones who paid.

- `PantrixFunnelChart` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel`, `com.pantrixui:components`): The stages of something that fewer and fewer get through, one under another, each as wide as the number that reached it, with its share of the first, a tooltip for the stage pointed at and every stage reachable by keys and by a screen reader. Keywords: conversion, sales funnel, pipeline, drop off, stages.

## Features

- **Shape.** The largest stage is as wide as the chart; each stage narrows to the width of the one after it, and the stages make one funnel. The last keeps its width. A stage larger than the one before it does not narrow but widens: the chart draws what it is given. `shape = FunnelShape.Bars` draws each stage as a bar as wide as its value; `horizontal` lays the stages side by side from where lines start, each as tall as its value.
- **Words.** A stage's name and value are written in it; beside the value stands its share: of the first stage, of the one before, or both (`rate`). A stage too narrow for its words has its name and value beside it, under it in a horizontal funnel; where there is room for neither, only the name is left. `labels = null` writes nothing.
- **The stage pointed at.** The stage whose row the pointer or a finger is on is ringed, and the tooltip writes its name, its value and its share. On the keyboard the arrows go from stage to stage: up and down, right and left in a horizontal funnel.
- **Colours.** Each stage takes one of the theme's chart colours, by its place; the `color` field of `FunnelStage` gives a stage its own.
- **Screen reader.** First the chart's description, then each stage in its order: its name, its value and its shares. A share of the first stage written alone is read bare; otherwise each share is read with what it is a share of.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** The chart is tagged `Funnel_<tagKey>`, and a stage `Funnel_<tagKey>.Stage_<number>`. A press on a stage is reported as a `select` event with the stage's key.

## Usage

### From a visit to a payment

```kotlin
PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages = listOf(
        FunnelStage("visits", stringResource(Res.string.visits), report.visits),
        FunnelStage("signups", stringResource(Res.string.signups), report.signups),
        FunnelStage("trials", stringResource(Res.string.trials), report.trials),
        FunnelStage("paid", stringResource(Res.string.paid), report.paid)
    ),
    description = stringResource(Res.string.sales_funnel),
    tagKey = "sales"
)
```

### Values written short, and a stage that is pressed

```kotlin
val strings = PantrixTheme.strings
PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages = steps.map { FunnelStage(it.id, it.name, it.count) },
    labels = ChartDataLabels(format = { strings.compact(it) }),
    onSelect = { stage -> openStep(stage.series) },
    tagKey = "checkout"
)
```

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the stages, their values and their rates.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel.FunnelStage
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel.PantrixFunnelChart

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages = FUNNEL_STEPS,
    description = "The stages a visit goes through until it comes to a payment",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "visit-to-payment") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

private val FUNNEL_STEPS = listOf(
    FunnelStage("visits", "Visits", 3000),
    FunnelStage("signups", "Sign-ups", 1240),
    FunnelStage("trials", "Trials", 520),
    FunnelStage("paid", "Paid", 310)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixFunnelChart

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel.PantrixFunnelChart`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages: List<FunnelStage>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    labels: ChartDataLabels? = ChartDataLabels(),
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    shape: FunnelShape = FunnelShape.Funnel,
    horizontal: Boolean = false,
    rate: FunnelRate = FunnelRate.First,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A funnel: the stages of something that fewer and fewer get through, one under another, each as wide as the number that reached it. It shows where the others were lost: the visitors who signed up, the sign-ups who tried, the trials who paid.

The chart is given its `stages`, in the order they follow one another. The largest is as wide as the chart, and each narrows down to the width of the one after it, so that the stages make one funnel; the last keeps its width. A stage that is larger than the one before it widens instead: the funnel draws what it is given. Drawn as `FunnelShape.Bars`, each stage is a bar as wide as it counts for. A `horizontal` funnel lays its stages side by side from where lines start, each as tall as it counts for.

A stage has its name and its value written in it, the value with its shares after it as `rate` says, in the one of black and white that reads better on its colour. A stage too small for them has them beside it, or under it in a horizontal funnel, the name over the value where its column is too narrow for one line; where they have room in none of these places its name is written by itself, and a stage with no room for that has nothing. The `tooltip` and a screen reader always have both.

**Pointing at a stage.** A pointer over a stage's row points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the stage it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows go from stage to stage, up and down, or right and left in a horizontal funnel; Home and End go to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The stage is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the stage's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each stage with its name, its value and its shares, in their order: a share says which stage it is of, but where the funnel writes the first stage's alone.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says or, given no height, as the chart's style says.

```kotlin
PantrixFunnelChart(
    stages = listOf(
        FunnelStage("visits", "Visits", 3000),
        FunnelStage("signups", "Sign-ups", 1240),
        FunnelStage("paid", "Paid", 310)
    ),
    description = "From a visit to a payment",
    tagKey = "sales"
)
```

Parameters:

- `stages: List<FunnelStage>`: the stages, in the order they follow one another. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.
- `labels: ChartDataLabels?`: what is written at the stages: each stage's name and its value, written as `format` says or in the theme's language where it says nothing, with its shares. `null` writes nothing at them.
- `tooltip: ChartTooltip?`: what is shown for the stage that is pointed at: its name and its value with its shares. With both shares the value stands alone on the stage's row and each share on a row of its own under it, which a tooltip of the caller's own is handed as a point of the stage named by the share, with the share as its value and no text. A stage has no place to share and no line through it: `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.
- `empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.
- `state: ChartState`: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.
- `description: String?`: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its stages.
- `onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)?`: called with the stage that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `text` its value with its shares after it.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. Two stages are a `sliceGap` apart.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Funnel_<tagKey>`, its stages together `Funnel_<tagKey>.Plot`, a stage `Funnel_<tagKey>.Stage_<number>`, counted from one, and the tooltip `Funnel_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a stage is reported as a `Funnel` `select` event with the stage's key. Nothing of the values is reported.
- `shape: FunnelShape`: how the stages are drawn: as one funnel, or as bars.
- `horizontal: Boolean`: whether the stages stand side by side, from where lines start, and not one under another.
- `rate: FunnelRate`: which shares a stage's value is written with: of the first stage, of the stage before it, or both. At a stage they stand in brackets after the value, two of them apart by a dot; to a tooltip and a screen reader one of the stage before it, and each of two, says which it is (`PantrixStrings.shareOfFirst` and `shareOfPrevious`).
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

### FunnelStage

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel.FunnelStage`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class FunnelStage(
    public val key: String,
    public val name: String,
    public val value: Number,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

One stage of a `PantrixFunnelChart`: a step of what is followed, and how many reached it.

```kotlin
FunnelStage("signups", "Sign-ups", 1240)
```

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What tells the stage from the others of its funnel, and stays the same while its value changes: what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.
- `name: String`: What the stage is called: at the stage, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.
- `value: Number`: How many reached the stage. One that is no number, has no end or is under nought counts for nothing.
- `color: Color`: The colour the stage is drawn in. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the stages.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture the stage is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the stages: none for the first.

### FunnelShape

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel.FunnelShape`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class FunnelShape
```

How the stages of a `PantrixFunnelChart` are drawn.

Entries:

- `Funnel`: As one funnel: each stage narrows or widens to the size of the stage after it.
- `Bars`: As bars, each as large as it counts for all along its row.

### FunnelRate

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.funnel.FunnelRate`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class FunnelRate
```

Which shares a stage's value is written with in a `PantrixFunnelChart`.

Entries:

- `First`: Of the first stage: how much of all that was followed reached it.
- `Previous`: Of the stage before it: how much of those that reached that one went on to it. The first stage has none.
- `Both`: Of the first stage and of the stage before it.

### ChartDataLabels

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartDataLabels`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class ChartDataLabels(
    public val format: ((Double) -> String)? = null,
    public val position: ChartDataLabelPosition = ChartDataLabelPosition.Auto,
    public val total: Boolean = false
)
```

The values of a series written in the chart, each at its mark: over a point of a line, at the end of a bar, and inside a bar of a stack, in the one of black and white that reads better on the bar's colour.

```kotlin
BarSeries("revenue", "Revenue", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.revenue }, labels = ChartDataLabels())
BarSeries("online", "Online", months, x = { it.name }, y = { it.online }, stack = "sales",
    labels = ChartDataLabels(position = ChartDataLabelPosition.InsideEnd, total = true))
```

A value has its label where the label has room. Placed by itself, one that would stand on another, or reach out of the chart, is written under its point instead, or inside the end of its bar; where it has no room there either it is left out, as is one that a bar is too small to hold. Placed where its `position` says, it has no other place. The tooltip and the screen reader still have the value. A chart of more than two hundred places writes none.

A line the chart draws to read the values by, through a label, is covered where the label is: the label is written on a plate, of the tooltip's colour past a bar and of the bar's colour inside it.

Its `position` and its `total` are of a chart with axes: a pie and a heatmap write their labels where they do.

Two are the same where they write a value the same way, at the same place.

Parameters:

- `format: ((Double) -> String)?`: How a value is written. Left out, it is written as the axis the series is read by writes its values, and where that says nothing in the theme's language, short from ten thousand on. In a stack that stands as shares, it is given a value's share, and left out the share is written as a share of a hundred.
- `position: ChartDataLabelPosition`: Where on its bar a value is written. A point of a line has its label over it, or under it where it has no room over it, whatever this says.
- `total: Boolean`: Whether what a stack of the series comes to at each place is written past its end: over the stack where it comes to nought or more, and under it where it comes to less. It is written as `format` says, but in a stack that stands as shares in the theme's language, for it is no share. One series of the stack asking for it is enough.

# Sankey Chart

A chart that shows what flows from where to where, and how much. The nodes stand in columns; between them lie bands as wide as what flows: where the visitors of a site come from and what they go on to, what a budget is made of and what it is spent on.

- `PantrixSankeyChart` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey`, `com.pantrixui:components`): What flows from where to where: nodes in columns and between them bands as wide as what flows, set out from the links alone, with a tooltip for the node pointed at and every node reachable by keys and by a screen reader. Keywords: flow diagram, alluvial, flows, transfers, budget flow.

## Features

- **Nodes and links.** The chart takes its nodes (`SankeyNode`) and the links between them (`SankeyLink`); a link names its two nodes by their keys. Links between the same two nodes are one flow.
- **Columns.** The columns come from the links: a node nothing flows into stands in the first column, the others a column past the last of those that flow into them, and a node nothing flows out of in the last. `align` chooses where a node that could stand in more than one column stands: `Justify`, `Left`, `Right`, `Center`. The nodes of a column are put in the order that keeps their flows from crossing as far as it can; `order = SankeyOrder.Given` leaves them in the order they were given.
- **Size.** A node is as tall as the greater of what flows into it and what flows out of it; a band is as wide as what flows. A node's width and the room between two nodes of a column are `ChartStyle`'s `nodeWidth` and `nodeGap`.
- **The node pointed at.** The node under the pointer or a finger is ringed, its flows stand out and the others fade. The tooltip writes the node and each of its flows, with the name of the node at its other end. On the keyboard the arrows go to the nearest node the way they point.
- **The flow pointed at.** Where the pointer or a finger is on a flow, the flow stands out, the others fade, and the tooltip writes its two nodes the way it flows ("Search → Signed up"). The keyboard stays on the nodes.
- **What is refused.** A link from a node to itself, links that lead back to where they started, and a link that names a node the chart does not have are refused.
- **Screen reader.** First the chart's description, then each node, column by column: what it counts for, and each of its flows with where it comes from or goes to.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Automation.** The chart is tagged `Sankey_<tagKey>`, a node `Sankey_<tagKey>.Node_<number>`. A press on a node is reported as a `select` event with the node's key, and a press on a flow with the keys of its two nodes (`source>target`).

## Usage

### Where visitors come from and what they go on to

```kotlin
PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes = listOf(
        SankeyNode("search", stringResource(Res.string.search)),
        SankeyNode("social", stringResource(Res.string.social)),
        SankeyNode("signup", stringResource(Res.string.signup)),
        SankeyNode("left", stringResource(Res.string.left))
    ),
    links = listOf(
        SankeyLink("search", "signup", report.searchSignups),
        SankeyLink("search", "left", report.searchLeft),
        SankeyLink("social", "signup", report.socialSignups),
        SankeyLink("social", "left", report.socialLeft)
    ),
    description = stringResource(Res.string.visitor_flows),
    tagKey = "visitors"
)
```

### Nodes and links read from rows, with a node that is pressed

```kotlin
PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes = accounts.map { SankeyNode(it.id, it.name) },
    links = transfers.map { SankeyLink(from = it.source, to = it.target, value = it.amount) },
    onSelect = { node -> openAccount(node.series) },
    tagKey = "budget"
)
```

### Column alignment and order

Column alignment (`align`). Those from ads flow straight to a payment, and some of those from search leave at once: these two nodes could stand in more than one column. "Justify" puts a node nothing flows out of in the last column, "Left" as early as it can be, "Right" a node nothing flows into as late as it can be, and "Center" a column before the first node it flows into. Turn the switch: the nodes stand in a column in the order they were given (`order = SankeyOrder.Given`).

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.PantrixSankeyChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyAlign
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyLink
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyNode
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyOrder
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton

var align by remember { mutableStateOf(SankeyAlign.Justify) }
var given by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixSegmentButton(
    options = SANKEY_ALIGNS,
    selected = align,
    onSelect = { align = it },
    fullWidth = false,
    tagKey = "sankey_align"
)
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = given,
    onCheckedChange = { given = it },
    label = "In the given order",
    tagKey = "sankey_given"
)
PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes = ALIGN_NODES,
    links = ALIGN_LINKS,
    modifier = Modifier.height(260.dp),
    align = align,
    order = if (given) SankeyOrder.Given else SankeyOrder.Untangled,
    description = "Where visitors come from and where they end up",
    tagKey = "align"
)

private val ALIGN_NODES = listOf(
    SankeyNode("search", "Search"),
    SankeyNode("ads", "Ads"),
    SankeyNode("signup", "Signed up"),
    SankeyNode("browse", "Browsed"),
    SankeyNode("left", "Left"),
    SankeyNode("paid", "Paid"),
    SankeyNode("bounce", "Left at once")
)

private val ALIGN_LINKS = listOf(
    SankeyLink("search", "signup", 300),
    SankeyLink("search", "browse", 200),
    SankeyLink("search", "bounce", 100),
    SankeyLink("ads", "paid", 60),
    SankeyLink("signup", "paid", 120),
    SankeyLink("signup", "left", 180),
    SankeyLink("browse", "left", 200)
)

private val SANKEY_ALIGNS = listOf(
    SegmentOption(value = SankeyAlign.Justify, label = "Justify", tagKey = "justify"),
    SegmentOption(value = SankeyAlign.Left, label = "Left", tagKey = "left"),
    SegmentOption(value = SankeyAlign.Right, label = "Right", tagKey = "right"),
    SegmentOption(value = SankeyAlign.Center, label = "Center", tagKey = "center")
)
```

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the nodes, the flows and the names; a flow or a node that is pointed at does not stand out in it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue

import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport

import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.PantrixSankeyChart
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyLink
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyNode

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes = VISITOR_NODES,
    links = VISITOR_LINKS,
    modifier = Modifier.height(280.dp),
    description = "The sources visitors come from, what they do on the site, and how they end up",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "visitors") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

private val VISITOR_NODES = listOf(
    SankeyNode("search", "Search"),
    SankeyNode("social", "Social"),
    SankeyNode("direct", "Direct"),
    SankeyNode("signup", "Signed up"),
    SankeyNode("browse", "Browsed"),
    SankeyNode("paid", "Paid"),
    SankeyNode("free", "Stayed free"),
    SankeyNode("left", "Left")
)

private val VISITOR_LINKS = listOf(
    SankeyLink("search", "signup", 300),
    SankeyLink("search", "browse", 200),
    SankeyLink("social", "signup", 100),
    SankeyLink("social", "browse", 200),
    SankeyLink("direct", "signup", 120),
    SankeyLink("direct", "browse", 80),
    SankeyLink("signup", "paid", 220),
    SankeyLink("signup", "free", 300),
    SankeyLink("browse", "free", 180),
    SankeyLink("browse", "left", 300)
)
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

## API

### PantrixSankeyChart

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.PantrixSankeyChart`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes: List<SankeyNode>,
    links: List<SankeyLink>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    names: Boolean = true,
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    align: SankeyAlign = SankeyAlign.Justify,
    order: SankeyOrder = SankeyOrder.Untangled,
    export: ChartExport? = null
)
```

A sankey chart: what flows from where to where, and how much. Nodes stand in columns, and between them lie the flows as bands, each as wide as what flows: where the visitors of a site come from and what they go on to, what a budget is made of and what it is spent on, where the energy of a plant ends up.

The chart is given its `nodes` and the `links` between them, each link by the keys of its two nodes. The columns come from the links: a node nothing flows into stands in the first, every other a column past the last of the nodes that flow into it, and a node nothing flows out of in the last, as `align` has it by default. In a column the nodes are put in the order that keeps their flows from crossing where that can be helped, or the order they are given in where `order` says so. A node is as tall as the greater of what flows into it and what flows out of it; one that no link names has no place in the chart.

Two links between the same two nodes are one flow, of what they come to together. The links have to lead one way: a link from a node to itself, links that lead back to where they started, and a link that names a node the chart does not have are refused.

**Pointing at a node.** A pointer over a node points at it; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the node it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: an arrow goes to the nearest node the way it points, Home and End to the first node and the last, and Escape lets go. The node is ringed, its flows are drawn stronger and the others fainter, the tooltip is shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the node's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**Pointing at a flow.** A pointer over a flow, off the nodes, points at the flow, and a finger does by a tap: the flow is drawn stronger and the others fainter, and the tooltip names its two nodes, the way it flows, with how much flows. It is told to `state` as a selection whose `series` is the key of the node it leaves and whose `x` is the key of the node it reaches, and a press on it calls `onSelect`. The keys go from node to node, and leave the flows to the nodes' tooltips.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, then each node with what it counts for and, after it, each of its flows: where it comes from or goes to, and how much.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says or, given no height, as the chart's style says. In a language read from the right the first column stands at the right.

```kotlin
PantrixSankeyChart(
    nodes = listOf(SankeyNode("search", "Search"), SankeyNode("signup", "Sign-up"), SankeyNode("left", "Left")),
    links = listOf(SankeyLink("search", "signup", 420), SankeyLink("search", "left", 580)),
    description = "Where the visitors from search go",
    tagKey = "visitors"
)
```

Parameters:

- `nodes: List<SankeyNode>`: the nodes. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.
- `links: List<SankeyLink>`: what flows between the nodes: each from one node to another, by their keys.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.
- `names: Boolean`: whether each node's name is written beside it, where it has room.
- `tooltip: ChartTooltip?`: what is shown for the node that is pointed at: its name and what it counts for, and under them each flow into it and out of it, with the node at its other end. Its `format` writes the values; `shared` and `crosshair` are not read. `null` shows none.
- `empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.
- `state: ChartState`: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.
- `description: String?`: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its nodes.
- `onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)?`: called with the node that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, and its `value` what it counts for; and with the flow that is pressed: the key of the node it leaves is its `series` and of the node it reaches its `x`, its `name` the two nodes' names, and its `value` how much flows.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. A node is `nodeWidth` wide, two nodes of a column are a `nodeGap` apart, and a node's corners are as round as `barRadius` says.
- `colors: ChartColors?`: this chart's own colours, where they are not the theme's.
- `tagKey: String?`: the chart's automation key: the chart is `Sankey_<tagKey>`, its nodes and flows together `Sankey_<tagKey>.Plot`, a node `Sankey_<tagKey>.Node_<number>`, counted from one, column by column and in each from the top down, and the tooltip `Sankey_<tagKey>.Tooltip`. A press on a node is reported as a `Sankey` `select` event with the node's key, and a press on a flow with the keys of its two nodes, `from>to`. Nothing of the values is reported.
- `align: SankeyAlign`: which column each node stands in, of those it could stand in.
- `order: SankeyOrder`: the order the nodes of a column stand in: the one that keeps the flows from crossing, or as given.
- `export: ChartExport?`: what lets the reader take the chart out of the app as a PNG, an SVG or a PDF: a button over the chart makes the file of it as it is and hands it over (see `ChartExport`). `null`, the chart has no such button.

### SankeyNode

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyNode`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SankeyNode(
    public val key: String,
    public val name: String,
    public val color: Color = Color.Unspecified,
    public val pattern: ChartPattern? = null
)
```

One node of a `PantrixSankeyChart`: something that what the chart follows flows out of, into, or through.

```kotlin
SankeyNode("search", "Search")
```

Parameters:

- `key: String`: What tells the node from the others of its chart: what a link names it by, what a selection names, and what an event reports. Written as a test tag's key is, in small letters and digits.
- `name: String`: What the node is called: beside it, in the tooltip and to a screen reader.
- `color: Color`: The colour the node is drawn in, and the flows that leave it. Left out, it is the theme's chart colour for its place among the nodes.
- `pattern: ChartPattern?`: The texture the node is drawn with besides its colour. Left out, none, and where the chart's patterns are on (`ChartStyle.patterns`), its turn by its place among the nodes: none for the first.

### SankeyLink

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyLink`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
class SankeyLink(
    public val from: String,
    public val to: String,
    public val value: Number
)
```

One link of a `PantrixSankeyChart`: how much flows from one node to another.

```kotlin
SankeyLink(from = "search", to = "signup", value = 420)
```

Parameters:

- `from: String`: The key of the node it leaves.
- `to: String`: The key of the node it reaches: another node than the one it leaves.
- `value: Number`: How much flows. One that is no number, has no end or is not over nought is no flow.

### SankeyAlign

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyAlign`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SankeyAlign
```

Which column each node of a `PantrixSankeyChart` stands in. Every node stands a column past the nodes that flow into it; the four differ in where a node stands that could stand in more than one.

Entries:

- `Justify`: A column past the last of the nodes that flow into it, and a node nothing flows out of in the last column.
- `Left`: A column past the last of the nodes that flow into it: a node nothing flows out of too.
- `Right`: A column before the first of the nodes it flows into, and a node nothing flows into as late as it can be.
- `Center`: A column past the last of the nodes that flow into it, and a node nothing flows into a column before the first of those it flows into.

### SankeyOrder

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.sankey.SankeyOrder`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
enum class SankeyOrder
```

The order the nodes of a column of a `PantrixSankeyChart` stand in, from the top down.

Entries:

- `Untangled`: The order that keeps their flows from crossing where that can be helped.
- `Given`: The order the nodes are given in.

# Gantt Chart

A chart that shows the tasks of a plan: each task in a row, a bar from the moment it starts to the moment it ends. It shows what runs when, what overlaps, and how much of each task is done.

- `PantrixGanttChart` (`com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt`, `com.pantrixui:components`): The tasks of a plan, a row each, every one a bar from the moment it starts to the moment it ends along one axis of time, with how much of it is done, milestones, a line at today, a tooltip for the task pointed at and every task reachable by keys and by a screen reader. Keywords: timeline, schedule, project plan, roadmap, tasks.

## Features

- **Tasks.** The chart takes its tasks (`GanttTask`) in the order of their rows; each task has a key, a name, and the moments it starts and ends. Moments are `kotlin.time.Instant`: no date library is needed.
- **Time.** Time runs along the chart, from the start of the first task to the end of the last. Its axis is marked at round moments (day, week, month), as many as have room, and at each mark a line goes up through the rows. Moments are read by the device's clock and written in the theme's language, unless `time` (`ChartTime`) says otherwise.
- **Progress.** A task that gives `progress` has that much of its bar in full colour and the rest faint.
- **Milestone.** A task that ends when it starts is a moment, and is drawn as a diamond.
- **Today.** Where `today` is given and lies in the chart's time, a line runs over the bars at it and "Today" is written on a line of its own over the rows. The chart has no clock of its own: the moment it is read at is the caller's to give.
- **Groups.** Tasks that give a `group` gather under a row of the group's own: the group's bar runs from the start of its first task to the end of its last, with its ends pointing down; the tasks' names stand a little in from the group's. The group's name is the heading of its tasks' tooltip, and a screen reader says it too.
- **Rows.** Tasks that give the same `row` share a row, side by side in time, and the row is called by that name: a person's work in a row of their own. Tasks whose times overlap stand one under another in the row, and the row grows by a row's height for each. Within the row the pointer goes to the task it is over; the tasks share the row halfway between them.
- **Rings.** Tasks that follow one another cannot close a ring: a task that follows a task that follows it is refused.
- **Dependencies.** `after` holds the keys of the tasks a task follows: from where each ends to where this one starts an arrow is drawn, turning at right angles; where the task starts too soon the arrow goes round below or above. A key the chart does not have, or the task's own, is refused.
- **Weekends.** `weekends = true` shades the Saturdays and Sundays faint by the chart's clock; where a day is narrower than two pixels it shades none.
- **Names.** The tasks' names stand in a column at the start of the rows, no wider than two fifths of the chart; a name that does not fit is cut short with three dots. `names = false` takes the column away.
- **The task pointed at.** The bar of the task whose row the pointer or the finger is in is ringed, and the tooltip writes its name, the moments it starts and ends and, where it is said, how much of it is done. With the keyboard the arrows up and down go from task to task.
- **Size.** Given no height, the chart is as tall as its rows need, group headers among them: thirty-two dp a row, and one more over them where "Today" is written.
- **Screen reader.** First the chart's description, then where the today line is drawn "Today" and its day, then each task in the tasks' order: its group and row where it has them, its name, its start, its end and its progress.
- **Export.** `export` puts a button over the chart: the chart is made, as it is on the screen and without the part that is pointed at or its tooltip, into a PNG, an SVG or a PDF file and handed to the app.
- **Zoom.** With `zoom` a part of the time is shown as wide as the chart: a wheel (with Ctrl or Command), two fingers, the plus and minus keys and the buttons look closer; a drag and the buttons move along the time.
- **Automation.** The chart is tagged `Gantt_<tagKey>` and a task `Gantt_<tagKey>.Task_<number>`. A press on a task is reported as a `select` event with the task's key.

## Usage

### The plan of a release

```kotlin
PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = plan.steps.map { step ->
        GanttTask(step.id, step.name, start = step.start, end = step.end, progress = step.done)
    },
    today = now,
    description = stringResource(Res.string.release_plan),
    tagKey = "release"
)
```

### Days of UTC, a milestone, and a task that is pressed

```kotlin
PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = steps.map { GanttTask(it.id, it.name, it.start, it.end) } +
        GanttTask("launch", stringResource(Res.string.launch), start = launch, end = launch, color = brand.accent),
    time = ChartTime(offset = { Duration.ZERO }),
    onSelect = { task -> openStep(task.series) },
    tagKey = "plan"
)
```

## Examples

### The plan of a release

The plan of a release: four tasks and two milestones. The tasks that are finished are in full colour; of those under way the part that is done is in full colour and the rest faint. The upright line shows today (`today`): what is to its left is past.

Move the pointer over a row, or touch the row: the bar is ringed and the tooltip writes the task's start, its end and how far it is. The days are days of UTC, so the chart is read by UTC too (the `offset` of `ChartTime`).

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartTime
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.GanttTask
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.PantrixGanttChart
import kotlin.time.Duration
import kotlin.time.Instant

PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = RELEASE_PLAN,
    time = ChartTime(offset = { Duration.ZERO }),
    today = dayAt("04-14"),
    description = "The plan of the spring release: from research to release",
    tagKey = "plain"
)

private val RELEASE_PLAN = listOf(
    GanttTask("research", "Research", start = dayAt("03-02"), end = dayAt("03-14"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("design", "Design", start = dayAt("03-09"), end = dayAt("03-28"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("build", "Development", start = dayAt("03-23"), end = dayAt("04-25"), progress = 0.55f),
    GanttTask("test", "Testing", start = dayAt("04-13"), end = dayAt("05-02"), progress = 0.1f),
    GanttTask("candidate", "Release candidate", start = dayAt("04-27"), end = dayAt("04-27")),
    GanttTask("release", "Release", start = dayAt("05-04"), end = dayAt("05-04"))
)

private fun dayAt(day: String): Instant = Instant.parse("2026-${day}T00:00:00Z")
```

### Your own colours and rows with no names

Each task can carry a colour of its own (the `color` field of `GanttTask`): here the design work is in one colour, the software work in another and the milestones in a third. Turn the switch: the names' column goes away (`names = false`) and the bars take the whole width; the names stay in the tooltip and for a screen reader.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue

import kotlin.time.Instant

var named by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

    names = named,
    description = "The plan of the spring release, in the teams' colours",
    tagKey = "own_colors"
)

private val RELEASE_PLAN = listOf(
    GanttTask("research", "Research", start = dayAt("03-02"), end = dayAt("03-14"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("design", "Design", start = dayAt("03-09"), end = dayAt("03-28"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("build", "Development", start = dayAt("03-23"), end = dayAt("04-25"), progress = 0.55f),
    GanttTask("test", "Testing", start = dayAt("04-13"), end = dayAt("05-02"), progress = 0.1f),
    GanttTask("candidate", "Release candidate", start = dayAt("04-27"), end = dayAt("04-27")),
    GanttTask("release", "Release", start = dayAt("05-04"), end = dayAt("05-04"))
)

private fun dayAt(day: String): Instant = Instant.parse("2026-${day}T00:00:00Z")
```

### Pressing a task


The tasks in their teams' groups (`group`): each group has a row of its own and a bar that sums its tasks up from start to end. The arrows show which task follows which (`after`): Development starts once Design ends. Testing starts before Development ends, so its arrow goes round below.

### Export

`export = ChartExport(...)` puts an export button over the chart: press it and choose the kind (PNG, SVG or PDF). The chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`; below, its name and size show, and a PNG's picture, and "Save the file" hands it over in the platform's way.

The file has the rows, the bars, the marks of time and the line of today with its name.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartTime
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExport
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.export.ChartExportFile
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.GanttTask
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.PantrixGanttChart
import kotlin.time.Duration
import kotlin.time.Instant

var file by remember { mutableStateOf<ChartExportFile?>(null) }
PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = RELEASE_PLAN,
    time = ChartTime(offset = { Duration.ZERO }),
    today = dayAt("04-14"),
    description = "The plan of the spring release: from research to release",
    tagKey = "exported",
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "spring-release") { file = it }
)
ExportedFile(file, tagKey = "exported")

private val RELEASE_PLAN = listOf(
    GanttTask("research", "Research", start = dayAt("03-02"), end = dayAt("03-14"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("design", "Design", start = dayAt("03-09"), end = dayAt("03-28"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("build", "Development", start = dayAt("03-23"), end = dayAt("04-25"), progress = 0.55f),
    GanttTask("test", "Testing", start = dayAt("04-13"), end = dayAt("05-02"), progress = 0.1f),
    GanttTask("candidate", "Release candidate", start = dayAt("04-27"), end = dayAt("04-27")),
    GanttTask("release", "Release", start = dayAt("05-04"), end = dayAt("05-04"))
)

private fun dayAt(day: String): Instant = Instant.parse("2026-${day}T00:00:00Z")
```

What the code calls of the demo app itself, which an app writes for itself:

- `ExportedFile`: Shows the file a chart made: its name, its type and its size; a PNG's picture itself, no larger than its own size; and the "Save the file" button, which hands the file over in the platform's window for saving (the library's `rememberFileSaver`). It says so while there is no file yet.

### Looking closer at the time

`zoom = ChartZoom()` lets the reader look closer at the time: a wheel with Ctrl or Command, two fingers, plus and minus on the chart, and the buttons over it show a part of the time as wide as the chart. A drag of the mouse and the buttons move along it; the task the arrows go to comes into view.

What lies past the part in view is cut off at the time's two ends, and the names stay. The part is kept in the state (`state.window`): this chart opens on the first half of the plan, and nought or the last button shows all of it again.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.LaunchedEffect
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.cartesian.ChartTime
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.ChartZoom
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.common.rememberChartState
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.GanttTask
import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.PantrixGanttChart
import kotlin.time.Duration
import kotlin.time.Instant

val state = rememberChartState()
// The chart opens on the first half of the plan.
LaunchedEffect(state) { state.zoomTo(start = 0f, end = 0.5f) }
PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = RELEASE_PLAN,
    time = ChartTime(offset = { Duration.ZERO }),
    today = dayAt("04-14"),
    state = state,
    description = "The plan of the spring release: from research to release",
    tagKey = "zoomed",
    zoom = ChartZoom()
)

private val RELEASE_PLAN = listOf(
    GanttTask("research", "Research", start = dayAt("03-02"), end = dayAt("03-14"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("design", "Design", start = dayAt("03-09"), end = dayAt("03-28"), progress = 1f),
    GanttTask("build", "Development", start = dayAt("03-23"), end = dayAt("04-25"), progress = 0.55f),
    GanttTask("test", "Testing", start = dayAt("04-13"), end = dayAt("05-02"), progress = 0.1f),
    GanttTask("candidate", "Release candidate", start = dayAt("04-27"), end = dayAt("04-27")),
    GanttTask("release", "Release", start = dayAt("05-04"), end = dayAt("05-04"))
)

private fun dayAt(day: String): Instant = Instant.parse("2026-${day}T00:00:00Z")
```

## API

### PantrixGanttChart

`import com.pantrixui.components.chart.gantt.PantrixGanttChart`, from `com.pantrixui:components`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks: List<GanttTask>,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    time: ChartTime? = null,
    today: Instant? = null,
    names: Boolean = true,
    tooltip: ChartTooltip? = ChartTooltip(),
    empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    state: ChartState = rememberChartState(),
    description: String? = null,
    onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)? = null,
    style: ChartStyle? = null,
    colors: ChartColors? = null,
    tagKey: String? = null,
    weekends: Boolean = false,
    export: ChartExport? = null,
    zoom: ChartZoom? = null
)
```

A Gantt chart: the tasks of a plan, a row each, every one a bar from the moment it starts to the moment it ends along one axis of time. It shows what runs when, what overlaps, and how far each task is.

The chart is given its `tasks`, in the order of their rows. Time runs from the start of the first task to the end of the last, along the chart, and its axis is marked at round moments, days, weeks, months, as many as have room, with a line up the rows at each. The tasks' names stand in a column where lines start, no wider than two fifths of the chart; a name too long for it is cut short, and the tooltip and a screen reader have it whole.

A task that says how much of it is done has that much of its bar in full colour and the rest fainter. A task that ends when it starts is a milestone, a diamond at its moment. Where `today` is given and lies in the chart's time, a line is drawn over the bars at it, what is to its left is past, and the word for today is written over it, on a line of its own over the rows.

**Groups, rows and what follows what.** Tasks that name a `group` stand together under a row of the group's own, whose bar runs from the earliest of them to the latest, with a point down at each end; their names stand a gap in from the group's. Tasks that name a `row` share it, side by side along its time, and the row is called by that name: a person's tasks in a lane of their own; those whose times overlap stand one under another. A task that names others in `after` follows them: an arrow leads from where each ends to where it starts, turning at a right angle, and round below or above where it starts too soon. With `weekends` the Saturdays and Sundays are shaded faint under all, where a day is wide enough to show.

Moments are read by the screen's clock (`LocalPantrixClock`) and written in the theme's language, unless `time` says otherwise: see `ChartTime`. The chart takes no clock of its own: the moment it is read at is the caller's to give.

**Pointing at a task.** A pointer over a task's row points at it, its name's part of the row too; a finger does by a tap, and a tap on the task it points at lets go of it. With the keyboard the chart is one stop for Tab: the arrows up and down go from task to task, Home and End to the first and the last, and Escape lets go. The task's bar is ringed, the tooltip shown for it, and it is told to `state`, as a selection whose `x` is the task's key. A press, Enter or Space on it calls `onSelect`.

**To a screen reader** the chart is its `description`, and where the line at `today` is drawn, the word for today and its day; then each task with its group and its row where it has them, its name, when it starts and ends, and how much of it is done, in the order of the tasks.

**Its size.** The chart is as wide as it is given room, and as tall as its modifier says; given no height, it is as tall as its rows need: thirty-two dp a lane, a group's header among them, under them a line of writing for the marks of time, and over them one for the word for today where it is written.

```kotlin
PantrixGanttChart(
    tasks = listOf(
        GanttTask("design", "Design", start = monday, end = monday + 5.days, progress = 1f),
        GanttTask("build", "Build", start = monday + 5.days, end = monday + 19.days, progress = 0.4f),
        GanttTask("launch", "Launch", start = monday + 21.days, end = monday + 21.days)
    ),
    today = now,
    description = "The plan of the spring release",
    tagKey = "release"
)
```

Parameters:

- `tasks: List<GanttTask>`: the tasks, in the order of their rows. Their keys tell them apart, and two with one key are refused.
- `modifier: Modifier`: the chart's modifier. A height here is the chart's.
- `time: ChartTime?`: how the chart's moments are written and by which clock. Left out, in the theme's language and by the screen's clock (`LocalPantrixClock`).
- `today: Instant?`: the moment the chart is read at: a line is drawn at it where it lies between the start of the first task and the end of the last. `null` draws none.
- `names: Boolean`: whether the tasks' names are written beside their rows. Without them the bars have the whole width, and the names stay in the tooltip and for a screen reader.
- `tooltip: ChartTooltip?`: what is shown for the task that is pointed at: its group and its row as the heading, where it has them, and under it its name, when it starts and ends, and how much of it is done. A task has no place to share and no line through it: `shared`, `crosshair` and `format` are not read. `null` shows none.
- `empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)?`: what the chart shows while it has no value to draw, in the place of the theme's words for it ("No data"), which a screen reader is then not told either. `null` writes the words.
- `state: ChartState`: what the reader points at: the chart's own where none is given.
- `description: String?`: what the chart shows, in a few words, for a screen reader: the first thing it says of the chart. Left out, the chart is announced by the names of its tasks.
- `onSelect: ((ChartPoint) -> Unit)?`: called with the task that is pressed: its key is its `series` and its `x`, its name its `name` and its `label`, its `value` how many days it takes, and its `text` when it starts and ends as the chart writes it.
- `style: ChartStyle?`: this chart's own geometry: the fields set here, with the theme's for the rest. A bar's corners are as round as `barRadius` says, and the lines at the marks of time as wide as `gridWidth`.
