- **Touch target.** `Modifier.minTouchTarget(min)` reserves at least `min` in the layout without changing what is drawn: a 24dp icon is pressed in a 48dp area. The value comes from the platform, `PantrixTheme.platform.minTouchTarget`.
- **Compose's slop.** The theme fits Compose's touch slop to the platform's: `PantrixViewConfiguration` gives it to `LocalViewConfiguration`.

## Examples

### Your own control's focus and touch target

Your own control's focus ring and touch target. The star is 24dp; `minTouchTarget` makes it pressable in the platform's touch target. `focusRing` draws the ring, in the theme's `focusRing` colour and the platform's width. Come to the star with Tab: the ring shows, and the line beside it writes what `rememberFocusRingVisible` says; on a mouse press the ring does not show.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.interaction.MutableInteractionSource
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.selection.toggleable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.Role
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.icon.PantrixIcon
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.focusRing
import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.minTouchTarget
import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.rememberFocusRingVisible
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.primitives.pantrixPressIndication
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val interaction = remember { MutableInteractionSource() }
var starred by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
val platform = PantrixTheme.platform
Row(
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
) {
    Box(
        modifier = Modifier
            .minTouchTarget(platform.minTouchTarget)
            .focusRing(
                interactionSource = interaction,
                shape = PantrixTheme.shapes.full,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.focusRing,
                width = platform.focusRingWidth
            )
            .toggleable(
                value = starred,
                interactionSource = interaction,
                indication = pantrixPressIndication(),
                role = Role.Checkbox,
                onValueChange = { starred = it }
            ),
        contentAlignment = Alignment.Center
    ) {
        PantrixIcon(
            imageVector = PantrixIcons.Star,
            contentDescription = if (starred) "Starred" else "Not starred",
            size = 24.dp,
            tint = if (starred) PantrixTheme.colors.warning.color else PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
    PantrixText(
        text = "Ring visible: ${if (rememberFocusRingVisible(interaction)) "yes" else "no"}",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
    )
}
```

### Compose's touch slop

Where an element is small, Compose gives it a touch in the room around it too; `LocalViewConfiguration` says how much. The theme fits this value to the platform's touch target: `PantrixViewConfiguration` wraps Compose's configuration and gives the smallest touch target as the platform's. The line underneath reads it.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalViewConfiguration
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.PantrixViewConfiguration
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val configuration = LocalViewConfiguration.current
val target = configuration.minimumTouchTargetSize
PantrixText(
    text = "The theme's configuration: ${if (configuration is PantrixViewConfiguration) "yes" else "no"} · " +
        "smallest touch target ${target.width.value.toInt()} × ${target.height.value.toInt()} dp",
    style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
)
```

## API

### Modifier.focusRing

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.focusRing`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun Modifier.focusRing(
    interactionSource: InteractionSource,
    shape: Shape,
    color: Color,
    width: Dp,
    inset: Boolean = false
): Modifier
```

Draws the focus ring around the element, outside its bounds.

The ring is `width` wide and leaves a gap as wide between itself and the element, so it stays apart from the element's own fill and border: a button filled in the ring's colour is still told apart from its ring. Its corners follow `shape`, grown by the gap and the ring, so a rounded element gets a ring with the same centre of curvature. A `width` of nothing draws no ring.

The ring is drawn, not laid out, so it takes no space. Put the modifier before any `clip` or layer in the element's own chain, which would cut it off, and leave the element room: an ancestor that clips cuts it off as well. `inset` draws it inside the bounds instead, for an element as wide or as tall as its container — a list row, a pane divider — whose ring outside would run past the container's edges.

Whatever scrolls the element brings it into view when it takes the focus, and no further than its own edge. As the ring appears it asks for the room it is drawn in as well, so that a row or a column that scrolls shows the ring whole and not the element with a side of its ring cut. Only what can be scrolled to is asked for: at the very end of what a scroller holds there is nothing past the element, and the scroller's content needs that room as padding, the ring and its gap, twice `width` (`PantrixPlatform.focusRingReach`). A lazy list is asked for the element alone: how far its items go on cannot be told from an item. There the room is the list's content padding, and each item says so with `scrollPadding`.

Parameters:

- `interactionSource: InteractionSource`: the element's interaction source, whose focus decides whether the ring is drawn.
- `shape: Shape`
- `color: Color`: the ring's colour: the theme's `focusRing`, or on a fill what is written on that fill, so that the ring reads there as the text does.
- `width: Dp`
- `inset: Boolean`

### rememberFocusRingVisible

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.rememberFocusRingVisible`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberFocusRingVisible(interactionSource: InteractionSource): Boolean
```

Whether a focus ring should be visible right now: the element is focused, no modal overlay is shown over it, and the focus came by the keyboard, or the platform shows the ring for every focus (`PantrixPlatform.showFocusRingOnlyForKeyboard`).

How the focus came is Compose's own `androidx.compose.ui.input.InputMode`, Touch or Keyboard: a key press puts the window in keyboard mode and a touch takes it out. It says nothing of how precise the pointing device is.

Under a modal overlay the focus stays where it was, to be there again when the overlay closes, but no key reaches it: the ring is not shown there until the overlay has closed (`PantrixModalLayer`).

Parameters:

- `interactionSource: InteractionSource`: the element's interaction source: the ring follows the focus it reports.

### Modifier.minTouchTarget

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.minTouchTarget`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun Modifier.minTouchTarget(min: Dp): Modifier
```

Reserves at least `min` in the layout without changing what the component draws.

This half of the problem is the easy half. The other half is hit-testing, which Compose takes from `ViewConfiguration.minimumTouchTargetSize` — a fixed value this modifier cannot reach. A component that only applies this modifier lays out at 48dp and still only *responds* within its visual bounds, which is the kind of defect that never shows up in a screenshot.

`PantrixTheme` therefore also overrides `LocalViewConfiguration` with `PantrixViewConfiguration`, so both halves use the same number. The pair is the Foundation-only equivalent of Material 3's `LocalMinimumInteractiveComponentSize`.

While the theme's diagnostics are on, a component that is given less room than `min` for half a second is reported as `PantrixCheck.SmallTouchTarget`: whatever stands around it laid it out, and lets it be pressed, in less.

Parameters:

- `min: Dp`

### PantrixViewConfiguration

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.PantrixViewConfiguration`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
class PantrixViewConfiguration(
    private val delegate: ViewConfiguration,
    private val minTouchTarget: Dp
) : ViewConfiguration by delegate
```

Makes Compose's hit-test expansion agree with the platform preset.

Provided by `PantrixTheme`; delegates everything except the touch target so future Compose additions to `ViewConfiguration` keep working without a change here.

Parameters:

- `delegate: ViewConfiguration`: The configuration everything but the touch target comes from: the one already in effect.
- `minTouchTarget: Dp`: The touch target, the same both ways.

# Language and words

What the components say by themselves: "Close", "Loading", "Per page", everything said to a screen reader. The theme takes them from its language; the app's own texts are the app's.

## Features

- **Language.** `PantrixLocale` is a language and the direction of its script; `forLanguageTag("ar-EG")` works the direction out from the tag. `PantrixTheme(locale = …)` gives the language to what is in it, and `PantrixTheme.locale` is the nearest theme's.
- **Words.** `PantrixStrings` is the components' words. Turkish, English and Arabic packs come with it (`PantrixStrings.forLocale(locale)`); another language is given by a pack's `copy`: `PantrixTheme(strings = …)`.
- **The words of time.** `PantrixTimeWords` is the words that count time: "Last 15 minutes", "~ 2 hours ago", "in 3 days"; a pack's `timeWords`.

## Examples

### Three packs

The words of three packs: each line is a pack's "Close", its "Loading" and how it writes a number. Arabic writes in its own digits. The pack is found from the language: `PantrixStrings.forLocale(PantrixLocale.forLanguageTag("ar-EG"))` is Arabic's.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixLocale
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val packs = listOf(
    "tr" to PantrixStrings.Turkish,
    "en" to PantrixStrings.English,
    "ar-EG" to PantrixStrings.forLocale(PantrixLocale.forLanguageTag("ar-EG"))
)
packs.forEach { (tag, strings) ->
    PantrixText(
        text = "$tag · ${strings.close} · ${strings.loading} · ${strings.number(1_234_567)}",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
    )
}
```

### A language Pantrix does not know

A language Pantrix has no pack for: German. The inner theme was given `PantrixLocale.forLanguageTag("de-DE")` and a copy of the English pack translated into German. The page size picker reads its word from the new pack. The line underneath reads the language and "Close" straight from the locals (`LocalPantrixLocale`, `LocalPantrixStrings`).

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.data.pagination.PantrixPageSize
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.LocalPantrixLocale
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.LocalPantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixLocale
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixStrings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

var pageSize by remember { mutableIntStateOf(25) }
PantrixTheme(locale = PantrixLocale.forLanguageTag("de-DE"), strings = GERMAN) {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.sm)) {
        PantrixPageSize(pageSize = pageSize, onPageSizeChange = { pageSize = it }, tagKey = "german_size")
        PantrixText(
            text = "${LocalPantrixLocale.current.languageTag} · ${LocalPantrixStrings.current.close}",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
}

private val GERMAN = PantrixStrings.English.copy(
    close = "Schließen",
    loading = "Wird geladen",
    perPage = "Pro Seite",
    goToPage = "Gehe zu Seite"
)
```

### The words of time

The words of time in three languages: a range ("last 15 minutes"), an approximate past ("~ 2 hours ago") and a future ("in 3 days"). After a number the noun stays singular in Turkish, takes the plural in English, and changes with the number in Arabic.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.date.PantrixTimeUnit
import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixTimeWords
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

listOf(PantrixTimeWords.Turkish, PantrixTimeWords.English, PantrixTimeWords.Arabic).forEach { words ->
    PantrixText(
        text = "${words.last(15, PantrixTimeUnit.Minutes)} · " +
            "${words.ago(2, PantrixTimeUnit.Hours, approximate = true)} · " +
            words.fromNow(3, PantrixTimeUnit.Days, approximate = false),
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
    )
}
```

## API

### PantrixLocale

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixLocale`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
data class PantrixLocale(
    public val languageTag: String,
    public val layoutDirection: LayoutDirection,
    public val firstDayOfWeek: Int = firstDayOfWeekOf(languageTag)
)
```

A language, the direction its script runs in, and the day its calendars start a week on. `forLanguageTag` works the direction out from the tag.

Parameters:

- `languageTag: String`: The language as a BCP 47 tag, e.g. `tr`, `en-GB`, `ar`.
- `layoutDirection: LayoutDirection`: The direction the language's script runs in: right to left for Arabic.
- `firstDayOfWeek: Int`: The day a week starts on in the language's calendars, as ISO 8601 numbers the days: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. Unless given, Monday in Turkish, Saturday in Arabic, and Sunday in English and in every other language. A date picker that is given no first day of its own starts its weeks on this one. `firstDayOfWeekOf`: The day `languageTag`'s calendars start a week on: Monday in Turkish, Saturday in Arabic, Sunday otherwise.

Members:

- `language: String`: The primary subtag, lower-cased: `en-GB` -> `en`.

On the type:

- `PantrixLocale.English: PantrixLocale`: English, written from left to right, its weeks starting on Sunday.
- `PantrixLocale.Turkish: PantrixLocale`: Turkish, written from left to right, its weeks starting on Monday.
- `PantrixLocale.Arabic: PantrixLocale`: Arabic, written from right to left, its weeks starting on Saturday.
- `PantrixLocale.forLanguageTag(tag: String): PantrixLocale`: Builds a locale from a tag, inferring direction.

  `tag`: the language as a BCP 47 tag, `tr`, `en-GB` or `ar`: its primary subtag decides the direction and the day a week starts on.

### PantrixTimeWords

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.PantrixTimeWords`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
interface PantrixTimeWords
```

The phrases that count time: "Last 15 minutes", "~ 2 hours ago", "in 3 days".

A function for each phrase rather than a template: languages put the number, the unit and the direction in orders of their own, a noun's form follows the number by each language's rules of plurals, and Arabic says two of something by a dual that takes no number. Each function writes its number in the language's own digits.

`English`, `Turkish` and `Arabic` come with their packs. An app with words of its own, or a fourth language, writes one and gives it with its strings: `PantrixStrings.English.copy(timeWords = MyTimeWords)`. An amount is a count of units and never less than nought; the phrase says which way it goes.

Members:

- `now: String`: "now" inside a phrase: the end of "~ 15 minutes ago to now".
- `fun unit(unit: PantrixTimeUnit, count: Int): String`: The unit alone, in the form that goes with `count`: "minutes" beside a 15, in a choice of units.

  `unit`: the unit of time named.
- `fun unitAgo(unit: PantrixTimeUnit, count: Int): String`: The unit and "ago" beside a number: "minutes ago".

  `unit`: the unit of time named.

  `count`: the number the unit stands beside, which picks its form: "minute" beside a 1, "minutes" beside a 15.
- `fun unitFromNow(unit: PantrixTimeUnit, count: Int): String`: The unit and "from now" beside a number: "minutes from now".

  `unit`: the unit of time named.

  `count`: the number the unit stands beside, which picks its form: "minute" beside a 1, "minutes" beside a 15.
- `fun last(amount: Int, unit: PantrixTimeUnit): String`: A range that ends now: "Last 15 minutes".

  `amount`: how many of `unit` the range runs back from now: the 15 of "Last 15 minutes".

  `unit`: the unit the range is counted in.
- `fun next(amount: Int, unit: PantrixTimeUnit): String`: A range that starts now: "Next 15 minutes".

  `amount`: how many of `unit` the range runs on from now: the 15 of "Next 15 minutes".

  `unit`: the unit the range is counted in.
- `fun ago(amount: Int, unit: PantrixTimeUnit, approximate: Boolean): String`: A moment before now: "15 minutes ago", or "~ 2 hours ago" where `approximate`.

  `amount`: how many of `unit` the moment lies before now.

  `unit`: the unit the moment is counted in.
- `fun fromNow(amount: Int, unit: PantrixTimeUnit, approximate: Boolean): String`: A moment after now: "in 15 minutes", or "~ in 2 hours" where `approximate`.

  `amount`: how many of `unit` the moment lies after now.

  `unit`: the unit the moment is counted in.
- `fun roundTo(unit: PantrixTimeUnit): String`: The switch that rounds a moment: "Round to the minute".

  `unit`: the unit a moment is rounded to: "minute" in "Round to the minute".
- `fun roundedTo(phrase: String, unit: PantrixTimeUnit): String`: A `phrase` whose ends were rounded to `unit`: "Last 15 minutes, rounded to the minute".
- `fun range(start: String, end: String): String`: Two ends of a range, each already in words: "~ 15 minutes ago to now".

  `start`: the range's start, already in words: "~ 15 minutes ago".

  `end`: the range's end, already in words: "now".

On the type:

- `PantrixTimeWords.English: PantrixTimeWords`: A noun takes an s unless the count is one: "1 minute", "0 minutes", "15 minutes".
- `PantrixTimeWords.Turkish: PantrixTimeWords`: A noun after a number stays as it is: "15 dakika önce".
- `PantrixTimeWords.Arabic: PantrixTimeWords`: One and two are said by the noun alone, "دقيقة" and "دقيقتين"; 3 to 10 take the plural, "٣ دقائق"; 11 to 99 the singular in the accusative, "١٥ يومًا"; and 100 and more the singular, "١٠٠ يوم". "About" is a word, "حوالي", where the other languages write a tilde.

### LocalPantrixLocale

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.LocalPantrixLocale`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalPantrixLocale: ProvidableCompositionLocal<PantrixLocale>
```

The language in effect, which `PantrixTheme` provides: what `PantrixTheme.locale` reads. Outside a theme, English.

### LocalPantrixStrings

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.l10n.LocalPantrixStrings`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalPantrixStrings: ProvidableCompositionLocal<PantrixStrings>
```

The components' own words in effect, which `PantrixTheme` provides: what `PantrixTheme.strings` reads. Outside a theme, `PantrixStrings.English`.

# Analytics

The components' events: a press, a change, a menu that opened. An event is told by identity, not by content: which component, what happened, the test tag, the screen's name. A text typed or read does not go into the event; something chosen goes in by the key the app gave it.

## Features

- **Event.** A `PantrixUiEvent` has a `component`, an `action`, a `testTag`, a `screen` and optional `props`.
- **Where it goes.** `PantrixTheme(analytics = PantrixAnalytics { event -> … })` gives the events somewhere: to the app's analytics library, to a log. Left out, the events are dropped (`PantrixAnalytics.NoOp`).
- **The app's own event.** `LocalPantrixAnalytics.current` gives the same place: the app sends its own event there too.
- **The app's keys.** A table's row, an option's value, a tree's node goes into the event by its key: the key must not be personal data. Which component sends which key is in docs/guide/analytics/ANALYTICS_GUIDE.md.

## Examples

### The components' events

The components' events. The inner theme gives the events to a list: press the button and turn the switch, the last events are written underneath, the newest on top. An event has the component's name, what happened and the test tag, and Pantrix's own values too, such as the button's variant and whether the switch was turned on.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateListOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixUiEvent
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val events = remember { mutableStateListOf<PantrixUiEvent>() }
var notify by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
val sink = remember { PantrixAnalytics { event -> events.add(0, event) } }
PantrixTheme(analytics = sink) {
    PantrixButton(text = "Save", onClick = {}, tagKey = "save")
    PantrixSwitchButton(checked = notify, onCheckedChange = { notify = it }, label = "Notifications", tagKey = "notify")
}
EventLines(events)

@Composable
private fun EventLines(events: List<PantrixUiEvent>) {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        if (events.isEmpty()) {
            PantrixText(text = "No events yet", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        }
        events.take(5).forEach { event ->
            val props = event.props.entries.joinToString { (key, value) -> "$key=$value" }
            PantrixText(
                text = "${event.component} · ${event.action} · ${event.testTag ?: "-"}" +
                    (event.screen?.let { " · $it" }.orEmpty()) + (if (props.isEmpty()) "" else " · $props"),
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
            )
        }
    }
}
```

### The app's own event

The app's own event. The share button reads the theme's event sink with `LocalPantrixAnalytics.current` and sends its own event there: its component, what happened, its screen and some `props`. It goes to the same place as the components' events.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateListOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.LocalPantrixAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixUiEvent
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val events = remember { mutableStateListOf<PantrixUiEvent>() }
val sink = remember { PantrixAnalytics { event -> events.add(0, event) } }
PantrixTheme(analytics = sink) { ShareButton() }
EventLines(events)

@Composable
private fun ShareButton() {
    val analytics = LocalPantrixAnalytics.current
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Share the link",
        onClick = {
            analytics.track(
                PantrixUiEvent(
                    component = "ShareSheet",
                    action = "share",
                    testTag = null,
                    screen = "Product",
                    props = mapOf("channel" to "link")
                )
            )
        },
        variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
        tagKey = "share"
    )
}

@Composable
private fun EventLines(events: List<PantrixUiEvent>) {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        if (events.isEmpty()) {
            PantrixText(text = "No events yet", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        }
        events.take(5).forEach { event ->
            val props = event.props.entries.joinToString { (key, value) -> "$key=$value" }
            PantrixText(
                text = "${event.component} · ${event.action} · ${event.testTag ?: "-"}" +
                    (event.screen?.let { " · $it" }.orEmpty()) + (if (props.isEmpty()) "" else " · $props"),
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
            )
        }
    }
}
```

## API

### PantrixAnalytics

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixAnalytics`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun interface PantrixAnalytics
```

Sink for `PantrixUiEvent`.

Defaults to a no-op, so the cost of components emitting events unconditionally is one virtual call into an empty body. Products wire their own SDK in through `PantrixTheme(analytics = ...)`; Pantrix itself depends on no analytics vendor.

A component built on a Pantrix control, as a field of dates on two text fields, hears that control's events beside its own, and one press is counted twice. It gives the control a sink of its own with `LocalPantrixAnalytics`, which drops what the component reports itself and hands the rest on under the component's name: `PantrixPageSize` does so with the select it is built on.

Members:

- `fun track(event: PantrixUiEvent)`: Called with each `event` a component emits, as it happens, on the UI thread. A sink hands the event on and returns: what takes time, sending above all, is done off this thread.

On the type:

- `PantrixAnalytics.NoOp: PantrixAnalytics`: The sink that drops every event: where a theme reports to unless it is given one.

### PantrixUiEvent

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixUiEvent`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
data class PantrixUiEvent(
    public val component: String,
    public val action: String,
    public val testTag: String?,
    public val screen: String?,
    public val props: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()
)
```

A UI interaction, described by identity rather than content: which component it was, what happened, and on which screen.

**Text the user typed or read never goes in here.** A field reports that it took the focus or was cleared, never what it holds, and a test of every component that takes text holds that. A value out of a closed set does go in: a selection is reported by the key of what was selected, a page by its number. Some of `props` are the app's own keys, and an app whose keys are personal data sends that data with them: `docs/guide/analytics/ANALYTICS_GUIDE.md` names the components that report them.

Parameters:

- `component: String`: Component name, e.g. `Button`.
- `action: String`: What happened, in the component's own word: `click`, `toggle`, `select`, `open`, `dismiss`, `focus`, `expand`, and others the guide lists by component.
- `testTag: String?`: The component's automation tag, the same identity tests bind to, whatever the `TestTagPolicy`: built from its `tagKey`, or, where it has none, from the place it was called from, which changes with the code around it. Null for an event an app reports without one.
- `screen: String?`: The enclosing `TestScope` chain, e.g. `Checkout.PaymentForm`, or null outside one.
- `props: Map<String, String>`: The event's values, of three kinds: Pantrix's own words and yes-or-no values, such as `variant`, `via` and `state`; numbers, such as `index`, `page` and `count`; and keys the app gave the component, such as `row`, `option` and `destination`.

### LocalPantrixAnalytics

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.LocalPantrixAnalytics`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalPantrixAnalytics: ProvidableCompositionLocal<PantrixAnalytics>
```

Where the components here report their events: `PantrixTheme(analytics = …)`. An app's own code reads it to report its own events to the same place.

# Analytics connector

The class with which an app connects Pantrix's events to its analytics product: the connector given to `PantrixTheme(analytics = …)`. Under which name the events go, when they are sent, what happens while there is no network and what is never in them are its decisions. The connector on this page is `ProductAnalytics`, from the samples/pantrix-analytics sample.

## Features

- **Tracking plan.** `TrackingPlan` gives the product's names to the events told by a component's tag and action, and says which values each of them carries.
- **Generic event.** Every event the plan does not name goes as one `ui_interaction`: with its component, its action, its screen, the tag built from its key and Pantrix's own values. The app's keys and the tags built from where a component is called do not go in.
- **Consent.** Until the user says yes, no event is collected; when consent is taken back, what waits is dropped.
- **Sending.** `track` puts the event in the queue and returns. The events go in batches and off the UI thread: when a batch is full, when its first event has waited long enough, or when the app calls `flush()`.
- **Offline.** The events wait; the send is tried again at ever longer intervals, and the events reach the product in the order they happened. When the queue is full the oldest is dropped.
- **No text.** A text that was typed goes into no Pantrix event, nor into anything the connector sends. The sample is described in samples/pantrix-analytics/README.md, and every event in docs/guide/analytics/ANALYTICS_GUIDE.md.

## Examples

### Tracking plan

The events the plan names. A press of the pay button becomes `checkout_pay_tapped` and carries only the button's variant. A choice of shipping becomes `shipping_chosen` and carries the key of the shipping chosen: the plan says it is no personal data. Make a choice or press the button: the events the product heard are written underneath, the newest on top.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateListOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestScope
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.pantrixTestTagOf
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.PlannedEvent
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.ProductEvent
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.TrackingPlan
import kotlin.time.Clock

val plan = remember {
    TrackingPlan(
        listOf(
            PlannedEvent(
                tag = pantrixTestTagOf(component = "Button", tagKey = "pay", scope = "Checkout"),
                action = "click",
                name = "checkout_pay_tapped",
                keep = setOf("variant")
            ),
            PlannedEvent(
                tag = pantrixTestTagOf(component = "SegmentButton", tagKey = "shipping", scope = "Checkout"),
                action = "select",
                name = "shipping_chosen",
                notPersonal = setOf("segment")
            )
        )
    )
}
val heard = remember { mutableStateListOf<ProductEvent>() }
val analytics = remember {
    PantrixAnalytics { event -> heard.add(0, plan.productEventOf(event, Clock.System.now())) }
}
PantrixTheme(analytics = analytics) {
    TestScope("Checkout") {
        ShippingChoice(tagKey = "shipping")
        PantrixButton(text = "Pay", onClick = {}, tagKey = "pay")
    }
}
HeardEvents(heard)

@Composable
private fun ShippingChoice(tagKey: String) {
    var shipping by remember { mutableStateOf("standard") }
    PantrixSegmentButton(
        options = listOf(
            SegmentOption(value = "standard", label = "Standard", tagKey = "standard"),
            SegmentOption(value = "express", label = "Express", tagKey = "express")
        ),
        selected = shipping,
        onSelect = { shipping = it },
        tagKey = tagKey
    )
}

@Composable
private fun HeardEvents(events: List<ProductEvent>) {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        if (events.isEmpty()) {
            PantrixText(text = "The product has heard nothing yet", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        }
        events.take(5).forEach { event ->
            val properties = event.properties.entries.joinToString { (key, value) -> "$key=$value" }
            PantrixText(
                text = if (properties.isEmpty()) event.name else "${event.name} · $properties",
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
            )
        }
    }
}
```

### The generic event

Every event the plan does not name goes as `ui_interaction`: with its component, its action, its screen, its tag and Pantrix's own values, such as whether the switch is on. The plan is empty: the shipping choice's key does not go in, as it is the app's key and may be personal data. Nor does the tag of the button with no `tagKey`: it is built from where the button is called, and changes when the code does.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateListOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.PantrixSegmentButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.segmentbutton.SegmentOption
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestScope
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.ProductEvent
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.TrackingPlan
import kotlin.time.Clock

val plan = remember { TrackingPlan(emptyList()) }
val heard = remember { mutableStateListOf<ProductEvent>() }
val analytics = remember {
    PantrixAnalytics { event -> heard.add(0, plan.productEventOf(event, Clock.System.now())) }
}
var gift by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
PantrixTheme(analytics = analytics) {
    TestScope("Cart") {
        ShippingChoice(tagKey = "shipping")
        PantrixSwitchButton(
            checked = gift,
            onCheckedChange = { gift = it },
            label = "Gift wrap",
            tagKey = "gift"
        )
        @Suppress("UntaggedControl") // No tagKey on purpose: the example shows that its tag stays out of the event.
        PantrixButton(text = "Back to shopping", onClick = {}, variant = ButtonVariant.Outline)
    }
}
HeardEvents(heard)

@Composable
private fun ShippingChoice(tagKey: String) {
    var shipping by remember { mutableStateOf("standard") }
    PantrixSegmentButton(
        options = listOf(
            SegmentOption(value = "standard", label = "Standard", tagKey = "standard"),
            SegmentOption(value = "express", label = "Express", tagKey = "express")
        ),
        selected = shipping,
        onSelect = { shipping = it },
        tagKey = tagKey
    )
}

@Composable
private fun HeardEvents(events: List<ProductEvent>) {
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        if (events.isEmpty()) {
            PantrixText(text = "The product has heard nothing yet", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        }
        events.take(5).forEach { event ->
            val properties = event.properties.entries.joinToString { (key, value) -> "$key=$value" }
            PantrixText(
                text = if (properties.isEmpty()) event.name else "${event.name} · $properties",
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
            )
        }
    }
}
```

### Consent

Until the user says yes, the connector collects no event. Once they do, the events wait in the queue and go when five of them wait, or with "Send now". When consent is taken back, what waits is dropped. Underneath is the connector's log, the newest on top.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.collectAsState
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.Consent
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.Outcome
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.ProductAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.SendPolicy
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.TrackingPlan
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.Transport
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlin.time.Clock
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.minutes

val connector = rememberConnector(online = { true })
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
var consent by remember { mutableStateOf(connector.consent) }
PantrixSwitchButton(
    checked = consent == Consent.Granted,
    onCheckedChange = { yes ->
        consent = if (yes) Consent.Granted else Consent.Denied
        connector.consent = consent
    },
    label = "Allow analytics",
    tagKey = "consent"
)
PantrixTheme(analytics = connector) {
    PantrixButton(text = "Like", onClick = {}, tagKey = "like")
}
PantrixButton(
    text = "Send now",
    onClick = { scope.launch { connector.flush() } },
    variant = ButtonVariant.Outline,
    tagKey = "send_now"
)
ConnectorLog(connector)

@Composable
private fun rememberConnector(
    online: () -> Boolean,
    policy: SendPolicy = SendPolicy(batch = 5, every = 1.minutes),
    consent: Consent = Consent.Unknown
): ProductAnalytics {
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    return remember(scope) {
        ProductAnalytics(
            plan = TrackingPlan(emptyList()),
            transport = Transport { online() },
            clock = Clock.System,
            scope = scope,
            policy = policy
        ).also { it.consent = consent }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ConnectorLog(connector: ProductAnalytics) {
    val log by connector.log.collectAsState()
    val waiting by connector.waitingEvents.collectAsState()
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        PantrixText(text = "Waiting: $waiting", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        log.asReversed().take(6).forEach { outcome ->
            PantrixText(
                text = outcome.line(),
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
            )
        }
    }
}

private fun Outcome.line(): String = when (this) {
    is Outcome.NotCollected -> "not collected · ${event.component} ${event.action} · no consent"
    is Outcome.Waiting -> "waiting · ${event.name}"
    is Outcome.Sent -> "sent · events: ${batch.size}"
    is Outcome.Failed -> "not sent · events: $size · again in $retryIn"
    is Outcome.Overflowed -> "dropped · the queue is full, the oldest"
    is Outcome.Withdrawn -> "dropped · events: $count · consent taken back"
}
```

### Offline

Turn the network off and press the button a few times: a send is tried every three events, fails, and is tried again after one, two, four seconds. The queue keeps six events; when it is full the oldest is dropped. Turn the network on: what waits goes at the next try, in the order it happened.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.collectAsState
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.switchbutton.PantrixSwitchButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.Consent
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.Outcome
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.ProductAnalytics
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.SendPolicy
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.TrackingPlan
import com.pantrixui.samples.analytics.Transport
import kotlin.time.Clock
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.minutes
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

var online by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
val connector = rememberConnector(
    online = { online },
    policy = SendPolicy(batch = 3, every = 1.minutes, capacity = 6, longestRetry = 8.seconds),
    consent = Consent.Granted
)
PantrixSwitchButton(checked = online, onCheckedChange = { online = it }, label = "Network", tagKey = "network")
PantrixTheme(analytics = connector) {
    PantrixButton(text = "Share", onClick = {}, tagKey = "share")
}
ConnectorLog(connector)

@Composable
private fun rememberConnector(
    online: () -> Boolean,
    policy: SendPolicy = SendPolicy(batch = 5, every = 1.minutes),
    consent: Consent = Consent.Unknown
): ProductAnalytics {
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    return remember(scope) {
        ProductAnalytics(
            plan = TrackingPlan(emptyList()),
            transport = Transport { online() },
            clock = Clock.System,
            scope = scope,
            policy = policy
        ).also { it.consent = consent }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ConnectorLog(connector: ProductAnalytics) {
    val log by connector.log.collectAsState()
    val waiting by connector.waitingEvents.collectAsState()
    Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.xs)) {
        PantrixText(text = "Waiting: $waiting", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
        log.asReversed().take(6).forEach { outcome ->
            PantrixText(
                text = outcome.line(),
                style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
                color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
            )
        }
    }
}

private fun Outcome.line(): String = when (this) {
    is Outcome.NotCollected -> "not collected · ${event.component} ${event.action} · no consent"
    is Outcome.Waiting -> "waiting · ${event.name}"
    is Outcome.Sent -> "sent · events: ${batch.size}"
    is Outcome.Failed -> "not sent · events: $size · again in $retryIn"
    is Outcome.Overflowed -> "dropped · the queue is full, the oldest"
    is Outcome.Withdrawn -> "dropped · events: $count · consent taken back"
}
```

## API

### PantrixAnalytics

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.analytics.PantrixAnalytics`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun interface PantrixAnalytics
```

Sink for `PantrixUiEvent`.

Defaults to a no-op, so the cost of components emitting events unconditionally is one virtual call into an empty body. Products wire their own SDK in through `PantrixTheme(analytics = ...)`; Pantrix itself depends on no analytics vendor.

A component built on a Pantrix control, as a field of dates on two text fields, hears that control's events beside its own, and one press is counted twice. It gives the control a sink of its own with `LocalPantrixAnalytics`, which drops what the component reports itself and hands the rest on under the component's name: `PantrixPageSize` does so with the select it is built on.

Members:

- `fun track(event: PantrixUiEvent)`: Called with each `event` a component emits, as it happens, on the UI thread. A sink hands the event on and returns: what takes time, sending above all, is done off this thread.

On the type:

- `PantrixAnalytics.NoOp: PantrixAnalytics`: The sink that drops every event: where a theme reports to unless it is given one.

# Test tags

The tag automation finds a component by: `Section.Component_key`. The tag comes from a key that is the same in every language, not from the visible text: the tests do not break when the app opens in another language.

## Features

- **Key.** A component's `tagKey`, and in a form-bound component the field's `id`: `PantrixButton(tagKey = "pay")` becomes `Button_pay`. Left out, a key is derived from the place of the call.
- **Section.** `TestScope("Checkout") { … }` puts the section's name in front of the tags in it; nested sections join: `Checkout.Payment.Button_pay`. `LocalTestScope` is the section at that point.
- **Policy.** `TestTagPolicy.Stable` tags, `Off` tags nothing; `PantrixTheme(testTagPolicy = …)` or `LocalTestTagPolicy`.
- **Your own component.** `rememberPantrixTestTag(component, tagKey)` gives a tag by the same rule, `Modifier.pantrixTestTag(tag)` sets it. The key of a control built on a component is `derivedTagKey`.
- **What a test looks for.** `pantrixTestTagOf(component, tagKey, scope)` gives the tag a component carries with a key and in a section, without building the screen: a test or a device automation flow looks for this tag.

## Examples

### A button in a section

A button's tag inside two sections. The button was given only `tagKey = "pay"`; the sections (`TestScope`) put their names in front of the tag. The line underneath builds the same tag with `rememberPantrixTestTag("Button", "pay")`, and reads the section from `LocalTestScope` and the policy from `LocalTestTagPolicy`.

```kotlin
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.LocalTestScope
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.LocalTestTagPolicy
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestScope
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.rememberPantrixTestTag
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

TestScope("Checkout") {
    TestScope("Payment") {
        PantrixButton(text = "Pay", onClick = {}, tagKey = "pay")
        val tag = rememberPantrixTestTag(component = "Button", tagKey = "pay")
        PantrixText(
            text = "Tag: $tag · section: ${LocalTestScope.current} · policy: ${LocalTestTagPolicy.current.name}",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
}
```

### Your own component's tag

The app's own component is tagged by the same rule: `PriceRow` builds its tag with `rememberPantrixTestTag` and sets it with `pantrixTestTag`. The button in it is built on the row: its key is `derivedTagKey("total", "edit")`, `total_edit`. The line underneath writes the tags.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.derivedTagKey
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.pantrixTestTag
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.rememberPantrixTestTag
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PriceRow(label = "Total", amount = "TRY 1,240", tagKey = "total")

@Composable
private fun PriceRow(
    label: String,
    amount: String,
    tagKey: String
) {
    val tag = rememberPantrixTestTag(component = "PriceRow", tagKey = tagKey)
    val editKey = derivedTagKey(tagKey, "edit")
    Row(
        modifier = Modifier.pantrixTestTag(tag),
        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(PantrixTheme.spacing.md),
        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
    ) {
        PantrixText(text = "$label: $amount")
        PantrixButton(text = "Edit", onClick = {}, tagKey = editKey)
    }
    PantrixText(
        text = "Row: $tag · the button's key: $editKey",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
    )
}
```

### A release with no tags

A release with no tags: a theme given `TestTagPolicy.Off` puts no tag in the tree. A component still knows its tag, and its events go with it: `rememberPantrixTestTag` builds the tag, `Modifier.pantrixTestTag` does not put it in the tree. A `Modifier.testTag` the app sets itself still stays: for the few tags an outside tool expects.

```kotlin
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestTagPolicy
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.rememberPantrixTestTag
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

PantrixTheme(testTagPolicy = TestTagPolicy.Off) {
    val tag = rememberPantrixTestTag(component = "Button", tagKey = "save")
    PantrixText(text = "The events' tag: $tag · in the tree: none", style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote)
}
```

### The tag a test looks for

The tag a test looks for, without building the screen: `pantrixTestTagOf("Button", "Save draft", scope = "Editor")`. The key goes into the tag in small letters, with `_` in the place of what is not a letter or a digit: `Editor.Button_save_draft`. It is the tag the button carries on the screen too.

```kotlin
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestScope
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.pantrixTestTagOf
import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.rememberPantrixTestTag
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

TestScope("Editor") {
    PantrixButton(text = "Save draft", onClick = {}, tagKey = "Save draft")
    val carried = rememberPantrixTestTag(component = "Button", tagKey = "Save draft")
    val lookedFor = pantrixTestTagOf(component = "Button", tagKey = "Save draft", scope = "Editor")
    PantrixText(
        text = "Looked for: $lookedFor · carried: $carried",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
    )
}
```

## API

### TestScope

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestScope`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun TestScope(
    name: String,
    content: @Composable () -> Unit
)
```

Names a screen or section so tags inside it are qualified: `TestScope("LoginScreen") { ... }`.

Nesting concatenates, which is what makes a tag readable in a test failure without the reader having to know where in the tree the component sat.

Parameters:

- `name: String`: the screen's or the section's name, put before the tags inside it: `LoginScreen.Button_save`.
- `content: @Composable () -> Unit`: the screen or the section, whose components' tags `name` qualifies.

### LocalTestScope

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.LocalTestScope`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalTestScope: ProvidableCompositionLocal<String?>
```

The enclosing `TestScope` chain, e.g. `Checkout.PaymentForm`.

### TestTagPolicy

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.TestTagPolicy`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
enum class TestTagPolicy
```

Whether components put their automation tags in the semantics tree, where tests and the platform's UI automation find them, and what they build a tag from.

Entries:

- `Stable`: The key — `tagKey`, or the field id in form-bound overloads — then the call-site key.
- `Off`: Pantrix puts no tag in the semantics tree. A component still knows its tag, and its analytics events carry it: a release build that keeps its tags out of the tree still tells its events apart. A `Modifier.testTag` the app sets itself is unaffected, which is how a release build keeps the few tags an external tool depends on.

### LocalTestTagPolicy

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.LocalTestTagPolicy`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalTestTagPolicy: ProvidableCompositionLocal<TestTagPolicy>
```

Whether the components here put their automation tags in the semantics tree: `PantrixTheme(testTagPolicy = …)`. Its readers follow it: a tag's node takes its tag out of the tree, or puts it back, when the policy around it changes.

### rememberPantrixTestTag

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.rememberPantrixTestTag`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberPantrixTestTag(
    component: String,
    tagKey: String? = null
): String
```

Produces a component's automation tag: `Scope.Component_key`.

The key is `tagKey` — form-bound overloads pass their field's id — and without one, the call-site key: `Scope.Component#1k3z9`. **Visible text is never a source**: a tag derived from translated text changes when the app runs in another language, which silently breaks every automation suite the moment a second locale ships.

There is deliberately no parameter for a finished tag. A caller that must match an id an external suite already uses sets it with Compose's own `Modifier.testTag` in the component's `modifier`, which replaces this tag in the semantics tree.

The tag is built whatever the `TestTagPolicy`: the component's analytics events carry it either way, and `pantrixTestTag` puts it in the semantics tree only while the policy is `TestTagPolicy.Stable`.

Parameters:

- `component: String`: component name, e.g. `Button`
- `tagKey: String?`: a locale-independent developer key, e.g. `save`: written in small letters and digits, of which the tag carries the first `MAX_TAG_KEY_LENGTH`. The key of a control built on this one is made with `derivedTagKey`.

### Modifier.pantrixTestTag

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.pantrixTestTag`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun Modifier.pantrixTestTag(tag: String?): Modifier
```

Sets `tag` as the test tag while the `TestTagPolicy` where it stands is `TestTagPolicy.Stable`, and nothing while it is `TestTagPolicy.Off` or for null: no node at all is added to the semantics tree then.

While the theme's diagnostics are on, a tag that two nodes of the window carry for a second and a half is reported as `PantrixCheck.DuplicateTestTag`: a test that looks for it would find them both. A page transition, which shows the page that goes and the one that comes with the same tags, is over before then.

Parameters:

- `tag: String?`

### derivedTagKey

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.derivedTagKey`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun derivedTagKey(
    tagKey: String,
    part: String
): String
```

The key of a control that another control is built on: the select of a page size, the menu of a breadcrumb. It is the outer control's own `tagKey` and, after it, `part`, the name of the inner one: `orders` and `page_size` are `orders_page_size`, and the select is tagged `Select_orders_page_size`.

A tag carries no more than the first `MAX_TAG_KEY_LENGTH` characters of a key. Joined by hand, a long key would lose the part's name to that cut, and two parts of one control would come to the same key. Here the outer key is what gives way: it is cut as short as leaves `part` whole.

Parameters:

- `tagKey: String`: the outer control's key, as its caller wrote it.
- `part: String`: what the inner control is in the outer one, in the letters a key is written in: `page_size`.

### pantrixTestTagOf

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.pantrixTestTagOf`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun pantrixTestTagOf(
    component: String,
    tagKey: String,
    scope: String? = null
): String
```

The automation tag a component given `tagKey` carries inside `scope`: what a test, or a flow of the platform's UI automation, finds it by. A `Button` given `save` is `Button_save`, and inside `TestScope("Checkout")` it is `Checkout.Button_save`. `rememberPantrixTestTag` builds a keyed tag with this, so a tag built here is the one the component carries.

Parameters:

- `component: String`: the component's name, e.g. `Button`.
- `tagKey: String`: the key the component was given, as its caller wrote it: the tag writes it in small letters and digits, as the component does.
- `scope: String?`: the chain of `TestScope`s the component stands in, e.g. `Checkout.PaymentForm`; null outside one.

# Diagnostics

Defects only a running screen can show: a theme whose diagnostics are on looks for them and hands what it finds to a sink. Pantrix does not know what kind of build it runs in; the app turns the diagnostics on in its own debug build. In this app the diagnostics are on, and they are turned off in "Settings".

## Features

- **Sink.** `PantrixTheme(diagnostics = …)`: `PantrixDiagnostics.Off`, the default, looks for nothing; `PantrixDiagnostics.Log` writes to the platform's log; `PantrixFindings` keeps the findings for tests and for the inspector. A theme inside can take a sink of its own; `LocalPantrixDiagnostics` is the sink at that point.
- **Six checks.** `PantrixCheck`: one tag on two nodes, colours that do not read, a squeezed touch target, a blank name, a theme with no strings for its language and a shadowed shortcut.
- **Finding.** `PantrixFinding`: its check, component, tag, section, English message and the values it measured.
- **When.** A finding is reported once while it lasts; one the layout finds once it has lasted half a second, a repeated tag once it has lasted a second and a half: a page transition shows two pages with the same tags together.
- **Your own component.** `Modifier.checkName` and `Modifier.checkContrast` (`ContrastPair`, `ContrastNeed`) bring a component into the checks; `contrastRatio` is the WCAG ratio of two colours.

## Examples

### Colours that do not read

A brand's pale colour with white written on it: the button's words are hard to read. The example's own theme keeps what it finds in a sink of its own and writes it underneath: the ratio, the ratio needed and the two colours.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonColors
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixFindings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val findings = remember { PantrixFindings() }
PantrixTheme(diagnostics = findings) {
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Send",
        onClick = {},
        colors = ButtonColors(container = Color(0xFFFFE082), content = Color.White),
        tagKey = "send"
    )
}
Found(findings)

@Composable
private fun Found(findings: PantrixFindings) {
    if (findings.all.isEmpty()) {
        PantrixText(
            text = "No findings yet.",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
    findings.all.forEach { finding ->
        PantrixText(text = finding.check.name, style = PantrixTheme.typography.callout)
        PantrixText(
            text = finding.message,
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
}
```

### One tag on two nodes

### A shadowed shortcut

A screen's root and a field inside it listen for the same shortcut: when the key is pressed the outer one runs, and the inner one never does.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.input.key.Key
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixFindings

import com.pantrixui.foundation.keyboard.onShortcut

import com.pantrixui.foundation.testing.rememberPantrixTestTag
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val findings = remember { PantrixFindings() }
val search = PantrixShortcut(Key.F, command = true)
PantrixTheme(diagnostics = findings) {
    Column(Modifier.onShortcut(search) {}) {
        val tag = rememberPantrixTestTag(component = "SearchBox", tagKey = "inner")
        PantrixText(
            text = "The inner field listens for the same shortcut too",
            modifier = Modifier.pantrixTestTag(tag).onShortcut(search) {}
        )
    }
}
Found(findings)

@Composable
private fun Found(findings: PantrixFindings) {
    if (findings.all.isEmpty()) {
        PantrixText(
            text = "No findings yet.",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
    findings.all.forEach { finding ->
        PantrixText(text = finding.check.name, style = PantrixTheme.typography.callout)

            text = finding.message,
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
}
```

### Checking a component of your own

A component of the app's own takes part in the checks too: `Swatch` tells its name with `checkName`, and the pair of its text and its ground with `checkContrast`. The line under it writes the ratio of the two colours with `contrastRatio`.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.background
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.ContrastNeed
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.ContrastPair
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixFindings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.checkContrast
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.checkName
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme
import com.pantrixui.foundation.token.color.contrastRatio

val findings = remember { PantrixFindings() }
PantrixTheme(diagnostics = findings) {
    Swatch(name = "Sand", fill = Color(0xFFF5E6C8), label = Color(0xFFB0A080))
}
Found(findings)

@Composable
private fun Swatch(
    name: String,
    fill: Color,
    label: Color
) {
    Column(
        modifier = Modifier
            .checkName("Swatch", name)
            .checkContrast("Swatch") { listOf(ContrastPair("label on fill", label, fill, ContrastNeed.Text)) }
            .background(fill)
            .padding(12.dp)
    ) {
        PantrixText(text = name, color = label)
    }
    PantrixText(
        text = "Ratio: ${(contrastRatio(label, fill) * 100).toInt() / 100f}",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
    )
}

@Composable
private fun Found(findings: PantrixFindings) {
    if (findings.all.isEmpty()) {
        PantrixText(
            text = "No findings yet.",
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
    findings.all.forEach { finding ->
        PantrixText(text = finding.check.name, style = PantrixTheme.typography.callout)
        PantrixText(
            text = finding.message,
            style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
            color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
        )
    }
}
```

### To the log and to a test

For a test or a log: `PantrixFindings(then = PantrixDiagnostics.Log)` both keeps the findings and writes them to the log. `LocalPantrixDiagnostics` is the theme's sink at that point; a finding's fields are read one by one.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.iconbutton.PantrixIconButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.LocalPantrixDiagnostics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixCheck
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixDiagnostics
import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixFindings
import com.pantrixui.foundation.icons.PantrixIcons
import com.pantrixui.foundation.theme.PantrixTheme

val findings = remember { PantrixFindings(then = PantrixDiagnostics.Log) }
PantrixTheme(diagnostics = findings) {
    PantrixIconButton(imageVector = PantrixIcons.Search, contentDescription = "", onClick = {}, tagKey = "search")
    val here = LocalPantrixDiagnostics.current
    PantrixText(
        text = "Is the sink here the one that keeps the findings: ${here === findings}",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote
    )
}
findings.all.forEach { finding ->
    val missing = finding.check == PantrixCheck.MissingName
    PantrixText(
        text = "${finding.check.name} · ${finding.component} · ${finding.testTag} · blank name: $missing",
        style = PantrixTheme.typography.footnote,
        color = PantrixTheme.colors.textSecondary
    )
}
```

## API

### PantrixDiagnostics

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixDiagnostics`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun interface PantrixDiagnostics
```

Where a theme's diagnostics send what they find.

`Off`, the default, turns the checks off as well: they return at their first line, and a release build pays next to nothing for them. Pantrix does not know what kind of build it runs in, so an app turns them on in its debug build: `PantrixTheme(diagnostics = if (debug) PantrixDiagnostics.Log else PantrixDiagnostics.Off)`. A test or an inspector keeps them with `PantrixFindings`.

A finding is reported once while it lasts, and again if it comes back after it was put right. A squeezed touch target, which a layout makes, is reported once it has lasted half a second: a row that opens squeezes what it holds for a moment. Two nodes with one tag are reported once they have lasted a second and a half, longer than a page transition, which shows the page that goes and the one that comes together.

Members:

- `fun report(finding: PantrixFinding)`: Called with each `finding` on the UI thread, outside composition and layout.

On the type:

- `PantrixDiagnostics.Off: PantrixDiagnostics`: Turns the checks off: nothing is looked for, and nothing is reported.
- `PantrixDiagnostics.Log: PantrixDiagnostics`: Writes each finding to the platform's log: Logcat on Android, the console on iOS and in a browser, and the standard error on the JVM.

### PantrixFindings

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixFindings`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
class PantrixFindings(
    private val then: PantrixDiagnostics = PantrixDiagnostics.Off
) : PantrixDiagnostics
```

Keeps what a theme's diagnostics find, for a test to read and for an inspector to show, and hands each finding on to `then` as well.

```kotlin
val findings = PantrixFindings()
setContent { PantrixTheme(diagnostics = findings) { CheckoutScreen() } }
assertEquals(emptyList(), findings.all)
```

Parameters:

- `then: PantrixDiagnostics`: Where each finding goes on to once it is kept: `PantrixDiagnostics.Log` writes it to the log too.

Members:

- `all: List<PantrixFinding>`: What has been found since this was made or last cleared, in the order it was found: the list as it is when read, which equals any list of the same findings. A finding that comes back after it was put right is kept once; read in a composition, the list is followed as it grows.
- `fun clear()`: Forgets what has been found.
- `fun boundsOf(finding: PantrixFinding): Rect?`: Where the node `finding` was made on is now, in the coordinates of the window it is drawn in: what an inspector outlines. Null where that node is gone, and for a finding made on no node, as one about a theme's colours.

### PantrixFinding

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixFinding`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
data class PantrixFinding(
    public val check: PantrixCheck,
    public val component: String?,
    public val testTag: String?,
    public val screen: String?,
    public val message: String,
    public val values: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()
)
```

What a check found: which check, where, and why.

Parameters:

- `check: PantrixCheck`: The check that found it.
- `component: String?`: The component it was found in, e.g. `Button`, or null where no component is known.
- `testTag: String?`: The automation tag of the node it was found on, or null where the node carries none.
- `screen: String?`: The enclosing `TestScope` chain, e.g. `Checkout.PaymentForm`, or null outside one.
- `message: String`: What is wrong and how it is put right, in English: a developer reads it, not the app's user.
- `values: Map<String, String>`: The measured values the message speaks of, such as the `ratio` a contrast has and the one it needs.

### PantrixCheck

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.PantrixCheck`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
enum class PantrixCheck
```

A kind of defect that only a running screen shows, which a theme's diagnostics look for while they are on.

Entries:

- `DuplicateTestTag`: Two nodes of one window carry the same automation tag, and a test that looks for it cannot tell which of them it found.
- `LowContrast`: A colour is hard to read on the colour it is drawn on: text under 4.5:1, large text and the mark of a control under 3:1, as WCAG 2.2 measures them.
- `SmallTouchTarget`: A control is laid out in less room than the platform's touch target, and answers to a press in less than it.
- `MissingName`: What a screen reader says for a control or a picture is blank.
- `NoStringsForLanguage`: The theme's language has no strings of its own, and the components speak English in it.
- `ShadowedShortcut`: A keyboard shortcut is heard first by a node around the one it is on, and never runs there.

### LocalPantrixDiagnostics

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.LocalPantrixDiagnostics`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
val LocalPantrixDiagnostics: ProvidableCompositionLocal<PantrixDiagnostics>
```

Where the checks of the components inside a theme send what they find: the theme's `diagnostics`.

A theme whose diagnostics change while its content is shown turns the checks of that content on or off at once.

### ContrastPair

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.ContrastPair`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
data class ContrastPair(
    public val what: String,
    public val foreground: Color,
    public val background: Color,
    public val need: ContrastNeed
)
```

A colour a component draws on another, and how readable it must be there.

Parameters:

- `what: String`: The pair's name in a finding, e.g. `label on container`.
- `foreground: Color`: The colour drawn: text, an icon, a mark.
- `background: Color`: The colour it is drawn on.
- `need: ContrastNeed`: How readable it must be.

### ContrastNeed

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.ContrastNeed`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
enum class ContrastNeed(
    public val ratio: Float
)
```

How readable a colour must be on the colour under it, as WCAG 2.2 asks.

Parameters:

- `ratio: Float`: The contrast it needs at the least, as `contrastRatio` measures it.

Entries:

- `Text`: Text: 4.5:1.
- `LargeText`: Text of 18pt and more, or of 14pt and more in bold: 3:1.
- `Mark`: What shows a control or its state without words, as a checkbox's box, a field's edge or a focus ring: 3:1.

### Modifier.checkContrast

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.checkContrast`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun Modifier.checkContrast(
    component: String,
    pairs: () -> List<ContrastPair>
): Modifier
```

Tells the theme's diagnostics, while they are on, which colours `component` draws on which: a pair that reads under what it needs is reported as `PantrixCheck.LowContrast`, once for the component and those colours however many of it show them. `pairs` is called only while the diagnostics are on, and again when they or the theme's colours change.

A background that lets through what is under it, as that of a button without a fill, is measured on the theme's background and on its surface, where the component stands on one of the theme's own grounds, and the lower of the two counts. On a fill of another colour, which gives what stands on it a content colour of its own, such a pair is not measured: what is under it is not known. Nor is a pair with an unspecified colour.

Parameters:

- `component: String`: The component's name in a finding, e.g. `Button`.
- `pairs: () -> List<ContrastPair>`: The colours it draws on which, in the state it is in. A disabled component, which no one is asked to read, gives none.

### Modifier.checkName

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.diagnostics.checkName`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun Modifier.checkName(
    component: String,
    name: String?
): Modifier
```

Tells the theme's diagnostics, while they are on, what a screen reader says for `component`: a blank `name` is reported as `PantrixCheck.MissingName`. A null name is no name given here, as for a picture that is only decoration or a control that is named by its text, and is not reported; a control that has no other name passes a blank one.

Parameters:

- `component: String`: The component's name in a finding, e.g. `IconButton`.
- `name: String?`: What a screen reader says for it: its `contentDescription`, its `label` or its `title`.

### contrastRatio

`import com.pantrixui.foundation.token.color.contrastRatio`, from `com.pantrixui:foundation`

```kotlin
fun contrastRatio(
    foreground: Color,
    background: Color
): Float
```

How far `foreground` stands out from `background`, as WCAG 2.2 measures it: the relative luminance of the lighter of the two over that of the darker, each plus 0.05. It runs from 1, for a colour on itself, to 21, for black on white. Text is read at 4.5 and more; large text and the mark of a control, as a checkbox's box, at 3 and more.

A `foreground` that lets the background through is measured as it is drawn: laid over `background`. The `background` is measured as it is given; one that lets through what is under it is laid over that first.

Parameters:

- `foreground: Color`
- `background: Color`

# Building blocks

The building blocks the library's components are built on: an app that writes its own layer, its own hint or its own control uses them too.

## Features

- **Portal.** `PantrixPortal { … }` composes its content at a root of the window, not where it is called: for a `Popup` or a `Dialog`. A layout that throws its content away while it measures cannot close the layer in the middle of a measurement.
- **Modal layer.** `PantrixModalLayer { … }` says its content is a layer that takes the keys and the presses until it closes: the focus rings under it are hidden (`PantrixTheme.isUnderModal`).
- **Comes up by itself.** `PantrixTransient(shown, onDismiss)` says something came up that no one opened, as a hint does: Escape puts it away wherever the focus is. A layer hears Escape inside itself with `pantrixTransientsRoot()`.
- **Automation root.** `Modifier.pantrixAutomationRoot()` opens the tags under it to the platform's automation. The theme does so for the app's window, and Pantrix's overlays for their own windows; the root of a `Popup` or a `Dialog` of your own, a window of its own on Android, carries it too.
- **Press indication.** `pantrixPressIndication()` draws a light veil in the content colour while pressed, `pantrixPressIndicationWithColor(color)` in the colour given; both are a `PantrixPressIndication`.
- **Conditional modifier.** `thenIfElse(condition, ifTrue, ifFalse)` goes on with a modifier chain by a condition.
- **Scroll bar.** `Modifier.pantrixVerticalScroll(state)` scrolls a column with Pantrix's scroll bar, and `Modifier.pantrixScrollBar(listState)` gives a lazy list its bar.

## Examples

### Your own layer

Your own layer: the button opens a `Popup` in the middle of the window. The popup is composed through a portal (`PantrixPortal`), its content is a modal layer (`PantrixModalLayer`), and it hears Escape inside itself (`pantrixTransientsRoot()`). While the layer is open the page's focus rings under it are not shown: the line under the button writes that the page is under a modal (`PantrixTheme.isUnderModal`). The layer's own content is not under it.

On Android the popup is a window of its own: the theme's mark that opens the tags to automation does not reach it. The layer's root says so itself (`pantrixAutomationRoot()`): a Maestro flow finds the "Close" button as `Button_close_layer`.

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.widthIn
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup
import androidx.compose.ui.window.PopupProperties
import com.pantrixui.components.container.surface.PantrixSurface
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.ButtonVariant
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.button.PantrixButton
import com.pantrixui.components.elements.text.PantrixText
import com.pantrixui.foundation.a11y.PantrixModalLayer
import com.pantrixui.foundation.overlay.PantrixPortal
```
