# Analytics Guide: Connecting the Components' Events to a Product

This document explains which events Pantrix's components report, what an event carries and what it never carries, and how an app connects these events to its own analytics product (Firebase, Amplitude, PostHog…). The problem is not Pantrix's own: **every** Compose Multiplatform app with analytics writes a class that turns the interface's events into the events that go to the product, and the real decisions are in that class. The library gives the events and the hook that takes them (section 2). The sample `samples/pantrix-analytics` gives that class with its tests and the shells of four platforms (section 3). Section 4 shows where the call of three products goes, and section 6 how an app without the library sets up the same class.

Everything said about the components and the sample was seen in tests that run in this repository, or on devices. The products' calls were read in their own documentation and were not run here. Which was seen where is written in section 7.

## 1. The Problem

A component library says "this button was pressed". What goes to the product is the app's decision:

*   **Under which name:** does the product see `Button click`, or `checkout_pay_tapped`? Names live in the product's reports for years, and must not change when a component's name changes.
*   **Never carrying what:** a text the user typed, a table row keyed by a person's name. Personal data once sent cannot be taken back.
*   **When:** a network request at every press costs battery and data. When the app goes to the background, the events waiting can be lost.
*   **With no network:** are the events thrown away, is their order kept, how large does the queue grow?
*   **With consent:** nothing must be collected before the user says yes. When they say no, the events waiting must not be sent either.
*   **In the release:** automation tags are taken out of the semantics tree in the release build, but the events must go on telling the components apart.

If these decisions are not made in one place, every screen sends its own event under its own name, personal keys leak into the product, and a network outage leaves gaps in the reports.

## 2. Pantrix's Events

### The event

Every component gives what the user did to the theme's analytics as a `PantrixUiEvent`:

| Field | What | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `component` | The name the component reports under | `Button`, `SegmentButton`, `Chart` |
| `action` | What happened | `click`, `select`, `toggle`, `open` |
| `testTag` | The component's automation tag | `Checkout.Button_pay` |
| `screen` | The `TestScope` chain, that is, the screen's name | `Checkout` |
| `props` | Values from a closed set | `variant=Solid`, `segment=express` |

```kotlin
PantrixTheme(analytics = PantrixAnalytics { event -> /* give it to the connector */ }) {
    App()
}
```

*   `track` is called on the UI thread the moment the event happens. The event has no time field: the connector stamps the time. `track` takes the event and returns; the sending is done off the UI thread.
*   If no analytics is given to the theme, the events are thrown away (`PantrixAnalytics.NoOp`).
*   The app's own event goes to the same place: `LocalPantrixAnalytics.current.track(PantrixUiEvent(…))`.

### Identity: the tag and the screen

*   `testTag` is built from the component's `tagKey`: `PantrixButton(tagKey = "pay")` inside `TestScope("Checkout")` becomes `Checkout.Button_pay`. A test or a plan finds the same tag without the screen being set up, with `pantrixTestTagOf("Button", "pay", scope = "Checkout")`.
*   The tag of a component without a `tagKey` is built from the place of the call (`Button#1k3z9`), and changes when the code changes. A component the product counts is given a `tagKey`.
*   **The release build:** `TestTagPolicy.Off` does not put the tags into the semantics tree. The component still knows its tag, and its events go with that tag. A `Modifier.testTag` the app puts on itself does not change the event.
*   `screen` comes from the `TestScope` chain, and does not depend on the tag policy.
*   **A page is a screen.** A `PantrixPageScaffold` given a `tagKey` puts what it holds inside `TestScope(tagKey)`: the events of the components on it are on the screen `orders`, and their tags start with `orders.`.

### What never goes into an event

*   **Text typed and read.** No text typed into a field, standing in a field or shown by a component goes into an event. This promise is held by a regression test in every component that takes text (`TypedTextIsNeverReportedTest`). The components it covers: `PantrixTextField`, `PantrixFilledTextField`, `PantrixAutoResizeTextField`, `PantrixFilledAutoResizeTextField`, `PantrixSecureTextField`, `PantrixFilledSecureTextField`, `PantrixDateTextField`, `PantrixDateFilledTextField`, `PantrixTimeTextField`, `PantrixTimeFilledTextField`, the search field of `PantrixSelect` and of `PantrixMultiSelect`, `PantrixCommandPalette`, the fields of `PantrixElasticDatePicker`, and the document and the search of `PantrixJsonView`. The test types a word into every field, then a number in its place, and leaves the field by the keyboard action and by giving the focus elsewhere. At the end it verifies that neither is in any field of any event.
*   **A free value.** An event's `props` carries only values of the three kinds below. The one value the user writes themselves is `PantrixPageJump`'s page number, and that is a number within the pagination's range.

### The three kinds of properties

| Kind | Keys | Personal? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pantrix's words and true/false values (20) | `action`, `checked`, `collapsed`, `copied`, `destructive`, `direction`, `duration`, `external`, `folded`, `format`, `part`, `reselected`, `revealed`, `selected`, `shown`, `state`, `to`, `tone`, `variant`, `via` | No: their values are the library's own words (`Solid`, `back`, `true`) |
| Numbers (8) | `block`, `cell`, `count`, `index`, `level`, `rejected`, `rows`, `size` | No |
| The app's keys (14) | `row`, `column`, `option`, `node`, `series`, `slice`, `stage`, `task`, `tile`, `destination`, `section`, `page`, `command`, `segment` | **They can be:** each is the key the app gives a thing |

`page` is of two kinds. In `PantrixCarousel`, `PantrixPagination` and `PantrixPageJump` it is a number, while in `PantrixBreadcrumb` it is the key the app gives the page. The sample therefore does not count it among Pantrix's values.

The components that send the app's keys:

| Key | Component | Its value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `row`, `column` | `PantrixDataTable` | The row's and the column's key |
| `option` | `PantrixSelect`, `PantrixMultiSelect` | The option's key |
| `node` | `PantrixTreeView`, `PantrixSankeyChart` | The node's key; in a Sankey, a flow is `source>target` |
| `series` | The charts with axes, `PantrixScatterChart`, `PantrixRadarChart`, `PantrixPolarChart` | The series' key |
| `slice` | `PantrixPieChart` | The slice's key |
| `stage` | `PantrixFunnelChart` | The stage's key |
| `task` | `PantrixGanttChart` | The task's key |
| `tile` | `PantrixTreemap` | The tile's key |
| `destination` | `PantrixNavigationBar`, `PantrixNavigationRail`, `PantrixSidebar` | The destination's key |
| `section` | `PantrixAccordion`, `PantrixSidebar` | The section's key |
| `page` | `PantrixBreadcrumb` | The page's key |
| `command` | `PantrixCommandPalette` | The command's key |
| `segment` | `PantrixSegmentButton` | The option's `tagKey`, or else its index |

The library always gives these keys to the theme's analytics; whether they go to the product is the connector's decision. In the components' tests the values of `row` were people's names (`ada`, `grace`): every event of a table that keys its users by name carries that name.

### Events that come without the user doing anything

| Component | Event | When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PantrixCarousel` | `change`, `via=auto` | When it turns by itself |
| `PantrixSnackbarHost` | `dismiss`, `via=timeout` | When its time runs out |
| `PantrixElasticDatePicker` | `autoRefresh` | When it refreshes by itself |
| `PantrixDialog`, `PantrixSheet`, `PantrixMenu`, `PantrixPopover`, `PantrixCommandPalette` | `open` | When the program opens it, too |
| `PantrixPageScaffold`, `PantrixLazyPageScaffold` | `show` | Each time a page with a `tagKey` comes into the composition: a screen's view |

A connector that does not want to count these as the user's interaction looks at `via`, or gives them a separate name in its plan.

The components not in the table do not report events themselves; the components inside them report their own: `PantrixTopBar`'s back button (`PantrixBackButton`) is a `PantrixIconButton`, and reports that one's event.

## 3. The Connector

The connector is the `PantrixAnalytics` given to the theme: it takes Pantrix's events and builds the events that go to the product itself. The sample's connector is `ProductAnalytics`, and all the decisions are gathered in its constructor:

```kotlin
@Composable
fun App() {
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    val analytics = remember(scope) {
        ProductAnalytics(
            plan = CHECKOUT_PLAN,            // which event under which name, with which values
            transport = productTransport,    // the one call that gives to the product (section 4)
            clock = Clock.System,            // the moment the event happened
            scope = scope,                   // the timer and the sending stop with the screen
            policy = SendPolicy()            // batches of 20, 30 seconds, a queue of 500 events
        )
    }
    // On going to the background the waiting events are sent: there may be no other chance.
    LifecycleEventEffect(Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP) { scope.launch { analytics.flush() } }
    PantrixTheme(analytics = analytics, testTagPolicy = TestTagPolicy.Off) {
        CheckoutScreen()
    }
}
```

### The tracking plan

```kotlin
val CHECKOUT_PLAN = TrackingPlan(
    listOf(
        PlannedEvent(pantrixTestTagOf("IconButton", "more", "Checkout"), "click", "quantity_increased"),
        PlannedEvent(
            tag = pantrixTestTagOf("SegmentButton", "shipping", "Checkout"),
            action = "select",
            name = "shipping_chosen",
            notPersonal = setOf("segment")
        ),
        PlannedEvent(
            tag = pantrixTestTagOf("Button", "pay", "Checkout"),
            action = "click",
            name = "checkout_pay_tapped",
            keep = setOf("variant")
        )
    )
)
```

*   The plan recognises an event by its component's tag and its action. The tag is built by `pantrixTestTagOf`, and it is the same as the tag the component on the screen carries.
*   `keep` says which of Pantrix's values go with the event. `notPersonal` says which of the app's keys are not personal. A planned event carries only what these two count.
*   While it is being built, the plan checks three things: no two events are given to the same tag and action; no tag built from the place of the call (one carrying `#`) is in the plan; `keep` counts only Pantrix's values. Writing one of the app's keys into `keep` is an error in the constructor: the key passes only with `notPersonal`, that is, by saying it is not personal.

### The general event

Every event the plan does not name goes as a single `ui_interaction`, and carries these: `ui_component`, `ui_action`, `ui_screen`, `ui_tag` (only if it was built from a key), and Pantrix's words and numbers. The app's keys and the tags built from the place of the call do not go in.

There are two reasons for a single general event. Products limit the separate event names (500 in Firebase), and a name for each component would share that limit with the plan's names. And in the product's reports only the plan's names show in the product's language; the rest is filtered in one place.

### Consent

`Consent` has three values: `Unknown`, `Granted`, `Denied`. Until it is `Granted` no event enters the queue, and each is entered in the log as "not collected". When consent is taken back, the waiting events are thrown away and the timers stop. A batch on its way at that moment, if it fails, is not tried again but thrown away. The product's own SDK has its consent too, and the two must change together (section 4).

### Sending and time

*   `track` stamps the event with its time, puts it in the queue and returns. There is no network on the UI thread.
*   A batch goes in three cases: when `SendPolicy.batch` events have gathered, when the first event has waited `SendPolicy.every`, and when the app says `flush()`. While nothing waits, nothing wakes up.
*   The sending is done on `sendOn` (`Dispatchers.Default`), and only one batch is on its way at a time. The dispatcher of `scope` is the UI's: between `track` and the sending, the events change hands on that single thread.

### With no network

*   A failed batch is put back at the head of the queue, in its order, and the events reach the product in the order they happened.
*   The retry is made after `firstRetry` (1 second), doubles at every failure, and is at most `longestRetry` (5 minutes). A sending that succeeds starts the waits from the beginning.
*   The queue holds `capacity` (500) events. When it is full the oldest is thrown away and counted in the log.
*   The sample's queue is in memory: if the process dies, the waiting events are lost. If there is an SDK that writes the events to disk, leaving the queue to it is sturdier (section 4).

## 4. Connecting to the Product

The connector's one point of contact with the product is `Transport`:

```kotlin
fun interface Transport {
    /** Gives [batch] to the product: true if it arrived. */
    suspend fun send(batch: List<ProductEvent>): Boolean
}
```

A `ProductEvent` has a name (`name`), properties (`properties`, all `String`) and a time (`at`). If the sender returns false or throws an error, the batch waits and is tried again.

### SDKs with a queue of their own

The three SDKs below all gather the events themselves and send them batch by batch. The connector's queue is then a second queue. The recommended setup: keep the plan and the consent in the connector, give every event to the SDK at once (`SendPolicy(batch = 1)`), and leave the gathering, the retrying and the sending in the background to the SDK. The sender returns true when the SDK has taken the event.

### Firebase (Android)

```kotlin
val transport = Transport { batch ->
    batch.forEach { event ->
        Firebase.analytics.logEvent(event.name) {
            event.properties.forEach { (key, value) -> param(key, value) }
        }
    }
    true
}
```

*   Setup: `implementation(platform("com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:…"))` and `implementation("com.google.firebase:firebase-analytics")`.
*   Limits: an event carries at most 25 parameters. Parameter names are at most 40 characters, start with a letter and hold only letters, digits and underscores. Text values are at most 100 characters (500 in Google Analytics 360). At most 500 separate event names can be used. The prefixes `firebase_`, `google_` and `ga_` are reserved. The general event's `ui_` names keep these rules. The `ui_tag` of a component under many nested `TestScope`s can come close to 100 characters: such a component that the product counts is written into the plan under its own name.
*   Consent: `setAnalyticsCollectionEnabled(false)` turns collecting off. With `setConsent`, `ANALYTICS_STORAGE` is denied. They are called together with the connector's `consent`.

### Amplitude (Android, Kotlin SDK)

```kotlin
val amplitude = Amplitude(AMPLITUDE_API_KEY, applicationContext) {
    flushQueueSize = 20          // its default is 30
    flushIntervalMillis = 30000  // its default is 30000
}
val transport = Transport { batch ->
    batch.forEach { event ->
        amplitude.track(event.name, mutableMapOf<String, Any?>().apply { putAll(event.properties) })
    }
    true
}
```

*   Consent: while `amplitude.optOut = true`, the SDK neither keeps nor sends events.
*   `amplitude.flush()` sends the waiting events at once: the connector's `flush()` can call it too.

### PostHog (Android)

```kotlin
PostHogAndroid.setup(context, PostHogAndroidConfig(apiKey = POSTHOG_API_KEY, host = POSTHOG_HOST))
val transport = Transport { batch ->
    batch.forEach { event -> PostHog.capture(event = event.name, properties = event.properties) }
    true
}
```

*   Gathering: `flushAt` (by default 20 events) and `flushIntervalSeconds` (by default 30). `PostHog.flush()` sends the waiting events at once, but by its documentation does not guarantee the sending.
*   Consent: `PostHog.optOut()`, or `config.optOut = true` before the setup.

### The other platforms

The products' iOS and web SDKs are written in Swift and in JavaScript. Common code calls them in two ways:

*   **`expect`/`actual`:** `expect fun productTransport(): Transport` in common code, and on each platform an `actual` that calls that platform's SDK. On the web the SDK's JavaScript interface is called from Kotlin with `external` declarations.
*   **A function from the shell:** the platform's shell gives common code a plain function, and the sender calls it. On iOS, something like `MainViewController(onEvent: { name, properties in Analytics.logEvent(name, parameters: properties) })`. Kotlin's type `(String, Map<String, String>) -> Unit` is a closure in Swift. There is no need to implement a `suspend` interface in Swift.

## 5. Testing

*   **The connector's decisions:** inside `runTest`, with `scope = backgroundScope` and `sendOn = StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler)`. The timer and the retry run in the test's virtual time: with `advanceTimeBy(policy.every - 1.milliseconds)` one says "it did not go before its time", and with 2 milliseconds more, "it went". The clock is `TestClock` (`com.pantrixui.testing`). The sample's `ProductAnalyticsTest` (15 tests) holds each decision in a test of its own.
*   **The plan:** the way from a Pantrix event to the product's event is a pure function (`TrackingPlan.productEventOf`), and is tested without a screen (`TrackingPlanTest`).
*   **A screen's events:** `PantrixTestTheme(analytics = RecordingAnalytics())` keeps what the components report, in order: `eventsOf("Button")` (the testing guide).
*   **The screen and the connector together:** in a UI test the connector is given `sendOn = Dispatchers.Unconfined`. In the browser there is one thread, and while `waitUntil` waits, `Dispatchers.Default` gets no turn: the sending never happens, and the test runs into its timeout. The sample's `SampleScreenTest` also verifies that what was typed into the promotion code is in no batch.
*   **Like a release build:** on a screen set up with `TestTagPolicy.Off`, it is tested that the semantics tree has no Pantrix tag and that the plan's event still comes.
*   The sample's tests: `./gradlew :samples:pantrix-analytics:shared:jvmTest`, `iosSimulatorArm64Test`, `jsBrowserTest`, `wasmJsBrowserTest`, and `connectedAndroidDeviceTest` while a device or an emulator is connected.

## 6. Without the Library

The one part of the connector bound to Pantrix is `track(event: PantrixUiEvent)`, which takes the event, and the four fields the plan reads from that event (`component`, `action`, `testTag`, `screen`), with `props`. An app that takes events from another source writes `productEventOf` with its own event type. The queue, the consent, the sending and `Transport` stay as they are: the sample's files `ProductAnalytics.kt`, `SendPolicy.kt`, `Transport.kt` and `Consent.kt` are not bound to Compose either.

## 7. What Was Verified and What Was Not

### Verified

*   **The inventory of events:** the components' JVM tests (4896 tests, `c808f18b`) were run in a trial lane, with every event that passed through the test theme written to a file: 2537 events, 134 (name, action) pairs from 65 names. Section 2's table was written from these events and from the sources. The `select` of the date and time fields was read in `date/common/PickerField.kt`, and the search fields' `clear` in the shared search field of `SelectList.kt`. `autoRefresh` later took the place of `auto_refresh`.
*   **No text goes in:** `TypedTextIsNeverReportedTest` (15 tests) was tried with two fake fields that leak the text at the keyboard action and on leaving the field, and caught both.
*   **The tag under `TestTagPolicy.Off`:** `TestTagTest` and `OwnTestTagTest`. The test that checks the event's tag failed with empty tags on the old code.
*   **The connector:** the sample's 22 tests passed on five targets: the JVM, Android (an emulator, API 33), the iOS simulator, JS and Wasm. The connector was broken on purpose in 12 separate places, and every break was caught by at least one test: the consent, the doubling wait, the queue's limit, the timer, `flush`, the order, one batch at a time, the reset of the waits, the general event's values and the call-site tag.
*   **The app:** it was opened in the iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator, the Pixel 7 Pro emulator (API 33), the browser (Wasm) and on the desktop. The flow of consent, quantity, shipping, promotion code, payment and "Send now" was tried. The promotion code typed was not in the JSON sent.

### Read, not run

*   **Firebase:** the `logEvent` builder and the setup from the Android documentation ("Log events", "Get started"); the limits from Firebase's Swift reference (the `Analytics` class); the consent calls from the Kotlin reference (`FirebaseAnalytics.ConsentType`). A length limit for an event's name could not be found on Firebase's own pages; the names are kept short and in `snake_case` in the plan.
*   **Amplitude:** the Android Kotlin SDK page (setup, `track`, `optOut`, `flushQueueSize`, `flushIntervalMillis`, `flush`). The type of `track`'s property parameter was taken from the documentation's example (`MutableMap<String, Any?>`).
*   **PostHog:** the Android page (setup, `capture`, `optOut`, `flush`, `flushAt`, `flushIntervalSeconds`).
*   None of the three products is a dependency in this repository: the calls were not compiled and not run. Giving a function from the shell on iOS and `external` declarations on the web were not tried either.
*   The documents were read on 2026-10-24.

# Guide to Exporting a Chart as a File

This document explains how a Pantrix chart is exported as PNG, SVG and PDF, what the library does and what it leaves to the app, how the file made reaches the user on each platform, and the limits of the three kinds of file.

The chart **makes** the file and **hands** it to the app; it does not save it, share it or download it. Foundation's `FileSaver` gives it to the user, with each platform's window for saving a file (section 3); the share sheet is the app's.

Everything said here of the library was seen in tests that run in this repository, or by looking at the files made; which was seen where is written in section 6. The two pieces for sharing in section 3 are the demo's old code, and compiled on four platforms; where they were tried is in section 6.

## 1. Use

Exporting is a parameter: in a chart given no `export`, nothing shows.

```kotlin
PantrixLineChart(
    data = months,
    x = { it.name },
    values = revenue,
    export = ChartExport(fileName = "revenue") { file ->
        // file.name = "revenue.svg", file.mimeType = "image/svg+xml", file.bytes = the content
        share(file)
    }
)
```

Given `export`, an export button comes up among the chart's own buttons (beside the zoom buttons where there are any). The reader presses the button and chooses the kind; the chart makes the file and hands it to `onExport`.

| Field | What it says | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `formats` | The kinds the reader chooses from, in their order. Where one kind is given, no choice opens: the button makes that file | All three: PNG, SVG, PDF |
| `fileName` | The file's name, without its extension | `"chart"` |
| `scale` | The PNG's pixels to a dp. It does not depend on the screen's density | `2f` |
| `background` | The picture's ground. `Color.Unspecified` is the theme's `background`; `Color.Transparent` draws no ground | The theme's ground |
| `padding` | The room the picture leaves around the chart, on each side. The ground is under the room too | `12.dp` |
| `onExport` | The `ChartExportFile` made is handed to it | Required |

`export` is in `PantrixChart` and the six short charts above it (line, area, bar, range, waterfall, candlestick), and in every one of the other fourteen kinds: pie, gauge, progress circle, meter group, status tracker, sparkline, scatter, radar, polar, heatmap, treemap, funnel, sankey and Gantt. In each it is at the end of the signature; in `PantrixProgressCircle` alone it comes before `content`, so that the last lambda stays the content inside the ring.

The button stands in a row above the chart, on the side where the lines end. In a chart with axes it is in the same row as the zoom buttons. A chart given no height grows by this row; a chart given a height keeps its height, and its drawing is that much shorter.

## 2. What Is in the File

The file shows the chart **as it is on the screen**:

*   A series taken out from the legend is out in the file too (it stands faint in the legend).
*   Of a chart that is looked at closer (`zoom`), the part in view goes into the file.
*   The place pointed at, the tooltip, the zoom buttons and the navigator's strip are **not** in the file.
*   The legend, wherever it stands on the screen, is under the plot in the file. So is the colour scale of a heatmap and of a treemap with a scale: the least value, the colours' run and the greatest value, from the side where the lines start.
*   Content the caller gives as a composable is not in the file: the `center` in a pie's hole, the `center` in a gauge's middle, the `content` inside a progress circle. The value the gauge writes in its middle itself is in the file. The line under a status tracker that writes the name of the block shown is not in the file either.
*   There is `padding`'s room around the chart. The chart's box on the screen ends where its text ends (the room around it is given by the card it stands in); in a picture with no room, an axis's numbers stand right at the picture's edge.
*   A file taken while the entry animation runs shows the chart's end state too.

The three kinds are made from the same drawing; the differences between them are these:

| Kind | What | Text | Size (a chart of two series over twelve months) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PNG | A picture of pixels; as sharp as `scale` | In the app's typeface, as on the screen | Tens of kilobytes |
| SVG | Lines and shapes; sharp at every size | Real text (`<text>`), in the sans-serif typeface of whoever opens the file | A few kilobytes |
| PDF | One page, lines and shapes; sharp at every size | Real text in Helvetica; a line Helvetica cannot write as a picture | A few kilobytes |

### Why the Text Differs From the Screen's

SVG and PDF do not carry the app's typeface: the library does not have the typeface's file. In SVG the text is written in the sans-serif typeface of the program that opens the file, in PDF in Helvetica, which every PDF reader has. These typefaces' letters can be narrower or wider than the app's; each line is written in the **middle** of the room it takes on the screen. A number beside an axis may therefore stand a pixel or two closer to the axis, or farther from it.

In PDF, Helvetica writes the letters of the Western European languages and of Turkish (for Turkish's six letters the file carries an encoding of its own). A line that holds a letter Helvetica cannot write (an Arabic name, the sign `₺`) is put on the page as **its own picture**: four times as sharp as the screen's density, but not endlessly sharp like everything else, and it cannot be selected as text.

## 3. Getting the File to the User

`onExport` takes a `ChartExportFile`: `name`, `mimeType`, `format`, `bytes`. Foundation's `FileSaver` gives it to the user: each platform's window for saving a file (the files guide, 3.4).

| Platform | The usual way | What it asks for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Android | "Save as" (`ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT`), `FileSaver`'s way; or the share sheet (`Intent.ACTION_SEND`) | To save, an `Activity`'s result; to share, a `FileProvider` in the manifest |
| iOS | Exporting to Files (`UIDocumentPickerViewController`), `FileSaver`'s way; or the share sheet (`UIActivityViewController`) | A temporary file, and a view controller to present the window |
| Desktop | The save dialog | Nothing |
| Web | The browser's download | Nothing |

`FileSaver` does not open the share sheet: on Android sharing needs a `FileProvider` and a file of paths, and were the library to declare them in its own manifest, every app that uses the library would get a provider. An app that wants to give the file to a message or an email opens the sheet itself, as the two pieces below do.

The export example among the chart examples (`ChartExported`) first shows the file made, and hands it to the library's saver with the button "Save the file" too:

```kotlin
val saver = rememberFileSaver()
PantrixLineChart(
    // ...
    export = ChartExport { file ->
        saver.save(PantrixFile(file.name, file.bytes, file.mimeType)) { result -> saved = result }
    }
)
```

The two pieces below were the demo's own saver until 2026-10-28 (the package `com.pantrixui.cmp.demo.platform` in `app/shared`); they were taken out when the demo moved to the library's saver, and stay here for an app that wants to share.

### Android: the share sheet

```kotlin
val context = LocalContext.current
// save:
val folder = File(context.cacheDir, "exports").apply { mkdirs() }
val file = File(folder, name).apply { writeBytes(bytes) }
val uri = FileProvider.getUriForFile(context, context.packageName + ".files", file)
val send = Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND)
    .setType(mimeType)
    .putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_STREAM, uri)
    .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION)
context.startActivity(Intent.createChooser(send, name))
```

The app chosen in the sheet reads the file by the address the `FileProvider` gives. The provider is declared in the app's manifest and opens only one folder of the cache:

```xml
<!-- AndroidManifest.xml, inside <application> -->
<provider
    android:name="androidx.core.content.FileProvider"
    android:authorities="${applicationId}.files"
    android:exported="false"
    android:grantUriPermissions="true">
    <meta-data
        android:name="android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS"
        android:resource="@xml/file_paths" />
</provider>
```

```xml
<!-- res/xml/file_paths.xml -->
<paths>
    <cache-path name="exports" path="exports/" />
</paths>
```

`FileProvider` is in the library `androidx.core` (`androidx.core.ktx`, added to the app's `androidMain`). The manifest's `authorities` has to be the same as the address in the code; if it is not, `getUriForFile` throws. So it does if the file is outside the folder.

### iOS: the share sheet

```kotlin
val path = NSTemporaryDirectory() + name
val data = if (bytes.isEmpty()) {
    NSData()
} else {
    bytes.usePinned { NSData.create(bytes = it.addressOf(0), length = bytes.size.toULong()) }
}
data.writeToFile(path, atomically = true)
var top = UIApplication.sharedApplication.keyWindow?.rootViewController
while (top?.presentedViewController != null) top = top.presentedViewController
val sheet = UIActivityViewController(listOf(NSURL.fileURLWithPath(path)), null)
sheet.popoverPresentationController?.sourceView = top?.view
top?.presentViewController(sheet, animated = true, completion = null)
```

"Save to Files" is in the sheet too. The sheet is presented from the topmost view controller: a controller that is presenting another refuses a second presentation. On an iPad the sheet is presented as a popover, and asks what it is anchored to (`popoverPresentationController.sourceView`). The address of an empty array cannot be given to `NSData.create`: an empty file is written apart.

## 4. What to Know

*   **The file is made with the press, on the main thread.** In a chart of twelve places it is not noticed. The vector file of a chart of tens of thousands of points, with its thinned line, can be hundreds of kilobytes, and making it can take longer than a frame; how long was not measured.
*   **An area fill with a gradient** is a real gradient in SVG, and in PDF is written as the colours with a grey mask beside them: the bars under it look as they do on the screen.
*   **Every number of the PDF is written in the page's own unit**; the page is not scaled and moved as a whole. macOS's drawing of PDF (Preview, Quick Look) drew a mask set up under a scaled page at the wrong size, and the gradient fill vanished; this would have shown in a file made on every device whose screen density is not 1 (every phone).
*   **The file of a chart with no values says "No data".** Where the chart is given content of its own with `empty`, that content is on the screen alone: a composable cannot be drawn into a file, so the file writes the theme's words.
*   **In the dark theme** the file's ground is dark too, and its text light. For a file to be printed on paper, `background = Color.White` is not enough: the text's colour comes from the theme. Such a file should be made in the light theme.
*   **Motion and the look.** The file is the size the chart last settled at on the screen: a file made on a narrow phone is narrow, one made in a wide window wide.
*   **SVG and PDF cannot be made in Android's host tests (Robolectric).** A drawing's path is read step by step with Compose's path iterator, which on Android loads the native library of `androidx.graphics.path`. The library comes with the app (it is there on a device and an emulator), and not on the machine the tests run on: a Robolectric test that presses the button and chooses SVG or PDF fails with `UnsatisfiedLinkError`. A PNG is made there too.

## 5. Automation and Reporting

The export button's tag is `.Export` after the chart's own tag: `Chart_<tagKey>.Export`, `PieChart_<tagKey>.Export`, `Gantt_<tagKey>.Export` and the others. Where a choice of kind opens, its rows' tags are `.Export_png`, `.Export_svg` and `.Export_pdf`. When a file is made, an `export` event is reported with the chart's own component name (`Chart`, `PieChart`, `Gauge`, `Gantt` …); its `format` property is the file's extension (`png`, `svg`, `pdf`). The file's name and content are not reported.

## 6. How It Was Verified

| What | Where |
| :--- | :--- |
| The drawing kept as lines, shapes and words; how SVG and PDF are written; the PDF's table of parts and the length of its streams | `ChartExportFilesTest` (the desktop, the iOS simulator and the two browser targets) |
| The button, the choice of kind and its closing, the file's name and type, the PNG's size in pixels, the ground, the room, the screen's density, the part in view, a series taken out, dashed lines, marks, value labels, an axis's title, the picture of an Arabic name in the PDF | `ChartExportTest` (the same four targets) |
| The picture's legend: lines, centring, sample and name, right to left, a line by the tallest name | `ChartExportLegendTest` (the same four targets) |
| The other fourteen kinds: the button's place, each kind's file's name, event and text, the place pointed at not being in the file, the middle of the pie and of the gauge, the heatmap's scale and right to left, the button row's relation to the height | `ChartExportKindsTest` (the same four targets) |
| The other kinds on the web | On 2026-10-15 the PNGs of a pie, a heatmap, a gauge, a progress circle, a sparkline and a Gantt were made in the web demo and compared with the screen (the tooltip of the cell under the mouse was not in the file); their SVGs and PDFs were not opened in a browser |
| The PNG's pixels: the ground around, the chart inside | `ChartExportDesktopTest` (the desktop, read back with Skia), `ChartExportOnAndroidTest` (Android, Robolectric: with Android's own bitmap) |
| The look of the three kinds | The files made on the desktop were looked at with macOS's drawing (Quick Look, `sips`): screen densities 1 and 2.75 |
| Making them on Android | In the emulator (screen density 3.5) the three kinds were made; the PNG was shown back in the demo, and the three files were taken off the device and drawn on macOS |
| Making them on iOS | In the simulator (screen density 3) the three kinds were made; the PNG was shown back in the demo, and the three files were taken off the simulator and drawn on macOS |
| The pieces for sharing in section 3 | Compiled on four platforms as the demo's old saver. In the iOS simulator, PDF was chosen and "Save the file" pressed: the share sheet opened with the file's name, type and size ("visits", PDF, 5 KB), and "Save to Files" was in the sheet; it was not saved anywhere. Where the library's saver was tried is in the files guide |

Not verified: the files of a chart with axes could not be looked at on the web (the browser pane was not on the screen; the tests run in a browser, but a file made was not opened in a browser); of the other kinds, only the PNG was looked at on the web, and their files were not looked at on Android and iOS; the PDF was not looked at in the drawing of Adobe Acrobat, Chrome and Firefox (only in macOS's); the SVG was not looked at in a browser and in a drawing program (only in macOS's Quick Look); the piece for sharing on Android in section 3 was only compiled, not tried; printed output was not looked at; it was not tried on a real phone.

# Guide to Copying Plain Text to the Clipboard

This document explains why copying a text to the clipboard is not a single call in Compose Multiplatform, what the library gives for it, what a copy button should say and when, and how this is tested. The problem is not Pantrix's own: it is seen the same way in **every** Compose Multiplatform project that has a "copy" button in its common code. Section 3 of the document gives the solution with Pantrix's API, section 4 without the library, in a form that can be copied into any project.

Everything said here about Compose was read in the sources of Compose Multiplatform 1.12.1 or seen in a test that runs in this repository; which was seen where is written in sections 7 and 8. What could not be verified is counted apart in section 8.

## 1. The Problem

### Symptom

*   In common code it used to be one line: `LocalClipboardManager.current.setText(AnnotatedString(text))`. This interface was deprecated; the compiler says "Use LocalClipboard instead which supports suspend functions".
*   `LocalClipboard`, which came in its place, has no call for "copy this text". The one write call is `setClipEntry(clipEntry: ClipEntry?)`, and a `ClipEntry` cannot be built in common code.
*   The call suspends (`suspend`): it cannot be called straight from a button's `onClick`; it needs a coroutine.
*   How a copy ends changes from platform to platform. The browser can refuse the write; on a page not in a secure context nothing is copied, and no one says so; on Android 13 and above the system shows what was copied itself. A button that says "copied" the moment it is pressed says something wrong in all three.

### Cause

`ClipEntry` is only a name in common code: `expect class ClipEntry { val clipMetadata: ClipMetadata }` (`ClipboardManager.kt`). Its constructor and everything in it are in the platform's own declaration (Compose Multiplatform 1.12.1; on Android, `androidx.compose.ui` 1.12.1):

| Platform | What `ClipEntry` is there | How plain text is built | Mark |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Android | A class that wraps a `ClipData`: `ClipEntry(val clipData: ClipData)` | `ClipEntry(ClipData.newPlainText(label, text))` | None |
| Desktop (JVM) | A class that wraps an object: `ClipEntry(nativeClipEntry: Any)`. The clipboard reads it as a `java.awt.datatransfer.Transferable` | `ClipEntry(StringSelection(text))` | The constructor is `@ExperimentalComposeUiApi` |
| iOS | Compose's own class; its constructor is `internal` | `ClipEntry.withPlainText(text)` | `@ExperimentalComposeUiApi` |
| Web, `js` | `ClipEntry(clipboardItems: Array<ClipboardItem>)` | `ClipEntry.withPlainText(text)` | The constructor is experimental, `withPlainText` is not |
| Web, `wasmJs` | `ClipEntry(clipboardItems: JsArray<ClipboardItem>)` | `ClipEntry.withPlainText(text)` | The constructor is experimental, `withPlainText` is not |

Source files: `AndroidClipboardManager.android.kt`, `PlatformClipboard.desktop.kt`, `PlatformClipboard.ios.kt`, `PlatformClipboard.js.kt`, `PlatformClipboard.wasm.kt`.

Three details make the work bigger:

1.  **The two web targets are two separate declarations.** `ClipEntry` is declared separately for `js` and for `wasmJs`; the source set the two share (`webMain`) sees only the empty declaration in common code. The counterpart of an `expect` function is therefore written five times: Android, iOS, desktop, JS, Wasm.
2.  **Experimental marks.** The desktop's constructor and iOS's `withPlainText` carry `@ExperimentalComposeUiApi`; every place that uses them needs `@OptIn`.
3.  **Writing suspends, because it does in the browser.** The browser's clipboard returns a `Promise`; Compose waits for it, and if it is rejected the error is thrown from that call. The old interface started the write in the browser and did not wait for its result (`JsPlatformClipboardManager.setText`); its read, too, always returned empty there (`getText(): AnnotatedString? = null`). It was an interface that could not tell the result.

### How the Platforms Finish the Write

| Platform | What Compose does | What can go wrong |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Android | `ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip(clipData)` | The system service's error is thrown from the call as a `RuntimeException` (`rethrowFromSystemServer`, the Android SDK's source) |
| Desktop | `setContents(transferable, owner)` on the system's clipboard | `IllegalStateException` if the clipboard is not available at that moment (the JDK's documentation). In a headless JVM (`java.awt.headless=true`) there is no clipboard: the write is silently skipped |
| iOS | `UIPasteboard.generalPasteboard.string = text` | No error path in the source |
| Web | If the full clipboard interface is there, `navigator.clipboard.write([ClipboardItem])`, and if not, `writeText(text)`; both are waited for | If the browser refuses, the error is thrown from the call. In an insecure context there is no clipboard: the write is silently skipped, and a warning falls into the console |

In the two places where it says "silently skipped", `setClipEntry` returns without throwing: the code that wraps it thinks the text was copied.

## 2. The Solution: Three Pieces

| # | Piece | What it gives |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Build the type on the platform.** One `expect` function, five counterparts | Common code says "this text"; it does not know the platform's type |
| 2 | **Make the result an answer.** A suspending function that wraps the write: was it copied | The button says what happened, not that it was pressed. Everything the platform throws is one answer: it could not be copied. The one exception is cancellation, which is thrown again |
| 3 | **Know the clipboard's traits beforehand.** Is there a clipboard to write to; does the system show what was copied itself | The two cases that throw no error are told right too: the page with no clipboard, and Android 13 |

Without the third piece the first two go wrong in two places. On a page with no clipboard no error is thrown, and the answer is "copied"; on Android 13 the answer is right, but the app says once more what the system has just shown.

## 3. With Pantrix

The library gives all three pieces (`com.pantrixui.foundation.platform`):

| API | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `rememberPantrixClipboard()` | A clipboard for plain text: over the clipboard `LocalClipboard` gives, with the traits of `LocalClipboardTraits`. It is the same object across recompositions; when the clipboard or the traits change, a new one is given |
| `PantrixClipboard.copyText(text, label)` | Puts the text on the clipboard and says whether it was put (`suspend`, `Boolean`). If there is no clipboard to write to, it does not go to the clipboard at all and says `false`. `label` is carried only on Android |
| `PantrixClipboard.traits` | This clipboard's traits |
| `ClipboardTraits(writable, announcedBySystem)` | Two traits: is there a clipboard to write to; does the system show what was copied itself |
| `currentClipboardTraits()` | The platform's traits, as they are at the moment asked. On Android from API 33, `announcedBySystem`; in the browser if the page is not in a secure context, and on the desktop if the JVM runs headless, `writable` is false |
| `LocalClipboardTraits` | The traits `rememberPantrixClipboard()` looks at. If none are given, the platform's; a test gives another platform's from here |

### 3.1. The Copy Button

```kotlin
// commonMain
@Composable
fun CopyLinkButton(link: String) {
    val clipboard = rememberPantrixClipboard()
    val snackbars = LocalPantrixSnackbars.current
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    PantrixButton(
        text = "Copy the link",
        onClick = {
            scope.launch {
                // Suspends: in the browser it returns when the write is done.
                // The answer says what happened, not that it was pressed.
                val copied = clipboard.copyText(link, label = "Link")
                val message = when {
                    !copied -> "The link could not be copied"
                    // Android 13 and above: the system shows what was copied itself.
                    clipboard.traits.announcedBySystem -> null
                    else -> "Link copied"
                }
                message?.let { snackbars?.show(message = it) }
            }
        }
    )
}
```

Not one line looks at the platform: the same button compiles on all five targets. `rememberCoroutineScope()` is the button's own scope; if the screen is left, a copy left halfway is cancelled too, and no answer comes.

### 3.2. What the Button Says, and When It Keeps Quiet

| Case | `copyText` | Trait | The button |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Copied; the system shows nothing (desktop, iOS, browser, Android 12L and below) | `true` | `announcedBySystem = false` | Says "Copied" |
| Copied; the system shows it itself (Android 13 and above) | `true` | `announcedBySystem = true` | **Keeps quiet** |
| The platform refused (the browser did not allow it, the clipboard is not available at that moment) | `false` | — | Says "Could not be copied" |
| There is no clipboard to write to (a page not in a secure context) | `false`; the clipboard is not gone to | `writable = false` | Says "Could not be copied" |

*   **On every platform a failed copy is said.** The system does not show it; on Android 13 too, the app says it.
*   **`writable` is known before the press.** Drawing the button disabled from the start, or not drawing it at all, is a choice too: `enabled = clipboard.traits.writable`. The sample app in this repository draws the button, and says "could not be copied" when it is pressed.
*   **The rule is the app's.** The library says what happened; the app decides what to say. In the sample app this decision is one function, and is tested apart (`copyMessage`, `CopyMessageTest`).

### 3.3. The Label

`label` says what was put on the clipboard: "Link", "Code". Only Android carries it; the documentation of `ClipData.newPlainText` calls it "User-visible label for the clip data", so it is given in the app's language. On the other platforms it is ignored. If it is not given, it is empty.

## 4. Without Pantrix

The same solution, with Compose Multiplatform's own API only. The code below can be copied into any project; it is a simplified form of its counterparts in the library.

### 4.1. Common Code (`commonMain`)

```kotlin
/** [text], in the type this platform's clipboard takes. Only Android carries the label. */
expect fun plainTextClipEntry(label: String, text: String): ClipEntry

/** The clipboard's two traits on this platform. */
data class ClipboardTraits(
    val writable: Boolean = true,
    val announcedBySystem: Boolean = false
)

/** This platform's clipboard traits, as they are at the moment asked. */
expect fun currentClipboardTraits(): ClipboardTraits

/** The traits the buttons look at. A test gives another platform's traits from here. */
val LocalClipboardTraits = staticCompositionLocalOf { currentClipboardTraits() }

/** Puts [text] on the clipboard and says whether it was put. */
suspend fun Clipboard.copyText(
    text: String,
    label: String = "",
    traits: ClipboardTraits = currentClipboardTraits()
): Boolean = traits.writable &&
    try {
        setClipEntry(plainTextClipEntry(label, text))
        true
    } catch (cancelled: CancellationException) {
        // Cancellation is not an answer: if it is swallowed, the cancelled coroutine goes on its way.
        throw cancelled
    } catch (_: Throwable) {
        // The browser's refusal is not a Kotlin `Exception`.
        false
    }
```

`CancellationException` here is `kotlin.coroutines.cancellation.CancellationException`.

### 4.2. Platform Counterparts

```kotlin
// androidMain
actual fun plainTextClipEntry(label: String, text: String): ClipEntry =
    ClipEntry(ClipData.newPlainText(label, text))

// From Android 13 (API 33) on, the system shows what was put on the clipboard with its own preview.
actual fun currentClipboardTraits(): ClipboardTraits =
    ClipboardTraits(announcedBySystem = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU)
```

```kotlin
// jvmMain
@OptIn(ExperimentalComposeUiApi::class)
actual fun plainTextClipEntry(label: String, text: String): ClipEntry = ClipEntry(StringSelection(text))

// A JVM with no screen (headless) has no system clipboard; Compose skips writing there without throwing.
actual fun currentClipboardTraits(): ClipboardTraits =
    ClipboardTraits(writable = !GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless())
```

```kotlin
// iosMain
@OptIn(ExperimentalComposeUiApi::class)
actual fun plainTextClipEntry(label: String, text: String): ClipEntry = ClipEntry.withPlainText(text)

actual fun currentClipboardTraits(): ClipboardTraits = ClipboardTraits()
```

```kotlin
// jsMain and wasmJsMain: the same line, in two separate files
actual fun plainTextClipEntry(label: String, text: String): ClipEntry = ClipEntry.withPlainText(text)
```

```kotlin
// webMain
actual fun currentClipboardTraits(): ClipboardTraits = ClipboardTraits(writable = browserClipboardWrites())

// The browser gives the clipboard only in a secure context: https, or the machine itself.
@OptIn(ExperimentalWasmJsInterop::class)
private fun browserClipboardWrites(): Boolean =
    js("window.isSecureContext === true && Boolean(window.navigator.clipboard && window.navigator.clipboard.writeText)")
```

The question asked of the browser is written once, in `webMain`; `ClipEntry.withPlainText` cannot be, and stands apart on the two targets (see section 7, "A counterpart written in `webMain`"). In a project with only one web target, both are written in that target's source set.

### 4.3. Use

```kotlin
// commonMain
@Composable
fun CopyLinkButton(link: String, snackbars: SnackbarHostState) {
    val clipboard = LocalClipboard.current
    val traits = LocalClipboardTraits.current
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    Button(
        onClick = {
            scope.launch {
                val copied = clipboard.copyText(link, label = "Link", traits = traits)
                val message = when {
                    !copied -> "The link could not be copied"
                    // Android 13 and above: the system shows what was copied itself.
                    traits.announcedBySystem -> null
                    else -> "Link copied"
                }
                message?.let { snackbars.showSnackbar(it) }
            }
        }
    ) {
        Text("Copy the link")
    }
}
```

## 5. What the Helper Does Not Do

The helper does one job: it puts a plain text on the clipboard and says whether it was put. It does not do these:

*   **It does not read from the clipboard.** It has no call for pasting.
*   **It puts nothing but plain text.** It carries no styled text, HTML, address (URI), image or file.
*   **It does not empty the clipboard.** In Compose that is `setClipEntry(null)`.
*   **It does not mark the content as sensitive.** On Android, the mark that asks for content such as a password to be hidden while it is shown is `ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE` (the Android SDK's source); `ClipData.newPlainText` does not put it.
*   **It does not tell.** The app shows the snackbar; the helper only says what happened.

If a project is to write the first two itself, the way again parts from platform to platform. What Compose's sources show is below; the reading column is taken from Compose Foundation's own reader, which its text fields use when pasting (`ClipboardUtils.*.kt`, `readText()`). That reader is `internal`; an app cannot call it.

| Platform | Reading the text back | Something other than plain text |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Android | `getClipEntry()?.clipData?.getItemAt(0)?.text?.toString()`. At the first access to the clipboard's content the system shows a warning (by its name in Compose's documentation, "App pasted from Clipboard"); only to ask what is on the clipboard, `clipboard.nativeClipboardManager.primaryClipDescription` | Any `ClipData`: `ClipEntry(clipData)` or `clipData.toClipEntry()`. For the first address in it, `firstUriOrNull()` (experimental) |
| Desktop | `getClipEntry()?.asAwtTransferable` (experimental); if `isDataFlavorSupported(DataFlavor.stringFlavor)`, `getTransferData(DataFlavor.stringFlavor) as? String`. Foundation does this on `Dispatchers.IO`, and counts an `IOException` as "no text" | Any `Transferable`: `ClipEntry(transferable)`. If it is also a `ClipboardOwner`, it is given as the clipboard's owner |
| iOS | `getClipEntry()?.getPlainText()` (experimental). If the clipboard is empty, `getClipEntry()` returns null | Compose's `ClipEntry` carries only text ("Currently, it operates only with string(s)"); for the rest, `UIPasteboard` is used directly |
| Web | `getClipEntry()?.clipboardItems` (experimental); the first item's `getType("text/plain")` gives a `Blob`, and the text comes with `blob.text()`, as a `Promise`. The array is `Array` in `js` and `JsArray` in `wasmJs`: it is written apart on the two targets. If the browser refuses the read, Compose throws no error and returns an empty entry; if there is no `read` at all, it returns null | `ClipEntry(clipboardItems)` with your own `ClipboardItem`s (the constructor is experimental). In a browser without the full clipboard interface, Compose writes only plain text, with `writeText` |

## 6. Testing

### 6.1. A Fake Clipboard

Compose gives a test the real clipboard (see section 7, "A clipboard given no fake"). Every test that copies gives its own clipboard with `LocalClipboard`:

```kotlin
/** A clipboard that keeps everything put on it and does not touch the machine's clipboard. */
class RecordingClipboard(private val refuses: Boolean = false) : Clipboard {
    val entries = mutableListOf<ClipEntry?>()

    override suspend fun getClipEntry(): ClipEntry? = entries.lastOrNull()

    override suspend fun setClipEntry(clipEntry: ClipEntry?) {
        check(!refuses) { "NotAllowedError: Write permission denied." }
        entries += clipEntry
    }
}
```

`Clipboard` is in common code: this fake can be written in a common test too. What can be looked at there is how many times it was written to and what `copyText` says; the text inside the `ClipEntry` that comes cannot be read in common code.

### 6.2. Another Platform's Traits

The behaviour of Android 13, or of a page with no clipboard, is tested in a test that does not run on that platform too: the traits are given with `LocalClipboardTraits`.

```kotlin
// jvmTest
@OptIn(ExperimentalTestApi::class, ExperimentalComposeUiApi::class)
class CopyLinkButtonTest {
    @Test
    fun a_copy_the_system_shows_itself_is_not_told_twice() = runComposeUiTest {
        val clipboard = RecordingClipboard()
        val snackbars = PantrixSnackbarState()
        setContent {
            PantrixTheme {
                CompositionLocalProvider(
                    LocalClipboard provides clipboard,
                    // Android 13's traits, in a test that runs on the desktop.
                    LocalClipboardTraits provides ClipboardTraits(announcedBySystem = true),
                    LocalPantrixSnackbars provides snackbars
                ) {
                    CopyLinkButton(link = "https://example.com")
                }
            }
        }
        onNodeWithText("Copy the link").performClick()
        waitForIdle()
        // The text is read as the desktop reads it: with the `Transferable`'s text flavour.
        val copied = clipboard.entries.single()?.asAwtTransferable?.getTransferData(DataFlavor.stringFlavor)
        assertEquals("https://example.com", copied)
        assertEquals(null, snackbars.current)
    }
}
```

With `ClipboardTraits(writable = false)` the same test tries the page with no clipboard: nothing comes to the fake clipboard, and the button says "could not be copied". `RecordingClipboard(refuses = true)` is a browser that refuses.

### 6.3. Reading the Text That Came

Each platform's test looks at the text itself its own way:

| Platform | Where the test runs | How the text is read |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Desktop | `jvmTest`, with the fake clipboard | `entry.asAwtTransferable?.getTransferData(DataFlavor.stringFlavor)` |
| Android | Robolectric, with the real clipboard: Robolectric's clipboard is in the test's memory | `LocalClipboard.current.nativeClipboardManager.primaryClip`: the first item's `text`, `description.label` |
| iOS | The simulator, with the fake clipboard | `entry.getPlainText()` |
| Web | The browser, with Compose's own clipboard | The test's functions are put in place of `navigator.clipboard.write` and `writeText`; the `text/plain` part of the item that comes to `write` is read |

On the web the way is different. `webTest`, like `webMain`, is the source set the two targets share, and the inside of `ClipEntry` cannot be written there in one form: its items are an `Array` on one target and a `JsArray` on the other. What the test stands in for is not Compose's clipboard but the browser's: so what Compose really gives the browser is seen, and a refused write goes its real way too (`Promise.reject(new DOMException(…, 'NotAllowedError'))`). Both functions are stood in for; Compose decides which to call by looking at the browser.

## 7. Pitfalls

| Pitfall | What happens | What is done | Where it was seen |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A clipboard given no fake** | In a test, `LocalClipboard` is the platform's real clipboard: on the desktop, the system's clipboard. A test that copies writes over whatever is copied on the machine at that moment | Give your own `Clipboard` in every test | Source: `RootNodeOwner.skiko.kt` (`createPlatformClipboard()`) |
| **Reading the text in common code** | The one member, in common code, of the `ClipEntry` that comes to the fake clipboard is `clipMetadata`; the text cannot be reached | In the common test, count the writes; read the text in the platform's own test (6.3) | Source; while these tests were written |
| **`clipMetadata`** | On the desktop, iOS and the web it is `TODO()`: when called it throws `NotImplementedError` | Do not call it | Source: the four `PlatformClipboard.*.kt` (CMP-1260) |
| **An insecure context** | A page served over plain http has no clipboard. Compose skips the write, writes a warning to the console and throws no error: a button that tells the result from an error says "copied" | Ask before writing: `traits.writable` | Compose's skipping in the source: `PlatformClipboard.js.kt`, `.wasm.kt`. `writable` saying "none" in a test, with `navigator.clipboard` hidden |
| **A headless JVM** | With `java.awt.headless=true` there is no system clipboard. Compose skips the write and throws no error: a button that tells the result from an error says "copied" | Ask before writing: on the desktop `writable` is `!GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless()` | Source: `PlatformClipboard.desktop.kt`. Before the trait was added, in a temporary test: the answer `true`, what was read back `null`. The trait's rule in a test: `desktopClipboardTraits(headless = true)` |
| **`catch (e: Exception)`** | The browser's refusal is not a Kotlin `Exception` (in JS it is the browser's own error, in Wasm a `JsException`). Code that catches only `Exception` misses it; the error is thrown from the button's coroutine | Catch `Throwable` | Test: with the catch narrowed to `Exception`, `a_write_the_browser_refuses_is_answered_false` is red on both JS and Wasm |
| **A swallowed cancellation** | `catch (e: Throwable)` catches cancellation too: the coroutine of a screen that was left goes on its way with the answer "could not be copied" | Catch `CancellationException` first and throw it again | Test: `a_copy_whose_coroutine_is_cancelled_is_cancelled_and_answers_nothing` |
| **A copy told twice** | On Android 13 and above the system shows what was copied with its own preview; if the app says so too, the same thing is said twice | Keep quiet while `announcedBySystem`; still say a failed copy | Android's documentation; see section 8, "Not Verified" |
| **A counterpart written in `webMain`** | If `ClipEntry.withPlainText` is called in `webMain`, the two targets' builds pass; the shared source set's build (`compileWebMainKotlinMetadata`) and the editor say "Unresolved reference 'withPlainText'" | Write the counterpart in `jsMain` and in `wasmJsMain` separately | By compiling with a temporary file |
| **Experimental marks** | The desktop's constructor, iOS's `withPlainText` and, on the reading side, `asAwtTransferable`, `getPlainText()` and `clipboardItems` carry `@ExperimentalComposeUiApi`; they can change in a later version of Compose | Let the `@OptIn` stand in one place, inside the helper | Source |
| **A web test that stands in for one function** | Compose calls `write` if the full clipboard interface is there, and `writeText` if not. If the test stood in for only one, the other writes to the real clipboard | Stand in for both; before copying, see that they are in place | Source: `PlatformClipboard.js.kt`, `.wasm.kt` |
| **`nativeClipboard` on a fake clipboard** | The interface's `nativeClipboard` is deprecated, and throws `NotImplementedError` if it is not given. On the desktop a text field's right-click menu still asks the clipboard with it | Not needed for a copy button. If the same test also has a text field's menu, give it on the fake clipboard too | Source: `Clipboard.kt`, `ClipboardUtils.desktop.kt`. In this repository, `TextFieldDesktopTest` |
| **Reading on Android** | `getClipEntry()` reaches the clipboard's content; at the first access the system shows the warning "App pasted from Clipboard" | Only to ask what is there, `primaryClipDescription` | Source: the documentation of `Clipboard.kt` |
| **A label that carries no language** | The label is a text the user sees; a label buried in the code stays in the old language when the app's language changes | Let the caller give the label, in the app's language | The Android SDK's source (`ClipData.newPlainText`); test: the label comes on Android and not elsewhere |

## 8. Verification

### Tests

| Test | Where it runs | What it looks at |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ui/foundation`, `PantrixClipboardTest` | The JVM, the iOS simulator, JS, Wasm (9 tests) | A copy puts an entry on the clipboard and says `true`; while there is no clipboard to write to it says `false` and does not touch the clipboard at all; whatever the clipboard throws, the answer is `false`; a cancelled copy is cancelled and gives no answer; the remembered clipboard is the same across recompositions, is a new one when the clipboard or the traits change, and looks at the new one |
| `ui/foundation`, `PantrixClipboardOnTheDesktopTest` | The JVM (3 tests) | What comes is a `Transferable` whose text flavour is the text given; line ends, non-ASCII letters and emoji come whole; the desktop's traits: written on a JVM with a screen, not on a headless one |
| `ui/foundation`, `PantrixClipboardOnAndroidTest` | Robolectric (7 tests) | The first item on the system's clipboard is the text given, its label the label given, its type plain text; if no label is given it is empty; `announcedBySystem` is true on API 33 and 34, and false on 32 and 30 |
| `ui/foundation`, `PantrixClipboardOnIosTest` | The iOS simulator (3 tests) | The `getPlainText()` of the entry that comes is the text given; a hard text comes whole; iOS's traits |
| `ui/foundation`, `PantrixClipboardOnTheWebTest` | JS and Wasm in ChromeHeadless (5 tests) | On the test runner's page `writable` is true; with `navigator.clipboard` hidden it is false; the `text/plain` part of the item given to the browser is the text given; a hard text comes whole; the answer to a write the browser refuses is `false` |
| `app/shared`, `CodeBlockTest` | The JVM (5 tests) | The sample app's copy button puts the code on the clipboard and says so; it says "could not be copied" for a refusing clipboard and for a page with no clipboard; it does not say a copy the system shows |
| `app/shared`, `CopyMessageTest` | The JVM, the iOS simulator, JS, Wasm (3 tests) | The rule of what is said after a copy |

For 32 on Android no separate runtime was downloaded: Robolectric keeps the version number in a writable field, and the test writes 32 into that field on 33's runtime and puts it back. 30, 33 and 34 run on their own runtimes.

### Behaviours Broken by Hand

Each behaviour was broken once by hand, and which test turned red was looked at; then it was put back.

*   **Common code:** the write never made; `false` said after writing; `writable` not looked at; `true` said to a clipboard that throws; only `Exception` caught; the cancellation swallowed; `remember` removed; the clipboard or the traits taken out of its keys; the traits not read from `LocalClipboardTraits`; the label and the text swapped. In all eleven a test turned red.
*   **The platforms:** on each platform, the label put in place of the text; on Android, the bound moved to 34, to 32 and to 30; on the desktop and iOS, the traits changed; in the browser, the question always saying "there is" and always "there is none". In all of them a test of that platform turned red.
*   **Seen in one place only:** when the default of `LocalClipboardTraits` is empty traits instead of the platform's, no test turns red on the JVM, because the two are the same there. On Android `on_android_14_a_remembered_clipboard_knows_the_system_shows_a_copy_itself` turns red.

### Not Verified

*   **Android 13's preview.** That the system shows what was copied itself, and asks the app not to say it a second time, is from Android's documentation. That it was seen in this repository on an Android 14 emulator is written in `docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md`; it was not looked at again while this guide was written. Robolectric does not draw the preview: the tests look only at what the trait says on which version.
*   **A real http page.** The insecure context was not tried on a page served over plain http. In the test, `navigator.clipboard` was hidden from the page; that Compose skips the write in that case was read in the source, not seen in a test.
*   **The browser's real refusal.** Under which conditions a browser refuses the write was not looked at. The refusal in the test is one the test put there itself; no test wrote to a real clipboard.
*   **A browser without the full clipboard interface.** The way where Compose falls back to `writeText` (by the note in the source, Firefox older than 127) did not run in any browser. The tests ran only in ChromeHeadless 154.
*   **The real clipboards.** On the desktop, iOS and the browser no test wrote to the system's clipboard. That what was copied can be pasted into another app was not looked at for this guide.
*   **A very large text on Android.** That a text too large for the system to carry is refused was not tried. What is seen in the source is that the service's error is thrown as a `RuntimeException`.
*   **A clipboard not available on the desktop.** `IllegalStateException` is written in the JDK's documentation; it was not seen.
*   **A headless JVM itself.** AWT decides once for a JVM whether it has a screen, and it cannot be changed later. The test tries the rule (`desktopClipboardTraits`) and looks at whether the answer of the JVM it runs on comes from that rule; it did not run on a headless JVM.
*   **The iOS simulator's clipboard.** The simulator can share its clipboard with the machine it runs on; the iOS tests therefore run with the fake clipboard. The sharing itself was not tried.
*   **The quiet systems.** That the system does not show a copy itself on the desktop, iOS, the browser and Android 12L and below is the library's assumption (`announcedBySystem = false`); it was not looked at on real devices.
*   **A screen reader.** How a copy is announced aloud was not looked at.
